title: Severed-IndexedDB recovery only wired into voice; all Liquids tabs fail every save until reload and swallow the cause
description: db.ts documents that Android Chrome severs the IndexedDB connection (issue #287), after which Dexie rejects EVERY operation with DatabaseClosedError until db.open() is called, and autoOpen does not cover it. recoverClosedDatabase() exists but its only caller is voice-panel. WaterTab/BeverageTab/PresetTab and the Liquids edit form catch with a bare `catch {}` and show a generic toast. They never reopen or retry, and never log the error, so the error-log/bug-report pipeline never records the cause. Live queries on the card also stop updating, so totals go stale.
evidence:
grep recoverClosedDatabase -> only components/voice/voice-panel.tsx:391. water-tab.tsx:56-68: `await waterIntake.addRecord(pendingAmount, "manual"); ... } catch { toast({ title: "Error", description: "Failed to record intake" ...` (no console.error, no recovery). db.ts:680: "After that Dexie rejects every operation with DatabaseClosedError until `open()` is called again; autoOpen does NOT cover this case".
---
[repro-water-save#5] water-tab.tsx:63-68 `} catch { toast({ title: "Error", description: "Failed to record intake", variant: "destructive" }); }`; `grep -rn recoverClosedDatabase apps/web/src` shows it only in voice-panel.tsx:20,391 and its definition in db.ts:689. GitHub #296 triage: 'the app has no handling for the IndexedDB connection being dropped'. Not reproduced here: fake-indexeddb cannot simulate a severed backend.
failure_scenario: On the Android app/PWA, the browser evicts or severs the IDB connection while the app is backgrounded. The user returns and taps Confirm Entry: the toast says 'Failed to record intake'. Every retry fails the same way until the app is fully reloaded. Nothing is logged, and the totals and Recent list are frozen. This matches 'saving doesn't work all the time'.
suggested_fix: Move DatabaseClosedError recovery into a shared layer (e.g. a withDbRecovery wrapper used by useIntake.addRecord, useLogDrink, useAddComposableEntry, update/sync mutations, or a global db.on('close') guarded against intentional close). Replace the bare catches with console.error(cause) so the error-log captures it.
verifier_corrections: 1) Wrong premise: Dexie 4.4.5 auto-reopens after an unexpected connection close (idbdb.onclose -> close({disableAutoOpen:false}); dexie.mjs:4577), after InvalidStateError (dexie.mjs:1195) and after pagehide/versionchange. The db.ts comment "autoOpen does NOT cover this case" was inferred, not observed (commit 97335f39 says the #287 report had no error logs). The persistent-failure state only arises once a reopen attempt has itself failed (dbOpenError set with openComplete=true). So "every retry fails until reload" applies only after a failed reopen, not after every sever. 2) Adding console.error would not fix "nothing is logged" in that state, because the error log is stored in the same broken Dexie DB (_errorLogs). 3) The live-query staleness claim is unverified. 4) Additional bare catches were missed: beverage-tab.tsx:126 and preset-tab.tsx:227 and :325. Severity lowered from high to medium.

1. Part of "every retry fails until the app is fully reloaded" is overstated: a voice-panel save that hits the error calls db.open(). That restores the connection for the whole app, including the Liquids tabs and live queries.
2. The logging claim needs a correction. The error-log pipeline (error-log-service.ts:91, `db._errorLogs.put`) writes to the same severed IndexedDB. Adding console.error to the catches would show the cause in devtools, but it would not be saved to the bug-report log until the database is reopened. So the fix has to reopen the database first. Adding console.error alone would not make the cause show up in bug reports.
3. The finding also points at the Liquids edit form but gives no line for it. I only verified the water, beverage and preset tab catches.

One claim is overstated. Adding console.error in the catch blocks would not get the cause into the error-log/bug-report pipeline in this scenario. The error log is itself an IndexedDB table (db._errorLogs, written by lib/error-log-service.ts), so while the connection is severed that write would fail with DatabaseClosedError too, unless recovery runs first or the log is buffered in memory. The missing logging still makes debugging harder in general, but the fix is recovery; logging alone won't help here. The finding lists 7 file:line locations; the full set of bare catches is water-tab.tsx:63/87, beverage-tab.tsx:101/126 and preset-tab.tsx:227/291/325. I did not check the Liquids edit form specifically.

title: Deleting a beverage-with-sugar or a solute-only preset drink orphans its sugar/salt rows (and a test enshrines it)
description: classifyLiquidDelete only deletes the whole group when the group has a live SubstanceRecord (caffeine/alcohol). A Beverage-tab entry with sugar is stored as a water+sugar group with no substance, and a preset/voice drink logged via logDrink with only salt/sugar/potassium has no substance either. Deleting the water row from the Liquids card therefore soft-deletes only the water row. The sugar/salt rows stay live, keep counting toward daily sugar/sodium totals, and become invisible in the Liquids card. The existing unit test asserts this wrong behaviour.
failure_scenario: User logs 'Cola 330 ml, 35 g sugar' on the Beverage tab, realises it was a mistake, and deletes it from Recent. Water drops by 330 ml but 35 g sugar stays in today's sugar total with no UI entry left to delete it from.
suggested_fix: Treat a group as a drink when it has no live eating record, regardless of substances (any non-eating group whose water row is deleted should take its solutes/substances). Update the test to expect 'group'.
verifier_corrections: The finding says there is "no UI entry left to delete it from", which is overstated. The orphaned sugar and salt IntakeRecords are still listed in the Analytics records tab (`components/analytics/records-tab.tsx` renders `RecordRow`, and `record-row.tsx` handles sugar and salt types), so a user who notices can delete them there. What the user actually sees: the rows vanish from the Liquids card while the daily sugar/sodium totals stay inflated, with no hint at the point of deletion. Undo is a partial restore of the same kind: the delete only removed the water row, so undo only restores that row. I lowered severity to medium because the data can be recovered and it is not corrupted. It is still a real integrity bug in totals shown to the user, and sodium matters here because this user tracks salt limits. The finding lists `composable-entry-service.ts` twice with overlapping line ranges (226-244 and 232-247); the function body is at roughly 227-245.

"No UI entry left to delete it from" is overstated. The orphaned sugar and salt rows are still intake records. They show up in, and can be deleted from, the History/Analytics records tab (records-tab.tsx uses useDeleteIntake, and record-row.tsx renders sugar and salt rows with a Delete button). The user can recover, but only if they notice that the daily total is still inflated. Because the fix is manual and nothing is permanently lost, I lowered the severity from high to medium. Everything else in the finding (the code quote, the reachability through the Beverage tab and logDrink, and the test that expects this behaviour) is accurate.

The claim that no UI entry remains to delete the orphaned rows from is wrong. Analytics > Records (apps/web/src/components/analytics/records-tab.tsx:188-198, Sugar/Salt filters) lists the orphaned sugar and salt intake rows and can delete them. The effect is silently inflated sugar and sodium totals that the user can fix by hand, not unrecoverable data. Severity should be medium, not high.

title: Undo of a group delete resurrects substances/sugar the user had previously removed
description: undoDeleteEntryGroup restores every record in the group with deletedAt !== null. It does not restore only the ones the delete just tombstoned. Records soft-deleted earlier by edits (caffeine cleared in the edit form, duplicate substances de-duplicated by syncLiquidEntrySubstances, a removed sugar row) come back to life.
evidence:
`for (const record of records) { if (record.deletedAt !== null) { await table.update(record.id, { deletedAt: null, ... })`. Scratch test: logDrink(Irish coffee, caffeine 80, abv 10) → edit caffeineMg:0 → live caffeine 0 → deleteEntryGroup → undoDeleteEntryGroup → live caffeine 1.
---
[food-salt-voice#5] `if (record.deletedAt !== null) { await table.update(record.id, { deletedAt: null, ...` (no check against the delete timestamp). Scratch test: meal with salt 500 and water 100, then edit waterMl to 0, then deleteEntryGroup, then undoDeleteEntryGroup. Live rows afterwards were `['water:100','salt:500']`, so the water row the user removed came back.
failure_scenario: User edits a drink to remove its caffeine, later deletes the drink, then taps Undo. The drink returns with the 80 mg caffeine they had removed, inflating caffeine totals and syncing to the server.
suggested_fix: Have deleteEntryGroup return the ids it tombstoned (or the shared `now` stamp). Undo should restore only records whose deletedAt equals that stamp.
verifier_corrections:
1. The meal scenario from the merged `food-salt-voice#5` report (meal with water set to 0, then group delete and undo) can't happen from the UI at HEAD. `deleteEntryGroup` is only called from `useDeleteLiquidEntry`, and `classifyLiquidDelete` returns record scope whenever the group has a live eating record. The scratch test only shows the service-level behaviour.
2. The drink scenario needs at least one substance still live after the edit. Removing caffeine only leads to group delete and wrongful restore when, for example, alcohol remains.
3. Severity is overstated. Medium fits better than high.

Severity is overstated. Triggering it needs edit, then group delete, then Undo within the 5 s toast window, so medium fits better than high. Everything else in the finding is accurate. For the reproduction to work, logDrink takes `description` (not a name field), and syncLiquidEntrySubstances needs the intake id from the group.

The meal scenario from food-salt-voice#5 (meal with salt and water, set waterMl to 0, deleteEntryGroup, undo) cannot happen from the UI at HEAD. deleteEntryGroup is only reached through useDeleteLiquidEntry, and classifyLiquidDelete returns single-record scope whenever a live eating record exists, so a meal group never goes through the group delete and undo. The drink scenario is also narrower than described. With only caffeine on the drink, clearing it leaves no live substance, so the later delete is single-record and nothing comes back. The bug needs a drink with at least two substances where one of them stays live. Severity should drop from high to medium.

title: Editing a drink's time/volume leaves its sugar/salt/potassium rows (and hidden sugar) at the old timestamp
description: syncLiquidEntrySubstances moves only caffeine/alcohol/sugar, and only when the matching patch field is non-null. Salt and potassium solute rows written by logDrink are never touched. Sugar is skipped when the sugar tracker is disabled (sugarG null). It is also skipped whenever the field was not prefilled. Food water-content rows edited from the Liquids card move without their eating record. The group is split across days.
evidence:
liquids-card.tsx:227 `const sugarG = sugarEnabled ? parse(editSugarG, prefilled.sugar) : null;`. The sync has no salt/potassium branch. Scratch test: logDrink(ts=3 days ago, caffeine 80, sugar 10, salt 100) then edit timestamp=now with sugarG null ⇒ `[ 'salt', 100, 'OLD' ], [ 'water', 250, 'NEW' ], [ 'sugar', 10, 'OLD' ]`, caffeine 'NEW'.
---
[substance-sugar#7] syncLiquidEntrySubstances patch type: `{ timestamp; volumeMl; description?; caffeineMg; alcoholAbv; sugarG }` (no salt/potassium). Alcohol branch: `standardDrinksFromAbv(abvPercent, patch.volumeMl)`; caffeine branch: `amountMg = Math.round(patch.caffeineMg)` (unchanged form value).
failure_scenario: User logs a salted broth or sugary drink at the wrong time (yesterday) and fixes the time in the edit form. Water and caffeine move to today, but the salt/sugar stay on yesterday's totals.
suggested_fix: On every liquid edit, update timestamp on all live group members (intakes, substances, eating) in the same transaction, independent of which substance fields were patched.
verifier_corrections: Minor. The claim that food water-content rows edited from the Liquids card move without their eating record was not traced in detail. It is plausible, since syncLiquidEntrySubstances never touches eatingRecords, but it is unverified. The cited range 646-858 also covers alcohol and caffeine handling that is correct. The core claim about salt, potassium and conditional sugar is accurate.

This is mostly accurate. I did not independently repro the sub-claim that food water-content rows edited from the Liquids card move without their eating record, but it follows from the same code, which never touches eatingRecords. Potassium is also left behind, not just salt and sugar. In the UI, the salt and potassium rows are mainly produced through the voice-panel logDrink path.

title: Edit form resurrects a deleted caffeine/alcohol record from the current preset's values
description: For source 'preset:<id>' entries, onOpen synchronously prefills caffeine/ABV from the CURRENT preset settings and marks them prefilled=true. The async group fetch only overrides when a live substance exists. If the group's caffeine was removed (via history or dedup), or the entry is a legacy group-less row, the preset-derived value stays. Saving any unrelated change (e.g. the note) then creates a fresh caffeine/alcohol record (and a new group for legacy rows, duplicating the legacy substance). If Save is pressed before the fetch resolves, the stored value is overwritten with the preset's current value.
evidence: `if (preset.caffeinePer100ml !== undefined && preset.caffeinePer100ml > 0) { ... setEditCaffeineMg(mg.toString()); prefilledRef.current.caffeine = true; }`. The async path: `if (caffeine?.amountMg !== undefined) {...}` with no reset when absent. Scratch service test: caffeine soft-deleted, then syncLiquidEntrySubstances(caffeineMg: 80) ⇒ `live caffeine 1`.
failure_scenario: User removes the caffeine record of a decaf mistakenly logged with the Coffee preset, then opens the water row to fix the time and saves. The 95 mg caffeine record reappears.
suggested_fix: Do not prefill substance fields from presets when the record has a groupId. Wait for the group read and prefill only from stored records, and disable Save until the prefill resolves.
verifier_corrections: The failure scenario given ("remove the caffeine record via history, then reopen the water row") cannot happen. deleteSubstanceRecord removes the whole drink group, water row included (apps/web/src/lib/substance-service.ts:150-170), so no water row is left to edit. The path that does work: clear the caffeine or ABV field in the edit form and save, then reopen the entry. The preset value is pre-filled again, and the next save of any change brings the substance back. The value is visible in the form, so the user can catch it before saving. "Removed via dedup" has no supporting evidence. The save-before-fetch race is realistic only in theory, because the group read is from local IndexedDB. Severity should be low rather than medium.

The failure scenario is wrong. "Remove the caffeine record via history, then edit the water row" cannot happen: deleteSubstanceRecord (apps/web/src/lib/substance-service.ts:150-192) also soft-deletes the grouped water row and sibling substances, so there is nothing left to edit. The dedup part of the claim was not verified either. The path that does reach the bug is inside the same edit form: clear the caffeine field and save (the record is soft-deleted, the water row stays with source `preset:<id>` and its groupId), then reopen the row for an unrelated edit and save. The preset prefill (liquids-card.tsx:128-132) is not cleared by the group read (lines 156-159), so the caffeine record is created again.

title: Future-dated entries count toward 'today' and the 24h total every day until their date
description: getDailyTotal and getRecordsInLast24Hours only apply a lower bound (aboveOrEqual cutoff). The inline edit form's datetime-local has no max, and the manual dialog only uses the HTML `max` attribute. A mistyped future date (e.g. 2027) therefore makes that entry count in every day's total and sit at the top of Recent until that date passes.
evidence:
`.where("timestamp").aboveOrEqual(cutoffTime).filter(...)` with no upper bound. Scratch test: addIntakeRecord('water', 500, 'manual', now+5 days) ⇒ getDailyTotal=500, getTotalInLast24Hours=500.
---
[core-duplication#14] intake-service.ts:106 `.where("timestamp").aboveOrEqual(cutoffTime)`; text-metrics.tsx `useSubstanceRecordsByDateRange(dayStart, now, "caffeine")`; mcp/queries.ts `lte(intakeRecords.timestamp, nowTs)`.
failure_scenario: User edits an entry's date and slips to next year. The daily water total is inflated by that amount on every day until then, and the progress bar/limit warnings are wrong.
suggested_fix: Bound both queries with `.between(cutoff, Date.now(), true, true)` and reject future timestamps in useEditRecord and ManualInputDialog.
verifier_corrections: Some line numbers are a little off. getRecordsInLast24Hours is at lines 87-97, and getDailyTotal's aboveOrEqual is at lines 106-108. The core claim is accurate. The manual dialog's HTML `max` may stop future dates in native mobile pickers, so the edit dialogs are the main way this happens. I did not re-verify the text-metrics.tsx and mcp/queries.ts citations, which are secondary. The finding does not depend on them.

Minor corrections only. `getRecordsInLast24Hours` does not use `.filter()` in the query; it filters the array afterwards, which gives the same result. The line numbers are slightly off (the queries are at about lines 90 and 106). The HTML `max` on the manual dialog does exist (manual-input-dialog.tsx:186), but the browser does not enforce it on the datetime-local value in JavaScript, so the claim that it is an insufficient guard still stands.

title: Coffee/alcohol drinks logged via AI lookup or edited values show with no name; renaming a drink never changes its label
description: PresetTab tags the water row `preset:manual` whenever no preset is selected: after an AI lookup, or as soon as the volume or per-100ml value is touched, since those clear selectedPresetId. getLiquidTypeLabel returns null for 'preset:manual' and ignores the note, even though logDrink stores the drink name in the note. For 'preset:<id>' rows the label is always the preset's current name, or 'Beverage' once the preset is deleted. Presets live only in localStorage, so after a restore on a new device they are gone too. The edit form's 'Beverage name' updates only SubstanceRecord.description (source is rewritten only for beverage: rows), so the label shown in Recent/History never changes. The drink name also shows up duplicated in the 'Note' field.
failure_scenario: User looks up 'Flat white' with AI and logs it. Recent shows '250ml' with no label, identical to plain water. They open it, set Beverage name to 'Flat white' and save. Label still blank, so the edit appears not to have saved.
suggested_fix: Label preset:/drink rows from the note/substance description first and fall back to the preset name. Have the edit form's beverage name also update the water row's note (or a dedicated name field).
verifier_corrections:
Minor clarifications:
- The AI lookup path gives an unlabeled row only when the user presses plain "Log". "Save & Log" tags the row with the new preset's id, so it shows the preset name. That label still won't follow later renames and becomes "Beverage" if the preset is deleted.
- The "restore on a new device" point assumes liquidPresets are not synced or backed up. I did not verify that. The rest of the finding holds as stated.

Minor corrections:
- The Beverage name field only appears when the entry has a linked caffeine or alcohol record (liquids-card.tsx:154-155). A drink with only salt, sugar or no substances can't be renamed there at all.
- The finding cites liquids-card.tsx:202-210 for the edit logic. The rewrite that matters is at lines 207-210.
- The finding's line references for the `logDrink` water-row note are slightly off. The `note: input.description` line is in the transaction block around line 108 of drink-service.ts.
- The claim that presets are lost on a new device (localStorage only) is plausible, but I did not verify it.

title: Amount parsing silently truncates: '1e3' logs 1 ml, '250.7' logs 250 ml
description: Both the manual dialog and the edit form use parseInt on a type=number input. Scientific notation and decimals that the input accepts are truncated without a warning, unlike the Settings helpers, which use Number() for this exact reason.
evidence: `const amount = parseInt(value, 10);`. Scratch DOM test: set amount '1e3' → Add Entry ⇒ DB amounts `[ 1 ]`.
failure_scenario: User types 1e3 (or a keyboard autocorrect produces it) and 1 ml is logged instead of 1000 ml, with no error.
suggested_fix: Use Number(value) with an integer check (or Math.round) and show a field error on non-integers.
verifier_corrections: The '250.7 logs 250 ml' half is not reachable in a real browser. Native constraint validation blocks it in the manual dialog (step="1", no noValidate on the form) and in the edit input (the default step for type=number is 1). The scratch test ran in jsdom, which skips constraint validation. Only the '1e3' → 1 ml truncation is a real silent-truncation path, and on mobile it needs a keyboard that offers the 'e' key. The claim that Settings uses Number() "for this exact reason" is an inference: liquid-presets-section.tsx does use Number() and is inconsistent with these forms, but the code gives no reason for the choice.

title: Beverage tab clears the name on Confirm but not after a dialog entry; the Beverage dialog is titled 'Water'
description: handleConfirm resets pendingAmount, beverageName and sugar. handleManualSubmit resets only sugar and closes the dialog, so the next quick log silently reuses the previous beverage name. The dialog opened from the Beverage tab is type='water' ('Enter Water Amount').
evidence: handleManualSubmit: `setShowManualInput(false); setSugarG("");` (no setBeverageName). handleConfirm: `setPendingAmount(waterIncrement); setBeverageName(""); setSugarG("");`.
failure_scenario: User logs 'Juice' through the dialog, then later taps Log Beverage for a smoothie without noticing the name field. That entry is saved as 'Juice'.
suggested_fix: Share one post-save reset between both paths.
verifier_corrections:
- **Wrong line numbers:** the file is only 263 lines, so lines 305-307, 331-332 and 463 do not exist. The correct lines are 98-100 (handleConfirm reset), 124-125 (handleManualSubmit reset) and 256 (`type="water"`). The title string is at manual-input-dialog.tsx:104.
- **"Silently" overstates it:** the name input stays visible above the controls, still showing the old text, so a careful user could notice it.
- **Also missed:** the dialog path does not reset pendingAmount either, but that has no effect on which name is saved.

title: Water tab 'isLoading' guard is dead — useLiveQuery defaults make it always false
description: useIntakeTotal/useDailyIntakeTotal pass a default of 0 to useLiveQuery, so dailyTotal/rollingTotal are never undefined and isLoading is always false. The Confirm button's `waterIntake.isLoading` disable is a no-op, and the header/progress show 0 ml during the initial query (or permanently if the query dies, see the DB-closed finding) instead of a loading state.
evidence: `return useLiveQuery(() => getDailyTotal(type, dayStartHour), [type, dayStartHour, tick], 0);` … `isLoading: dailyTotal === undefined || rollingTotal === undefined`.
failure_scenario: Right after cold start, or after the IDB connection is severed, the card shows '0 ml / 2000 ml today', which looks like data loss, with no way to tell it is still loading.
suggested_fix: Drop the default (undefined while loading) and render a loading state, or remove the dead isLoading field.
verifier_corrections: The failure scenario overstates the impact. On a normal cold start the Dexie query finishes within milliseconds, so the '0 ml' flash is barely visible and would not look like data loss. The 'permanently if the query dies' case depends on a separate DB-closed finding, not on this one. Having the Confirm button enabled while loading does no harm, because saving a record doesn't depend on the totals. What's left is a dead guard plus a brief, misleading zero on first paint. That fits low severity.

title: 'Save as preset & log' saves the preset before logging, and a stale salt value carries over after AI lookup
description: handleSaveAndLog calls addPreset (synchronous, persisted) before logDrink. If logging fails, the preset exists anyway and the toast wrongly says 'Failed to save preset'. handleAiLookup resets caffeine/alcohol but not saltPer100ml, and the tab has no salt input. A salt value from a previously selected preset is silently logged with the AI result and saved into the new preset. calculatedDisplay hides salt whenever caffeine/ABV is present.
evidence: handleAiLookup sets caffeine/alcohol/volume/name/waterContent only; `if (parts.length === 0 && saltPer100ml > 0)` for the salt display.
failure_scenario: User taps a custom salted preset, then AI-looks-up 'cola' and logs it. Hidden sodium from the earlier preset is added to the cola and saved into the new 'Cola' preset.
suggested_fix: Reset saltPer100ml (and all derived fields) at the start of an AI lookup, always show salt in the calculated line, and add the preset only after logDrink succeeds.
verifier_corrections: No factual errors. Two small gaps: (a) the AI lookup also doesn't clear `sugarG`, but the user can see and edit that field, so it's a smaller problem. (b) On the beverage tab the lookup sets caffeine but never resets alcohol, so a leftover ABV value can carry over there too, the same way salt does.

title: LiquidPreset has no sugar field: 'Save as preset & log' silently drops sugar and selecting a preset never sets/clears sugar
description: Presets store caffeine, alcohol and salt per 100 ml but not sugar. handleSaveAndLog builds the preset without sugar. selectPreset and deselect never touch sugarG, so sugar typed for one drink carries over to the next preset tapped. Sugar is also absolute grams while every other preset nutrient is per-100ml, so changing the volume (250→500 ml) doubles caffeine and salt but leaves sugar unchanged. The Settings preset editor has no sugar input either.
evidence:
constants.ts LiquidPreset: `caffeinePer100ml?`, `alcoholPer100ml?`, `saltPer100ml?` (no sugar). preset-tab.tsx addPreset({... ...(caffeinePer100ml > 0 && ...), ...(alcoholPer100ml > 0 && ...), ...(saltPer100ml > 0 && ...)}) has no sugar; selectPreset sets volume/caffeine/alcohol/salt/water/name only. buildDrink: `caffeineMg: Math.round((volumeMl / 100) * caffeinePer100ml)` vs `sugarG: sugar` (unscaled).
---
[repro-sugar#2] constants.ts LiquidPreset fields: `caffeinePer100ml?`, `alcoholPer100ml?`, `saltPer100ml?`, no sugar. Scratch test: `SAVED PRESET: {"name":"Coca-Cola","tab":"coffee","defaultVolumeMl":330,"waterContentPercent":90,"caffeinePer100ml":10,"isDefault":false,"source":"ai",...}`. Re-tapping the preset gives `SUGAR FIELD after selecting saved preset: ""`, and a second log leaves `SUGAR ROWS R3 after 2nd log of same preset: [ 35 ]` (still only the first drink's sugar).
failure_scenario: The user logs 'Oat latte 350 ml, 14 g sugar' and taps 'Save as preset & log'. Next day, tapping the 'Oat latte' preset shows Sugar blank, and the logged latte records 0 g sugar. If sugar is typed and the user then picks a 500 ml size, sugar stays 14 g while caffeine scales.
suggested_fix: Add sugarPer100ml (and potassiumPer100ml) to LiquidPreset. Scale it by volume in buildDrink like caffeine and salt, set it in selectPreset, clear it on deselect, and persist it in handleSaveAndLog and the Settings editor.
verifier_corrections:
1. The "sugar doesn't scale with volume" point is a design choice, not a bug. The input is explicitly labelled "Sugar (g) — optional" (preset-tab.tsx:527), so it is an absolute per-drink amount the user types. Leaving it unscaled matches that label. It would only be a problem once presets store sugar per 100 ml.
2. The cited apps/web/src/components/liquids-card.tsx:121-139 is the edit-dialog prefill logic, and that code already handles sugar (lines 151-181). It is not evidence for this finding.
3. I did not open the Settings editor (liquid-presets-section.tsx), so I didn't check the "no sugar input" claim directly. It follows necessarily from the type having no sugar field.
4. The "potassiumPer100ml" in the suggested fix is out of scope for this finding.

The core claim holds. Presets have no sugar field, `handleSaveAndLog` drops the typed sugar, and `selectPreset` and deselect leave sugar untouched. Three corrections: (1) Sugar only carries over between presets before logging, because `resetFields()` clears it after every log, so the next day's drink starts blank rather than inheriting old sugar. (2) Sugar not scaling with volume follows from the input being labelled as absolute grams ("Sugar (g)"); it is a UX inconsistency, not a calculation bug. (3) Lower the severity to medium: an optional nutrient is lost from saved presets, with no corruption or core-feature failure.

Sugar does not carry over between logged drinks, because resetFields clears sugarG after each log. It only persists across preset taps made before logging. Sugar not scaling with volume matches the "Sugar (g)" absolute-grams label, so it is not an inconsistency in the current design. The confirmed part is that presets never store or restore sugar, so later logs from a saved preset record 0 g sugar. Severity should be medium, not high: sugar goes under-reported, no existing data is corrupted, and dosing is not affected.

title: Historical alcohol standard-drink values mix 14 g and 10 g conventions; nothing re-derives them
description: Between commit 66781c98 (2026-03-29) and 2dfc4ed7 (2026-05-08), the preset tab stored amountStandardDrinks = vol × ABV × 0.789 / 14. Since then it uses 10 g (GRAMS_PER_STANDARD_DRINK = 10). Every alcohol total and trend (text-metrics, analytics, MCP) sums amountStandardDrinks directly, so the same beer counts ~0.93 drinks in April and ~1.30 drinks in June. No Dexie upgrade or backfill recomputes amountStandardDrinks from abvPercent × volumeMl. title: Editing an older meal adds a second sodium row, doubling sodium

failure_scenario: At 21:00 the user dictates 'for lunch at 1pm I had a ham sandwich, and at 4pm a latte'. Both are logged at 21:00. The latte's caffeine shows as an evening dose and the sandwich's sodium lands in the wrong part of the day, or on the next day if the user records after the day-start hour.
suggested_fix: Add an optional `time` (HH:mm or relative offset) to each item in the prompt and schema, resolve it to a timestamp on the client with the day-start rules, and show and edit it in ParsedItemRow.
verifier_corrections: This is a missing capability rather than a logic error: the voice pipeline was never built to handle times, and no code misreads a time. The finding cites only line 245, but addComposableEntry at line 307 (caffeine with no volume) also omits the timestamp, as do all the other service calls in saveItem. The "next day" part of the failure scenario only happens when the event falls before the day-start boundary and the save happens after it.

No factual errors. One gap: the finding focuses on food and caffeine, but the same problem affects every voice item kind, including blood pressure, weight, water, salt, alcohol, urination and defecation. A spoken time like "my BP this morning was..." is ignored the same way.

title: Food card AI parse drops a drink's caffeine
description: The Food card parse prompt handles drinks explicitly ('330 ml can of cola -> ~330'), but its tool returns only water, sodium, sugar and potassium, and the Food card saves an eating record plus a food-water-content row. The same drink said by voice becomes a caffeine item through logDrink, with a caffeine substance record. The same input therefore gives different records depending on the entry point, and the Food card path silently omits caffeine.
evidence: PARSE_RESULT_TOOL properties: water_ml, sodium_mg, sugar_g, potassium_mg (no caffeine). food-section.tsx:344-350 pushes `{ type: "water", source: "manual:food_water_content" }`; voice-panel.tsx:261-272 routes caffeinated drinks through logDrinkEntry with caffeineMg.
failure_scenario: The user types 'can of Coke' in the Food card and parses. 330 ml water and 35 g sugar are saved as a 'meal', with no caffeine logged. Saying 'can of Coke' by voice records ~34 mg caffeine and a drink group. Caffeine totals and the delete behaviour differ for the same drink.
suggested_fix: Have the parse tool return caffeine_mg and abv (or an is_drink flag). When the item is a drink, route it through logDrink (or send the user to the Liquids card) instead of creating an eating record.
verifier_corrections: The finding is accurate. The voice-panel line numbers are close but a little off: the caffeine branch starts at about line 256, and the logDrinkEntry call runs from about line 262 to line 273. The finding does not mention that the voice path only uses the caffeine route when the voice parser labels the item as caffeine. Voice parsing also depends on the model, but the voice prompt rules make "caffeine" the expected label for cola.

None of substance. The line ranges are approximate but point to the right code. One missing point: the Food card is aimed at food, and a separate Liquids flow exists for drinks. That limits how often this happens, but the parse prompt itself invites drink input.

title: The sodium and sugar headline caps at the limit and hides the real total when the buffer is 0
description: The headline shows `Math.min(dailyTotal, limit)`. The overshoot appears only on the 'extra' line, which is rendered only when extendedTotal > 0. The settings allow a buffer of 0, and in that case the card shows e.g. '1,500 / 1,500 mg' at any real intake above the limit. Potassium is not capped, so the three nutrient rows behave differently.
evidence: `{formatAmount(Math.min(dailyTotal, limit), "mg")} / {formatAmount(limit, "mg")}` and `{saltProgress.isOverTarget && saltProgress.extendedTotal > 0 && (...extra...)}`; settings-store.ts:359 `sanitizeNumericInput(value, 0, 10000)`.
failure_scenario: With the extended buffer set to 0, the user eats 3200 mg of sodium. The card reads '1,500 / 1,500 mg' in red. The 3200 figure appears only in the separate rolling-24h line, which may include yesterday's intake.
suggested_fix: Always show the true daily total in the headline (as potassium does), or show the extra line whenever isOverTarget is true, whatever the buffer.
verifier_corrections: None of substance. One detail: when the buffer is above 0, the headline is still capped, but the extra line shows the full overshoot (extendedCurrent is not capped at the buffer). So the real total is only lost when the buffer is 0, which is what the finding says.

title: Dead code in the food and composable area
description: ComposablePreview (286 LOC plus tests) is imported only by its own test. recalculateFromCurrentValues is a stub that always errors. useEntryGroup, useDeleteSingleGroupRecord and deleteSingleGroupRecord are used only by tests. Settings exposes a salt 'Increment (mg): Amount added with each +/- tap', but no salt +/- control exists, and useSaltSettings has no callers.
evidence: `grep ComposablePreview` finds only composable-preview.tsx and its .dom.test; composable-entry-service.ts:865 `return err("Not implemented — deferred to Phase 13/14...")`; saltIncrement is read only in the settings section and use-settings.ts.
failure_scenario: The user changes 'Salt increment' in Settings expecting faster logging, and nothing changes. Future maintainers may wire up the unused per-record delete or preview flows, assuming they are live and tested end to end.
suggested_fix: Delete ComposablePreview, recalculateFromCurrentValues, useEntryGroup, useDeleteSingleGroupRecord and the salt increment setting, or wire them up on purpose.
verifier_corrections: Minor precision fix: deleteSingleGroupRecord does have one non-test caller, the useDeleteSingleGroupRecord hook, but that hook is itself used only by tests, so the code is still unreachable from the app. Everything else is accurate.

title: Saving a Food card edit before the pre-fill loads deletes the meal's nutrients
description: openEdit blanks every nutrient field, then fills them asynchronously through fetchEntryGroup. If Save runs before the promise resolves (slow device, IndexedDB reopening), buildUpdates sends sodiumMg 0 and waterMl 0 (and 0 sugar and potassium when those trackers are enabled). syncEatingGroup reads 0 as 'soft-delete the linked row'. The form has no loading or disabled state while pre-filling.
evidence: `setEditSodiumMg(""); ... if (record.groupId) { void fetchEntryGroup(record.groupId).then(...)`; syncEatingGroup: `} else if (existingSalt) { await patchIntake(existingSalt.id, { deletedAt: now, ...`
failure_scenario: On a slow phone the user taps Edit, changes the time and taps Save straight away. The meal's sodium and water rows are soft-deleted even though the user never touched those fields.
suggested_fix: Disable Save until the group pre-fill has resolved, or send null meaning 'untouched' for fields that were never pre-filled, as the Liquids card does with prefilledRef.
verifier_corrections: The code paths and the soft-delete behaviour are described correctly. The "slow phone" scenario overstates how easy this is to hit, because the pre-fill is a few indexed IndexedDB reads that usually finish in milliseconds. A more realistic trigger is fetchEntryGroup rejecting: the `void` promise chain has no catch, so the fields stay blank and a later Save deletes the linked sodium, water, sugar and potassium rows. The deletes are soft (deletedAt is set), so the data can in principle be recovered.

title: The parse route comment says it uses Opus, but it calls the Sonnet 'quality' tier
description: The route's doc comment says it 'Uses Opus + web_search for high-quality lookups', but it calls CLAUDE_MODELS.quality, which is claude-sonnet-4-6. Voice-parse and nutrient-analysis also use Sonnet 4.6, while the registry has claude-opus-5 as the premium tier. Anyone reviewing model currency from the comments will get it wrong.
evidence: route.ts:16 'Uses Opus + web_search'; route.ts:88 `model: CLAUDE_MODELS.quality`; models.ts:13 `quality: "claude-sonnet-4-6"`.
failure_scenario: The owner reads the parse route to judge accuracy, believes nutrition estimates come from Opus, and misjudges the quality and cost of the numbers being logged.
suggested_fix: Fix the comment. Decide on purpose which tier the nutrition parse should use and record why in models.ts.
verifier_corrections: The finding missed a second stale comment of the same kind. apps/web/src/app/api/ai/substance-enrich/route.ts:15 also says "Uses Opus + web_search", but that route calls CLAUDE_MODELS.quality (Sonnet 4.6) at lines 102, 114, 126 and 149. The fix should cover both comments. Everything else in the finding is accurate.

title: Editing a schedule rewrites history: past taken doses become 'missed' and taken doses show the new amount
description: A scheduled DoseLog stores no dosage, unit or pill count. Past days are rebuilt from the CURRENT active phase and schedules, filtered only by prescription.createdAt (not phase.startDate), and logs are matched by phaseId|scheduleId. updatePhase hard-deletes any schedule row that isn't passed back with its id. The edit drawer's remove-row plus add-time sends new rows without ids, so they get new ids. Any schedule change therefore orphans every historic log, and in-place dosage edits relabel doses already taken. Adherence analytics is computed from the same function, so historic adherence changes too.
evidence:
DoseLog has no dose field (records.ts:304-327). phase-service.ts:270 `await db.phaseSchedules.bulkDelete(toDelete);`. Scratch test: past day before edit `[["taken",50]]`; after updatePhase replacing the 08:00 row with 09:00 -> `[["missed",100,"09:00"]]`; `orphan schedule row exists? false`. Editing dosage 50->100 in place: today's taken slot shows `100 taken`.
---
[doses-titration-schedule#14] phase-service.ts:270 `await db.phaseSchedules.bulkDelete(toDelete);`. dose-log-service.ts `if (prescription && phase && schedule) { result.push(...) }`.
failure_scenario: The user took 50mg every day last week, then moves the dose from 08:00 to 09:00 and 100mg in the Schedule tab. Every past day now shows 'missed 100mg', history adherence drops to 0%, and today's already-taken dose reads '100mg taken'.
suggested_fix: Snapshot the dosage, unit, pills consumed and inventory strength on the DoseLog at take/skip time. Soft-delete schedules instead of bulkDelete, or version them. Build past days from the phase and schedules that were live on that date (startDate/endDate/deletedAt), not from the current active phase.
verifier_corrections: The failure scenario overstates one path. If the user changes the time from 08:00 to 09:00 by editing the existing row in place (updateRow), the row keeps its id. Past logs stay matched: they still count as taken and adherence does not drop. They are relabeled, though, as taken at the new 09:00 time and the new dose (e.g. "100mg taken"). That misstates the dose history but does not show them as missed. Past days become "missed" and adherence falls to 0% only when the user deletes the row and adds a new one, which creates a new schedule id and hard-deletes the old one. The core claim is correct: there is no dose snapshot, history is rebuilt from the current schedule, and schedule rows are hard-deleted.

The failure scenario overstates things. Changing an existing row's time (08:00 to 09:00) and dosage (50 to 100) in the Schedule tab keeps the schedule id: the drawer carries `r.id` and `updatePhase` updates in place. Past days would then read "taken 100mg" at 09:00, not "missed", and adherence would not drop to 0%. Past doses become 'missed' only when a row is deleted and re-added (a new id, with the old one removed by bulkDelete), or when a different phase becomes active (titration start, or startNewPhase). The claim that a titration phase overrides maintenance for all past dates is also accurate and makes the history rewrite worse. The rest of the evidence, including the missing dose fields on DoseLog, the bulkDelete, the createdAt-only date filter and the shared adherence path, is accurate.

The example scenario is partly off. Changing a row's time in place (updateRow patching `time`) keeps the row's id. So moving 08:00 to 09:00 in place does NOT orphan past logs. It only moves the displayed time and changes the dosage label. Past taken doses turn into "missed" only when the user deletes a row and adds a new one, or when the phase changes. Two more paths the finding does not mention cause the same history rewrite. First, adding any new schedule row immediately adds "missed" slots to every past day since the prescription was created, because the only date filter is prescription.createdAt. Second, when a titration phase becomes active, its schedules replace the maintenance phase for all past dates as well. The maintenance logs from before then stop matching and show as "missed", and titration doses appear as "missed" on days before the titration started.

title: Undo/skip/reschedule restores stock using the current dose and strength, not what was actually deducted
description: untakeDose, skipDose and rescheduleDose work out the reversal as calculatePillsConsumed(dosageMg, inventory.strength). dosageMg comes from the caller's current slot and strength from the current inventory row. The original consumed transaction records the exact amount deducted, but the reversal never reads it (in the take path doseLogId isn't even set on a first take).
evidence:
dose-log-service.ts:480 `pillsConsumed = calculatePillsConsumed(dosageMg, inventory.strength);` in untake; takeDose:309 `...(prev?.id !== undefined && { doseLogId: prev.id })` (unset on first take). Scratch test: take 50mg (strength 50) -> stock 29; edit schedule to 100mg; untake -> `STOCK after untake 31`.
---
[doses-titration-schedule#16] takeDose line 309 `...(prev?.id !== undefined && { doseLogId: prev.id })` (undefined on first take). untake line 480 `pillsConsumed = calculatePillsConsumed(dosageMg, inventory.strength);`.
---
[core-duplication#10] dose-log-service.ts:306 `...(prev?.id !== undefined && { doseLogId: prev.id })` ; :479 `pillsConsumed = calculatePillsConsumed(dosageMg, inventory.strength); const newStock = (inventory.currentStock ?? 0) + pillsConsumed;` ; :495 `amount: pillsConsumed, type: "consumed"`.
failure_scenario: The user takes their 50mg morning dose (1 pill deducted), later changes the schedule to 100mg, then taps Undo on the morning dose. Stock goes up by 2 pills, so one phantom pill is created each time this happens.
suggested_fix: Store pillsConsumed (or the consumed transaction id) on the DoseLog and reverse exactly that amount. Better still, soft-delete the original consumed transaction instead of writing a positive 'consumed' row.
verifier_corrections: Severity is too high: it takes a take, then a dose/strength edit, then an undo/skip/reschedule of that same dose, and only the pill count is affected. Dose records and dosing info stay correct, so medium fits better than high. Line numbers are close but slightly off: the untake calc is around 479-480, skip around 549, reschedule around 620. The phantom-pill direction only applies when the dose goes up. If the dose is lowered after taking, undo returns too few pills.

Line numbers are slightly off. The reversal calculations are at about 480 (untake), 549 (skip) and 620 (reschedule), and the takeDose doseLogId spread is at about 309. The user-facing path to change the dose is edit-medication-drawer -> updatePhase, which keeps the schedule id. The raw updateSchedule service has no UI caller. Severity is better rated medium than high because it needs an edit between take and undo, and the harm is stock drift, not wrong dosing.

The stock miscount only happens when the dose (or the inventory strength) is changed between taking a dose and reversing it. Ordinary undo works correctly, so "high" overstates how often users hit this. The error can go either way: raising the dose restores too many pills, lowering it restores too few. Not every reversal creates a phantom pill. There are two causes:
- the reversal reads dosageMg from the live schedule (it is changed in place by phase-service.ts:283-289), and inventory.strength from the current row;
- the reversal never reads the amount on the original consumed transaction.

A missing doseLogId on a first take is only a secondary reason the original amount can't be looked up.

title: Wizard dose-strength parsing can save 0mg or a silent 1mg default; preview and save use different regexes
description: dosageStrength is unvalidated free text. At save time parseStrength needs digits directly followed by letters, so '1,000 mg' skips the '1,' and matches '000 mg', giving strength 0. The DosageStep preview uses a different regex (first number), so it shows 1mg while 0 is saved. An empty field or text with no digits silently becomes 1mg. With strength 0, scheduleDosage = 0mg and calculatePillsConsumed returns 0, so doses never deduct stock.
evidence: wizard.tsx:264 `if (!str) return { strength: 1, unit: "mg" };`, :265 `str.match(/(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*([a-zA-Z]+)/)` ('1,000 mg' -> strength 0). dosage-step.tsx:19 `str.match(/(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)/)` ('1,000 mg' -> 1). dose-log-service.ts:89 `if (pillStrengthMg === 0) return 0;`.
failure_scenario: The AI search returns 'Metformin 1,000 mg'. The dosage step shows '1 pill = 1mg', and the saved prescription has strength 0 and schedule dosage 0mg. The card shows '0mg', and taking doses never lowers stock. Leaving strength blank silently saves a 1mg pill and a 1mg dose.
suggested_fix: Use one shared strength parser (strip thousands separators, handle mcg/g/ml), and make positive strength a required validated field in SearchStepSchema. Show the parsed value to the user and block save when it is <= 0.
verifier_corrections: No material errors. I did not confirm that the AI actually returns comma-formatted strengths like 'Metformin 1,000 mg'. A user can still type that format by hand, and the blank-field path needs no special input at all. Also, the preview's unit parser returns "mg" for "1,000 mg" (it matches "000 mg"), so the preview label reads "1mg", as the finding says.

The failure scenario overstates the blank-field case. A blank strength saves a 1mg pill with a 1mg schedule dose, and the DosageStep preview also shows 1mg, so there is no preview/save mismatch. Stock also still decreases (1 pill per dose); only the displayed strength is wrong. The preview/save divergence and the zero stock deduction happen only with thousands separators such as "1,000 mg" or "1 000 mg", which the AI prompt's examples do not encourage. Severity should be medium (wrong in edge cases), not high.

The finding says an empty field "silently" becomes 1mg. It doesn't: the DosageStep preview uses the same fallback (strengthNum=1, unit "mg"), so the user sees 1mg-based dose buttons before saving. There's no preview/save mismatch in the empty case. The comma mismatch is real but needs comma-formatted input that is uncommon, from either the AI or the user, so high severity is overstated; medium fits better. The finding also missed the ".5 mg" case, which both parsers read as 5, a 10x error.

title: Negative or zero doses pass validation; schedule-step validation checks a field that is never used
description: ScheduleEntrySchema validates `schedules[i].dosage > 0`, but ScheduleStep has no dosage input (it is always 1), and handleSave overwrites every entry with `scheduleDosage = (finalDosage || 1) * strength`. customDosage itself is never validated. A negative custom dose ('-2' pills or '-10' mg) saves a negative schedule dosage, and '0' silently becomes 1 pill. The wizard also can't express different doses at different times, because every time gets the same dose.
evidence: wizard.tsx:285 `const finalDosage = formState.customDosage ? parseFloat(formState.customDosage) : formState.dosageAmount;` and :296 `.map((s) => ({ ...s, dosage: scheduleDosage }))`. dosage-step.tsx:92 `onFieldChange("customDosage", isNaN(pills) ? "" : String(pills));` (no sign check; min="0" is only a browser hint).
failure_scenario: The user types -2 in 'Custom pills per dose' (e.g. a stray minus). The preview reads '-2 pills per dose = -200mg total' and saving succeeds. Each 'take' then gives a negative pillsConsumed, so taking the dose adds 2 pills to stock. A 5mg morning / 2.5mg evening regimen can't be entered at all.
suggested_fix: Validate the final computed dose (> 0 and finite) in validateStep('dosage'). Add a per-time dosage to ScheduleStep, or drop the unused per-entry dosage from the schema.
verifier_corrections: The cited location schedule-step.tsx:159-161 does not exist; the file has only 91 lines. The relevant line is schedule-step.tsx:32, where new entries are hard-coded to `dosage: 1`, and the file has no dosage input anywhere. The dosage-step onChange is at about lines 88-101. "0 silently becomes 1 pill" is slightly overstated: the preview also shows 1 pill (parseFloat('0') || 1), so what gets saved matches what the user sees. The problem is that no error is shown, not that the saved value differs from the preview. Reaching the bug requires a mistyped or deliberately entered negative value, so medium severity fits. The split-dose point applies only to the add wizard; phases or schedules edited elsewhere may still allow different doses per time.

"A 5mg morning / 2.5mg evening regimen can't be entered at all" goes too far. The creation wizard can't express it, but edit-medication-drawer.tsx (lines 88-185) has a per-row dosage input with > 0 validation, so the user can split doses after creating the medication. A negative dose also needs a user to type the minus sign on purpose or by accident. It cannot come from the preset dosage buttons. Medium severity stands.

title: Deactivated prescriptions and archived brands become unreachable in the UI
description: The only way to open PrescriptionViewDrawer (which holds the Active toggle and Delete) is CompoundCardExpanded inside PrescriptionCard, and PrescriptionsView renders only `isActive` prescriptions. getInactivePrescriptions exists but nothing calls it. Once toggled off, a prescription can't be reactivated, edited or deleted. In the same way, every inventory list filters `!isArchived`, so an archived brand can't be reopened to Unarchive or 'Delete Permanently' (that button only appears when the item is already archived). Meanwhile a deactivated prescription's brand stays in the Medications tab under 'Active'.
evidence: prescriptions-view.tsx:18 `.filter((p) => p.isActive)`; compound-list.tsx:27 `inventoryItems.filter((i) => !i.isArchived)`; the drawer copy says 'Turn off to hide from daily tracking'; the archive copy says 'Archiving hides this medicine from the active list but keeps its history.'
failure_scenario: The user turns off 'Active Prescription' for a paused drug. It vanishes from the Prescriptions tab and can never be turned back on, so they must create a duplicate prescription and lose the linked history. Archiving a brand then closing the drawer makes it impossible to unarchive or delete.
suggested_fix: Add an 'Inactive / Archived' section to the Prescriptions and Medications tabs (use getInactivePrescriptions), and route inventory items of inactive prescriptions out of the 'Active' group.
verifier_corrections: Two small corrections. First, archiving doesn't lock you out straight away: the drawer stays open, so you can still press Unarchive until you close it. Second, a deactivated prescription's history isn't deleted. It just can't be reached through the management UI, though the analytics titration tab still shows it read-only. Neither changes the finding.

One small correction to the failure scenario. The add-medication wizard's "existing prescription" dropdown (search-step.tsx:65) uses the unfiltered usePrescriptions() list, so an inactive prescription can still be selected there and a brand added to it. This path does not reactivate the prescription, so it stays hidden from the Prescriptions tab. The claim that it "can never be turned back on" therefore still holds. However, the user does not strictly have to create a duplicate. Also, the old dose logs are not deleted; they stay in the database but are orphaned from any visible prescription card.

title: Deleted inventory items stay visible, can be switched to, and can be picked for dose deduction
description: getInventoryForPrescription, getAllInventoryItems, getAllActiveInventoryItems and getActiveInventoryForPrescription ignore deletedAt, and deleteInventoryItem / deletePrescription don't clear isActive. Deleted brands, including every brand of a deleted prescription, keep showing in the Medications tab (as 'Active' with no 'For:' line, because the prescription map excludes deleted ones) and in BrandSwitchPicker. getActiveInventoryForPrescription (used by takeDose/logPrnDose) also ignores isArchived, unlike dose-schedule-service, so the brand shown on a slot and the brand debited can differ.
evidence: inventory-service.ts:31 `return db.inventoryItems.toArray();`; :27 `return items.find(i => i.isActive === true);`. Scratch test after deletePrescription: `ALL INVENTORY AFTER DELETE [[true,true,30]]` (deleted, still isActive, stock 30).
failure_scenario: After deleting a prescription, its 'Lopressor 50mg · 30 pills' card is still listed under Active medications, and the user can log refills against the deleted item. After the next launch the recalc (its transactions were hard-deleted) moves it to 'Out of stock'.
suggested_fix: Filter `deletedAt === null` in all inventory readers, set isActive=false on delete, and have getActiveInventoryForPrescription use the same `isActive && !isArchived && deletedAt === null` predicate as the schedule builder.
verifier_corrections: The isArchived part is mostly unreachable through the UI. The archive toggle (inventory-item-view-drawer.tsx:386) clears isActive when it archives an active item, and un-archiving doesn't set it again. So an item that is both isActive and isArchived can't normally exist, and the risk that the brand shown on a slot differs from the brand debited is latent at most. The deletedAt part of that same mismatch is real: dose-schedule-service.ts:163 filters only isArchived, not deletedAt, so both the slot display and the deduction would use the deleted item. They agree with each other, but both are wrong. The rest of the finding is accurate.

This is a minor under-statement, not an error. The dose-schedule-service builder (dose-schedule-service.ts:159-165) also ignores `deletedAt`, not just `getActiveInventoryForPrescription`. So when the active brand of a still-live prescription is deleted through the inventory item drawer, both the brand shown on the slot and the brand that gets debited are the deleted item. The worst impact is on that path, not only on the deleted-prescription path described in failure_scenario.

title: Brand switching is two separate non-atomic writes and does not enforce a single active brand
description: Switch Brand runs two independent updateInventoryItem mutations (deactivate old, then activate new), each its own transaction and sync op. If the second fails, or the two sync on different devices, the prescription ends up with 0 or 2 active brands. With 2 active, the schedule builder keeps the last item in its Map for display and pill math, while takeDose debits the first match from `find`.
evidence: brand-switch-picker.tsx:46-57 two sequential `await updateInventory.mutateAsync(...)`. dose-schedule-service.ts:164 `inventoryByPrescription.set(inv.prescriptionId, inv);` (last wins) vs inventory-service.ts:27 `items.find(i => i.isActive === true)` (first wins).
failure_scenario: The phone switches from Brand A (50mg) to Brand B (25mg) while the tablet, before syncing, reactivates A. Both end up active. The slot says '2 tablets of 25mg' (B) but the pills are deducted from A's stock at 50mg strength (1 pill).
suggested_fix: Add a service-level `setActiveBrand(prescriptionId, itemId)` that deactivates all siblings and activates the target in one Dexie transaction. Resolve the 'active brand' in one shared helper.
verifier_corrections:
No material errors. Two small points:
- The two writes can also end up split by a closed tab or a sync race, not only by the second write failing. A local Dexie write failing on its own is unlikely.
- The finding understates how far the readers diverge. `getActiveInventoryForPrescription` also ignores `isArchived`. The schedule builder filters archived items out. So an item that is both archived and active is treated differently even when only one item is active.

The finding is accurate, with three small additions.
- Dose-log details (`dose-log-service.ts:219-225`) also use the last-wins Map, so the mismatch shows up in history as well.
- `getActiveInventoryForPrescription` does not filter out archived brands, while the Map builders do. That is a second difference between the two lookups.
- Leaving zero brands active on a single device is unlikely because local Dexie updates rarely fail. The realistic trigger is the two-device sync race.

title: Adding a brand to an existing prescription has no unit or strength compatibility check
description: Unit is duplicated on MedicationPhase, InventoryItem and (optional, never written) PhaseSchedule. When adding a brand to an existing prescription, the unit is parsed from the new brand's strength text and never compared with the phase unit. Pill math is dosage/strength with no unit conversion. The edit drawer can also change phase.unit freely without touching any inventory unit.
evidence: wizard.tsx:302-303 `strength, unit,` passed straight to addMedicationToPrescription. dose-schedule-service.ts:200 `pillsPerDose = calculatePillsConsumed(dosageMg, inventory.strength);` (units ignored). buildSchedules never sets PhaseSchedule.unit.
failure_scenario: The levothyroxine phase is scheduled at 100 (mcg). The user adds a new box labelled '0.1 mg'. Once that brand is active, each dose is computed as 1000 tablets, stock goes massively negative, and the slot shows '1000 tablets of 100mcg'.
suggested_fix: Store the unit in one place (the prescription or phase), normalise strengths to it on entry (mg/mcg/g conversion), and reject or convert mismatched brands in addMedicationToPrescription and updatePhase.
verifier_corrections: One small overstatement: I did not check that the slot shows the exact text "1000 tablets of 100mcg". The slot carries unit: phase.unit (dose-schedule-service.ts ~219) and pillsPerDose = 1000, so the wrong pill count does reach the display, but the exact wording is unconfirmed. The new brand only drives the math once it is active. It becomes active automatically only when the prescription has no active brand; otherwise the user must pick Switch Brand. Everything else is accurate.

Mostly accurate. Four small corrections:
1. The wrong result is not limited to the schedule slot. Every dose-log path that deducts stock uses the same `calculatePillsConsumed` call (`dose-log-service.ts` lines 290/389/480/549/620), so taking the dose actually deducts 1000 pills.
2. The exact wording "1000 tablets of 100mcg" was not checked.
3. The dose detail dialog also mislabels the brand strength with the phase unit (`dose-detail-dialog.tsx:190`), so the new box shows as "0.1mcg".
4. The new brand only affects dosing once it is active: immediately if the prescription has no active brand, otherwise after a manual brand switch.

title: Dead or unreachable medication APIs and fields make the model harder to follow
description: getDailySchedule (a second, diverging schedule builder), activatePhase/useActivatePhase, deletePhase/useDeletePhase, useDoseLogsWithDetailsForDate and getInactivePrescriptions have no UI callers. PhaseSchedule.unit is never written. InventoryTransaction type 'initial' is only produced by the v10 migration: new prescriptions write the initial stock as type 'refill' with note 'Initial stock'. activatePhase also lacks updatedAt (see the sync finding), so bringing it back as-is would reintroduce the sync loss.
evidence: prescription-service.ts:99 `const tx = buildTransaction(inventory.id, input.currentStock, "refill", now, "Initial stock");`; grep shows no component uses useActivatePhase / useDeletePhase / useDoseLogsWithDetailsForDate / getDailySchedule.
failure_scenario: Future work reuses getDailySchedule, which filters schedule deletedAt but not prescription or phase deletedAt, or activatePhase, and gets results that differ from the Today view. Stock history labels the first stock as a 'Refill' that can be edited and deleted, unlike 'Initial'.
suggested_fix: Delete the unused builders and hooks. Write initial stock as type 'initial'. Remove or populate PhaseSchedule.unit.
