title: Completing a titration shows the old maintenance dose and the new dose together
description: completeTitrationPlan soft-deletes the old maintenance schedules (deletedAt only, enabled stays true) and copies the titration schedules onto the same maintenance phase. getDailyDoseSchedule does not filter deletedAt, so it returns both the old and new maintenance schedules. titSchedules (402-405) also includes soft-deleted schedules from earlier plan edits, so those get copied into maintenance as well.
evidence:
titration-service.ts:425 `await db.phaseSchedules.update(os.id, { deletedAt: now, updatedAt: now });`. Probe after completeTitrationPlan: ["08:00 50 maintenance","09:00 100 maintenance"]. After an edit followed by complete: ["08:00 50 maintenance","09:00 100 maintenance","09:00 100 maintenance"].
---
[prescriptions-model#0] dose-schedule-service.ts:140 `const enabledSchedules = allSchedules.filter(s => s.enabled === true);` (no deletedAt check). titration-service.ts:425 `await db.phaseSchedules.update(os.id, { deletedAt: now, updatedAt: now });`. Scratch test: before completion `[[100,"08:00","titration"]]`; after completeTitrationPlan `[[100,"08:00","maintenance",false],[50,"08:00","maintenance",true]]` (the last field is 'soft-deleted').
failure_scenario: The user finishes titrating from 50mg to 100mg and taps Complete. From then on the schedule lists 50mg at 08:00 and 100mg at 09:00 every day (plus a duplicate 100mg if the plan was ever edited). Following the app means taking 150mg or 250mg a day, and stock is decremented for each.
suggested_fix: Filter deletedAt in every schedule reader and set enabled=false on superseded schedules. Filter titSchedules and titrationPhases by deletedAt===null. Add a regression test for complete → getDailyDoseSchedule.
verifier_corrections: The failure scenario uses 08:00 and 09:00 as example times. In practice the old and new doses keep their original times, which may be the same (the second probe shows both at 08:00). I did not trace the edit path that soft-deletes titration schedules, so the extra "duplicate after an edit" claim is plausible from the unfiltered query at lines 402-405 but not independently verified. It does not affect the main finding.

The finding blames the duplicate on titSchedules at lines 402-405. The real cause is one step earlier. At lines 395-397, titrationPhases is built from allPhases without a deletedAt filter. updateTitrationPlan (lines 238-248) soft-deletes the old titration phase and its schedules, but that phase still has titrationPlanId and type "titration". So completeTitrationPlan loops over the deleted phase as well as its replacement, and copies the deleted phase's soft-deleted schedules into maintenance as new rows with deletedAt:null and enabled:true. The fix needs a deletedAt filter on both titrationPhases and titSchedules; the suggested fix already says this. The file list also names medication-notification-service.ts:78-79, which I did not check.

Minor points only:
- The two slots appear at whatever times the old and new schedules have; they don't need different times.
- If the titration schedule has the same time as the old maintenance schedule, the two show as two separate slots at the same time, not one merged slot.
- The totals in the failure scenario (150mg or 250mg) assume the user takes every slot shown. The core claim is correct.

title: Editing an active titration plan: taken doses revert to pending/missed, re-taking double-decrements stock
description: updateTitrationPlan soft-deletes the old phases and schedules without changing status, then creates new phases and schedules with new ids. It remaps dose logs to the new phaseId but leaves scheduleId pointing at the deleted schedule. getDailyDoseSchedule keys logs by prescriptionId|phaseId|scheduleId, so the log no longer matches any slot. Both the old and new phases are 'active' titration phases, so which one is shown depends on iteration order.
evidence: titration-service.ts:305 `await db.doseLogs.update(dl.id, { phaseId: newPhaseId, updatedAt: now });` (scheduleId not remapped). Probe: take the 100mg titration dose (stock 30→28), edit the plan without changing dosage → slot status 'missed' (it would be 'pending' today). Taking it again → stock 26.
failure_scenario: The user took this morning's dose and then fixes a typo in the plan title or notes, which also resubmits the entries. The dose shows as not taken, the user taps Take again, and the app logs a second dose and removes another 2 pills from stock. Past days of the titration show as missed.
suggested_fix: Update schedules in place (keep ids) when editing, or remap both phaseId and scheduleId by matching time/day. Mark replaced phases cancelled. Only replace entries when they actually changed.
verifier_corrections: One small detail: "which one is shown depends on iteration order" is right, but the outcome is the same either way. The old phase's soft-deleted schedules also stay visible, because getDailyDoseSchedule filters neither phases nor schedules on deletedAt, so neither choice matches the remapped log. There may also be a second problem: if the old phase is chosen, the user is shown the soft-deleted schedule rather than the edited one. The main claim and the failure scenario are accurate as stated.

Minor: in the repro, today's slot went back to "pending", not "missed". The finding's probe says "missed", but its own note that it would be "pending" today is the accurate part. "Missed" applies to past dates. Also, the claim that which phase is shown "depends on iteration order" did not matter here: the new phase and schedule were picked in the repro, and it breaks either way because the log's phaseId and scheduleId can never both match. Everything else holds.

Two small corrections, neither changes the verdict:
- It's not quite "old and new phases both active, so the shown one depends on order." The real cause is that getDailyDoseSchedule ignores deletedAt for phases and for schedules. So deleted old schedules can still be picked and shown if the old phase happens to win. The log fails to match either way.
- The edit form always sends entries, so this happens on any edit, not only when dosage or schedule change. For example, it happens when saving an edit that changes only the notes.

title: Activating an edited draft plan re-activates soft-deleted phases, so the schedule shows the pre-edit dose
description: After editing a draft plan, the old phases are soft-deleted but keep status='pending'. activateTitrationPlan picks up every phase with that titrationPlanId and status 'pending' without checking deletedAt, so it activates the deleted phases along with the new ones. The schedule then shows whichever active titration phase iterates last.
evidence: titration-service.ts:351 `const titrationPhases = planPhases.filter((p) => p.titrationPlanId === planId && p.status === "pending");`. Probe: create draft at 09:00 100mg → edit to 10:00 150mg → activate → phases ["titration active del=false","titration active del=true"], slots ["09:00 100 titration del=true"].
failure_scenario: The user drafts a titration, corrects it to 150mg at 10:00 before starting, then activates it. The schedule shows 100mg at 09:00, which is the discarded dose.
suggested_fix: Filter deletedAt===null in activate, complete, cancel and getPhasesForTitrationPlan. Cancel phases when replacing them in updateTitrationPlan.
verifier_corrections: The finding is accurate, but it should say the failure depends on UUID ordering. The deleted phase wins only when its UUID sorts after the new phase's, so it happens about 50% of the time, not every time. The finding also leaves out a second missing guard: dose-schedule-service.ts filters neither phases (lines 115-121) nor schedules (lines 138-142) on deletedAt. The fix therefore also needs deletedAt filtering in getDailyDoseSchedule, not only in the titration-service functions.

This is not deterministic. Which dose the schedule shows depends on the random UUID order of the phases, so the old dose appeared in about half the runs (7 of 12). The finding says the schedule shows the pre-edit dose, which is only true some of the time. The schedule builder also has the bug on its own: getDailyDoseSchedule does not filter deletedAt on phases or schedules. So the fix needs to go there too, not only in the titration-service functions.

The finding says "whichever iterates last". More precisely, the order comes from the Dexie index on status and then the primary key (a random UUID), so the stale dose shows up about half the time, not every time.

The root cause is also wider than activation. getDoseScheduleForDate (dose-schedule-service.ts:115-142) filters neither phases nor phaseSchedules on deletedAt. So editing a plan that is already active hits the same bug with no activation step: the old phases were already `active` and stay that way after being soft-deleted. The fix therefore also needs deletedAt filters in the schedule builder, and the replaced phases should have their status changed (for example to cancelled), not only deletedAt set.

title: Dose logs keyed by display time string: detail-dialog past-date Take, untake after schedule edit, and reschedule all miss the existing log
description: The service layer looks logs up by (scheduleId, date, scheduledTime=time), where time is the slot's localTime, and localTime changes when the schedule time, the device timezone or the DST offset changes. The schedule view matches logs by prescriptionId|phaseId|scheduleId only, ignoring time. Separately, DoseDetailDialog's past-date Take passes the user's chosen 'taken at' time as the lookup key `time` and never passes takenAtTime. schedule-view.tsx:157 does it correctly.
evidence:
dose-detail-dialog.tsx:66-73 `await takeMut.mutateAsync({ ..., date: slot.scheduledDate, time, dosageMg: slot.dosageMg });` (time = picked time). Probe P5: take with time '09:30' (stock 30→29), untake with slot.localTime '08:00' → stock still 29, slot still 'taken', logs ["08:00 pending","09:30 taken"]. Probe P8: take, change the schedule to 08:30 via updatePhase, untake → stock 29, still 'taken'.
---
[prescriptions-model#5] dose-detail-dialog.tsx:66-73 passes `time,` (the picked time) with no takenAtTime. Scratch test: `retro log "14:30" "2026-09-25T15:31…"` (actionTimestamp is today, not yesterday); after untake: slot `pending`, stock stays `29`, doseLogs `[["14:30","taken"],["08:00","pending"]]`.
---
[dates-timezones#1] Scratch test (TZ=Europe/Berlin, fake-indexeddb): take dose for 2026-10-20 in summer -> log ['08:00','taken'], stock 30->29. Clock moved to 2026-10-27: the view shows the Oct 20 slot as localTime '07:00', status 'taken'. untakeDose(time:'07:00') -> stock stays 29 (not restored); logs = [['08:00','taken'],['07:00','pending']]; the view now reports 'pending'.
---
[live-data-forensics#6] dose-log-service.ts:124 `l.scheduledTime === time &&`; dose-schedule-service.ts:149 ``const key = `${log.prescriptionId}|${log.phaseId}|${log.scheduleId}`;``. LIVE: on 2026-04-23 all 6 morning doses have scheduledTime '09:30' (actionTimestamp 08:41 Berlin), while every other day's key for the same schedules is '08:30'.
failure_scenario: The user taps a skipped or future dose from yesterday, taps Take and enters 09:30. The app records actionTimestamp=now instead of 09:30, creates a second log and decrements stock. Untaking afterwards does nothing: the dose stays 'taken' and the pill is never returned. The same thing happens to any dose taken before the user edits that schedule's time, or before a DST or timezone change.
suggested_fix: Key dose logs by (scheduleId, scheduledDate) and never by a display string, and add a unique natural-key index. Fix the dialog to pass time: slot.localTime and takenAtTime: time. Block Take on future dates.
verifier_corrections: I lowered the severity from critical to high. The damage is wrong inventory counts, duplicate or orphan dose logs, a wrong actionTimestamp and an untake that does nothing. It does not produce wrong dosing instructions or destroy existing records. The failure scenario's wording "skipped or future dose from yesterday" is muddled. The picker only opens when !isToday, which covers past dates and also future dates, because nothing blocks Take on future dates. Also, when a date has more than one log, the view's logMap uses last-write-wins, so which status it shows depends on IndexedDB iteration order. That order is not guaranteed to always be 'taken'.

- Reschedule in the detail dialog only exists for today (dose-detail-dialog.tsx:232). So reschedule misses the existing log only after a schedule time, DST or timezone change, not in the past-date Take flow.
- The view's last-write-wins `logMap` (dose-schedule-service.ts:149) means that after a duplicate log is created, the status shown for that slot depends on index order. It is not deterministically 'taken'.
- Severity lowered to high: the corruption is bounded to one dose-log and one inventory unit per occurrence, and it does not produce wrong dosing instructions.

The severity is overstated. This is high, not critical: nothing is lost, the prescribed dosage shown stays correct, and the harm is duplicate logs, stock off by one dose each time, a broken untake and a wrong taken-at timestamp.

The failure scenario's "untaking afterwards does nothing: the dose stays 'taken'" is not deterministic. The view's logMap ignores time and keeps whichever log comes last in Dexie iteration order (keyed by random UUID), so after the bad take the slot may already show pending, skipped or taken.

The schedule-edit, DST and timezone paths are real but uncommon: they only bite when the user reverses or reschedules a dose taken before the change. The dialog past-date Take is the frequent trigger.

The suggestion to "block Take on future dates" isn't backed by any evidence here. The dialog's non-today branch treats every non-today date as 'past'.

title: Reschedule has no effect: the new time never appears and the original slot shows a random log
description: rescheduleDose writes a 'rescheduled' log at the old time and a 'pending' log at the new time under the same scheduleId. getDailyDoseSchedule only creates slots from PhaseSchedules, so no slot ever exists at the new time. The two logs collide in logMap (last one wins, in random UUID order), so the original slot shows either 'skipped' or 'pending'.
evidence:
dose-log-service.ts:656 `const doseLog = await upsertDoseLog(prescriptionId, phaseId, scheduleId, date, newTime, "pending");`. dose-schedule-service.ts:154 `const key = `${log.prescriptionId}|${log.phaseId}|${log.scheduleId}`;`. Probe: reschedule 08:00→11:00 → slots ["08:00 pending log=11:00"]; no 11:00 slot.
---
[prescriptions-model#6] dose-schedule-service.ts:154 `const key = `${log.prescriptionId}|${log.phaseId}|${log.scheduleId}`;` (overwrites). Scratch test: after reschedule 08:00->12:00 slots `[["08:00","pending"]]`; after takeDose, still `[["08:00","pending"]]` with logs `[["08:00","taken"],["12:00","pending"]]`.
failure_scenario: The user reschedules the 08:00 dose to 11:00. Nothing appears at 11:00 and the 08:00 row either stays pending or shows as skipped. Taking it from the 08:00 row misses both logs because of the time-keyed lookup, so a third log is created. Reminders ignore the reschedule entirely.
suggested_fix: Render slots for logs with rescheduledTo, or store the override on a single log record (effectiveTime) and build the slot from it. Key the logMap on schedule and date and choose deterministically.
verifier_corrections: The claim that taking the dose from the 08:00 row "misses both logs because of the time-keyed lookup, so a third log is created" is wrong. takeDose passes time: slot.localTime (08:00). getDoseLogRaw matches on scheduledTime, so it finds the existing 08:00 "rescheduled" log and upsertDoseLog changes it to "taken". No third log is created. The finding's own scratch evidence shows this: two logs, [08:00 taken] and [12:00 pending]. What actually goes wrong is that the orphaned 12:00 "pending" log can still win the logMap collision, so the slot keeps showing "pending" after the dose was taken. I did not verify the claim that reminders ignore the reschedule, so it should not be treated as confirmed.

1. "Taking it from the 08:00 row misses both logs because of the time-keyed lookup, so a third log is created" is wrong. takeDose passes time=slot.localTime ("08:00"), so getDoseLogRaw finds the existing 'rescheduled' 08:00 log and changes it to 'taken'. The probe ended with exactly 2 logs: [08:00 taken, 11:00 pending]. The real problem after taking is that the slot can still show 'pending' when the 11:00 log wins the logMap. The 11:00 pending log is also left behind as an orphan.
2. "Reminders ignore the reschedule entirely" was not verified in this pass, so treat it as unconfirmed.
3. The UI shows 'skipped' only when the rescheduled log wins. deriveStatus maps 'rescheduled' to 'skipped'.

The failure scenario says that taking from the 08:00 row "misses both logs ... so a third log is created". That is wrong. takeDose/upsertDoseLog looks up the log by (schedule, date, time=08:00) with getDoseLogRaw (dose-log-service.ts:110-129). That lookup finds the existing "rescheduled" log at 08:00 and updates it to "taken". No third log is created, and the finding's own scratch evidence shows only two logs: [["08:00","taken"],["12:00","pending"]]. The actual problem is that the row can still display "pending" after the take, because the 12:00 pending log can win the time-less logMap key. title: Schedule times drift by an hour at every DST change (Berlin user; next shift 2026-10-25)
description: Schedules store scheduleTimeUTC computed with the offset in effect when saved (getTimezoneOffsetMinutes uses `new Date()`), and display converts back using today's offset. Timezone recalculation only runs when the IANA name changes, so a DST change within Europe/Berlin is never corrected. Every schedule saved in winter shows one hour later in summer, and every schedule saved in summer (all edits since March) will show one hour earlier after 2026-10-25. The stored `time` field keeps the original string, so the in-app reminder, which reads schedule.time, disagrees with the displayed slot.
evidence:
timezone.ts:48 `const now = new Date();` inside getTimezoneOffsetMinutes. timezone-recalculation-service.ts:33 `s.enabled === true && s.anchorTimezone !== newTimezone`. Probe with fake Date: save 08:00 Europe/Berlin on 2026-01-15, format on 2026-07-15 → "09:00".
---
[dexie-schema#4] timezone.ts: `function getTimezoneOffsetMinutes(timezone: string): number { const now = new Date(); ...`. dose-schedule-service.ts:188 `const localTime = formatLocalTime(schedule.scheduleTimeUTC, tz);`. Scratch test: with the clock set to 2026-01-15, localHHMMStringToUTCMinutes('08:00','Europe/Berlin') gave 420; with the clock set to 2026-07-15, formatLocalTime(420,'Europe/Berlin') gave '09:00'.
---
[dates-timezones#0] timezone.ts:48 `const now = new Date();` inside getTimezoneOffsetMinutes; localTimeToUTCMinutes: `const result = localMinutes - offsetMinutes;`. Scratch test (TZ=Europe/Berlin): created '08:00' on 2026-09-25 -> stored 360; formatLocalTime(360,'Europe/Berlin') on 2026-11-02 -> "07:00". Detection only compares names: `anchorTimezones.some((tz) => tz !== deviceTz)`.
---
[live-data-forensics#3] timezone.ts `function getTimezoneOffsetMinutes(timezone) { const now = new Date(); ...}`. Scratch test (since deleted): formatLocalTime(390,'Europe/Berlin') returns '08:30' with the system time at 2026-09-25 and '07:30' at 2026-11-02. LIVE: all 13 enabled schedules use scheduleTimeUTC 390/1110 with anchorTimezone Europe/Berlin.
failure_scenario: The user set 'Metoprolol 08:00' in summer. On 26 Oct the schedule, the push reminders and the late/overdue logic all say 07:00, while the in-app reminder still fires at 08:00. Doses meant to be 12h apart become 11h/13h apart, and today's logs taken before the shift no longer match by time string (see the time-key finding).
suggested_fix: Store the wall-clock time (HH:MM) plus the IANA zone as the source of truth and derive UTC per date using that date's offset. Drop fixed scheduleTimeUTC, or recompute it per calendar date.
verifier_corrections: Severity is overstated. The stored data is not corrupted, and the original time string is still in schedule.time, which makes recovery easy. What goes wrong is the displayed and notified dose time, which is an hour off (high, not critical). "Push reminders" here means the Capacitor local notifications in local-notifications.ts:72, which use raw UTC minutes. I found no server-side push code that uses scheduleTimeUTC. Otherwise the finding is accurate.

The finding is correct overall. It overstates a few details:
- It says "push reminders" will show 07:00. The only reminders confirmed to use `scheduleTimeUTC` are Capacitor local notifications (local-notifications.ts:72), and I did not check whether they treat hour/minute as UTC or as local time. The web in-app reminder uses `schedule.time`.
- "Doses 12h apart become 11h/13h" is misleading. Every slot shifts by the same hour, so the gap between them stays 12h. The mismatch is between the shifted UTC-based slots and the unshifted `time`-based reminder and log keys.
- Critical is too high. Dose amounts stay correct and only the displayed or reminded times move by one hour, so high fits better.

Severity should be high, not critical: no data is corrupted and dose amounts are unaffected. The '11h/13h apart' claim is wrong because all schedules shift by the same hour. Dose-log matching in dose-schedule-service uses schedule IDs, not time strings. The claim that 'push reminders' show 07:00 is imprecise: the native Capacitor reminders (local-notifications.ts:72-74) feed UTC hours in as local time, so they are wrong by the whole UTC offset all year, which is a separate and bigger bug.

title: Server push reminders never fire in the background, and payloads come from today's slots only
description: No cron is configured for /api/push/send (there is no vercel.json cron and no workflow calls it). The only trigger is a 60-second client ping to /api/push/check from usePushScheduleSync, which is mounted only on /medications, so a 'push' is only sent while that page is open. The server needs an exact minute match (time_slot = localTime), so a throttled ping skips the reminder. The synced schedule is built from getDailyDoseSchedule(today) but spread across the union of each slot's daysOfWeek. Medications not due today are dropped from every day, and today's medications are written onto other days. When today has no slots the sync returns early, so old server schedules remain.
evidence:
use-push-schedule-sync.ts:100 `const slots = useDailyDoseSchedule(todayStr);` :123 `if (!slots || slots.length === 0) return;` :78 `const days = daysSet.size > 0 ? Array.from(daysSet) : [0..6]` then an entry per day with the same medicationsJson. push-db.ts:538 `AND d.time_slot = ${userLocalTime}`. grep: no caller of /api/push/send outside tests.
---
[mcp-server-auth#5] `find . -name vercel.json` returns nothing. grep for push/send outside the route and its tests finds nothing. use-push-schedule-sync.ts:146: `const id = setInterval(ping, 60_000);` inside a React effect.
---
[state-settings-cache#1] use-medication-notifications.ts: export function useMedicationNotifications() { usePushScheduleSync(); ... }
grep: app/medications/page.tsx:25:  useMedicationNotifications();  (only caller)
use-push-schedule-sync.ts:145 ping(); const id = setInterval(ping, 60_000);
failure_scenario: Med A is at 08:00 daily and Med B at 08:00 on Mondays. The app is opened on Tuesday, so the sync writes 'A' for all 7 days. Next Monday's reminder omits B. If the app was last opened on a Monday, every day's reminder says 'A, B'. With the app closed, no push arrives at all. Deleting all medications leaves reminders firing forever.
suggested_fix: Add a real scheduler (a Vercel cron calling /api/push/send every minute, or a window match of ≥ slot and < slot+N with dedup). Build the push schedule per weekday from the regimen, not from today's slots. Sync an empty schedule when there are no slots.
verifier_corrections:
- The cited `push-db.ts:538` does not exist; the file has 270 lines. The exact-match clauses are at `push-db.ts:56` (`time_slot = ${currentTime}`) and `:246` (`time_slot = ${userLocalTime}`).
- "Reminders never fire in the background" is too absolute. It is true for web/PWA push as far as the repo shows. An external cron (such as cron-job.org, holding `CRON_SECRET`, which is declared in `turbo.json`) could call `/api/push/send`, and the repo cannot rule that out.
- The native Android app does not rely on this path. `apps/web/src/lib/local-notifications.ts` schedules per-schedule, per-weekday Capacitor LocalNotifications from the full `phaseSchedules` regimen (called from `providers.tsx:63` and `use-medication-queries.ts:186`), so Android users still get background reminders with correct per-day content.
- The impact is therefore limited to web/PWA push users. The wrong-content and stale-schedule bugs still apply to anyone who relies on web push.

- "Push never fires in the background" applies only to web/PWA push. The Capacitor Android app schedules OS-level reminders separately through apps/web/src/lib/local-notifications.ts (LocalNotifications, all enabled schedules per weekday), so native users still get background reminders.
- An external cron hitting /api/push/send with CRON_SECRET (the var is declared in turbo.json globalEnv) cannot be ruled out from the repo. The accurate claim is that no scheduler is configured in-repo.
- "Deleting all medications leaves reminders firing forever" overstates it. The stale server schedule does survive, but it only fires while /medications is open (or if an external cron exists).
- Severity lowered from high to medium because a working native reminder path exists.

Mostly accurate, with three corrections:
- "Reminders firing forever" after deleting all medications is overstated. The stale server rows do stay, but they can only fire while /medications is open, because nothing else triggers a send.
- The finding leaves out the native Android path. lib/local-notifications.ts schedules reminders on the device (via Capacitor LocalNotifications) independently of this push flow, so Android native users are partly covered. The breakage applies fully to web/PWA push.
- The missed-minute risk is from the ping landing in the wrong minute (timer throttling or network delay). The 60-second interval itself should cover every minute while the page is in the foreground.

title: Reminders keep firing after the dose is taken
description: Neither the server follow-up query nor the in-app reminder checks dose logs. The server has no dose-log knowledge (push_schedules only), so follow-ups 1..N go out on schedule even when the dose was taken on time. The in-app and push paths also use different tags (`dose-reminder-${time}` vs `dose-${time}`), so both show up together.
evidence:
getFollowUpNotifications joins push_sent_log/push_schedules only. in-app: `if (diff >= 0 && diff <= 5) { ... dueNow.push(...)` with no doseLogs lookup.
---
[mcp-server-auth#6] push-db.ts getFollowUpNotifications: `FROM push_sent_log l JOIN push_subscriptions s ... JOIN push_schedules d ... WHERE l.sent_date = ${today} AND l.follow_up_index = ${followUpIndex - 1} AND l.sent_at <= NOW() - ...` with no dose_logs predicate. sw.ts push handler calls showNotification unconditionally.
failure_scenario: The user takes the 08:00 dose at 08:00 and still gets 'Reminder: your 08:00 medications' at 08:10 and 08:20. With the app open they also get a second, differently-tagged notification. Users learn to ignore reminders.
suggested_fix: Suppress reminders for slots whose status is taken or skipped. For server push, sync taken status (or a per-slot ack endpoint) and check it before follow-ups. Use one reminder channel and one tag.
verifier_corrections:
1) The citation apps/web/src/lib/push-db.ts:368-397 does not exist, because the file is only 270 lines. The relevant code is push-db.ts:76-106 (getFollowUpNotifications) and 137-147 (syncDoseSchedules).
2) "The server has no dose-log knowledge" is inaccurate. Postgres has a dose_logs table (packages/db/src/schema.ts:486) that the sync engine fills. The follow-up query just doesn't consult it, so the fix could be a predicate on dose_logs rather than a new ack endpoint.
3) The in-app reminder does not keep firing. It fires once per slot inside the 0-5 minute window, deduped via notifiedDoses. The repeat reminders come only from server follow-ups.
4) There is no server cron. /api/push/check is only pinged every 60 seconds by usePushScheduleSync, which is mounted only on /medications (via useMedicationNotifications). Both reminder paths therefore run only while that page is open, which limits how often this happens.

1. "The server has no dose-log knowledge" is wrong. The sync engine mirrors every Dexie table, including doseLogs, to Neon Postgres, so the server does have that data. The push queries just never use it, and push_schedules carries no status.
2. The in-app reminder runs only while the /medications page is mounted (useMedicationNotifications is called only in app/medications/page.tsx). The duplicate-tag notification therefore needs the user to be on that page within 0-5 minutes of the slot, not just to have the app open.
3. The in-app channel shows at most one reminder per slot, in the 0-5 minute window, and has no follow-ups. The repeated reminders come only from the server push path.

title: History and adherence are recomputed from the current regimen, ignoring phase start and end dates
description: getDailyDoseSchedule(dateStr) uses the phases and schedules active now for any date. phase.startDate and endDate are never checked (only prescription.createdAt). Logs from an earlier phase or schedule don't match the current keys. adherenceRate walks past dates through this function.
evidence:
No reference to phase.startDate/endDate in dose-schedule-service.ts; filter is `where("status").equals("active")`. analytics-service.ts:285 `const scheduleMap = await getDoseScheduleForDateRange(startDate, endDate);`.
---
[dates-timezones#7] `const allActivePhases = await db.medicationPhases.where("status").equals("active")...` ; `const key = `${log.prescriptionId}|${log.phaseId}|${log.scheduleId}`` ; titration-tab: `adherenceRate(phaseRange, rx.id)` with `start: phase.startDate, end: phase.endDate`.
---
[analytics-history-export#6] const allActivePhases = await db.medicationPhases.where("status").equals("active").toArray();
...
const logKey = `${prescription.id}|${phase.id}|${schedule.id}`;

Titration tab: adherenceRate({start: phase.startDate, end: phase.endDate}, rx.id)

Probe P2: completed titration phase with 9 'taken' logs -> adherence for that phase's range = 0 / 11.
failure_scenario: The user took every maintenance dose for 3 months, then starts a titration today. Every past day now shows the titration dose as 'missed' and adherence drops to about 0%. Days before a schedule was added show the new schedule as missed.
suggested_fix: Resolve the regimen per date using phase start and end dates and schedule createdAt/deletedAt (effective-dated). Match past logs by their own phase and schedule.
verifier_corrections: No material corrections. One nuance: the damage is to history and adherence analytics, meaning wrongly shown data. Stored dose logs are not changed. High severity (wrong data shown) fits better than critical.

No material errors. One clarification: the past-day corruption applies once a titration phase with a titrationPlanId is active, or once a phase or schedule is completed, disabled or replaced. The maintenance phase itself is not deactivated when a titration starts; the titration phase just overrides it for every date. Also, when a titration phase is completed, the titration tab's per-phase adherence for that range comes back as 0 taken, because that phase is no longer 'active' and its logs can't match. That supports the evidence's probe P2.

Minor corrections only.
- The "about 0%" figure depends on the scenario. It is exact for a completed titration phase viewed in the Titration tab (its own logs never match once the phase is no longer active). For a maintenance-then-titration history, adherence is scored against the titration schedules, so taken maintenance logs don't count. The rate falls sharply, but the exact figure depends on overlapping schedule IDs.
- One more reachable surface to list: ScheduleView on past dates (`components/medications/schedule-view.tsx:35`). Logging a dose there saves it with the current phase and schedule IDs.
- The key detail behind the failure: `activateTitrationPlan` leaves the maintenance phase active, and the titration override is applied without regard to date.

title: Titration plans hardcode unit 'mg'; completing a plan overwrites the maintenance unit
description: Every titration entry is saved with unit 'mg' regardless of the prescription's unit (the wizard allows mcg, ml and others through parseStrength). completeTitrationPlan copies titPhase.unit onto the maintenance phase, so a mcg medication becomes mg.
evidence: titration-drawer.tsx:146 `unit: "mg",`. titration-service.ts:454 `unit: titPhase.unit,`.
failure_scenario: The user titrates levothyroxine 50→75 mcg. The schedule shows '75mg' during the titration, and after Complete the maintenance phase permanently says mg. That label is off by a factor of 1000.
suggested_fix: Take the unit from the prescription or its current phase and don't overwrite it on completion.
verifier_corrections: One small overstatement: "off by a factor of 1000" describes only how the label reads. The stored dose values and the pill arithmetic are not scaled. For ml and other non-mass units the mislabel is a unit mismatch rather than a factor of 1000. Combination drugs are already forced to mg by the wizard, so they are not affected.

Minor additions, nothing wrong in the finding. The update path (titration-service.ts:260) also stores the hardcoded "mg", so editing an existing plan rewrites its phase unit to mg as well. The dosage numbers are copied unchanged, so the problem is only the unit label: pill-count math is unaffected.

This is a labelling bug, not a factor-of-1000 data corruption. The stored dose numbers and pill math stay correct; only the unit string changes. The user can fix it through the edit-medication drawer's "Dosage unit" field. The wrong label also shows up in push and local notifications, the dose detail dialog and the MCP/analytics output, not just the schedule card.

title: Titration recommended start date never auto-activates; titrations have no steps
description: A draft plan with a start date creates 'pending' phases, but no code ever promotes pending phases when startDate arrives, and activatePhase has no UI caller. The date is only shown as a label. A 'titration' is a single fixed schedule with a manual Complete. There is no step or duration model, so 'titration step math' does not exist.
evidence:
grep recommendedStartDate: only titration-service write paths plus the card label. No scheduler checks phase.startDate or status 'pending'.
---
[dates-timezones#18] phase-service: `const isFuture = input.startDate && input.startDate > now; const status = isFuture ? "pending" : "active"`; titration-service activate: `update(phase.id, { status: "active", startDate: now, ...})`
failure_scenario: The user plans 'increase to 100mg starting Oct 1'. On Oct 1 the schedule still shows the old 50mg dose until they remember to tap Activate.
suggested_fix: Auto-activate pending phases whose startDate is on or before today (effective-dated regimen), or remove the date field from the UI.
verifier_corrections:
Four points to sharpen:
1. The UI caller that is missing is for phase-level `useActivatePhase`. Plan-level `activateTitrationPlan` does have an "Activate" button, so the plan can be started manually.
2. Manual activation replaces `startDate` with the activation time, so the planned date is lost from the record.
3. The "no step/duration model" point is a design limitation, not a bug. It is secondary to the auto-activation gap.
4. The `phase-service.ts:166` pending path is not reachable from the UI today, because the edit drawer always passes `Date.now()`.

Minor clarifications:
- The dead `activatePhase` path matters more for single-medication future phases (phase-service.ts:166). In the UI, however, edit-medication-drawer.tsx:182 always passes `startDate: Date.now()`, so no UI path currently creates a pending non-titration phase.
- For titrations there is an Activate button on the plan card, so activation is manual rather than completely missing.
- When the user does activate manually, the phase startDate is overwritten with the activation time (titration-service.ts ~357), which silently discards the planned date.

title: PRN doses are write-only: no screen shows, edits or undoes them
description: logPrnDose creates kind='prn' logs and decrements stock. getDoseLogsWithDetailsForDate explicitly excludes them, getDailyDoseSchedule has no slot for them, and no component reads PRN logs. The user can't see when they last took an as-needed dose, can't undo a mistaken log, and the stock decrement can't be reversed except through a manual inventory edit. The picker also accepts future times.
evidence: Comment at dose-log-service.ts:230 `// phaseId/scheduleId are absent for PRN doses — those fall through ... and are excluded here.` grep '"prn"' in components returns nothing.
failure_scenario: The user taps 'Log dose now' for furosemide twice by accident. Stock drops by 2, and there is nowhere in the app to see either log or remove one.
suggested_fix: Add a PRN log list (today and recent) to the prescription card with undo/delete that reverses the linked inventory transaction.
verifier_corrections: Two small corrections. First, the claim that "no component reads PRN logs" is true for the main UI, but debug-panel.tsx shows raw tables. Second, the PRN stock change can be seen and reversed: the 'consumed' transaction appears in the inventory item drawer (inventory-item-view-drawer.tsx:227-319) and can be deleted there. Deleting it leaves the PRN dose log behind. The external MCP tool `list_recent_doses` can also read PRN logs from the server copy. Neither point changes the verdict.

The finding says the stock decrement is completely invisible. That's slightly overstated. The linked `consumed` inventoryTransaction does show up in the inventory item view drawer's History tab as "Consumed -1" with a date (inventory-item-view-drawer.tsx:218-224, 292-296). So the stock change is visible there, but the PRN dose log itself is not. That row can't be edited or deleted either: `isEditable` is only true for refill or adjusted rows (line 245), so the only fix is a manual refill or adjustment entry, which is what the finding says. The dose log itself is never shown to the user anywhere; only the debug panel lists the dose_taken audit entry.

title: Prescription-creation cutoff uses the UTC date, and the in-app reminder uses the stored time string
description: The createdDate cutoff is `toISOString()` (UTC), while dateStr is a local date key. West of UTC, a medication created in the evening hides that day's doses. The in-app reminder compares schedule.time, which is static and never realigned after DST, whereas the UI uses localTime derived from scheduleTimeUTC.
evidence:
`new Date(prescription.createdAt).toISOString().split("T")[0]`. Reminder: `const timeParts = schedule.time.split(":")`.
---
[prescriptions-model#17] dose-schedule-service.ts:180 `? new Date(prescription.createdAt).toISOString().split("T")[0]`.
---
[dates-timezones#14] `const createdDate = prescription.createdAt ? new Date(prescription.createdAt).toISOString().split("T")[0] : undefined; if (createdDate && dateStr < createdDate) continue;`. Scratch test: created Sep 24 20:00 local in New York -> key '2026-09-25'.
failure_scenario: In New York, a medication added at 20:00 local (00:00 UTC next day) shows no dose that evening. After DST the in-app reminder fires an hour away from the time shown on the schedule.
suggested_fix: Use toLocalDateKey(createdAt), or better the phase startDate, and derive reminder times from the same helper as the UI.
verifier_corrections:
Two small corrections:
- **Which time is wrong after DST.** The finding treats the reminder as the one that is off. It is more the other way round: `schedule.time` keeps the wall-clock time the user entered, and the UI's `localTime` (from a `scheduleTimeUTC` that never gets re-aligned) is the one that drifts by an hour. The underlying bug is storing a fixed UTC minute value with no DST re-alignment. The mismatch is real either way.
- **Reminder scope.** The in-app reminder only runs while the /medications page is mounted.

Two related issues the finding does not mention:
- The reminder's de-duplication key uses a UTC date (`now.toISOString()` at line 69).
- apps/web/src/lib/local-notifications.ts:72 schedules native notifications from `scheduleTimeUTC`, so native reminders follow the drifting UTC value rather than the wall-clock time.

For the DST half, the time string the reminder reads (`schedule.time`) is the correct wall-clock time. What drifts is the UI's localTime. scheduleTimeUTC is stored with a fixed offset and converted back using today's offset, so after DST the schedule displays an hour off while the reminder fires at the time the user set. The fix is to make the displayed time (and local-notifications.ts, which also uses scheduleTimeUTC) derive from `time`/anchorTimezone, not to move the reminder onto scheduleTimeUTC. The createdDate half is accurate as described. Using toLocalDateKey(createdAt) fixes it.

title: AI titration-warnings request gets wrong unit, frequency and daily total
description: The drawer always labels doses 'mg', sets frequency to `${schedules.length}x daily` even when a schedule is not daily, and sums dosages across schedules as the 'daily' total regardless of daysOfWeek. It never sends currentDosage, so the model can't see how big the change is.
evidence:
`const totalNew = e.schedules.reduce((sum, s) => sum + (parseFloat(s.dosage) || 0), 0);` `frequency: `${e.schedules.length}x daily``.
---
[ai-routes-models#12] `const totalNew = e.schedules.reduce((sum, s) => sum + (parseFloat(s.dosage) || 0), 0);` ... `newTotalDaily: totalNew > 0 ? `${totalNew}mg/day` : undefined, frequency: `${e.schedules.length}x daily`,` with no `currentDosage` field set.
failure_scenario: A regimen of 25mcg on Mon/Wed/Fri is sent as '25mg/day, 1x daily', so the AI warnings are based on a dose 1000× too high and the wrong frequency.
suggested_fix: Send unit, days and currentDosage from the maintenance phase, and compute the weekly-averaged daily total.
verifier_corrections: The 1000x unit claim is wrong. Titration inputs are labelled mg and saved as `unit: "mg"` (titration-drawer.tsx handleSubmit; rx-entry-card.tsx:114-122), so the "mg" sent to the AI matches what the user entered and what is stored. A mcg regimen can't be entered as mcg in the titration drawer, which is a separate problem in the titration model. Still valid: the daily total ignores daysOfWeek, the frequency is always `${n}x daily`, and currentDosage is never sent. The per-schedule strings in the same prompt do list the correct days, so the prompt is internally inconsistent rather than entirely wrong. The impact is limited to advisory warning text the user can edit, so severity is low, not medium.

The frequency claim is somewhat overstated. Each newSchedule line does include the real days (for example "(Monday, Wednesday, Friday)"), so the model gets the correct days there. It is the summary line "New total: X/day, Nx daily" that contradicts them. The "1000x too high" scenario only applies to mcg prescriptions, which can be created through the wizard's strength parsing. The underlying problem is wider than the finding says: handleSubmit also hard-codes `unit: "mg"` when it saves titration phases (titration-drawer.tsx:146). So the AI request is not the only place where a mcg prescription gets mg-labelled titration data, and that save issue should be tracked with this finding or next to it. The finding's files list repeats the same ranges twice; the correct lines are titration-drawer.tsx:84-95 and route.ts:59-74.

title: Deleted prescriptions and deleted schedules still appear in the daily dose schedule, reminders and AI insights
description: Soft delete is a timestamp only. deletePrescription sets deletedAt on the prescription, its phases and its schedules, but leaves isActive=true, status='active' and enabled=true. deleteSchedule sets only deletedAt. Every medication read path treats isActive, status and enabled as the source of truth and never checks deletedAt: getDailyDoseSchedule, getActivePrescriptions, getActivePhaseForPrescription, checkDoseReminders, checkRefillAlerts, getDailySchedule for prescriptions and phases, and use-timezone-detection.

Scratch test: after adding prescriptions A and B, deletePrescription(A) + deleteSchedule(B's schedule), getDailyDoseSchedule(today) returned ["A","B"], the same as before the deletes. After delete, the prescription row had isActive=true, deletedAt set, and getActivePhaseForPrescription still returned the deleted phase with status 'active'.

Scratch probe: after deletePrescription(rx.id), getDailyDoseSchedule returned 1 slot.

Output: `RESULT before=1 after=1 invAfterDeleted=true listLen=1`.
