- The quick-log buttons also always record an amount, so the gap covers every way of creating a urination record, not just the details form.
- The hard-coded list in `EditUrinationDialog` currently has the same values as the shared constant. It is duplication that could drift later, not a present mismatch.

title: Every edit truncates the timestamp to the minute, even when time is untouched
description: The edit form loads the timestamp via timestampToDateTimeLocal (.slice(0,16), which drops seconds and ms) and always writes the parsed value back. Editing only the note therefore also moves the timestamp back by up to 59.999 s.
evidence: `return local.toISOString().slice(0, 16);` and buildUpdates always receives the re-parsed `timestamp`.
failure_scenario: Two readings logged at 08:15:10 and 08:15:40; editing the note on the second moves it to 08:15:00, so the two readings swap order in Recent and in BP 'latest reading'.
suggested_fix: Only include timestamp in updates when the datetime-local string differs from the original, or keep the original seconds when the minute is unchanged.
verifier_corrections: The line citations use-edit-record.ts:316 and :334 are wrong because the file is only 133 lines long. The relevant lines are 77 (the edit form is filled from the truncated value) and 93-102 (the value is always re-parsed and sent to buildUpdates). The same always-send-timestamp pattern also exists in records-tab.tsx lines 263-388, not only at line 211. The substance of the finding is correct.

title: Daily notes: hooks have no UI consumer, and the add path bypasses the sync queue and deletedAt filtering
description: useDailyNotes and useAddDailyNote are not imported by any component. The table is still synced and backed up. If the hook is ever wired up, useAddDailyNote does a raw db.dailyNotes.add (no writeWithSync, no schedulePush), so notes would never reach the server, and useDailyNotes returns soft-deleted rows because it does not filter on deletedAt === null.
evidence:
`await db.dailyNotes.add(entry);` (no writeWithSync); `return query.toArray();` (no deletedAt filter); grep for use-daily-notes-queries finds only its own test.
---
[dexie-schema#14] use-daily-notes-queries.ts `await db.dailyNotes.add(entry); return entry;` (no enqueue). grep: no component imports useAddDailyNote or useDailyNotes.
failure_scenario: The owner expects daily notes (listed as a table and in the prior audit's coverage matrix), but there is no way to create or view them. A future UI built on this hook would create notes that are never synced and show deleted ones.
suggested_fix: Either remove the hook/table from scope, or rewrite it on record-crud helpers (writeWithSync + schedulePush + active-only reads) and add a UI.
verifier_corrections: No factual errors. The only thing to add is that both defects are latent: no user can reach them today, because no UI uses the hook.

title: Undo action ignores the undo result; a failed restore is silent
description: onUndo calls undoFn(id) without awaiting it or checking the ServiceResult. If the restore returns err(...), for example a Dexie failure or a blocked transaction, the user gets no feedback and the record stays deleted.
failure_scenario: The user taps Undo, the restore fails, nothing is shown, and the user believes the record was restored.
suggested_fix: `onUndo: async () => { const r = await undoFn(id); if (!r.success) toast({ title: 'Could not restore', variant: 'destructive' }); }`
verifier_corrections: The two cited line ranges (22-23 and 22-24) are the same location listed twice. The finding misses that use-composable-entry.ts (useDeleteEntryGroup lines 106-108 and useDeleteSingleGroupRecord lines 152-154) also ignores the undo result. Those handlers await the call but never check the returned ServiceResult. One more detail: the services never reject (they return err), so the failure isn't even logged as an unhandled rejection.

title: Weight card defaults to a hard-coded 69 kg for new users, and the value can be saved with one tap
description: With no weight history, pendingWeight is set to 69 kg, which looks like the owner's personal value, and the Record button is enabled immediately.
evidence: `setPendingWeight(69);                        // D-04, D-12: first-time fallback`
failure_scenario: A new user (or someone after a data wipe) taps 'Record Weight' while exploring, and a 69.00 kg record is created. It becomes the latest weight, and the analytics/MCP get_today_summary report it.
suggested_fix: Start with no value (null / placeholder) and require input for the first entry, or use a profile-derived weight.
verifier_corrections: This is minor. The finding is accurate as written: line 59 exists and the button is enabled. However, the claim that analytics and the MCP get_today_summary report the record was not traced here. It is plausible, since any weight record would show up there, but it was not verified. In practice the scenario is limited to a fresh install or a post-wipe state in a single-user app.

title: Three reminder paths use three different definitions of dose time
description: The in-page web notifier compares against the deprecated `schedule.time` string and builds its de-duplication key from a UTC date. Native uses the UTC hour as if it were local (see the finding above). Web push uses `slot.localTime` converted from UTC with the current offset. The web notifier also ignores `deletedAt` and phase preference (titration vs maintenance), so it can fire for phases the schedule view hides.
evidence: medication-notification-service.ts: `const todayParts = now.toISOString().split("T"); const todayKey = todayParts[0]` ... `const timeParts = schedule.time.split(":")`
failure_scenario: After 2026-10-25, for one 08:00 dose: the web notifier fires at 08:00, push fires at 07:00, native fires at 06:00 (07:00 in winter), and the schedule view shows 07:00. Between 00:00 and 02:00 CEST the de-dup `todayKey` is still yesterday's UTC date. The key is cleaned at the next UTC-date change, so a reminder can fire again for the same local day.
suggested_fix: Derive every reminder from one function, `getDailyDoseSchedule(localDateKey)`. Remove the `time`-based path and the UTC `todayKey`.
verifier_corrections:
1. **`deletedAt` does not separate the notifier from the schedule view.** `deleteSchedule` sets `deletedAt` without setting `enabled=false`. The notifier ignores `deletedAt`, but `getDailyDoseSchedule` (`dose-schedule-service.ts`, filter `s.enabled === true`) ignores it too. So the schedule view does not hide deleted schedules either. The "fires for schedules the view hides" claim holds only for the titration-vs-maintenance phase preference.
2. **The double-fire window is only 5 minutes.** A dose fires only when 0 <= diff <= 5 minutes after its time. A key is cleaned at the UTC date change, so a repeat can only happen for a dose scheduled in the 5 minutes before UTC midnight (local 01:55-02:00 in CEST). Doses anywhere else in 00:00-02:00 cannot fire twice.
3. **The in-page notifier only runs while `/medications` is open.** It is not a background reminder path.
4. **The native offset is already its own finding.**

Severity is lowered from high to medium.

1. Drop the claim that the UTC `todayKey` lets a reminder fire twice on the same local day. The 0-5 minute local-time window with no wraparound means each schedule can match only once per local day.
2. The `deletedAt` claim is misframed. `getDailyDoseSchedule` (the schedule view) also ignores `deletedAt` on phaseSchedules, so the view does not hide deleted schedules. Only native filters them.
3. Native fires at 06:00 after 2026-10-25, not "07:00 in winter". In CEST it fires at 06:00 for an 08:00 dose, two hours early.
4. The phase-preference divergence is real and is the strongest part. `activateTitrationPlan` leaves maintenance active, so the web notifier and native both remind for the maintenance dose alongside the titration dose. Push follows `getDailyDoseSchedule` and reminds only for titration.
5. Impact is limited: the in-page notifier runs only while `/medications` is mounted (`apps/web/src/app/medications/page.tsx:25`). The native offset bug duplicates another finding.
6. Severity lowered to medium.

This is not high severity. The in-page web notifier runs only while /medications is open in the foreground (a 60 s interval started in useMedicationNotifications). On Capacitor Android the Notification API is effectively unavailable, so it is not a primary reminder path. The native wrong-hour problem and the push/schedule-view 07:00-after-DST problem belong to separate findings (the UTC-as-local bug and the offset-snapshot DST bug). They should not be counted again as this finding's impact. The claim that the UTC `todayKey` lets a reminder fire again for the same local day is overstated. It only happens for doses scheduled in roughly the 5 minutes before local 02:00 CEST (the UTC date change), not for any dose between 00:00 and 02:00. The `deletedAt` gap is confirmed: deleteSchedule sets only `deletedAt`, not `enabled=false`. The claim that it "can fire for phases the schedule view hides" holds when a prescription has both an active maintenance phase and an active titration phase.

title: The day-start hour setting only affects dashboard totals; every other 'today' or 'day' uses a different boundary
description: `dayStartHour` (default 2) is read only by `getDailyTotal` and text-metrics. The analytics daily buckets (`dayKey` = local midnight), the time-scope ranges (`startOfDay`), the Records-tab day groups, correlations, the Summary tab's active-days count, the medication 'today' (`toLocalDateKey()`) and dose 'missed' status all use local midnight. MCP uses UTC (see the MCP finding).
failure_scenario: The user drinks 500 ml at 01:30. The dashboard counts it in yesterday's total against yesterday's limit. Analytics 'daily' fluid balance, the Records tab, the correlations and the AI insight snapshot all count it in today. At 00:30 the Medications tab already treats yesterday's 22:00 dose as a past date ('missed' when not logged) while the dashboard still shows yesterday.
suggested_fix: Add one `logicalDayKey(ts, dayStartHour, tz)` / `logicalDayRange(date)` helper in @intake/core and use it for every day bucket, range and 'today' calculation, including medications (or document that medications deliberately use midnight).
verifier_corrections:
- MCP does not use UTC as such. mcp/queries.ts:54-56 calls `setHours` in the server's local timezone, which is UTC only on a UTC host such as Vercel.
- MCP does read `dayStartHour`, from the push_settings table. The real bug is that push/settings/route.ts:27 hardcodes that stored value to 2, so it never reflects the user's setting.
- Correlations in packages/core use an IANA-timezone calendar day rather than the device's local midnight. It is still midnight-based, but it is a different helper from the other views.
- The settings UI describes the setting as being "for budget tracking". Treating medications and analytics on midnight is therefore partly documented, which lowers the severity from high to medium.

Severity should be medium, not high: nothing is corrupted or lost, and the mismatch only affects records between local midnight and dayStartHour (00:00-02:00 by default). The medication 'missed' behaviour may be intentional calendar-date logic rather than a bug. The finding's grep claim leaves out that environment-info.tsx also reads dayStartHour, though only to display it. I did not separately check the claims about summary-tab and the AI insight snapshot; the grep shows neither reads dayStartHour, which fits the finding.

Severity is overstated. The mismatch only affects records logged between midnight and dayStartHour (default 00:00-02:00), and it is an aggregation difference, not data corruption, so it is medium, not high. The medication 'today'/missed argument is weak: dose schedules keyed on calendar dates are arguably correct, and a 22:00 dose shown as past at 00:30 is expected behaviour. The strongest part of the finding, which the finding under-weights, is that push/settings/route.ts:27 always saves dayStartHour: 2. As a result, MCP/server 'today' never follows the user's configured value.

title: MCP get_today_summary uses the server's UTC clock and a day-start hour hardcoded to 2
description: `todayStartTimestamp` calls `d.setHours(dayStartHour)` in the serverless runtime's local zone, which is UTC on Vercel. The day-start hour comes from `push_settings.day_start_hour`. The only writer is POST /api/push/settings, which always writes `dayStartHour: 2`, and the client never sends its setting. The user's IANA zone is already stored in `push_subscriptions.timezone` but is not used. Doses are counted by `actionTimestamp` rather than `scheduledDate`.
evidence:
`function todayStartTimestamp(dayStartHour, now = Date.now()) { const d = new Date(now); d.setHours(dayStartHour, 0, 0, 0); ...}`; settings route: `dayStartHour: 2,`. Scratch test with TZ=UTC: day start = 02:00Z = 04:00 CEST.
---
[analytics-history-export#12] await saveSettings(auth.userId!, { ..., dayStartHour: 2 });
...
function todayStartTimestamp(dayStartHour, now = Date.now()) { const d = new Date(now); d.setHours(dayStartHour, 0, 0, 0); ...
---
[mcp-server-auth#1] queries.ts:55-58: `const d = new Date(now); d.setHours(dayStartHour, 0, 0, 0); const ts = d.getTime(); return ts > now ? ts - 24 * 60 * 60_000 : ts;`. Reproduced: now=2026-09-25T00:30Z (02:30 SAST). TZ=UTC gives start 2026-09-24T02:00Z; TZ=Africa/Johannesburg gives 2026-09-25T00:00Z.
---
[mcp-server-auth#2] push/settings/route.ts: `await saveSettings(auth.userId!, { enabled: true, followUpCount: ..., followUpIntervalMinutes: ..., dayStartHour: 2, });`. SettingsSchema only has followUpCount/followUpIntervalMinutes.
---
[live-data-forensics#8] queries.ts:55 `const d = new Date(now); d.setHours(dayStartHour, 0, 0, 0);`. LIVE: get_today_summary returned day_started_at=1790301600000 (2026-09-25T02:00:00Z, i.e. 04:00 Europe/Berlin). The owner logs regularly in the 01:00-04:00 local range (e.g. urination at 01:44 and 04:36 on 09-13).
failure_scenario: The user asks Claude for today's water at 03:30 Berlin time. The window runs from yesterday 04:00 CEST, so it includes most of yesterday and reports almost double. After 04:00 local, anything logged between 02:00 and 04:00 is missing. A user who set a 5am day start in the app is still given a 2am boundary.
suggested_fix: Resolve the user's timezone (push_subscriptions.timezone, or pass tz with the tool call) and compute the day start with a zone-aware helper. Sync `dayStartHour` from the client settings store. Count doses by `scheduledDate = localToday`.
verifier_corrections:
The finding overstates the failure scenario. At 03:30 CEST the window runs from yesterday 04:00 CEST to now. That total is roughly yesterday's day plus whatever was logged between 02:00 and 03:30 local. It is not "almost double" today's total. It is the wrong day's data, because the app's "today" began at 02:00 local.

I lowered severity to medium. The bug only affects the read-only MCP summary shown to the assistant. Data is not corrupted, and the app's own dashboard computes the day start correctly on the client. It is also correct for UTC users who keep the default hour of 2.

The dose-counting point is secondary. Counting by `actionTimestamp` rather than `scheduledDate` is a design choice, and it only fails together with the wrong window.

"Almost double" overstates it. At 03:30 CEST the window is about 23.5 hours, mostly yesterday's data plus 0-3.5 hours of today. It is not two full days. The impact is limited to the MCP get_today_summary tool; the in-app dashboard is not affected, so medium fits better than high. Everything else holds: the hardcoded `dayStartHour: 2` in push/settings/route.ts:27, the UTC setHours, the unused stored timezone, and counting doses by actionTimestamp.

The failure scenario at 03:30 Berlin is technically correct: the window runs from yesterday 04:00 local, so it includes almost all of yesterday. But it only happens for queries made between midnight and 04:00 local. At other times the error is limited to entries logged between 02:00 and 04:00 local going missing. The client does POST to /api/push/settings. It just can't send dayStartHour, because the schema doesn't accept it. This does not affect the in-app dashboard or any stored data. Severity should be medium, not high.

title: 'Delete data older than N days' filters on createdAt and also deletes active prescriptions, schedules and inventory
description: The deletable tables are `TABLE_PUSH_ORDER` minus userProfile, which includes prescriptions, titrationPlans, medicationPhases, phaseSchedules and inventoryItems. The range is compared against `createdAt` (when the row was written), not the record's event `timestamp`. The dialog promises 'all records logged more than 90 days ago'.
failure_scenario: The user taps 'Older than 90 days' to trim old water logs. Their four-month-old active prescription, its phases, schedules and inventory are tombstoned and synced to the cloud, so the medication schedule is gone. Meanwhile a weight reading from last year that was entered yesterday (backdated) is kept.
suggested_fix: Limit time-framed deletion to time-series tables (intake, substance, weight, bp, eating, urination, defecation, and doseLogs by scheduledDate) and filter on `timestamp`. Never delete configuration tables by age.
verifier_corrections: Nothing material to correct. One small addition: the 'All data' preset deleting configuration can be argued as intended, but the age-based presets cannot. The deletion also reaches auditLogs and insightReports, which the finding does not mention.

Two small details are missing from the finding, and neither changes the verdict. First, the deletion also removes dailyNotes, auditLogs, insightReports, doseLogs and inventoryTransactions, so the reach is wider than the finding says. Second, it is a soft delete with a sync tombstone, not a hard delete: rows stay in local IndexedDB with deletedAt set, but the app has no restore option.

The finding is correct but understates the scope. The age filter also deletes inventoryTransactions (probably changing the computed pill stock), dailyNotes, auditLogs and insightReports, not just prescriptions, titration plans, phases, schedules and inventory items. A prescription deleted this way keeps isActive=true, but that has no effect because list queries already skip rows with deletedAt set. The deletion is a soft delete (tombstone) rather than a hard purge. But it syncs to the cloud and the app has no way to restore it, so it is effectively data loss.

title: Today's caffeine and alcohol totals leave out a new entry for up to 60 seconds, and water includes future-dated entries while caffeine excludes them
description: `now` is memoised on a 60-second tick and used as the inclusive upper bound for today's substance query. A record logged a moment later has `timestamp > now` and is excluded until the next tick. `getDailyTotal` for water/salt has no upper bound, so records dated later today or in the future count toward today. Range ends also differ between tables: `between()` excludes the end for intake/health/record-crud but includes it for substances.
evidence:
`const now = useMemo(() => Date.now(), [tick]); const caffeineRecords = useSubstanceRecordsByDateRange(dayStart, now, "caffeine");` vs `getDailyTotal: .where("timestamp").aboveOrEqual(cutoffTime)` (no upper bound).
---
[substance-sugar#9] `const now = useMemo(() => Date.now(), [tick]);` `const caffeineRecords = useSubstanceRecordsByDateRange(dayStart, now, "caffeine");` substance-service: `.between([type, startTime], [type, endTime], true, true)`
failure_scenario: The user logs an espresso. The water ring updates immediately, but the caffeine figure stays unchanged for up to a minute, which looks like the entry failed. A drink backdated as 23:30 tomorrow (typo) inflates today's water total but not today's caffeine.
suggested_fix: Use the end of the logical day (dayStart + 1 day, exclusive) as the upper bound for both queries, and one shared inclusive/exclusive convention.
verifier_corrections: The line citations are slightly loose. The substance `between` call is at `substance-service.ts:108-110`, and `getDailyTotal` starts at `intake-service.ts:104` with the `aboveOrEqual` query at lines 106-109. The finding also leaves out that ticks come from `useNowTick`. Neither point changes the conclusion.

Nothing material is wrong. One nuance: the lag is not only "up to 60 seconds" for new entries. A caffeine or alcohol record whose timestamp is set or edited to later today (edit-substance-dialog.tsx has a datetime-local input) stays out of today's caffeine or alcohol total until the clock actually reaches that time, while the water total counts it immediately. The "23:30 tomorrow typo" example only works if the input form accepts future timestamps; the no-upper-bound query in getDailyTotal would count such a record either way.

title: Time inputs pre-fill with the time the screen loaded, so an open PWA stamps records with an old time
description: `useState(getCurrentDateTimeLocal())` captures the time once, when the dashboard mounts, and only refreshes it after a successful submit. For urination and defecation, the 'details' submit always uses `detailTime`, even if the user never touched the time field. The one-tap buttons use now. Two equivalent inputs give different timestamps. The same stale default applies whenever the 'Set different time' section is opened on the weight/BP/food/manual cards.
evidence:
urination-card.tsx:43 `const [detailTime, setDetailTime] = useState(getCurrentDateTimeLocal());` and :98 `const timestamp = dateTimeLocalToTimestamp(detailTime);` (unconditional)
---
[health-records-inputs#5] `const [detailTime, setDetailTime] = useState(getCurrentDateTimeLocal());` ... `onClick={() => setShowDetails(!showDetails)}` ... `const timestamp = dateTimeLocalToTimestamp(detailTime);`
---
[health-records-inputs#6] `onClick={() => setShowDetails(!showDetails)}` (does not reset showTimeInput); `const timestamp = showTimeInput ? dateTimeLocalToTimestamp(customTime) : undefined;`
---
[food-salt-voice#12] `const [customTime, setCustomTime] = useState(getCurrentDateTimeLocal());` ... `onToggle={() => setShowTimeInput((v) => !v)}` (no refresh of customTime on expand).
failure_scenario: The dashboard is opened at 08:00 and left in the background. At 18:00 the user expands 'details' on the urination card, adds a note and saves. The record is stamped 08:00, which skews fluid-balance and intraday charts and can land on the previous logical day.
suggested_fix: Reset the time default when the details or custom-time panel opens (or use now unless the user edited the field). Keep the seconds.
verifier_corrections:
`manual-input-dialog.tsx:50` should be dropped from the finding. A `useEffect` on `open` (lines 59-67) resets `customTime` to the current time every time the dialog opens, so that dialog does not have the bug.

For weight, BP and food, the old default only matters when the user chooses to open "Set different time" and edits only part of the value. The default path (panel closed) uses now. Only urination and defecation "Add details" use the stored time unconditionally.

The old time is visible in the datetime input before saving, so the risk is that the user doesn't notice it, not a fully hidden error. Severity is lowered from high to medium.

- manual-input-dialog.tsx does not have this bug. Its useEffect (lines 59-67) calls `setCustomTime(getCurrentDateTimeLocal())` and `setShowTimeInput(false)` every time the dialog opens, so remove it from the finding.
- The stale timestamp is shown in a visible "When" / custom-time input before submit. It is not applied silently, so severity should be medium, not high.
- The claim that a record "can land on the previous logical day" needs the page to stay open overnight or across the day-start hour. It does not happen in the same-day scenario described.
- For weight, BP and food, the stale value only applies when the user expands "Set different time" and leaves it as it is.
The real defect is limited to urination and defecation: the details submit uses a mount-time default instead of now.

Severity is overstated. The stale time is shown in a visible, labelled datetime field ("When" / "Using custom time"), so the record isn't stamped silently. The user can see the value before saving, and the record can be edited afterwards. The main exposure is the urination/defecation "details" path, where the time field sits below the note field and the user isn't expecting to change it. On the weight/BP/food/manual cards the user has opened the time picker on purpose and sees the value, so the impact there is small (stale starting point, not a hidden wrong stamp). Medium, not high.

title: Custom analytics range parses 'YYYY-MM-DD' as UTC, one day off west of UTC; the preset ranges also go stale overnight
description: `fromDateInputValue` uses `new Date(val)` on a date-only string, which is parsed as UTC midnight, then calls setHours locally. The default custom range is `now - 7*24h … now` and is not aligned to days. `useTimeScopeRange` is memoised on `[scope]` only, so `end = endOfDay(now)` never moves past the day the page opened. The '24h' preset actually means 'since local midnight'.
failure_scenario: If analytics is left open overnight, nothing logged today shows until the scope changes. At 00:30 '24h' covers 30 minutes. For any user west of UTC, picking a custom start of 20 Sep covers 19 Sep, and an end of 20 Sep ends at 19 Sep 23:59.
suggested_fix: Parse with `new Date(y, m-1, d)` or `parseISO` + startOfDay. Include a tick or date key in the memo dependencies. Rename '24h' to 'Today' or make it a rolling 24h window.
verifier_corrections: The cited file `apps/web/src/lib/dose-schedule-service.ts:178` (`new Date(prescription.createdAt).toISOString().split("T")[0]`) is a separate issue. It compares a UTC date key of `createdAt` against a local `dateStr`, which is unrelated to the analytics range selector and should be tracked as its own finding. The "one day off" bug only affects users west of UTC (east-of-UTC users are fine). The overnight staleness only happens if the page stays mounted past midnight. The '24h' behaviour is intentional day alignment (documented in the JSDoc), so it is a naming issue, not a calculation bug.

- **'24h' preset:** this part is overstated as a bug. The JSDoc on `useTimeScopeRange` says the calendar-day alignment is intentional ("aligned to calendar-day boundaries ... so daily grouping never produces partial edge days"). The problem is the misleading label, not the logic.
- **Who is affected:** the UTC-parse bug only shows up in timezones west of UTC. In UTC+2 (for example `Africa/Johannesburg`) the result is correct. That limits the real-world impact to users who are west of UTC or travelling there.
- **Unrelated evidence:** the `dose-schedule-service.ts:178` reference (from `core-duplication#15`) is a separate issue and does not support this finding.
- **Severity:** medium still fits, since this is edge-case or timezone-dependent wrong data in analytics. It is not data corruption.

title: The medications screen's 'today' is fixed when the screen mounts and never rolls over at midnight
description: `selectedDate` is `useState(() => new Date())`, WeekDaySelector's `today` is `useMemo(() => new Date(), [])`, and `useDailyDoseSchedule` re-runs only on DB changes. Its 'pending'/'missed' status depends on `todayStr`, which is only computed when the query runs. Nothing updates any of these when the date changes.
evidence: page.tsx: `const [selectedDate, setSelectedDate] = useState(() => new Date());`; week-day-selector: `const today = useMemo(() => new Date(), []);`
failure_scenario: The PWA stays open on Medications overnight. The next morning it still shows yesterday as selected and highlighted as today, so tapping Take goes through the retroactive (non-today) path. Yesterday's unlogged doses stay 'pending' instead of 'missed' until something writes to the DB.
suggested_fix: Derive today from a shared day-key hook that ticks (useNowTick + toLocalDateKey), reset the selection when the day changes, and include todayStr in the live-query dependencies.
verifier_corrections: Some of the finding's framing is off. Several "today" checks are recomputed on every render and do roll over: `isToday` in page.tsx:27 and schedule-view.tsx:56, plus formatDateLabel. So after midnight the dose dialog correctly treats yesterday as not-today and takes the retroactive path, which is the right behaviour for yesterday's slot, not a bug in itself. The actual failures are different: the selection stays on yesterday, and the stale memoised `today` in WeekDaySelector keeps the header saying "Today, <yesterday>" and highlighting yesterday's tile. The user is misled into logging doses against the wrong date. The header and tile disagree with the dialog's isToday, so the UI contradicts itself. The pending-vs-missed staleness is secondary.

Small addition, not an error in the finding: some checks (page.tsx isToday, ScheduleView isToday, formatDateLabel) recompute the date on every render. So after midnight the screen disagrees with itself. The selector's memoized today still shows yesterday highlighted as "Today, <date>", while the dialog gets isToday=false. That makes the finding stronger.

title: A retroactive dose taken after midnight is recorded on the scheduled day, ~22h early
description: The 'taken at' time the user picks is always attached to the slot's `scheduledDate`, so a late dose taken after midnight gets a timestamp before its scheduled time.

title: Dashboard week buckets are fixed 24h blocks and start Monday; the medications week starts Sunday
description: `bucketByDay` uses `Math.floor((ts - weekStart) / ONE_DAY_MS)` and `weekEnd = weekStart + 7*ONE_DAY_MS`, which ignores 23h and 25h DST days. The dashboard week runs Mon–Sun and the medication week selector runs Sun–Sat.

verifier_corrections: No factual corrections. The "01:00-02:00 on Monday" scenario depends on the default dayStartHour=2. With dayStartHour=0, the missing hour would instead be Sunday 23:00-24:00. Either way, the week's last logical hour is dropped. The bug only happens in timezones that use DST.

title: Restoring a backup after any deletion imports nothing — tombstoned IDs make every backup row a 'duplicate'
description: The UI only offers merge mode. For health tables, importHealthTable skips any row whose id already exists locally, including soft-deleted tombstones. For medication/system tables, isContentEqual ignores deletedAt, so a live backup row that matches a local tombstone counts as 'equal' and is also skipped. No conflict is raised either way. Restoring cannot undo a deletion, which is the main reason people restore.
failure_scenario: User accidentally runs 'Clear All Data' (or a bad time-framed delete), then imports yesterday's backup. The result reads 'Last import: 0 new, N skipped'. The data stays deleted, while the UI implied duplicates were skipped.
suggested_fix: When the local row is tombstoned and the backup row is live, treat it as importable (or as a conflict). Stop ignoring deletedAt in isContentEqual. Offer a real 'replace' mode in the UI that runs inside a single Dexie transaction.
verifier_corrections: No substantive errors. One detail: at HEAD, clearAllData only soft-deletes intakeRecords. The "Clear All Data" scenario therefore shows the bug for intake rows. The medication and system table part applies to rows tombstoned through their own delete paths.

Minor points:
1. "Clear All Data" in the settings UI (`useClearAllData` -> `clearAllData`) only soft-deletes intakeRecords, not every table. The finding's example still holds for intake. The same skip also follows ordinary per-record soft deletes in every table.
2. Even if the tombstoned rows were imported, `bulkPut` does not add anything to `_syncQueue`. The next sync pull could therefore bring back the server tombstone (a related but separate issue). The suggested fix needs to enqueue sync operations, not only change the merge rule.

Nothing material is wrong. Two additions:
1. Single-record deletes and `deleteRecordsInRange` also leave tombstones, not only "Clear All Data", so this failure is broader than the failure scenario describes.
2. The suggested fix is incomplete. Rows restored with `bulkPut` are not added to the sync queue, so the server's tombstone may delete them again on the next pull. The fix also needs to enqueue upserts for restored rows.

title: Backup import and conflict resolution never enqueue sync — restored data never reaches the cloud or other devices
description: Sync is driven by explicit _syncQueue entries (writeWithSync/enqueueInsideTx). importBackup, importHealthTable, mergeTableWithConflicts and resolveConflicts all use raw bulkPut/put with no enqueue and no schedulePush. The rows also keep the backup's old updatedAt, so even a later touch would lose last-write-wins against the server. In replace mode, local tables are .clear()ed with no tombstones, so the server copy is never removed.
evidence:
if (toImport.length > 0) { await table.bulkPut(toImport); }   // no enqueue
...
const table = db.table(res.table); await table.put(res.backupRecord);  // resolveConflicts

Probe P4: importBackup(merge) of 1 new intake row -> rows 1, _syncQueue count 0.
---
[sync-engine#15] grep enqueue/schedulePush/_syncQueue in backup-service.ts returns nothing; :624 `await table.put(res.backupRecord);`
failure_scenario: User in cloud-sync mode restores a backup on their phone. The data appears locally, but the server, the web app, MCP tools (which read Neon) and any reinstalled device never see it. For a conflict resolved as 'use backup', the next pull of any newer server version of that row silently reverts it.
suggested_fix: Write imported and resolved rows through enqueueInsideTx in one transaction, bump updatedAt to now so LWW accepts them, and call schedulePush() afterwards. Replace mode should tombstone and enqueue rather than clear().
verifier_corrections: No substantive corrections. The line ranges are accurate: 420, 476-495, 607 and 616-624. The "silently reverts" point about resolved conflicts only applies when the server copy of the row is newer (the server has a higher updatedAt). If the server row is older, the resolved row just stays local and is never pushed. In replace mode there is a second effect beyond "server copy never removed": the _syncMeta pull cursors are not reset, so server rows that were cleared locally are not pulled back either.

Minor points:
1. A row resolved as "use backup" is only reverted if the server copy of that row changes again later, because pull is cursor-based. It does not happen on every pull.
2. Replace mode is somewhat worse than described. Records cleared locally stay on the server and can be pulled back onto the device later, so a replace restore does not really replace anything in the cloud.
3. I did not check the cited lines 67-79 of conflict-review-drawer.tsx. The finding stands on backup-service.ts alone.

One detail is slightly overstated. The claim that the next pull "silently reverts" a conflict resolved as "use backup" only holds if the server row changes again after the restore. Pull is cursor-based (sync-engine.ts:450-544), so an unchanged server row is not fetched again. The accurate statement: the resolved local row diverges from the server without any notice. It is overwritten only if that record is later edited on the server or another device. Also, replace mode does not reset the pull cursors, so server rows that no longer exist on the phone are never pulled back either. The finding leaves this out, and it makes the divergence in replace mode worse.

title: Correlations use each day's MEAN entry value instead of the day's total — intake correlations are meaningless; eating/defecation always 'none'

Salt/sugar/potassium/water/caffeine/alcohol end up correlating 'average size of one log entry'. Eating and defecation points are all value 1, so the daily mean is always 1, variance is 0 and the result is always 'No meaningful relationship'. The registry describes the metric as 'daily sodium intake'.

Minor corrections:
- Intake-domain correlations are not always "no relationship". They correlate the average entry size instead of the daily total, so results are unreliable or inverted rather than always zero.
- Only eating and defecation are guaranteed to return "none", because every value is 1 and the zero-variance guard fires.
- Urination is also affected: it averages estimated ml per event, which the finding did not mention.
No factual errors. Small nuance: "or even an inverted one" can happen but depends on entry-size patterns. The main effect is attenuated or zero correlation for multi-entry days.

title: CSV export drops diastolic/heart rate, presents estimated urination as measured ml, has an always-empty 'note' column, and omits medications

title: Adherence counts today's not-yet-due doses in the denominator
description: deriveStatus returns 'pending' for every unlogged slot today, including ones scheduled for later in the day. adherenceRate counts every slot in `total` and only 'taken' in the numerator. Ranges ending today (all presets, which end at endOfDay(now)) are therefore penalised for doses that are not yet due.
failure_scenario: User with a 08:00 and a 20:00 dose, perfect history, exports the PDF at 09:00. Today counts as 1/2, so the 7-day adherence prints 92.9% instead of 100%.
suggested_fix: Exclude slots whose scheduled time is still in the future (and possibly 'pending' ones still inside the dose window) from the denominator.
verifier_corrections: Preset ranges end at Date.now() (time-range-selector.tsx:56), not endOfDay(now). The effect is the same because today's date is still included. The bug also affects the titration tab badge for the active phase (end = Date.now()), not just the PDF export and History.

The finding is accurate. The same undercount also reaches two places it doesn't name: the titration-tab badge for an active phase (its range ends at Date.now()) and the daily trend's point for today. A minor nuance: a pending dose that is late but still inside its dose window is also counted as not taken. Whether that should count against adherence is a product decision.

title: Daily averages divide by the calendar span (including unlogged days), inconsistently across presets and the AI snapshot
description: The Summary tab divides totals by the range length in days for the 7d/30d/90d presets. For 'All' it divides by the number of days with ANY record type, so a weight-only day counts as a water day. The AI snapshot always divides by 30 using a rolling window. Days with no logging, and the partial current day, drag averages down. That triggers 'below your goal' observations and AI claims.
evidence:
const rangeDays = range.start > 0 ? Math.max(1, Math.round((range.end - range.start) / MS_PER_DAY)) : Math.max(1, totals.activeDays);
...avgWaterMl: sum(water) / days,  // days = 30
failure_scenario: A user who started tracking 10 days ago drinks 2 L/day. The 30d Summary shows 'Average daily water (667 ml) is below your 2000 ml goal', and the AI insight is told avgWaterMl ≈ 667. Switching to 'All' shows about 2000 ml for the same data.
suggested_fix: Divide by the number of days that have at least one record of that domain (or tracked days since first use) and exclude the incomplete current day, consistently in the Summary tab and the snapshot.
verifier_corrections: Two small wording issues; neither changes the finding. First, the 30d preset does include today, but the range runs to the end of today, so the current day isn't cut short in the span; the drag comes from the day's intake not being fully logged yet. Second, the "weight-only day" example depends on weight records being in the `useRecordsTabData` list; they may not be. Either way, `activeDays` counts days with any record type in that list (for example urination or eating), not only days with water logged.

Small refinements that do not change the verdict:
- A 'weight-only day' is not the only kind of day that inflates the 'All' divisor. Any non-water record counts, including BP, urination, meals and substances. So 'All' can also understate water, just less than the fixed-span presets do.
- The partial-current-day effect applies to the Summary presets, which count today as a full calendar day ending at endOfDay. The AI window is a rolling now-30d span, not calendar days.
- The AI path is not literally 'always 30'. It is `Math.round((end-start)/day)` over `insightsRange()`, which comes out as 30.

title: PDF export 'Recent Records' table is sorted as text and truncated, so the wrong records are kept
description: Rows are formatted as 'MMM d, HH:mm' strings, then sorted with localeCompare and cut to 50. The ordering is alphabetical by month name and day text, so 'Sep 9' sorts after 'Sep 10' and 'Oct' before 'Sep'. The cut to 50 therefore drops recent rows.
failure_scenario: A 90d PDF spanning Aug–Oct lists September rows first and October last, and among September puts 'Sep 9' above 'Sep 30'. The newest October readings can fall outside the 50-row cut.
suggested_fix: Sort on the numeric timestamp before formatting. Include the year for ranges that cross a year boundary.
verifier_corrections: Nothing material. One detail: the data fed into the sort is already capped at 10 rows per domain (at most 80 rows) before the text sort and 50-row cut. So the cut drops whole groups whose text sorts low (for example October when September is present), not arbitrary rows. The failure scenario still holds.

The finding is accurate. Two small points. First, rows are only dropped when there are more than 50 in total (at most 80: 10 per domain across 8 domains), so a sparse range still shows every row, just in the wrong order. Second, I noticed a related problem I did not verify: the per-domain `points.slice(-10)` only picks the newest 10 if getRecordsByDomain returns each domain oldest-first. At least one health-service query uses orderBy("timestamp").reverse(), so for some domains it may keep the oldest 10 rather than the newest.

title: PDF export with the 'All' preset iterates every day since 1970 with four full-table scans per day
description: 'All' sets range.start = 0. exportToPDF calls adherenceRate, which calls getDoseScheduleForDateRange('1970-01-01', today). That loops about 20,600 days, and each day's getDailyDoseSchedule does toArray() on prescriptions, phaseSchedules and inventoryItems plus two indexed queries. The CSV filename also becomes 'health-data-1970-01-01-…'.

Each day actually does three full-table scans (prescriptions, phaseSchedules, inventoryItems) plus two indexed queries (medicationPhases by status, doseLogs by scheduledDate), which matches the description text but not the title. The loop covers about 20,700 days, not 20,600. summary-tab.tsx:168 is not part of this bug: it already special-cases start=0 by using the number of active days as the divisor. It is only relevant to the merged dates-timezones#13 snapshot-average point.

This is a performance/UX problem, not a business-logic bug. The adherence numbers stay correct because of the createdAt guard at dose-schedule-service.ts:181-182. The cost is three full-table toArray scans (prescriptions, phaseSchedules, inventoryItems) plus two indexed queries per day. My measurement is about 14 s on an empty DB, which is consistent with the finding's ~8.5 s+ estimate. The line cited at summary-tab.tsx:168 is not part of this failure: it already handles start=0 by dividing by active days. Severity should be low, not medium.

title: Nutrient analysis results live only in component state — paid AI scans and 'Previous scans' vanish on navigation
description: Unlike AI insight reports, which are persisted to Dexie insightReports and synced, nutrient scans are kept in useState. The card renders a 'Previous scans (N)' history that only lasts until the tab/page unmounts.

The finding also missed a second trigger: summary-tab.tsx renders NutrientAnalysisCard in two branches (:260 empty-range, :294 normal), so a time-range change that flips between them resets the scans without leaving the tab. title: Titration tab ignores the selected time range and lists soft-deleted phases
description: TitrationTab receives `range` but discards it (`range: _range`), so the shared time selector and export controls silently do nothing on this tab. getPhasesForPrescription does not filter deletedAt, so deleted phases still get snapshot cards and trigger adherence/BP/weight queries.
evidence:
export function TitrationTab({ range: _range }: { range: TimeRange }) {
const phases = await db.medicationPhases.where("prescriptionId").equals(prescriptionId).sortBy("createdAt");
failure_scenario: User picks '7d' and still sees phase metrics for the whole phase durations. A phase they deleted still appears with 0% adherence.

verifier_corrections: The example "a deleted phase appears with 0% adherence" is not accurate. `adherenceRate(phaseRange, rx.id)` is keyed on the prescription and the date range, not on the phase ID. A deleted phase that covers the same dates as a live one therefore shows the same adherence, BP and weight numbers, not 0%. A more concrete failure is editing a titration plan's entries: the old phases are soft-deleted and new ones are created, so the tab shows duplicate or stale phase cards next to the new ones, with the same metrics repeated. Deleting a titration plan while keeping its prescription leaves ghost cards on the tab.

The finding says the export controls "silently do nothing on this tab". That is overstated: ExportControls receives effectiveRange at page level and exports that range no matter which tab is open. Only the displayed titration metrics ignore the range. It also says a deleted phase "appears with 0% adherence". That is not necessarily true: adherence is recomputed over the phase's own date range, so a deleted phase can show real non-zero metrics, or the no-data state if it has no records. title: Summary KPI totals print unrounded floating-point sums

The display defect is real but rare. It is a cosmetic formatting inconsistency rather than an input inconsistency.

title: Interaction lookup cache keyed only by substance: after adding a medication, results that don't include it are served for 24h
description: Lookup-mode results are cached in localStorage for 24h under a key that is just the normalised substance name. The active-prescription list, which decides what the answer is, is not part of the key. Adding, stopping or changing a prescription does not invalidate the cache.
evidence: `const cached = getCached<InteractionResult>(params.substance); if (cached) { setData(cached); ... return cached; }` and `setCache(params.substance, result);` ; `normalizeKey(key) { return CACHE_KEY_PREFIX + key.trim().toLowerCase(); }`
failure_scenario: The user checks 'ibuprofen' while on bisoprolol only and gets CAUTION/OK. An hour later they start warfarin and check 'ibuprofen' again. The cached result is shown with no warfarin row, so a dangerous AVOID interaction is missing and nothing indicates the result is stale.
suggested_fix: Include a sorted hash of the activePrescriptions generic names in the cache key, or clear the cache whenever prescriptions change. Also show the timestamp of cached results.
verifier_corrections: Minor citation error: `setCache` is at use-interaction-check.ts:114 (lines 112-115), not 117-119. Line 117 is `return result;`. Everything else in the finding is accurate.

The line citation "117-119" for setCache is off by a few lines: the cache write is at lines 113-115. The finding could also say that `clearCache()` exists but nothing outside its test calls it, and that a stale cached "no interactions" result shows a green "No significant interactions found" banner. Only lookup mode (InteractionSearch) is affected. Conflict mode in the add-medication wizard skips the cache.

Minor: the line reference 117-119 should be 113-115, which is where setCache is called. The finding should also say that the stale result can show medications that have been stopped, and that clearCache() exists but nothing outside its test calls it.

title: Model registry is a generation behind, and the routes can't be upgraded by swapping the id (temperature and forced tool_choice would 400)
description: Model ids in use: fast = 'claude-haiku-4-5-20251001' (current Haiku 4.5, used only by bug-report). quality = 'claude-sonnet-4-6' (previous generation; current is claude-sonnet-5), used by parse, voice-parse, substance-lookup, substance-enrich, nutrient-analysis and insights. premium = 'claude-opus-5' (previous; current is claude-opus-5-5), used by medicine-search, interaction-check, titration-warnings and deep insights. Every quality route sends temperature (0, 0.2 or 0.3), which is removed on Sonnet 5 and returns a 400. medicine-search, interaction-check and titration-warnings force tool_choice {type:'tool'}, and the Sonnet follow-up paths do too; forced tool_choice returns a 400 on Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1. No route uses strict:true or output_config structured outputs, so schema conformance depends on zod rejecting after the fact. Tests mock model ids ('claude-sonnet-test'), so no test would catch a 400 caused by parameters. Comments are also stale: the parse route says 'Uses Opus' (it uses Sonnet) and the deep route says 'Opus 4.6'. The SDK is pinned at ^0.124.0; 0.128.0 is the latest.
evidence: models.ts: `quality: "claude-sonnet-4-6" as const,` `premium: "claude-opus-5" as const,` ; parse/route.ts `temperature: 0,` ; medicine-search `tool_choice: { type: "tool", name: "medicine_search_result" }` ; deep/route.ts `with Opus 4.6 and the web-search tool`
failure_scenario: The owner bumps quality to 'claude-sonnet-5' in models.ts. Every food parse, voice parse, caffeine lookup, nutrient scan and insight call returns 400 'temperature is not supported', mapped to 502 'Failed to process request'. Bumping premium to 'claude-opus-5-5' makes medicine search, interaction checks and titration warnings all fail with 400.
suggested_fix: Remove temperature from all routes. Replace forced tool_choice with tool_choice auto plus strict:true tools and a retry, or use output_config.format structured outputs (messages.parse with zod). Then move to claude-sonnet-5 and claude-opus-5-5, setting effort explicitly (Opus 5.5 defaults to medium). Add one contract test that runs each route's params through a per-model parameter validator.
verifier_corrections: (1) Premium is not really "a generation behind". claude-opus-5 is the current default Opus; claude-opus-5-5 is still launching and meant only for users who ask for it by name. The "a generation behind" charge only fairly applies to quality (Sonnet 4.6 vs Sonnet 5). (2) "No test would catch a 400 caused by parameters" overstates it. apps/web/src/__tests__/premium-model-sampling.test.ts parses the source for temperature/top_p/top_k on any request that uses CLAUDE_MODELS.premium (added after issue #331, when Opus routes failed on temperature). What is true: that test deliberately leaves out the Sonnet/Haiku routes, and it does not check forced tool_choice. So bumping quality to sonnet-5, or premium to opus-5-5, would still get past the tests. (3) The stale "Uses Opus" comment is also in substance-enrich/route.ts:15, not only in parse. (4) The claim that SDK 0.128.0 is the latest was not verified, and it is not a defect either way. (5) Severity should be low, not medium: it is a latent hazard with no current user-visible failure.

The premium model is not a "generation behind". Claude Opus 5 (`claude-opus-5`) is still the current recommended default Opus id. Opus 5.5 is still launching and meant to be used only when explicitly chosen, so calling `claude-opus-5` "previous" overstates it. Only the quality tier (Sonnet 4.6 vs Sonnet 5) is really a generation behind. Forcing a tool on the Sonnet follow-up paths is not a problem for Sonnet 5, which still allows it; only `temperature` would break there. The "400 on upgrade" is conditional: it only happens if the ids are bumped and nothing else changes, so nothing fails now. I could not verify from the repo that SDK 0.128.0 is the latest version. Also missed: `WEB_SEARCH_TOOL` uses the older `web_search_20250305` variant, while `web_search_20260209` (dynamic filtering) is available on Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 5. That is minor.

title: Medicine search has no web_search tool, so pill colour/shape and country brand names come from model memory while the prompt claims 'research'
description: The prompt asks the model to 'research the most common commercially available form' and give country-specific brand names and pill appearance, but only the result tool is declared. pillColor and pillShape are then applied directly to the stored prescription and inventory form. Parse, substance-lookup and nutrient-analysis all have web_search; the one route where lookup accuracy matters most for safety does not.
evidence: `tools: [MEDICINE_SEARCH_TOOL], tool_choice: { type: "tool", name: "medicine_search_result" }` ; prompt: "Pay special attention to looking up the physical appearance of the pill (its color and shape) and country specific brand names."
failure_scenario: The user searches for a South-Africa-specific generic brand. The model guesses 'white, round' from the reference product and the wizard pre-fills that colour and shape. The pill card then shows the wrong appearance, which can lead to confusing it with another tablet.
suggested_fix: Add WEB_SEARCH_TOOL (web_search_20260209 on Opus 5+) with a follow-up that forces a result, as in parse. Or have isGenericFallback / 'unverified' flags suppress auto-filling pill appearance.
verifier_corrections: The cited lines are slightly off: the tools line is at route.ts:104-105, not across 98-111, and the pill-appearance pre-fill is at wizard lines 197-204, not 196-203. The failure is probabilistic model error, not a certain bug. Pre-filled values can be edited in the wizard before saving, so medium overstates the impact and low fits better. Substance-enrich also uses web_search and should be added to the list of routes that do.

The finding makes pre-filled appearance sound like it goes straight into the stored prescription and inventory. It does not: the value is a suggestion shown on a dedicated, editable Appearance step before saving, and only whitelisted colour names and shapes are applied. The suggested fix names "web_search_20260209 on Opus 5+", but the repo's shared WEB_SEARCH_TOOL is web_search_20250305 (packages/ai-prompts/src/models.ts:24-28), with premium = "claude-opus-5". The fix should reuse the existing constant. Severity should drop from medium to low.

title: Voice-parse timeout handling is dead code: SDK timeout errors have name 'Error', so timeouts become 502 after up to 3 retries per call
description: The route detects timeouts with e.name === 'APIConnectionTimeoutError'. In @anthropic-ai/sdk 0.124 that class does not set name, so the check never matches. The SDK also retries timeouts twice by default, so the '60s' budget can reach 180s per call, or about 6 minutes with the forced follow-up, before a generic 502 'Failed to parse transcript'.
evidence: `if (e instanceof Error && (e.name === "APIConnectionTimeoutError" || e.name === "AbortError"))`; verified in node: `new A.APIConnectionTimeoutError().name` -> `Error`; client.js `this.maxRetries = options.maxRetries ?? 2`
failure_scenario: A slow Sonnet response during peak load: the user waits several minutes on 'parsing' and then gets 'Failed to parse transcript' (502) instead of a prompt 504 'AI request timed out'.
suggested_fix: Use `e instanceof Anthropic.APIConnectionTimeoutError`, and pass maxRetries: 0 (or 1) alongside timeout for interactive routes.
verifier_corrections: Everything checks out. One caveat on the worst-case time: the route sets no `maxDuration`, so the hosting platform may kill the function before the full 3x60s per call, or about 6 minutes with the follow-up call. If that happens, the user still gets a failure instead of a clean 504, but the wait may be shorter than the finding states. The follow-up call only runs if the first response has no tool_use block, so in practice the worst case is usually about 180s.

The "about 6 minutes" worst case is overstated. The follow-up only runs if the first call succeeds without a tool call. Getting to about 6 minutes would need the first call to succeed on its 3rd attempt and then the follow-up to time out 3 times. The route also doesn't set maxDuration, so the platform's function limit (about 300s by default on Vercel Fluid) would probably end the request first. The user would then see a platform timeout instead of the 502. The typical failure is about 3 minutes, then a 502 instead of a quick 504. The existing test gives false confidence because it fakes the error name.

title: Only voice-parse sets any upstream timeout; the interaction-check client 'timeout' is armed after the response arrives
description: parse, substance-lookup, nutrient-analysis, medicine-search, interaction-check, titration-warnings and insights use the SDK default of a 10-minute timeout with 2 retries, and no route exports maxDuration. In useInteractionCheck the 15s abort timer is set only after apiFetch has resolved, i.e. after the whole Opus call has finished, so it can never abort a slow model call.
evidence: `const response = await apiFetch("/api/ai/interaction-check", {...}); ... timeoutId = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 15000);`
failure_scenario: An Opus interaction check that runs long leaves the Save step of the add-medication wizard stuck on 'checking' until the Vercel function limit kills the request with a non-JSON 504. The advertised 15s timeout never fires.
suggested_fix: Arm the timer before apiFetch. Set per-request timeout and maxRetries on each route, and export maxDuration.
verifier_corrections: One small correction: voice-transcribe also sets its own upstream timeout (a 30s AbortController on its fetch), so voice-parse is not the only route with one. The timer placement is also deliberate: a code comment says it is started late so it doesn't run while the sign-in modal is open. The finding treats it as an oversight, but either way it cannot cut off a slow model call. The '10-minute default with 2 retries' figure for the other routes comes from the SDK's defaults, not from anything in this repo's code.

title: substance-enrich route and runSubstanceEnrichment are dead; its caffeine prompt also re-allows the recalled figures that substance-lookup forbids (#262)

Substance records created from keywords in the v12 migration (aiEnriched=false) are therefore never refined. The route is still deployed and billable. If it is revived, its caffeine prompt says 'For generic items (drip coffee, espresso, black tea) you may answer from your own knowledge', which is the behaviour substance-lookup now blocks with a server-side web-search check. The ethanolGrams 'sanity check' field is requested from the model but never compared.

grep: runSubstanceEnrichment only appears in lib/substance-enrich.ts. enrich prompt: "2. For generic items (drip coffee, espresso, black tea) you may answer from your own knowledge." vs lookup: "ALWAYS use the web_search tool, for every query without exception."

title: AI-fetched waterContentPercent is stored but never used; spirits count as 100% water via drinks and about 60% via text parse

The food text parser instead tells the model that for neat spirits water_ml is about volume × 60%. The same drink gives different hydration depending on the input path.

Input type="number" ... min={0} max={100} with onChange Number(e.target.value) || 0 (no clamp)

failure_scenario: A 50 ml double vodka logged via the Alcohol preset or voice records 50 ml water. Typed as 'double vodka' in the food AI parser, it records about 30 ml. Fluid-balance totals depend on which screen was used.

title: Voice-parse silently drops malformed items and caps the list at 20 without telling the user
description: extractVoiceItems validates each item and discards failures (e.g. a caffeine item with no description, BP with systolic 38, water ml 0), then slices to 20. The route only logs the dropped count and never returns it, so the review panel looks complete. Heart rate spoken without BP is also dropped by prompt design (rule 2), with no feedback.
evidence:
`if (parsed.success) { items.push(parsed.data); } else { dropped++; }` ... `items: items.slice(0, MAX_ITEMS)`; route returns only `{ items, reasoning }`.
---
[food-salt-voice#10] route.ts:177-181 `if (extracted.dropped > 0) { console.warn(...) }` then `return NextResponse.json({ items, reasoning })`; parsed-item-row.tsx:80-83 `numberOrZero`; voice-panel.tsx:204-209 `addIntake.mutateAsync({ type: "salt", amount: item.sodiumMg, ... })` with no check that the amount is above 0.

suggested_fix: Return `dropped` (and whether truncation happened), and show a warning row in the review panel. Consider a standalone heart-rate item kind.
verifier_corrections:
- **The core claim is accurate.** The cited line ranges are about right: schema.ts 105-136 and route.ts 177-186.
- **The `failure_scenario` depends on the model leaving out `caffeineMg`.** That can happen because the tool schema only requires `kind`, but the prompt asks for `caffeineMg`, so it won't happen every time.
- **The model's reasoning text is shown in the panel.** It may mention a skipped heart rate, which partly makes up for the missing feedback in that case.
- **The 20-item cap is unlikely to matter in real voice use.**
- **The salt-at-0 point from food-salt-voice#10 is a separate issue.** It happens when the user clears a field while editing, so it isn't part of the dropped-item behaviour.

It is about the user editing a field to 0 or leaving it unparseable in the review row, not about server-side items being dropped. It should not count as support for this finding. 2. The model's `reasoning` text is shown in the panel (voice-panel.tsx:529-531), so the model may mention a skipped heart rate. Nothing guarantees that, and it never reports Zod drops, so the core claim still holds. 3. The line numbers are slightly off. The drop loop is schema.ts:112-119 and the slice is at line 132.
