title: AI cost tracking undercounts and can't be priced
description: (a) usage.server_tool_use.web_search_requests is never recorded, although parse, substance-lookup, nutrient-analysis and deep insights run up to 5-12 paid searches per call. (b) Anthropic calls that throw are never recorded (status 'error' is only used for Groq), and the ai-usage totals filter status='success'. (c) Deep batches bill at 50% but are recorded like standard calls. (d) Totals group by provider or route, never by model, so Haiku, Sonnet and Opus tokens are summed together. (e) Concurrent polls of an ended batch each call recordUsage before the completion CAS, so usage can be recorded twice. (f) The bug-report follow-up call is not recorded. (g) A Groq empty transcript (billed) is not recorded, and Math.round turns clips under 0.5s into 0 seconds.
evidence: tokensFromAnthropic reads only input/output/cache fields. ai-usage: `eq(aiUsage.status, "success")`, `.groupBy(aiUsage.provider)` ; jobs route calls recordUsage before `completeInsightJob` CAS.
failure_scenario: A grantor shares their key and sees '40 calls, 300k tokens' in Usage. The real bill also includes about 150 web searches ($1.50), failed calls, and Opus tokens priced at 5x Sonnet, none of which can be derived from the table.
suggested_fix: Record the model per row and group by it, plus web_search_requests, an is_batch flag and error rows (with the status code). Record deep-batch usage inside the completion CAS. Compute an estimated $ using a price table.
verifier_corrections: The list of routes using web search leaves out substance-enrich, which also uses it. The per-call search counts ("5-12") depend on `max_uses` settings that I didn't fully check. Nothing else is materially wrong.

The failure scenario overstates (d): aiUsage.model is stored on every row, so tokens split by model can be recovered from the table. Only the /api/user/ai-usage aggregation merges models. Web-search counts, batch discount and failed calls really cannot be recovered. Parse, substance-lookup, substance-enrich and nutrient-analysis do run paid searches, but the search counts quoted per call (5-12) were not verified. (e) needs concurrent polls to hit the same ended batch, so it is a race, not a deterministic double count. Severity is low, not medium: this is cost reporting only, with no effect on user health data.

title: Deep-insight polling uses the caller's current key: a key change or revoked share leaves the job stuck 'pending' and blocks new deep runs for 24h
description: Batches belong to the org of the key that created them. The poller re-resolves the key on every GET. If the user adds their own key, or a grantor revokes the share, after submitting, batches.retrieve fails (404, which aiErrorResponse does not map) and every poll returns 502. The job stays pending until the 24h expiry, and the one-pending-job-per-user unique index rejects new deep submissions with 409 for that whole time. A job whose attach step crashed (batchId null) is stuck the same way.
evidence: `({ client, resolved } = await getClaudeClientForUser(auth.userId!, auth.email));` then `batch = await client.messages.batches.retrieve(job.batchId);` catch → `{ error: "Failed to check deep-analysis status" }, { status: 502 }`; `insight_jobs_one_pending_per_user_uq`.
failure_scenario: The user starts deep analysis on the owner's shared key, then saves their own Anthropic key. Each poll returns 502, the paid report is never collected, and 'Deep analysis already running' blocks retries until the next day.
suggested_fix: Store keyOwnerId/keySource on the job and resolve that same key when polling. Treat NotFound as a terminal failure that releases the lock. Expire pending jobs with a null batchId after a few minutes.
verifier_corrections:
Three small corrections:

- **Revoked share gives 402, not 502.** If a grantor revokes the share and the user has no other key, `resolveAiKey` throws `NoAiKeyError`. `aiErrorResponse` maps that to 402 NO_AI_KEY at `route.ts:131-132`. The client still treats that as temporary and keeps polling, so the outcome is the same: stuck pending for up to 24h.
- **A 404 is not guaranteed.** It only happens when the new key belongs to a different workspace or org. A new key in the same workspace would still work.
- **The null-batchId case is narrower than stated.** Both the 'attach fails' and 'attach throws' paths in `deep/route.ts:137-163` delete the pending row. `batchId` only stays null if the process is killed between `batches.create` and `attachBatchToJob`, which is a rare serverless timeout or crash.

Severity stays medium: this is an edge-case trigger that clears itself after 24h.

Minor corrections:
- A revoked share with no fallback key returns 402 `NO_AI_KEY` from `aiErrorResponse`, not 502. The job is stuck either way.
- The 404/502 path needs the new key to belong to a different Anthropic org or workspace. A new key in the same workspace would still retrieve the batch.
- The null-`batchId` case only happens after a hard process crash or timeout between `batches.create` and `attachBatchToJob`. An attach that throws or returns false is cleaned up by `deletePendingJob`.

title: Deep report rejected entirely if the model lists a non-URL or more than 30 sources
description: The deep prompt says 'Pass every URL you used via web_search', with up to 12 searches each returning several results. The response schema requires z.array(z.url()).max(30), and the tool schema neither caps the array nor enforces the URI format. A single entry like 'AHA 2025 guideline', or 31 URLs, fails validation and marks the whole paid research job as failed.
evidence: `sources: z.array(z.url()).max(30).optional()` ; prompt: "Pass every URL you used via web_search in the analytics_insight tool's \"sources\" field." ; tool: `sources: { type: "array", items: { type: "string", format: "uri" } }` (no maxItems)
failure_scenario: After 10 minutes of Opus research the model returns 34 URLs, and the user gets 'Deep analysis returned a response that failed structural validation.' The summary and observations are thrown away.
suggested_fix: Coerce instead of rejecting: filter out invalid URLs and slice to 30 before validating the rest. Add maxItems to the tool schema and use strict:true.
verifier_corrections: None of the substance needs correcting. Two small points on framing. First, the length of "10 minutes of Opus research" in the failure scenario is an illustration, not something the code shows. Second, 12 searches is the maximum the code allows (max_uses), not a number the model always uses; the prompt only requires at least 2.

Minor corrections. A non-URL entry is less likely than the finding implies, because the model is explicitly asked for URLs. The more realistic trigger is going over 30 entries, which needs 12 searches and "every URL used". The "10 minutes" duration in the scenario is illustrative, not something the code shows. The rest is accurate.

title: Insights routes send conditions, medication names and prior narratives unsanitised, and persist them server-side, despite the 'aggregate-only' claim
description: The header comment says the payload has 'no free text'. In fact conditions (free strings up to 120 chars), medication name/dose/frequency and prior summaries go into the prompt without sanitizeForAI. nutrient-analysis runs sanitizeForAI on exactly these fields, so the two routes handle the same data differently. Deep jobs also store the full requestPayload (conditions and meds) in Postgres insight_jobs indefinitely.
evidence: buildInsightsPrompt: `User-reported medical conditions: ${profile.conditions.join("; ")}` (raw). nutrient-analysis: `conditions.map((c) => sanitizeForAI(c))`.
failure_scenario: A user types a condition entry like 'CKD stage 3 - Dr Smith 082 555 1234' on the profile page. Nutrient analysis redacts the phone number, but insights sends it verbatim to Anthropic and stores it in Neon insight_jobs.request_payload.
suggested_fix: Sanitise these fields in buildInsightsPrompt (or in the schema's transform). Drop the requestPayload from completed or failed jobs after finalisation. Correct the header comment.
verifier_corrections: The concrete failure scenario is wrong. Nutrient-analysis would not redact '082 555 1234'. redactPii's US phone regex `\b\d{3}[-.]?\d{3}[-.]?\d{4}\b` only allows '-' or '.' as separators, not spaces, and the international pattern needs a leading '+'. That example would go through verbatim on both routes. A working example would be '082-555-1234' or '+27 82 555 1234', or an email address. The finding also leaves out that sending conditions is opt-in through the shareConditionsWithAI setting. Also, the medical content (condition names, medications) is sent on purpose, so the privacy gain from sanitizing is limited to incidental PII.

title: PII redaction misses names, addresses and spaced SA IDs, and mangles barcodes and volumes
description: redactPii is regex-only. Tested outputs: 'John Smith, 12 Main St, Cape Town' passes unchanged; 'my ID 800101 5009 087' (SA ID with spaces) passes; the EAN-13 barcode '6001068301504' becomes '[id-number]' (hurting branded-food lookups); 'then +12 300ml' becomes 'then [phone]ml'. CLAUDE.md and ai-client.ts claim PII is stripped.
evidence: node run: "John Smith, 12 Main St, Cape Town, ate pizza" -> unchanged; "product barcode 6001068301504 " -> "product barcode [id-number] "; "...then +12 300ml" -> "...then [phone]ml"
failure_scenario: A user pastes a product barcode into food AI parse to get an exact match, and the model receives '[id-number]' and guesses. Meanwhile real names typed in meal notes reach Anthropic.
suggested_fix: Document the redaction as best-effort. Exempt EAN/UPC-length digit runs in food contexts, handle spaced SA ID formats, and avoid claiming full PII stripping.
verifier_corrections: Minor: the '+12 300ml' example is an unusual input, and users rarely type barcodes into the food text box, so the practical impact is small. The finding also cites CLAUDE.md, but the comment that claims PII is stripped is at apps/web/src/lib/ai-client.ts:19. The core claims all reproduce.

title: Interaction check doesn't verify every medication was assessed; an omitted drug looks the same as 'no interaction'
description: The prompt asks for 'an entry for every medication', but InteractionResultSchema accepts any array, including an empty one. The route never checks that the returned medication names cover activePrescriptions, so a skipped drug simply doesn't appear.
evidence: `interactions: z.array(z.object({...}))` with no length or coverage check; prompt: "Include an entry for every medication, even if the severity is OK."
failure_scenario: The user is on 6 meds and checks St John's Wort. The model lists 5, skipping sertraline. The UI shows no row for sertraline and the user reads that as safe, missing an AVOID-level serotonin interaction.
suggested_fix: After validating, compare the returned medication names against the request (case-insensitive). Retry, or add an 'Not assessed — check with pharmacist' row for any missing drug.
verifier_corrections: The failure is somewhat worse than described. If the omitted drug was the only one with an AVOID or CAUTION result, the lookup UI doesn't just leave out a row: it shows a green "No significant interactions found" banner, and that result is cached per substance. In the add-medication wizard, the same omission means the save proceeds with no conflict warning.

The UI description is slightly off. When every returned row is OK or the array is empty, the lookup UI doesn't just leave out a row for the skipped drug: it shows a green "No significant interactions found" banner, so the omission looks like an explicit all-clear. In the add-medication wizard's conflict check, an omitted conflict lets the save go through silently. The risk is the same or somewhat worse than described, not less.

title: Synchronous AI routes ignore stop_reason, so refusal, max_tokens and pause_turn surface as 'format invalid'
description: Only insights and the deep jobs route check stop_reason. On the other routes, a truncated tool call (max_tokens), an Opus safety refusal (stop_reason 'refusal', HTTP 200) on drug queries, or a web-search pause_turn all fall through to 'AI response format invalid'/'AI service unavailable'. On web-search routes, a paused turn is answered with a new user message plus forced tool_choice instead of being resumed.
evidence: medicine-search: `const toolBlock = response.content.find(b => b.type === "tool_use"); if (!toolBlock ...) return { error: "AI response format invalid", fallbackToManual: true }` with no stop_reason inspection.
failure_scenario: A medicine search for a controlled drug trips a classifier and returns stop_reason 'refusal'. The user sees 'AI response format invalid' and retries repeatedly, each time paying for Opus tokens.
suggested_fix: Add one shared helper that branches on stop_reason: refusal leads to a clear message (or server-side fallbacks), max_tokens to a retry with a larger budget, pause_turn to a resume with the same content.
verifier_corrections: The claim "only insights and the deep jobs route check stop_reason" is slightly off. nutrient-analysis/route.ts:224 also reads stop_reason, but only to log it, so its behaviour is still affected. The list of affected routes is also incomplete: voice-parse, substance-enrich and nutrient-analysis have the same pattern (they force the tool on a follow-up turn and never branch on stop_reason).

title: Key-decryption failure (e.g. secret rotation) breaks every AI route with a generic 502 while Settings still shows 'Using your key'
description: resolveAiKey calls decryptKey on the user's own row and lets GCM auth errors propagate. There is no fallback to shared or env keys and no mapped error code. The key-vault doc says rotation means 'users re-enter', but the status endpoint still reports configured:true, so nothing prompts re-entry.
evidence: `if (own && ownEncrypted) { return { apiKey: decryptStored(ownEncrypted, userId, provider), ... } }` ; aiErrorResponse only maps NoAiKeyError and Anthropic.AuthenticationError.
failure_scenario: The owner rotates API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_SECRET. Every food parse, voice log and medicine search returns 502 'Failed to process request', and Settings still says 'Using your key ending in AB12'.
suggested_fix: Catch decrypt errors in resolveAiKey and throw a typed KeyUnreadableError, mapped to a 'Re-enter your key' 4xx. Have GET /api/user/api-keys attempt a decrypt and report it as invalid.
verifier_corrections:
Minor gaps in the finding:
- The same unhandled throw happens on the shared-key path (line 116, the grantor's blob). A broken grantor key blocks the grantee without trying other shares or the env key.
- Voice transcription goes through the Groq provider row, so it breaks only if the Groq blob fails to decrypt. That is not always the same blob as the Anthropic one.
- Nothing else is wrong.

title: Rate limiting is per-IP and in-memory only; titration-warnings (Opus) has none
description: Limits reset on each serverless instance and are keyed on a spoofable x-forwarded-for rather than on the user. titration-warnings calls the premium model with no limiter at all. With key sharing, a grantee can spend the grantor's Opus budget without a meaningful cap.
evidence: rate-limit.ts header: "each cold start resets the counters"; titration-warnings route has no createRateLimiter import.
failure_scenario: A grantee's client loops on Generate warnings, or scripts it, and runs up the grantor's Anthropic bill on Opus with no throttle.
suggested_fix: Key the limiter on userId (and keyOwnerId for shared keys) with a durable store, add one to titration-warnings, and consider per-grantee monthly caps.
verifier_corrections: Minor points only. The IP limiter on the other routes is keyed on IP, not on the user, so the finding is right that it ignores userId. It is also correct that no limiter is imported in titration-warnings. The exposure is limited to authenticated, whitelisted users. The finding did not check the ai/interaction-check route, which may have the same gap; I did not verify it.

title: Parse tool description gives a salt-to-sodium conversion that is off by 1000x (grams vs mg)
description: The system prompt correctly says sodium_mg = salt_g * 1000 / 2.5. The sodium_mg tool field description says 'If the source reports salt, divide by 2.5 before returning' without converting units. For a label reading 'salt 1.2 g' that suggests 0.48, which is in g but returned in an mg field. The two instructions contradict each other.
evidence: tool: `"Sodium content in milligrams (NOT NaCl). If the source reports salt, divide by 2.5 before returning."` vs prompt `sodium_mg = salt_g * 1000 / 2.5`
failure_scenario: A UK label shows 'Salt 1.2g'. If the model follows the tool text, it returns sodium_mg 0.48, which the form rounds to 0, so a 480 mg sodium food is logged as zero sodium.
suggested_fix: Make the tool description match the prompt: 'salt in g × 400 = sodium mg'.
verifier_corrections:
1. The cited line numbers are wrong. The tool field description is at packages/ai-prompts/src/parse.ts:72-75, not 98-102. The system-prompt formula at line 11 is correct; the finding cited line 12.
2. The tool text does not literally state a 1000x-wrong conversion. It leaves out the g-to-mg step, which makes it ambiguous. Dividing salt in mg by 2.5 is correct.
3. The failure scenario (the model returns 0.48, so the entry is logged as 0 sodium) is hypothetical. It is not demonstrated, and it runs against the explicit system-prompt formula and worked example.
The suggested fix (state "salt g x 400 = sodium mg" in the tool description) is still a reasonable clarity improvement.

title: Web search uses the legacy web_search_20250305 on models that support web_search_20260209
description: Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 5 support the dynamic-filtering web_search_20260209, which filters results in code execution before they enter context. The legacy version puts full result pages into the prompt, increasing input tokens on every parse, lookup, nutrient and deep call.
evidence: `type: "web_search_20250305" as const,`
failure_scenario: Each web-searched food parse pays for several thousand extra input tokens of raw search results. On deep runs with 12 searches this also crowds the context and makes the search-heavy turns more likely to hit pause_turn.
suggested_fix: Switch to web_search_20260209 when upgrading the models, and handle its error object (non-array content), which hasCompletedWebSearch already does.
verifier_corrections: The cited code and model support are correct, and web_search_20260209 does exist for Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 5. The consequences are overstated. The "several thousand extra tokens per parse" figure and the pause_turn risk were never measured, and dynamic filtering adds its own code-execution overhead. This is a cost/efficiency optimisation, not a data or logic bug, and no user sees a wrong result. The fix is not a drop-in: the two-step routes (parse, substance-lookup, substance-enrich, nutrient-analysis) replay prior assistant turns containing server_tool_use blocks and then force tool_choice, so the new version's extra code-execution blocks must be tested through that replay path and the hasCompletedWebSearch check.

title: AI error details are thrown away on the client (substance lookup, interaction refresh, titration warnings)
description: The server returns actionable codes: NO_AI_KEY (402, 'Add one in Settings'), INVALID_KEY, SEARCH_REQUIRED and 429. preset-tab replaces them with a generic 'Lookup failed', useRefreshInteractions returns null with no toast, and titration-drawer swallows every failure. Food parse, voice and insights do show the server message, so behaviour is inconsistent across screens.
evidence: preset-tab: `if (!res.ok) throw new Error("Lookup failed");` ; refresh: `if (!response || !response.ok) { setIsRefreshing(false); return null; }` ; titration: `catch { // Silently fail }` and no else branch for !res.ok
failure_scenario: A user without a key taps the AI caffeine lookup and sees 'Try a different name', or taps Refresh interactions and the spinner just stops, with no hint that they need to add an API key.
suggested_fix: Read body.error/code in all three places and show the NO_AI_KEY / SEARCH_REQUIRED messages the server already provides.
verifier_corrections: Small correction: the titration check at lines 120-121 is `if (res && res.ok)`, and the silent catch is at about line 127. The cited 114-126 range is close enough. One more detail supports the finding: the interaction check hook in the same file (use-interaction-check.ts:102) already surfaces `body.error`, so the refresh path in that file is the odd one out.

title: 'Previous assessment' for comparison is simply the latest report, which may cover a later or overlapping period
description: includePrevious attaches getLatestInsightReport() regardless of its range. The prompt labels it 'Previous AI assessment(s) for earlier periods' and asks what changed.
evidence: `const previous = await getLatestInsightReport(); if (previous) { ... snapshot.priorAssessments = [priorAssessment]; }` ; prompt: "Previous AI assessment(s) for earlier periods, most recent first"
failure_scenario: The user generates insights for this week, then for last month with 'Include my previous summary' on. The model is told this week's report is from an 'earlier period' and writes 'BP improved from 128 to 134' with the time direction reversed.
suggested_fix: Choose the most recent report whose rangeEnd is at or before the current range.start, or pass the ranges and let the prompt state the real chronology.
verifier_corrections: The finding cites only the quick path. The same code is duplicated in the deep-insights path (use-insights.ts:404-415, POST /api/analytics/insights/deep), which the finding misses. The fix belongs in both places. The prompt also makes the bug worse than the finding says: it passes only the generation date and the length in days, not the range dates, so the model cannot spot the reversed order by itself.

title: Push reminder schedule is rebuilt from TODAY's slots only and replaces the whole weekly server schedule
description: usePushScheduleSync calls useDailyDoseSchedule(todayStr). That only returns schedules whose daysOfWeek include today (dose-schedule-service filters `s.daysOfWeek.includes(dayOfWeek)`). It groups those slots by time, merges the daysOfWeek of all meds at that time, and POSTs the result. syncDoseSchedules then does `DELETE FROM push_schedules WHERE user_id` before inserting. So the server's weekly schedule always reflects only the meds due today, and a combined time slot takes the union of days across meds. There is also an early return `if (!slots || slots.length === 0) return;`, so a day with no doses (or all prescriptions deleted or deactivated) never clears the server schedule.
failure_scenario: Case 1: Med A is daily at 08:00 and Med C is Mon-only at 08:00. On Monday the sync writes 08:00 = "A 10mg, C 5mg" for all 7 days, so Tuesday to Sunday pushes tell the user to take C. Case 2: Med B is Mon/Wed/Fri at 20:00. The user opens /medications on Tuesday, the sync replaces the schedule with Tuesday's slots only, B disappears, and there is no Wednesday 20:00 reminder unless the app is opened on Wednesday. Case 3: the user deletes their last scheduled prescription. slots is [], nothing syncs, and the server keeps pushing reminders for the deleted med. Titration dose changes are also only reflected once the app is opened on the day they take effect.
suggested_fix: Build the push schedule from all active phase schedules for all 7 days, with the per-day dose for each day, instead of from getDailyDoseSchedule(today). Always sync, including an empty list, so deletions clear the server. Key entries by (time, day) with only the meds that apply that day.
verifier_corrections: No factual errors. One detail to add: the sync runs only while `/medications` is mounted, not on every app open, which makes the "until the app is opened on that day" gap worse. Case 3 also needs reminders to still be enabled and the user signed in. The early return fires whenever `slots` is empty, so it covers both deleting everything and a day with no doses.

- The finding says the sync runs when the app is opened (for example, "unless the app is opened on Wednesday"). In fact the sync hook is mounted only on the `/medications` page (through `useMedicationNotifications` in `apps/web/src/app/medications/page.tsx:25`), so reminders go stale unless the user visits that page on the relevant day.
- The `files` list has duplicate line entries, but they point at the correct locations.

The finding treats server pushes as firing independently of the app (for example, "there is no Wednesday 20:00 reminder unless the app is opened on Wednesday"). No cron for /api/push/send is configured in the repo. The only trigger in the repo is the 60s /api/push/check ping from the same hook, which runs only on /medications and resyncs today's schedule when the page mounts. So Cases 1 and 2 cause wrong pushes only if an external scheduler exists. Native Android uses local-notifications.ts, which builds the full weekly schedule, and is not affected. Case 3 (stale rows never cleared) is still reachable. Severity is lowered from high to medium.

title: User data (limits, liquid presets, day-start hour, optional trackers, regions) lives only in localStorage: not synced, not restored from backup
description: The settings store persists to `localStorage` under `intake-tracker-settings`. No Dexie or Postgres table mirrors it, so the sync engine never carries waterLimit, saltLimit, sugarLimit, potassiumLimit, extended buffers, liquidPresets, dayStartHour, optionalTrackers or primaryRegion/secondaryRegion. exportBackup writes `settings: { state }` into the backup file, but importBackup/importEncryptedBackup never read `data.settings` (grep finds no reference), so restoring a backup silently drops them. The Android Capacitor WebView and the browser PWA have separate localStorage, so the same user sees different limits and presets per device. optionalTrackers also controls whether sugar/potassium entries are persisted at all, so the per-device flag changes what data gets written.
evidence:
settings-store.ts: name: "intake-tracker-settings", storage: createJSONStorage(() => localStorage)
backup-service.ts:196 const stored = localStorage.getItem("intake-tracker-settings"); ... settings,
(grep of importBackup body for settings|localStorage|useSettingsStore returns nothing)
optional-trackers.ts: "new entries are NOT persisted (even if the AI returns a value)"
---
[analytics-history-export#15] settings = { state: parsed.state }; ... settings,   // export
// importBackup: no reference to data.settings anywhere
---
[native-android#7] settings-store.ts: `dayStartHour: 2, // Default: 2am`, `waterLimit: 1000`, `saltLimit: 1500`, `storageMode: "local" as const`. No settings sync exists (grep for settings-sync/userSettings finds nothing).
failure_scenario: The user sets waterLimit=1500 and saltLimit=2000 and creates custom presets on the phone. On a new device, after clearing site data, or after restoring a backup, everything falls back to 1000ml/1500mg and the 8 default presets. Progress bars and over-limit warnings are then wrong, custom drinks are gone, and potassium logged on a device where the tracker is off is dropped.
suggested_fix: Move user-data settings (limits, buffers, presets, dayStartHour, optionalTrackers, regions) into a synced Dexie table (e.g. userProfile or a settings row) mirrored to Postgres. Keep only device-UI prefs in localStorage. At minimum, restore `settings` in importBackup.
verifier_corrections:
1. "Potassium logged on a device where the tracker is off is dropped" is how the feature is designed to work, as `optional-trackers.ts` documents. The actual bug is that the flag is not synced between devices.
2. Some of the cited line numbers are loose. `importBackup` starts at line 428, but the finding presents that line as evidence of a missing read, which cannot be shown on a single line.
3. Severity is overstated. Only configuration is lost, not record data, so medium fits better than high.
4. Whether settings should sync across devices is partly a design choice. The clear bug is that `importBackup` ignores the `settings` data it exported.

The failure is real, but the finding overstates the impact in two places.
(a) "Potassium logged on a device where the tracker is off is dropped" is how the toggle is designed to work. The actual problem is only that the toggle is not shared between devices.
(b) Having no cross-device sync is a design gap. It is a real one because a sync engine exists for everything else, but the only outright bug is that importBackup ignores the settings that exportBackup writes into the file.
Some of the cited line numbers are loose. The export code is at backup-service.ts:192-200 and 229. Line 428 is not where the import logic sits; the table clearing and merging is around lines 470-575, and settings are never referenced there.
Severity is better rated medium than high, because no health record data is lost.

Severity should be medium, not high. No health or medical records are lost; only preferences reset to visible defaults that the user can re-enter. The claim that "potassium logged on a device where the tracker is off is dropped" overstates the problem: when the tracker is off, the potassium input is hidden on every surface, so the user cannot enter a value that then gets lost. The strongest, most concrete part of the finding is that importBackup ignores the `settings` block that exportBackup writes (backup-service.ts:192-229, with no reader anywhere in the file). The fix could be as small as restoring that block on import, and it should be listed as a separate, lower-effort item from building a synced settings table.

title: Reset to Defaults silently wipes custom presets, disables cloud sync and dose reminders without server cleanup
description: `resetToDefaults: () => set(defaultSettings)` overwrites every field, and the button calls it with no confirmation dialog. That includes liquidPresets (custom presets are gone and records tagged `preset:<uuid>` lose their names), storageMode→"local" (useSyncLifecycle stops the engine, and useSyncAutoDetect's `checked` ref is already true for the session so it won't restore cloud-sync until reload), doseRemindersEnabled→false (only the store flag; unsubscribeFromPush is never called, so the server subscription and schedule stay live), and analyticsIntroSeen→false. It does NOT reset the actual theme (next-themes owns it), yet the toast says "All settings have been restored to defaults". Scratch test confirmed: after reset liquidPresets=8, storageMode=local, doseRemindersEnabled=false.
failure_scenario: A cloud-sync user taps Reset to Defaults, which has no confirmation. Sync stops for the session, and records logged afterwards are not pushed until the next app reload. The storage section now shows "local" and invites them to re-run migration. Their custom "Oat Latte" preset is gone, and past entries show as "Beverage". The reminders toggle shows off, but the server keeps sending dose pushes.
suggested_fix: Add a confirm dialog. Exclude storageMode, doseRemindersEnabled, liquidPresets and onboarding flags from reset, or route them through their proper flows (unsubscribeFromPush, the sync switch). Reset the next-themes theme too, or drop the dead `theme` field.
verifier_corrections:
I downgraded severity from high to medium. No health records are lost or corrupted. The intake records survive and only their preset label falls back to "Beverage". Sync stops only for the current session: on reload, the auto-detect hook restores cloud-sync if the server has data. Records written in the meantime are still in Dexie and should be pushed once sync resumes (plausible, not traced). The real harms are these:
- Custom presets are deleted with no confirmation and cannot be recovered.
- Dose pushes keep arriving while the toggle shows off.
I did not verify the claim that the server keeps sending pushes by tracing the server cron, but it follows from the subscription never being removed. I also did not verify the `theme` / next-themes point, which is minor either way.

The claim that "useSyncAutoDetect's checked ref is already true for the session" is false for users who start the session in cloud-sync mode. The ref is only set once the effect passes the `storageMode === "local"` guard, so after a reset it runs and restores cloud-sync whenever the server reports hasSyncedData. The claim that "the server keeps sending dose pushes" is unsupported: the client pinging `/api/push/check` stops when the flag goes false, and nothing in the repo schedules `/api/push/send`. Only a stale server subscription or schedule row remains. The reset also fails to reach next-themes, which is accurate, but that is a cosmetic mislabel in the toast. Severity is lowered from high to medium.

"Records logged afterwards are not pushed until the next app reload" is accurate, but there is no data loss: the writes are queued in `_syncQueue` and flush once auto-detect restores cloud-sync on the next load (this assumes the server reports hasSyncedData). The real irreversible harm is losing custom liquid presets, which changes past entries' labels but not their data. The server keeps sending pushes the user already had, so it is a UI/server state mismatch rather than a dosing error. Severity should be medium, not high.

title: Two divergent Medication Region settings UIs with incompatible stored values
description: /settings → Medication uses a Select with values US/UK/CA/AU/DE/ZA/Other plus a "None" option, and displays `primaryRegion || "US"`. /medications → Settings uses an ISO combobox where "" = "Not Specified (Global Search)" and the UK is "GB". Both write the same store fields. The comment says "Normalize old 'UK'/'none' values", but no normalization code exists: an unknown value just shows the placeholder.
evidence:
<Select value={primaryRegion || "US"} onValueChange={setPrimaryRegion}>
{ value: "UK", label: "United Kingdom" }, { value: "Other", label: "Other" }
---
{ value: "", label: "Not Specified (Global Search)" } ... { value: "GB", label: "United Kingdom" }
// Normalize old "UK"/"none" values   (followed by no normalization)
failure_scenario: A new user opens /settings and sees Primary Region = "United States", but the store is "", so medicine search sends no country and returns global results. A user who picks "United Kingdom" in /settings stores "UK", and the /medications combobox then shows "Select a country". Picking "Other" sends the literal country "Other" to the AI.
suggested_fix: Delete MedicationSettingsSection or make it reuse CountryCombobox. Add a settings migration that maps UK→GB, None/none/Other→"".
verifier_corrections:
No factual errors. Two minor additions:
- The /medications combobox also has no entry for the secondary value "None", so the /settings secondary default shows as the placeholder there too.
- "Other" can reach the AI through either field: as the primary country, or appended as "(and Other as secondary fallback)".

Minor corrections, none of which change the conclusion:
- The comment about normalizing old values is at about line 242 of medication-settings-view.tsx, and the combobox is used at line 427. The finding's line 218 is the start of the COUNTRIES list.
- Secondary region "None" is handled properly by use-medicine-search.ts:50, so only the primary region's "Other"/"UK"/"" handling is actually broken.

title: Time Format setting is dead; app hardcodes 12h for records and raw 24h for medication times
description: timeFormat (default "24h") is only read by its own Select. No formatter consults it. formatTimeOnly/formatDateTime hardcode `hour12: true` for all record cards. Medication dose rows print slot.localTime ("08:00") raw. The default "24h" contradicts what the record cards actually show.
evidence:
grep timeFormat: only medication-settings-view.tsx:300,404 and the store
date-utils.ts: toLocaleTimeString("en-US", { hour: "numeric", minute: "2-digit", hour12: true })
failure_scenario: The user selects "24-hour (14:00)". The water, weight, BP, urination and food cards still show "2:00 PM", while medication rows show "14:00" whatever the choice. Mixed formats on adjacent screens make dose times easy to misread.
suggested_fix: Route all time formatting through a helper that reads timeFormat, or remove the setting.
verifier_corrections: The cited lines are slightly off. The settings view shows `timeFormat` at lines 300 and 404 (Select at 402-412). date-utils starts at line 75. Dose rows print HH:mm in two places: `slot.localTime` for pending doses and a hardcoded HH:mm `formatTimestamp` (dose-row.tsx:33-35) for taken doses. The finding only mentions the raw `slot.localTime` path. The severity should be low, not medium: the times shown are accurate, and only the format is inconsistent.

The file references are accurate. The finding misses that `dose-row.tsx` also has a private `formatTimestamp` helper (lines 33-35) that hardcodes 24-hour `HH:MM` for taken-dose times, not just raw `slot.localTime`. I'd call medium overstated: the times shown are always correct, only the display format ignores the setting, and there is no data or dosing error.

title: Several persisted settings have UI or defaults but no consumer (weight-graph overlays, substanceConfig, aiAuthSecret, theme, dataRetentionDays)
description: weightGraphShowEating/Urination/Defecation/Drinking have four toggles described as "Choose which reference lines appear by default on the weight chart", but grep finds no chart that reads them. substanceConfig (caffeine/alcohol enabled flags and types) is never read. aiAuthSecret/getDeobfuscatedAuthSecret are never read, yet the value is exported in backups. The store's `theme` is never read, because next-themes owns the theme. dataRetentionDays ("Default: keep 90 days") is never read.
evidence: grep weightGraphShow → only weight-settings-section.tsx; grep substanceConfig|aiAuthSecret|dataRetentionDays outside the store → no hits; appearance-section.tsx uses `const { theme, setTheme } = useTheme();`
failure_scenario: The user turns off the "Drinking" overlay and nothing changes on any weight chart. Their substanceConfig caffeine defaults (Coffee 95mg) never affect logging. Toggles that do nothing erode trust in the settings screen.
suggested_fix: Remove the dead fields in a settings migration (bump SETTINGS_PERSIST_VERSION, delete the keys) and their UI, or wire them up.
verifier_corrections: This is slightly overstated. aiAuthSecret is exported in backups, but nothing ever calls setAiAuthSecret, so the value is always the default empty string and the backup leaks no secret. The only real result is a dead key. The same goes for substanceConfig: it can't be edited from the UI either, so users never see it. The only settings a user can actually change and see do nothing are the four weight-graph overlay toggles. The claim that the overlays are "not read by any chart" is also understated: no weight chart with overlays exists at all.

title: Analytics time range is memoized on scope only and goes stale after midnight
description: useTimeScopeRange computes `end = endOfDay(now)` inside `useMemo(..., [scope])`. There is no tick dependency, unlike the intake hooks, which use useNowTick. Every analytics and Records-tab useLiveQuery is keyed on range.end, so once midnight passes with the page open (or the PWA resumed from background), new records fall outside [start,end] and aren't shown.
failure_scenario: The user opens Analytics → Records at 23:30, backgrounds the PWA, and resumes at 08:00. The morning's water and BP entries are missing from Records and Summary, and the "7d" window is shifted a day, until the user switches scope or reloads.
suggested_fix: Include a day-granularity tick (e.g. useNowTick-derived date key) in the memo deps.
verifier_corrections: No material corrections. Three small notes. The query key that goes stale is effectiveRange, which is customRange ?? scopeRange, so a user-picked custom range is fixed by design and isn't affected by this bug. Resuming a PWA only reproduces the bug if the page was not evicted or reloaded while in the background. I checked the Records-tab wiring directly. I did not open every Summary and chart hook, but the correlation hook shown at use-analytics-queries.ts:225 also uses range.start and range.end as its dependencies, so the same staleness applies there.

Minor: the failure hits every scope, including "24h", which keeps showing the previous day. Only "all" (start=0) keeps its start correct, but its end is frozen too, so it also hides the new records. The memo sits at lines 240-265, which matches the cited range. The Summary tab and other analytics hooks get the same `effectiveRange`, so they go stale in the same way.

title: Settings migrations give upgraded users different shake defaults than new users
description: Migrations v<11 and v<12 force shakeThreshold 15→8 and shakeRequiredJolts=3. Fresh installs get shakeThreshold 10 / shakeRequiredJolts 5. Scratch test: migrateSettings({}, 10) gave threshold 8, jolts 3; fresh state gave 10, 5. There are also no migration tests covering the full chain (only optional-trackers and presets tests exist in stores/__tests__).
failure_scenario: The owner's long-lived install fires shake-to-report on 3 jolts at threshold 8 (much more sensitive), while a fresh install needs 5 jolts at 10. Bug reports about accidental triggers can't be reproduced on a clean device.
suggested_fix: Align the defaults, or document the divergence. Add a table-driven test that migrates from every past version and asserts the resulting shape equals the defaults except for user-set fields.
verifier_corrections: The finding blames the divergence on the v<11 and v<12 migrations alone, which is too narrow. Before 4da8050c, the persisted-state version was already at 12 or higher. Those users' stored settings already hold shakeThreshold 8 and jolts 3, so Zustand keeps those values whether or not the old migrations run. The real cause is that the default change in 4da8050c came with no version bump and no migration, so the "fewer accidental triggers" fix never reached any existing install, including the owner's. The old migrations hardcoding 8/3 only add to that. Aligning the old migrations with the new defaults would not fix it. It needs a new migration (v17) that moves users still on the old 8/3 defaults to 10/5.

title: Unused hooks and an unmounted HistoryDrawer that double-toasts over the undo toast
description: HistoryDrawer is imported only by its own test. Its delete handler always fires a plain "Entry deleted" toast after undo-toast mutations, which TOAST_LIMIT=1 would use to replace the Undo button (the bug that useDeleteWithToast's undoToast flag exists to prevent). useHistoryData is only used by that drawer. useWaterSettings, useSaltSettings, useSugarSettings, usePotassiumSettings, useIntakeRecords and useAllIntake have zero callers.
evidence: grep HistoryDrawer → only history-drawer.dom.test.tsx; history-drawer.tsx:119 toast({ title: "Entry deleted", description: "Record removed" }); grep counts: useWaterSettings 0, useAllIntake 0, useIntakeRecords 0
failure_scenario: If the drawer is re-mounted in the styling refresh, deleting an intake, eating, urination or defecation record there hides the Undo button immediately.
suggested_fix: Delete HistoryDrawer, useHistoryData and the unused hooks, or fix the toast logic before reusing them.
verifier_corrections: One small correction: useIntakeRecords is called in use-intake-queries.test.tsx, so it does not have literally zero references. It does have zero callers in production code. Everything else in the finding is accurate.

title: list_medications reports maintenance AND titration phases as simultaneously active for the same drug
description: activateTitrationPlan flips the plan's pending titration phases to 'active' but never completes the prescription's existing maintenance phase. The app deals with this in getDailyDoseSchedule by keeping one phase per prescription ("Titration overrides maintenance"). The MCP query returns every phase with status='active' along with all of its enabled schedules. It also leaves out titrationPlanId, so the model has nothing to tell it which phase takes precedence.
evidence: queries.ts: `.where(and(eq(medicationPhases.userId, userId), eq(medicationPhases.status, "active"), inArray(medicationPhases.prescriptionId, prescIds), ...))` then `active_phases: phases.filter((ph) => ph.prescriptionId === p.id)`. titration-service.ts:350: `const titrationPhases = planPhases.filter((p) => p.titrationPlanId === planId && p.status === "pending")` -> set to active; maintenance phase untouched. dose-schedule-service.ts:129: `} else if (phase.type === "titration" && phase.titrationPlanId) { // Titration overrides maintenance`
failure_scenario: The user is on carvedilol 6.25mg twice a day (maintenance) and activates a titration plan with a 12.5mg twice-a-day step. The app's schedule shows only 12.5mg. When asked "what am I taking", Claude sees two active phases with enabled 08:00 and 20:00 schedules and reports either 6.25+12.5mg per slot (18.75mg twice a day) or two conflicting regimens.
suggested_fix: Apply the same phase-precedence rule as getDailyDoseSchedule, ideally through a shared helper in @intake/core, and return only the effective phase per prescription. Also select titrationPlanId and phase type. Separately, fix activateTitrationPlan so it sets the superseded maintenance phase to completed or paused.
verifier_corrections: 1. The finding says the query leaves out phase type. It doesn't: `type: medicationPhases.type` is selected, so the output does mark which phase is titration and which is maintenance. Only `titrationPlanId` is missing, along with any precedence rule. 2. Leaving maintenance active during titration is intended, not a bug in `activateTitrationPlan`: `completeTitrationPlan` promotes titration schedules into that active maintenance phase. It does also handle a 'completed' maintenance phase, so pausing or completing it may be workable, but the suggested fix would change a deliberate lifecycle. The right fix is in the MCP query (and a shared precedence helper), not in activation. 3. Severity is high, not critical: the output is ambiguous to the LLM, and no stored data is corrupted.

1. The suggested fix says to "also select … phase type", but `type` is already selected (`type: medicationPhases.type`). Only `titrationPlanId` is missing.
2. The severity is overstated. The app's own schedule and UI are correct and only the MCP/AI read path is wrong, so this is high rather than critical.
3. There is one more piece of evidence the finding doesn't cite: the list_medications tool description (tools.ts:275) promises "their currently-active phase" (singular), which contradicts the multi-phase payload.
4. Completing or pausing maintenance inside `activateTitrationPlan` would conflict with the current design. `completeTitrationPlan` already handles the maintenance phase when the plan finishes, and the UI and schedule are built to keep maintenance active during a titration. The correct fix is to apply the precedence rule in the MCP query (for example, reuse `getEffectivePhase`), not to change activation.

1) The finding implies the model can't tell the phases apart, but `type` is already selected and returned. Only `titrationPlanId` and a precedence rule are missing, so the suggested fix to "also select phase type" is already done. 2) Keeping maintenance active during titration looks deliberate, not an `activateTitrationPlan` bug. `completeTitrationPlan` (titration-service.ts ~451) writes the final dose back into the maintenance phase and sets it active again ("Re-activate maintenance if it was completed"). `getDailyDoseSchedule` is written to expect two active phases. So the "separately, complete/pause maintenance on activation" part of the fix would change a design decision and would have to be checked against the completion and cancel flows. The actual defect is only that the MCP query doesn't apply the precedence rule. 3) The severity should be high, not critical: the app's own data and schedules are correct, and the risk is an LLM misreading output that is labelled.

title: Inventory stock is cast to int, so fractional (half-tablet) balances are rounded
description: inventory_transactions.amount is `real`, and fractional consumption is normal (for example a 6.25mg dose from a 12.5mg tablet uses 0.5). The app displays fractional stock (compound-card.tsx isFractional / formatPillCount). The MCP subquery casts SUM(...) to ::int, which rounds with rint (round-half-to-even). The code comment says the cast avoids a bigint string, but SUM(real) already comes back as a float, so the cast isn't needed.
evidence:
queries.ts:561: `(SELECT SUM(${inventoryTransactions.amount})::int FROM ...`. schema.ts: `amount: real("amount").notNull()`
---
[prescriptions-model#16] queries.ts:561 `(SELECT SUM(${inventoryTransactions.amount})::int` ; schema.ts:561 `amount: real("amount").notNull()`.
---
[live-data-forensics#15] queries.ts:561 `(SELECT SUM(${inventoryTransactions.amount})::int`. LIVE: Spironolactone (0.5 tablet per daily dose) reports stock 38 and Carvedilol (0.5 + 1 per day) reports 88, both integers even though 46 and 81 half-tablet consumptions are logged.
failure_scenario: The app shows 2.5 tablets left and MCP reports stock: 2. At 27.5 it reports 28. A refill-timing question like "how many days until I run out" gets a wrong answer, and a 0.5 balance is reported as 0, meaning out of stock.
suggested_fix: Drop the ::int cast, or use ::double precision and round to 4 decimals the way the app does (Math.round(x*10000)/10000).
verifier_corrections: The "files" list cites queries.ts twice (560-568 and 560-567). The cast is on line 561. Otherwise accurate. The impact is limited to MCP tool output (get_inventory_status), not the in-app stock display.

Minor point: removing the cast still leaves float4 rounding noise, because SUM(real) returns real. The fix should be SUM(amount)::double precision, or ROUND(SUM(amount)::numeric, 4)::float8, to match the app's 4-decimal rounding. The claim that 0.5 is reported as 0 is correct, because ties round to even.

title: The push schedule on the server is never cleared when the local schedule becomes empty
description: The sync effect returns early when `slots.length === 0`. syncDoseSchedules (DELETE then INSERT) only runs with a non-empty list, so deactivating or deleting the last medication, or a day with no doses, leaves the old push_schedules rows in place. The sync is also built only from today's slots (useDailyDoseSchedule(todayStr)) and then expanded across every weekday, so the payload for other days (dose and meds) reflects today's phase.
evidence: use-push-schedule-sync.ts:123: `if (!slots || slots.length === 0) return;` then `syncSchedule(entries)`; push-db.ts: `await sql`DELETE FROM push_schedules WHERE user_id = ${userId}``, which is only reached with entries.
failure_scenario: The user stops their last scheduled medication. The dashboard shows no doses, but the server still has 08:00 and 20:00 slots with the old medicationsJson, so /api/push/check keeps pushing "Time for your 08:00 medications: Carvedilol 6.25mg" for a drug they no longer take.
suggested_fix: Always sync, including an empty array, once the live query has resolved (slots !== undefined). Build entries from each schedule's own daysOfWeek using the phase actually in effect on that day, not today's slots.
verifier_corrections:
Minor points. The hook is mounted only on /medications, so a sync (and the 60s check ping) runs only while that page is open. The staleness happens because the sync is skipped whenever today's list is empty.

The finding also understates the today-only problem. A schedule whose daysOfWeek excludes today is left out of the payload entirely. For example, a Monday-only medication synced on a Tuesday is dropped. The DELETE-then-INSERT then wipes its Monday rows, so that reminder is lost as well as mislabeled.

"A day with no doses" is only a skipped sync: the previous day's rows stay in place. That leftover is mostly harmless, because each row is keyed to its own day_of_week.

The finding says "a day with no doses" is a failure case. On such a day the sync is skipped, so the previous day's rows stay on the server. That keeps existing reminders rather than adding a new wrong one, unless the empty day came from a medication being stopped. The second half understates the issue. It is not only that other days show today's dose and phase text: schedules whose `daysOfWeek` does not include the sync day are dropped completely, because the DELETE wipes them and nothing is re-inserted. Those medications get no reminders until a sync happens on one of their own days. The sync only runs while `/medications` is mounted.

title: The subscribe upsert resets the user's timezone to UTC
description: savePushSubscription defaults tz to 'UTC' and the ON CONFLICT clause writes `timezone = EXCLUDED.timezone`. SubscribeSchema has no timezone field and the client doesn't send one. Only sync-schedule corrects it, and that is debounced by an in-memory hash, so it doesn't re-run in the same session unless the schedule changes.
evidence: push-db.ts: `const tz = sub.timezone ?? "UTC";` ... `timezone = EXCLUDED.timezone`. The subscribe body contains only endpoint and keys.
failure_scenario: The user toggles reminders off and back on in the same session. Unsubscribe deletes the row, subscribe inserts it with timezone='UTC', and the sync effect sees the same hash and skips. /api/push/check now compares UTC wall-clock time with local-time slots, so a user at UTC+2 gets the 08:00 reminder at 10:00 local until they reload.
suggested_fix: Send Intl timezone in the subscribe body and accept it in SubscribeSchema, or leave the timezone column untouched on conflict when none is supplied.
verifier_corrections: No factual errors. One detail to add: the effect also returns early when `slots` is empty (use-push-schedule-sync.ts:123). That means sync-schedule never sends a timezone on a day with no scheduled slots.

One small correction: the wrong timezone does not last "until they reload". It lasts until the medications page remounts, because `useMedicationNotifications` is mounted in `apps/web/src/app/medications/page.tsx` and `lastHashRef` is per-mount. It also clears if the dose schedule or follow-up settings change. Leaving the medications route and coming back, or reloading, triggers a resync. Otherwise the finding is accurate.

title: get_today_summary counts doses by actionTimestamp and never shows missed doses
description: The app's daily dose view uses scheduledDate and derives missed or pending slots from the schedule. MCP groups dose_logs by status where actionTimestamp falls in the UTC-computed day window. Slots with no log at all (not yet acted on or missed) never show up, and a dose taken or edited late is counted on the day it was acted on, not the day it was scheduled.
evidence: queries.ts: `gte(doseLogs.actionTimestamp, startTs), lte(doseLogs.actionTimestamp, nowTs)` ... `.groupBy(doseLogs.status)`; app: `db.doseLogs.where("scheduledDate").equals(dateStr)`.
failure_scenario: The user has 4 scheduled doses today and has logged only 1. MCP returns doses:[{status:'taken',count:1}] with no sign that 3 are outstanding, so "did I take everything today?" gets a misleading answer. Yesterday's 22:00 dose logged at 02:30 today counts toward today.
suggested_fix: Compute today's expected slots on the server from phases and schedules (the same logic as getDailyDoseSchedule, shared through @intake/core) keyed by scheduledDate in the user's timezone, and report taken, skipped, and outstanding counts.
verifier_corrections: The tool is documented as "doses logged today", so leaving out unlogged or outstanding slots is by design, not a contradiction. The finding's "did I take everything today?" framing is really a feature gap or missing documentation. The one behavioural mismatch that holds is attribution by actionTimestamp instead of scheduledDate, which affects late-logged doses near the day boundary. Also, the window is not literally a "UTC-computed day": todayStartTimestamp uses the server's local setHours plus dayStartHour, which on Vercel usually means UTC, so the timezone issue is real but comes from server locale. Severity should be low.

This is partly by design: the tool description at `tools.ts:131` literally promises "doses logged today". The real defect is that the MCP view doesn't match the app's schedule-based daily view, so answers built on it are misleading. The finding calls the window "UTC-computed". More precisely, it uses the server process's local timezone via `setHours`, which is UTC on Vercel. The finding also leaves out one more exclusion: logs with a null `actionTimestamp` are silently dropped.

title: MCP input-validation errors come back as a generic 'internal error'
description: validateRange runs inside the runTool body, so its thrown errors hit the catch block, which replaces every message with a generic string and records the call as an error in the audit log.
evidence: tools.ts: `(userId) => { validateRange(args); ... }` and catch: `text: "An internal error occurred while processing your request."`, isError: true.
failure_scenario: The user asks "show my weight over the last 2 years". The model requests a 730-day range and gets "An internal error occurred" with no hint that the limit is 1 year. It tells the user the service is broken instead of splitting the query.
suggested_fix: Validate the range before entering runTool's try, or throw a typed validation error whose message is returned verbatim. Better still, put the range limit into the Zod schema.
verifier_corrections: The cited line ranges are slightly off. validateRange is called at lines 160, 179, 197, 215, 243 and 262, and the runTool catch spans lines 99-121. The substance of the finding is accurate. The end_ms < start_ms case is masked the same way.

title: History truncation keeps the oldest 5000 rows and drops the most recent
description: The queries sort ascending, apply LIMIT 5001, and then slice the first 5000. When a range is over the cap, the rows dropped are the newest ones, which are usually the most relevant.
evidence: `.orderBy(asc(intakeRecords.timestamp)).limit(MAX_ROWS + 1)` then `rows.slice(0, MAX_ROWS)`.
failure_scenario: query_intake_history(type='all') over a year with about 15 rows a day (about 5475 rows) returns data only up to about late August. Claude's "recent trend" analysis leaves out the last month, and only a truncated:true flag signals it.
suggested_fix: Order by desc, limit, then reverse, so the newest rows are kept. Or return the timestamp of the last included row so the model can page.
verifier_corrections: The finding is scoped too narrowly. The same oldest-first sort plus capRows pattern is used by the weight (lines 314-315), blood pressure (344-345), eating (368-369), substance (414-415) and urination (618-619) history queries, not just intake. The header comment shows the cap and flag are intentional. The actual gap is that the newest rows are the ones dropped and no cutoff timestamp is returned for paging.

title: MCP tokens can't be revoked; revokedAt is never written
description: lookupAccessToken and rotateRefreshToken check revokedAt, but no route, UI, or job ever sets it. purgeExpired isn't wired up either. Apart from deleting the whole account, the only ways to cut off a connector are removing the email from ALLOWED_EMAILS or waiting for the 30-day refresh expiry. The refresh token also doesn't rotate by design.
evidence: grep for revokedAt outside tests finds only oauth.ts:288,314,358,365 (reads). oauth.ts:381: "Periodic cleanup helper — not wired to a cron".
failure_scenario: The user suspects their claude.ai account was compromised or wants to disconnect the connector. The access token stays valid for up to 24h and the refresh token for up to 30 days, with nothing in the app to revoke them.
suggested_fix: Add a settings action or an RFC 7009 /revoke endpoint that sets revokedAt on all of the user's tokens, and schedule purgeExpired.
verifier_corrections: Minor clarification: the refresh token's 30-day window counts from when it was first issued, because refresh never extends `refreshExpiresAt`. So "up to 30 days" is accurate. The ALLOWED_EMAILS workaround requires changing an env var and redeploying, so the user can't do it from the app. Otherwise the finding is accurate.

title: native-auth/mint inserts a row that references users_sync without making sure the user exists there
description: native_auth_codes.user_id has an FK to users_sync. Only withAuth and the MCP authorize route upsert users_sync, and mint calls neither. A first-time Google sign-in through the Android bridge, before any withAuth call, fails with an FK violation that turns into an unhandled 500.

suggested_fix: Upsert users_sync (id and email) in the mint route before inserting, reusing the helper from auth-middleware, and wrap the insert in a try/catch that returns JSON.
verifier_corrections: No real errors. One detail is off. The FK target is neon_auth.users_sync, and it is declared in migration 0018. The cited schema.ts lines 1103-1105 point to the correct .references() call. A minor addition: the mint route also skips the ALLOWED_EMAILS whitelist check that withAuth performs. description: The consent page lists intake, weight, BP, food, medications/doses and inventory. The same scope also grants caffeine and alcohol history (query_substance_history), urination history, and titration plans with clinical notes and warnings.

title: list_recent_doses leaves out kind, doseMg and phaseId, so PRN doses have no amount
description: dose_logs now has kind ('scheduled'|'prn') and doseMg (for PRN doses), but listRecentDoses selects neither, and no phaseId/scheduleId either. PRN doses (e.g. as-needed furosemide) look like scheduled ones, and their dose amount is unavailable over MCP.

title: Three disagreeing stock computations: cached currentStock, getCurrentStock (counts deleted transactions), and MCP SUM::int (rounds away fractions)
description: The UI shows the cached inventoryItems.currentStock. getCurrentStock, which recalculateAllStock uses from the debug panel to 'fix drift', sums every transaction without filtering deletedAt. The prior Fable audit flagged this as a latent bug, and it is still present at HEAD. The MCP get_inventory_status filters deleted rows but casts SUM(real) to ::int, so a half-pill balance is rounded to a whole number. It also claims to 'mirror getCurrentStock', which it doesn't.
evidence: inventory-service.ts:269-275 `const transactions = await db.inventoryTransactions.where("inventoryItemId").equals(inventoryItemId).toArray(); const sum = transactions.reduce((acc, tx) => acc + tx.amount, 0);` (no deletedAt filter). mcp/queries.ts:561 `(SELECT SUM(${inventoryTransactions.amount})::int … AND ${inventoryTransactions.deletedAt} IS NULL)`. inventory_transactions.amount is `real("amount")` (schema.ts:561).
failure_scenario: The user deletes a mistaken +30 refill transaction, and the UI correctly drops to 12.5 pills. Running 'Recalculate stock' in the debug panel counts the deleted +30 again and writes 42.5 into currentStock. Meanwhile Claude via MCP reports 12 pills. The same box has three different counts.
suggested_fix: Make one canonical derivation that filters deletedAt === null, and use it for the cache refresh, the debug recalculation and (via SQL) the MCP query. Drop the ::int cast, or use ::numeric/round to 4 decimals to match the client's precision.
verifier_corrections: The finding understates how the bug is triggered. The debug panel's "Recalculate stock" is not needed: `initStockRecalculation()` in `apps/web/src/app/providers.tsx:58` runs `recalculateAllStock` each time the app loads. Any deleted inventory transaction is therefore counted again in `currentStock` on the next cold start, and the change syncs to the server. The MCP `::int` cast rounds rather than truncates: 12.5 may come out as 12 or 13 depending on Postgres's float-to-int rounding. Either way the fraction is lost.

The scenario's MCP number is wrong. Postgres rounds `::int` to the nearest whole number with halves going away from zero, so 12.5 is reported as 13, not 12. The finding also frames the drift as needing the user to run the debug panel's "Recalculate stock". In fact `recalculateAllStock` runs automatically on every app launch through `initStockRecalculation` (providers.tsx:58). Any user-deleted inventory transaction is counted again on the next cold start, which makes the impact wider than described.

The bad recalculation does not need the user to press "Recalculate stock" in the debug panel. initStockRecalculation() in app/providers.tsx:58 runs recalculateAllStock() on every app launch, so any deleted transaction is added back into currentStock on the next cold start and synced to the server. The ::int cast rounds to the nearest whole number rather than truncating: 12.5 becomes 12 (round-half-even), but 12.75 becomes 13. This part is low-impact next to the deletedAt bug.

title: Validation ranges for BP/weight differ across add, voice, card-edit, records-tab edit and the dead HistoryDrawer adapters

title: Android medication reminders use UTC hour/minute as device-local time: they fire hours early or late, and can land on the wrong day
description: PhaseSchedule.scheduleTimeUTC is 'minutes from midnight UTC'. The web converts it with formatLocalTime(schedule.scheduleTimeUTC, tz). The native scheduler instead splits the raw UTC minutes into hour/minute and passes them to Capacitor's `on` trigger. That plugin's DateMatch builds the trigger with Calendar.getInstance(), which uses the device's local timezone. daysOfWeek are local weekdays, but the UTC time can fall on the previous or next UTC day, so both the time and the day are wrong. The unit test enshrines the bug: 540 UTC is expected to produce hour 9.
evidence:

DateMatch.kt:23 `val cal = Calendar.getInstance()` (default = device TZ). Scratch vitest (TZ=Africa/Johannesburg, deleted afterwards): a schedule created as 08:00 Monday gives scheduleTimeUTC=360 and native `{hour:6,minute:0,weekday:2}`. A 01:00 Monday dose gives scheduleTimeUTC=1380 and native `{hour:23,minute:0,weekday:2}`.
---
[doses-titration-schedule#8] `const utcMinutes = schedule.scheduleTimeUTC; const hour = Math.floor(utcMinutes / 60) % 24; ... schedule: { on: { hour, minute, weekday: capWeekday } }`. The test (__tests__/local-notifications.test.ts:203) only checks UTC=local.
---
[dexie-schema#5] `const utcMinutes = schedule.scheduleTimeUTC; const hour = Math.floor(utcMinutes / 60) % 24; const minute = utcMinutes % 60; ... schedule: { on: { hour, minute, weekday: capWeekday }`
---
[dates-timezones#2] `const utcMinutes = schedule.scheduleTimeUTC; const hour = Math.floor(utcMinutes / 60) % 24; ... schedule: { on: { hour, minute, weekday: capWeekday } }`
---
[live-data-forensics#2] local-notifications.ts:71 `const utcMinutes = schedule.scheduleTimeUTC; const hour = Math.floor(utcMinutes / 60) % 24;` ... `schedule: { on: { hour, minute, weekday: capWeekday } }`. The Capacitor 8.3.1 DateMatch.kt:23 uses `Calendar.getInstance()`. LIVE: every schedule is anchored Europe/Berlin with scheduleTimeUTC 390 (08:30 local) or 1110 (20:30 local), so the reminders fire at 06:30 and 18:30 local.
failure_scenario: The user is in South Africa (UTC+2) and sets Metoprolol for 08:00 daily. The web Schedule tab shows 08:00, but the Android notification 'Take 50mg of Metoprolol' fires at 06:00 every day. A 01:00 Monday dose is reminded at 23:00 Monday, 22 hours late. In New York (UTC-4/-5), a 21:00 dose is reminded around 01:00-02:00 local.

Line numbers are off by about one. The hour/minute math is at lines 71-73, and `on: { hour, minute, weekday }` is at about line 98.

The mechanism and failure scenario are accurate as described. The claim that the unit test "enshrines" the bug is slightly overstated: the test only covers a case where UTC and local time are the same, so it can't catch the bug, rather than asserting the wrong behaviour.

title: Native reminders fire for BOTH the maintenance and titration phase: two conflicting doses announced at once
description: The web daily schedule picks one active phase per prescription and lets a titration phase (with a titrationPlanId) override maintenance. activateTitrationPlan() sets the titration phases to 'active' but does not complete the existing maintenance phase, so both are active. The native scheduler schedules every enabled schedule of every active phase with no per-prescription selection.

dose-schedule-service.ts: `} else if (phase.type === "titration" && phase.titrationPlanId) { // Titration overrides maintenance phaseByPrescription.set(...)`. local-notifications.ts only filters `p.status === "active" && p.deletedAt === null`. Scratch test with an active maintenance phase (50mg) and an active titration phase (25mg) at the same time produced two notifications: 'Take 50mg of Metoprolol' and 'Take 25mg of Metoprolol'.
---

failure_scenario: The user is on 50mg maintenance and activates a titration plan stepping down to 25mg. The web Today view shows only the 25mg titration dose. The Android phone shows two reminders, 'Take 50mg' and 'Take 25mg', at the same time, which invites a double dose or the wrong one.

- `activateTitrationPlan` activates every pending phase of the plan at once. A plan with several steps therefore gets several active titration phases, and native would announce every step's dose, not just two.
- `getDailyDoseSchedule` only keeps the first titration phase it sees. The web side is also shaky with multi-step plans, so a shared helper built from it would carry that behaviour over.

Small correction: in the web-push path (medication-notification-service), a same-time conflict is deduped by the time + prescription key. It produces a single reminder that can be the wrong (maintenance) dose, not two reminders. The finding's line references are slightly off. 1. Maintenance and titration being active together is intended behaviour, not an omission in activateTitrationPlan. completeTitrationPlan relies on the maintenance phase still being there. The real bug is that the notification schedulers lack the titration-first selection that getDailyDoseSchedule has, so the fix should go in the schedulers rather than in completing maintenance on activation.

title: After the first firing, repeat reminders use non-wakeup RTC alarms and can be deferred indefinitely while the phone sleeps
description: The app schedules with isExactNotification:false and allowWhileIdle:true, so the first alarm uses setAndAllowWhileIdle(RTC_WAKEUP). When it fires, the plugin reschedules the next weekly occurrence itself with `alarmManager.set(AlarmManager.RTC, ...)`. That is a non-wakeup alarm with no allow-while-idle. Since reminders are rebuilt only on cold start (see above), every occurrence after the first week of a long-lived process gets delivered only when something else wakes the device.
evidence: TimedNotificationPublisher.kt:64-71: `val wantsExact = storedNotification?.getBoolean("isExactNotification", true) ?: true ... if (wantsExact && canExact) { setExact(RTC, ...) } else { ... alarmManager.set(AlarmManager.RTC, trigger, pendingIntent) }`.
failure_scenario: A Monday 08:00 reminder fires correctly the first Monday after install. The following Monday the phone is idle on the nightstand in Doze, so the RTC alarm is not delivered until the user picks up the phone, possibly hours later, and the dose is missed or late.
suggested_fix: Schedule concrete one-shot `at` notifications for the next N days on every resync, using setAndAllowWhileIdle each time, instead of perpetual `on` schedules. Alternatively request SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM/USE_EXACT_ALARM properly (a medication reminder qualifies) and use exact alarms.
verifier_corrections:
The finding says reminders are rebuilt only on cold start. That is too narrow: syncMedicationNotifications also runs after medication mutations (apps/web/src/hooks/use-medication-queries.ts:186), not just from initLocalNotifications in providers.tsx:63. Either path puts the reminder back on a setAndAllowWhileIdle(RTC_WAKEUP) alarm. So the problem only hits occurrences where neither a cold start nor a medication edit happened since that reminder last fired. This softens the impact but does not remove it.

The claim of delay "possibly hours" / "indefinitely" is also overstated. Doze maintenance windows and any screen wake deliver pending RTC alarms, so it means late delivery, not delivery that never happens.

The "after the first week of a long-lived process" wording is misleading. Rescheduling happens in the BroadcastReceiver whether or not the app process is running. The accurate statement is that every firing after the most recent resync is non-wakeup.

Medium severity stands: it means late medication reminders, not wrong dosing data.

"Deferred indefinitely" and "until the user picks up the phone" overstate it. A non-wakeup RTC alarm is delivered the next time the device wakes for any reason, such as another app's wakeup alarm, an FCM message, or a Doze maintenance window. That can be minutes or hours later, not never. The impact is also narrower than "every occurrence after the first week of a long-lived process". Each notification id covers one weekday, so its next occurrence is 7 days away, and any app launch or WebView page load in between cancels it and restores a RTC_WAKEUP alarm. Only occurrences that come after a fired reminder with no app open in between (a full week or more without opening the app) are affected. Also, the "(see above)" cold-start remark is really about reloads: init runs on every page load, not only a process cold start.

title: useAuth on native wipes the session token on any non-2xx validate reply (including an upstream Neon Auth outage) and never retries after an offline start, so sync silently stops
description: On native there is no cookie session, so `authenticated` depends on each useAuth() instance calling /api/auth/validate (15 call sites, and each keeps its own state and validated ref). If the reply is not ok, the token is permanently cleared. validateBearerToken() returns null on any upstream error or its 5s timeout, which withAuth turns into 401, and a 500 or 429 also counts as not ok. If the fetch throws (offline), the catch swallows it, validated.current stays true, and that instance stays unauthenticated for the whole session with no retry when the network returns. SyncLifecycleMount relies on this flag to start the sync engine.
evidence: auth-guard.tsx: `validated.current = true; ... .then((res) => (res.ok ? res.json() : null)).then((data) => { if (data?.user) {...} else { clearAuthToken(); } }).catch(() => {})`. auth-middleware.ts: `if (!res.ok) return null; ... } catch { return null; }`, then `{ error: "Invalid or expired token" }, { status: 401 }`.
failure_scenario: (a) The user opens the Android app on a plane. Every useAuth instance fails, sync never starts, and writes queue locally. After landing, sync still does not start until the app is killed and relaunched. (b) Neon Auth has a brief outage, or get-session takes more than 5s. /api/auth/validate returns 401, the app deletes the token, and the user is silently signed out, with sync stopped until they redo Google sign-in.
suggested_fix: Clear the token only on an explicit 401 with requiresAuth or a 403, not on 5xx, 429 or network errors. Distinguish upstream failure (return 503) from an invalid token in validateBearerToken. Move validation into a single shared store (Zustand or a React Query query) that retries when the network comes back online.
verifier_corrections: These are minor points; the core claim stands. I counted about 27 matches for useAuth()/saveAuthToken combined rather than checking the exact "15 call sites", so treat that number as approximate. It doesn't change the finding. In scenario (a), an instance that mounts later (on navigation, after the network is back) would make its own fresh validation call, so only the instances that mounted while offline stay unauthenticated. SyncLifecycleMount mounts once at the root, so sync still does not start until relaunch, as claimed. A 403 from the whitelist check also clears the token; that part is arguably correct behaviour.

Minor corrections only:
- I count 13 non-test files that call useAuth(), not 15 call sites. The count of instances doesn't change the conclusion.
- Components that remount do get a new ref and validate again, so some UI instances may recover after navigation. The root-mounted SyncLifecycleMount does not remount, so sync stays off until the app is relaunched.
- A missing NEON_AUTH_URL on the server also produces the 401 that wipes the token.

The finding counts 15 `useAuth` call sites; there are about 16. The 429 case is speculative: the validate route never returns 429 itself, and `validateBearerToken` maps any upstream non-ok reply to 401 anyway. The real triggers are an upstream error, a timeout over 5s, or a platform 5xx. Nothing is lost: records stay in Dexie and the sync queue is kept, so the impact is delayed sync or a forced re-sign-in, not data loss. That fits medium better than high.

title: Nutrient analysis uses a raw relative fetch(): always fails in the Android static-export app
description: Every other API call goes through apiFetch(), which prefixes NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL and adds the Bearer token in Capacitor mode. NutrientAnalysisCard calls `fetch("/api/ai/nutrient-analysis")` directly. In the Android build the WebView origin is https://localhost, and cap-build.js stashes src/app/api out of the export, so the request hits the local asset server (no such route) without auth.
evidence:
nutrient-analysis-card.tsx:256 `const res = await fetch("/api/ai/nutrient-analysis", { method: "POST", ... })`. cap-build.js: `Stash the server-only api/ routes + middleware OUTSIDE apps/web during the static export`.
---
[ai-routes-models#3] nutrient-analysis-card.tsx:256 `const res = await fetch("/api/ai/nutrient-analysis", {`; capacitor.config: "Deliberately NOT `server.url`"; android-release.yml: `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL: https://intake-tracker.ryanjnoble.dev`
failure_scenario: On Android the user opens Analytics > Summary and taps Analyze. The request goes to https://localhost/api/ai/nutrient-analysis and gets a 404 (or an HTML fallback that fails res.json()). The user sees 'Couldn't analyze your food log', while the same button works on web.
suggested_fix: Replace the call with apiFetch (or useAiFetch). Add a lint rule or unit test that forbids a bare `fetch("/api/` outside api-fetch.ts (the native-auth bridge page, which runs on the real origin, is the exception).
verifier_corrections: Severity is overstated: this is an optional AI analysis feature with no data-integrity or dosing impact, so medium fits better than high. It is unconfirmed whether the failure shows up as a 404 or as a static HTML fallback that then fails the json parse. Either way the user gets the same error toast.

I lowered severity from high to medium. The broken feature is an optional AI nutrient analysis card, and it fails only in the Android build. It is not core tracking, it causes no data loss or corruption, and it shows no wrong data: the user gets an explicit error toast. Everything else in the finding checks out.
