This is a minor imprecision. The finding says the response is "a 404 (or an HTML fallback)". Capacitor's WebViewLocalServer may serve index.html with a 200 for an unknown path. In that case the request fails on JSON parsing instead of the `!res.ok` branch. The user still sees a failure either way.

title: Sign-out on Android leaves reminders scheduled and the local health DB intact, and does not revoke the server session
description: handleSignOut stops the sync engine and calls signOut(), which clears the local Bearer token and calls the Neon client's signOut. On native the auth client has no cookie and no bearer, so the server session behind the token is not revoked. Nothing cancels the LocalNotifications or clears Dexie or the sync cursors. The next account to sign in on the device inherits the previous user's local records and reminders.
evidence: sign-out.ts: `stopEngine(); detachLifecycleListeners(); ... await Promise.race([signOut(), ...]); window.location.href = "/auth";` with no LocalNotifications.cancel and no db clear. auth-client.ts: `clearAuthToken(); return _signOut(...args);`.
failure_scenario: The user signs out of the Android app, for example to hand the phone on. 'Time for Metoprolol, take 50mg' notifications keep appearing on the lock screen. If another account signs in, the previous user's medication rows are still in Dexie and can be pushed into the new account.
suggested_fix: On sign-out: call LocalNotifications.cancel on all pending notifications, and wipe or quarantine Dexie and _syncMeta (after a confirm prompt if there are unpushed ops). On native, send the Bearer token to the sign-out endpoint so the server session is revoked.
verifier_corrections:
These parts are literally true: sign-out does not cancel notifications or clear Dexie or the sync cursors, and on native the server session is not revoked because the Bearer token is cleared before the Neon signOut call, which never sends it anyway.

Corrections:
- Only the notification and session-revocation parts are Android-specific. Dexie is kept on web too, and that looks like an intentional local-first design choice (see the account-service.ts comment about keeping local data in local-only mode).
- Cross-account contamination needs a second whitelisted email (ALLOWED_EMAILS) on the same device, which is an edge case for this single-user app.
- The unrevoked session is only a latent risk, because the token no longer exists on the device.
- Severity should be low, not medium. It is not critical data integrity in normal use.

Keeping Dexie data and local reminders after sign-out matches the local-first, single-user design; deleteAccount explicitly keeps the local copy. It is not an accidental data leak. The cross-account push only needs a second whitelisted email, and only ops still pending in `_syncQueue` would go to the new account, not all local rows. The finding missed that stale `_syncMeta` pull cursors would make the new user's pull skip older rows. The server-session revoke gap on native is plausible, since no Bearer header is attached to the Neon client's signOut call. It has low impact because the token is wiped locally. Severity should be low, not medium.

title: allowBackup=false together with the default storageMode 'local' means an Android reinstall or phone change loses all un-synced health data
description: The manifest disables Auto Backup on the premise that 'the data syncs to Neon Postgres (the device is not the system of record)'. But storageMode defaults to 'local', and auto-detection only switches to cloud-sync when the server already has data. A user who installs the APK and starts logging without enabling cloud sync has Dexie as the only copy, with no OS backup.
evidence: AndroidManifest.xml comment: `No user data is lost: the data syncs to Neon Postgres (the device is not the system of record)`. settings-store.ts:216 `storageMode: "local" as const`.
failure_scenario: A new Android user logs months of intake and doses without turning on cloud sync, then gets a new phone or reinstalls the APK (e.g. after an Obtainium signature change). Everything is gone: no cloud copy and no Auto Backup.
suggested_fix: On native, default to cloud-sync after sign-in, or block local-only mode with a clear warning. Alternatively keep allowBackup=false but add an explicit export/backup prompt when storageMode is 'local'.
verifier_corrections:
Minor corrections:
- The finding doesn't mention the manual export in Settings (data-management-section.tsx), which partly mitigates the risk but only if the user remembers to use it.
- It also doesn't mention that signing out resets storageMode to "local" (account-service.ts:35).
- "A new Android user" should be read as "the allowlisted owner on a device where cloud sync was never turned on", because ALLOWED_EMAILS limits sign-in to allowlisted emails.
- The core claim is accurate.

Nothing material is wrong. Two small additions:
- A manual Export button exists in Settings (`data-management-section.tsx`), so a user can protect themselves. Nothing prompts them to, though.
- Losing data this way needs an uninstall (for example a signing-key change or a new phone). A normal APK update over the existing install keeps IndexedDB.

title: syncMedicationNotifications is not serialized: concurrent runs can leave stale notifications with old content
description: The function does getPending, then cancel, then read the DB, then schedule, with sequential IDs starting at 1 and no lock. If two runs interleave (the cold-start init plus any future resync trigger), both cancel before either schedules. If run A produced more notifications than run B, IDs above B's count survive with A's stale content. This is latent today only because the resync hooks are dead; wiring them in (the fix above) makes the race real.
evidence: `const pending = await LocalNotifications.getPending(); if (pending.notifications.length > 0) await LocalNotifications.cancel(...)` ... `let notifId = 1;` ... `await LocalNotifications.schedule({ notifications });`
failure_scenario: The app cold-starts, which runs init, and a schedule edit triggers a resync in the same moment. The first run schedules IDs 1-14, the second (after a schedule was removed) schedules 1-7, and IDs 8-14 keep reminding for the deleted schedule.
suggested_fix: Serialize with a module-level promise chain or mutex. Derive stable notification IDs from a hash of scheduleId and weekday, and cancel every pending ID not in the new set.
verifier_corrections: The failure scenario (a schedule edit during cold start triggering a resync) cannot happen at HEAD, because useAddSchedule, useUpdateSchedule and useDeleteSchedule have no callers, so syncMedicationNotifications only ever runs once, from the providers.tsx mount effect. The race is a latent risk that only matters if the resync hooks get wired up, or in dev StrictMode where the effect runs twice without a guard. It is not a current bug that users see.

title: Native network listener leaks on fast detach: duplicate push/pull triggers after an auth flip
description: On Capacitor, the listener handle is assigned asynchronously after the dynamic import. If detach runs before the import and addListener resolve (for example useSyncLifecycle cleanup when `authenticated` flips quickly), removeListener is still null. The listener is never removed, and a later attach registers another one.
evidence: `let removeListener: (() => void) | null = null; import("@capacitor/network").then(({ Network }) => { ... .then((handle) => { removeListener = () => handle.remove(); }); }); return () => { removeListener?.(); };`
failure_scenario: On Android, useAuth briefly reports authenticated, then not, then authenticated during startup validation. Each reconnect then calls schedulePush(0) and schedulePull() several times, causing redundant pull cycles and refetch storms.
suggested_fix: Track a `disposed` flag and remove the handle as soon as it resolves if dispose already ran.
verifier_corrections: The listener leak is real, but "redundant pull cycles and refetch storms" is wrong. schedulePush uses a single debounced timer, and runPullCycle has a synchronous `pullInFlight` guard, so duplicate triggers coalesce into one push and one pull. The actual residual effect is different: schedulePull has no `engineStarted` check. After sign-out, or after leaving cloud-sync mode, a leaked listener can still start a pull on reconnect. Nothing in the code backs the specific trigger in the finding, useAuth flipping authenticated/unauthenticated during Android startup. The race also needs detach to happen within the few milliseconds of the dynamic import plus addListener.

title: Web medication reminder/refill service ignores soft-deleted (tombstoned) prescriptions, phases and inventory; diverges from native path; 0% test coverage
description: deletePrescription() only tombstones rows (sets deletedAt) and leaves isActive/status/enabled untouched. The browser reminder loop (started from /medications via useMedicationNotifications) reads raw tables and filters only on isActive/status/enabled, never deletedAt. The native path (local-notifications.ts) and getSchedulesForPhase both correctly filter `deletedAt === null`, so the two reminder implementations disagree. Coverage run shows medication-notification-service.ts at 0% lines (100 lines), so nothing catches this.
evidence:
medication-notification-service.ts: `const activePrescriptions = allPrescriptions.filter(p => p.isActive === true);` / `db.medicationPhases.where("status").equals("active").toArray()` / `allPhaseSchedules.filter(s => s.enabled === true)` / `const inventories = await db.inventoryItems.where("prescriptionId")...; const activeInventory = inventories.find(i => i.isActive && !i.isArchived);`
prescription-service.ts deletePrescription: `await db.prescriptions.update(id, { deletedAt: now, updatedAt: now });` (isActive untouched)
local-notifications.ts:46: `.filter((p) => p.isActive && p.deletedAt === null)`
coverage-summary: `0   100 src/lib/medication-notification-service.ts`
failure_scenario: User deletes a prescription such as Furosemide 40mg scheduled at 09:00. Every day at 09:00–09:05 with /medications open and notification permission granted, the PWA still shows 'Time for your 09:00 medications — Lasix 40mg'. The phase, schedule and inventory rows are all tombstoned with isActive/status unchanged, so they still pass every filter. Refill alerts also keep firing for the deleted inventory. The user is prompted to take a medication they stopped.
suggested_fix: Filter `deletedAt === null` on every table read in medication-notification-service (or reuse the service-layer getters that already filter). Better still, share one query function between local-notifications.ts and the web service. Add unit tests with fake-indexeddb covering tombstoned rows.
verifier_corrections: Minor points. In checkRefillAlerts, schedules come from getSchedulesForPhase, which does filter deletedAt. For a fully deleted prescription, that set is empty, so dailyPills is 0 and daysLeft is Infinity. The refill alert then fires only through the refillAlertPills threshold, not through refillAlertDays. Also, the problem is wider than whole prescriptions: deleting a single schedule (medication-schedule-service.ts:158 only sets deletedAt) still triggers web dose reminders, because line 80 checks only `enabled`. The 0% coverage figure was not independently re-verified.

Minor corrections:
- **Refill alerts are narrower than described.** `getSchedulesForPhase` does filter `deletedAt`, so a deleted prescription's schedules are gone. That makes the daily dose 0 and days-left Infinity, so the `refillAlertDays` check never fires. Only the `refillAlertPills` stock threshold can still trigger a refill alert for deleted inventory.
- **The file:line list is off.** The inventory lookup in the dose-reminder path is at lines 109–110; line 162 is not a separate issue.
- **The example text is illustrative.** "Lasix 40mg" and the exact notification wording are made up, but the brand name really is used when an inventory row has one.

The code facts and the divergence from the native path are accurate. The severity is overstated: the web reminder only runs while /medications is open, only fires 0-5 minutes after the scheduled time, and is throttled in background tabs. Refill alerts fire at most once per prescription, so the claim that they "keep firing" is wrong. The dose-reminder fallback `?? activeInv[0]` also means a tombstoned inventory row can supply the brand name even when no active one exists. Adjusted from high to medium.

title: Flaky unit test: prescription-card PRN test races the async phases hook (failed under TZ=Europe/Berlin full run)
description: The test awaits findByText('Furosemide'), which renders at once from props, then synchronously asserts getByText('As needed'). That label only appears after usePhasesLoaded resolves (`isAsNeeded = phasesLoaded && !effectivePhase`). Before that the card shows 'No doses today'. Under full-suite load the assertion runs first. The comment on line 129 ('a scheduled med briefly shows "As needed"') is also stale now that the gate exists. CI runs the suite twice (test:tz:sa and test:tz:de), so this randomly fails CI.
evidence: TZ=Europe/Berlin npx vitest run → `FAIL src/components/medications/prescription-card.dom.test.tsx > PrescriptionCard > shows 'Log dose now' for an as-needed prescription and logs a PRN dose` / `TestingLibraryElementError: Unable to find an element with the text: As needed.` DOM snapshot shows `No doses today`. `Test Files 1 failed | 226 passed (227) Tests 1 failed | 2243 passed (2244)`. Re-running the file alone 5× (3 Berlin, 2 default): `Tests 6 passed (6)` every time.
failure_scenario: A PR that doesn't touch medications fails CI's unit-tests-de job at random. Developers learn to re-run failing CI, which hides real failures.
suggested_fix: Use `expect(await screen.findByText("As needed")).toBeInTheDocument()`, and delete the stale comment on line 129.
verifier_corrections: Severity is too high. Medium is meant for incorrect behaviour in edge cases, but this is a flaky test with no effect on users, so it should be low (it could reasonably be tracked separately as build health). The mechanism, cited lines, stale comment, and suggested fix are all accurate. The fix should also make the following `getByRole('button', {name: /log an as-needed dose/})` wait (or come after the awaited findByText), because that button has the same phasesLoaded gate.

The race exists in the test code, but I could not reproduce it: the file alone, the whole components dir under TZ=Europe/Berlin (2 runs) and a scratch probe all passed, and the full-suite run timed out. So "randomly fails CI" is unconfirmed; the failure is plausible but rare. It is a test-reliability issue, not an app logic or data defect, so severity should be low rather than medium. The suggested fix (`await screen.findByText("As needed")` and removing the stale comment at line 129) is correct.

title: @intake/ui CSS tree-shake guard never runs in CI (describe.skipIf without build)
description: The guard skips unless `.next/static` contains CSS. The CI unit-test jobs (test:tz:sa, test:tz:de, coverage) run right after `pnpm install` with no build. The build job only runs bundle-security.test.ts after `pnpm build`. The guard that is supposed to turn silent unstyled-UI regressions into a hard failure therefore always skips in CI. It passes locally only because a stale `.next` build is present.
evidence: `const hasBuild = cssFiles.length > 0; describe.skipIf(!hasBuild)("@intake/ui compiled-CSS tree-shake guard", ...` ; ci.yml build job: `- name: Bundle security scan\n run: pnpm --filter @intake/web exec vitest run src/__tests__/bundle-security.test.ts` (tree-shake test not listed); unit jobs: `- run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` → `pnpm --filter @intake/web test:tz:sa` (no build).
failure_scenario: Someone drops the `@source` line in packages/ui globals.css. CI stays green, and production ships unstyled accordions and primitives.
suggested_fix: Add `src/__tests__/ui-css-tree-shake.test.ts` to the build job's vitest invocation next to bundle-security.test.ts.
verifier_corrections: The evidence, line numbers and suggested fix are accurate. Three small corrections: (1) the coverage job's command is at ci.yml line 435, which the finding does not cite, and line 140 is only the step name (the command is on line 141); (2) "passes locally only because a stale .next build is present" should say it runs for real only when a local `.next` build exists and silently skips otherwise; (3) severity is overstated, since this is a CI gap for a styling-only regression, which is out of scope for this audit, so low rather than medium.

The facts are correct. I lowered severity from medium to low: the issue is CI coverage of a CSS/styling regression guard, not a data or logic defect, and styling is out of scope for this audit. One small point: "stale `.next` build" is a guess. It is just whatever local build exists, and it could be fresh. The suggested fix (add the test to the build job's vitest invocation) is valid.

title: e2e specs are neither type-checked nor linted; 5 latent type errors
description: The web tsconfig excludes `e2e`, and eslint only runs over `src`. Typechecking e2e/ plus playwright.config.ts under the project's strict settings (via a scratch tsconfig, since deleted) produced 5 errors. The chaos spec's clock-skew Date override is typed wrong: TS reports the `args.length === 0` branch as a no-overlap comparison, so whether that branch runs as intended is unverified.
evidence:
`"exclude": ["node_modules", ".next", "out", "e2e", "src/app/sw.ts"]`
tsc output:
`e2e/auth.setup.ts(74,45): error TS2379 ... Type 'string | undefined' is not assignable to type 'string'` (exactOptionalPropertyTypes)
`e2e/chaos.spec.ts(199,15): error TS2367: This comparison appears to be unintentional because the types '1' and '0' have no overlap.`
`e2e/chaos.spec.ts(205,16): error TS4114: This member must have an 'override' modifier`
`e2e/chaos.spec.ts(210,7): error TS2578: Unused '@ts-expect-error' directive.` (and 212)
failure_scenario: If PLAYWRIGHT base URL is unset, auth.setup passes `baseURL: undefined` with no compile-time signal. Type-level regressions in e2e helpers go unnoticed until a CI e2e run, which is expensive and depends on the Neon quota.
suggested_fix: Add an `e2e/tsconfig.json` and a `typecheck:e2e` script wired into turbo typecheck, extend eslint `files` to `e2e/**`, and fix the 5 errors.
verifier_corrections: 1) The chaos.spec clock-skew override works at runtime. TS2367 comes from `ConstructorParameters<typeof Date>` resolving to the last constructor overload (a 1-tuple), so TypeScript types `args.length` as the literal 1. At runtime `new Date()` still has `args.length === 0`, so the fakeNow branch runs as intended. The branch is not "unverified". 2) The auth.setup failure scenario is mostly unreachable. The fixture `baseURL` comes from playwright.config's `use.baseURL`, and line 48 already falls back with `baseURL ?? "http://localhost:3000"` for the origin. The TS2379 error only reflects `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` strictness on the `apiRequest.newContext({ baseURL })` call. It is not a real undefined-URL bug in practice. 3) Standalone tsc also reports extra `process`/`fs` "cannot find name" errors, but those came from my scratch config's types resolution, so the "5 errors" count is fair.

title: Service worker (sw.ts) and apps/native are outside every typecheck/lint/test gate; 4 of 6 packages have no lint script
description: sw.ts holds the push, notificationclick and SKIP_WAITING handlers. It is excluded from tsc and compiled by esbuild at request time, which does not type-check. @intake/native has no typecheck, lint or test scripts, so capacitor.config.ts is never checked. Turbo lint ran in only 2 packages (web, core). packages/db (schema.ts, sync-payload.ts, the server sync contract) and packages/ai-prompts (model IDs and prompts) are type-checked but never linted.
evidence: turbo typecheck: `Tasks: 6 successful, 6 total` for 9 packages in scope; turbo lint: `Tasks: 2 successful, 2 total`. sw.ts header: `this file is excluded from the project tsconfig`. apps/native scripts: `{ "sync": ..., "cap": "cap" }` only.
failure_scenario: A type error in the push handler, such as a wrong notification payload field, compiles fine under esbuild and breaks dose-reminder push clicks in production with no CI signal.
suggested_fix: Add a `tsconfig.sw.json` with `lib: ["webworker"]` and run it in typecheck. Add typecheck for apps/native/capacitor.config.ts, and add `lint` scripts to packages/db, ai-prompts, types and ui.
verifier_corrections: sw.ts IS linted: `eslint src` in apps/web covers src/app/sw.ts and no ignore pattern excludes it. It is only excluded from tsc. It is also bundled by esbuild at build time (force-static route, including cap-export), not just per request, so build errors are caught but type errors are not. The rest holds: apps/native has no typecheck, lint or test scripts, and packages/db, ai-prompts, types and ui have no lint script.

title: Large logic modules have 0% or near-0% unit coverage (timezone detection, account, permissions, version check, insights)
description: The coverage run passes its thresholds overall (59.58% lines), but several state and logic modules that touch user data and scheduling are essentially untested in the unit suite. mcp/queries.ts and mcp/tools.ts also show 0% in unit coverage but are exercised by the integration suite (mcp-queries.integration.test.ts, 69/69 passing), so they are excluded here.
evidence: coverage-summary (lines% / total): `8 78 src/hooks/use-push-schedule-sync.ts`, `6 49 src/hooks/use-timezone-detection.ts`, `0 29 src/lib/account-service.ts`, `0 84 src/hooks/use-permissions.ts`, `20 110 src/hooks/use-insights.ts`, `9 32 src/lib/server/insight-job-service.ts`, `0 34 src/hooks/use-version-check.ts`
failure_scenario: Regressions in push-schedule sync (server-side dose reminder times) or in timezone detection (which moves day boundaries for all totals) ship with green unit CI. The only possible catch is e2e, and those journeys are mostly uncovered per the prior e2e audit.
suggested_fix: Add fake-indexeddb and hook tests for use-push-schedule-sync and use-timezone-detection first, since they affect dosing reminders and day bucketing. Then add per-file coverage floors for them.
verifier_corrections: The finding says timezone detection is "essentially untested". More precisely, it has a 194-line test file (src/hooks/use-timezone-detection.test.ts), but that file copies the hook's detection logic instead of importing the hook. So the tests can pass while the real hook is broken, which is a more specific problem than having no test. The evidence rounds use-push-schedule-sync to 8%; the actual figure is 7.69%. This is a coverage gap, not a demonstrated defect, so the severity should stay low.

title: Lint baseline: 6 warnings (3 a11y click-without-keyboard on medication/history rows, 3 hard window.location navigations)
description: Lint passes with 0 errors and 6 warnings. The a11y warnings mean dose rows and history record rows respond only to mouse or touch clicks, not to keyboard. On a mobile PWA this is mainly an assistive-tech problem, but it is an input-behaviour inconsistency: the same action works by tap and not by keyboard.
evidence: `dose-row.tsx 70:7 warning Visible, non-interactive elements with click handlers must have at least one keyboard listener jsx-a11y/click-events-have-key-events` (same at compound-card-expanded.tsx 71:5, record-row.tsx 125:7); `error-boundary.tsx 55:5 / 72:5, sign-out.ts 21:3 warning Do not use window.location.href ... @next/next/no-location-assign-relative-destination`; `✖ 6 problems (0 errors, 6 warnings)`
failure_scenario: Users on a keyboard or switch access can't open a dose row to mark it taken or skipped, or open a history record to edit it.
suggested_fix: Make the rows `<button>` elements, or add role=button, tabIndex and onKeyDown. Consider `--max-warnings 0` so warnings can't pile up.
verifier_corrections: The keyboard failure scenario is mostly wrong. History records can already be edited by keyboard (record-row.tsx:101-111 has role=button, tabIndex and an onKeyDown for Enter and Space). The warning at line 125 is only a stopPropagation wrapper around real Buttons. compound-card-expanded.tsx:71 is also just a stopPropagation container with no action. In dose-row.tsx the Take and Skip controls are real Buttons. Only the detail-open click on taken, skipped or future dose rows is missing an onKeyDown, even though that row has role=button and tabIndex=0. The window.location.href uses are intentional full reloads (error recovery, sign-out), not defects. The real finding is one minor a11y gap in dose-row.tsx:70-81 plus a correct lint count.

title: Vitest config emits deprecation warnings; the `esbuild.jsx` setting is silently ignored
description: Every vitest run warns that both esbuild and oxc options are set, so the esbuild `{ jsx: 'automatic' }` option the config comments rely on is ignored. It also warns that vite-tsconfig-paths is superseded by native `resolve.tsconfigPaths`, and that the config is ESM loaded as CJS. Tests pass today, but the documented JSX setting is dead config and will break on the next Vite major.
evidence: `Both esbuild and oxc options were set. oxc options will be used and esbuild options will be ignored. The following esbuild options were set: { jsx: 'automatic' }` / `The plugin "vite-tsconfig-paths" is detected. Vite now supports tsconfig paths resolution natively` / `ESM syntax in a file loaded as CommonJS (vitest.config.ts:1:1)`
failure_scenario: A future Vite or Vitest major makes `configLoader: 'native'` the default, and the whole unit suite fails to load.
suggested_fix: Replace `esbuild: { jsx: "automatic" }` with the oxc equivalent, switch to `resolve.tsconfigPaths: true`, and rename the file to vitest.config.mts or set type:module.
verifier_corrections: The ignored esbuild option does no current harm: oxc already uses the automatic JSX runtime by default, so JSX transforms behave the same with or without it. The "will break on the next Vite major" failure scenario is a guess, not something shown. The ESM-as-CJS warning comes from the package having no "type": "module" (the finding says this correctly). The config comment at line 16 is about tsconfig paths. The JSX comment is at lines 23-24. There is no user-visible failure and the issue is outside the data/logic audit scope, so this should stay low or be dropped as informational.

title: deletePrescription hard-deletes dose logs and inventory transactions locally without syncing them. Server and device histories diverge (81 orphan dose logs live on the server)
description: Inside the delete transaction, `db.doseLogs.where("prescriptionId").equals(id).delete()` and `db.inventoryTransactions.where("inventoryItemId").equals(item.id).delete()` physically remove rows and never call enqueueInsideTx. The server keeps those rows with deletedAt=NULL for good. The device has lost the history while the server and MCP still show it, and a fresh install or full pull brings back dose logs for a prescription that no longer exists.
evidence:
prescription-service.ts:146 `await db.doseLogs.where("prescriptionId").equals(id).delete();` and :150 `await db.inventoryTransactions.where("inventoryItemId").equals(item.id).delete();`. Scratch test sync queue after delete: [[inventoryItems,delete],[phaseSchedules,delete],[medicationPhases,delete],[prescriptions,delete],[auditLogs,upsert]], with no doseLogs or inventoryTransactions ops, while the local doseLogs and inventoryTransactions counts dropped to 0. LIVE: 81 non-deleted server dose logs point at the soft-deleted prescription b194a930.
---
[prescriptions-model#8] prescription-service.ts:146 `await db.doseLogs.where("prescriptionId").equals(id).delete();` and :150 `await db.inventoryTransactions.where("inventoryItemId").equals(item.id).delete();` (no enqueueInsideTx for either).
---
[doses-titration-schedule#18] `await db.doseLogs.where("prescriptionId").equals(id).delete();` and `await db.inventoryTransactions.where("inventoryItemId").equals(item.id).delete();` with no enqueue.
---
[mcp-server-auth#4] prescription-service.ts:146: `await db.doseLogs.where("prescriptionId").equals(id).delete();` and :150 `await db.inventoryTransactions.where("inventoryItemId").equals(item.id).delete();`. No enqueue for either, while phases/schedules/items get `enqueueInsideTx(..., "delete")`.
failure_scenario: The user deletes a prescription on the phone. The phone's adherence and history views lose all past doses for it, but the MCP/AI and any newly installed device (e.g. the Android APK) still see them. Adherence and inventory numbers now differ between surfaces for the same account.
suggested_fix: Soft-delete instead: set deletedAt on each dose log and inventory transaction and enqueue a 'delete' op for each, or keep them as history and just hide them. Never physically delete synced rows.
verifier_corrections: Keeping the server copy is arguably the intended behaviour: the MCP code comments say historic doses for archived prescriptions should still resolve their name. The actual defect is the local hard delete that is never synced, which makes the device disagree with the server. The server rows are not wrong in themselves. The fix should keep the history, either by leaving the rows in place or by soft-deleting them and enqueuing the change, and not by purging the server. The line references are accurate.

Small clarification: the rows only come back on a device that does a full or fresh pull (new install or cursor reset). An existing device whose cursor has already passed them will not get them back. The live count of 81 was not re-verified in this pass.

The failure scenario gets the direction wrong. The phone losing the dose history is intended: the confirm dialog promises "Permanently delete ... and all its history". The bug is that the server, MCP (`getTodaySummary` dose counts and `listRecentDoses`) and fresh installs still keep and show history the user explicitly deleted. The suggested "soft-delete and keep as history" fix also contradicts that dialog. Either enqueue deletes for the dose logs and transactions, or change the dialog wording and stop the local hard delete. The "81 orphan server dose logs" figure is taken from the finding's live evidence; I did not re-check it. Severity goes down to medium because this is a rare user action and the harm is an inconsistency, not data loss.

title: Replacement Entresto inventory reads -7 because a new prescription gets no initial-stock transaction when stock is entered as 0, and consumption went to the zombie item
description: addPrescription only writes an initial 'refill' transaction when `input.currentStock > 0`. For the replacement Entresto (bddbea47) the stock was never initialised, and its 8 logged doses drove it negative, while the doses logged against the deleted b194a930 decremented that tombstoned item. The authoritative stock (sum of transactions) is therefore wrong for a med the user physically has.
evidence: get_inventory_status: `"brandName": "Entresto", "stock": -7, "strength": 200, "refillAlertDays": 7`. prescription-service.ts:98 `if (input.currentStock > 0) { const tx = buildTransaction(... "refill" ...` . Only 8 dose logs exist for bddbea47.
failure_scenario: The refill alert for Entresto (refillAlertDays 7) is permanently triggered, and the days-of-supply maths for a heart-failure drug is meaningless. A real low-stock warning cannot be told apart from this noise.
suggested_fix: When adding a replacement prescription, prompt for current stock (or offer to transfer stock from the prescription being replaced). Block or warn on a second active prescription with the same generic name.
verifier_corrections:
The root cause is wrong. The `input.currentStock > 0` guard at prescription-service.ts:97 does not cause the negative stock: a zero-amount initial transaction would give the same sum. The negative value comes from (a) the user never entering a starting stock or a refill for the replacement Entresto, and (b) negative stock being allowed on purpose (dose-log-service.ts comment). A refill UI exists (inventory-item-view-drawer.tsx), so the state can be fixed by hand. The real, smaller issue is the missing workflow when replacing a prescription:
- A blank stock field silently becomes 0 (add-medication-wizard.tsx:308/329 `parseInt(...) || 0`).
- There is no option to transfer stock from the old prescription.
- There is no warning about a duplicate active prescription with the same generic name.

The -7 does not match the stated 8 dose logs exactly. Severity should be low, not medium.

The `input.currentStock > 0` guard is correct behaviour: 0 stock needs no transaction and sums to 0. It is not the root cause. With 8 doses the result is -7, not -8, so the item was initialised with non-zero stock (or has a fractional or refill entry). The item was not left 'never initialised'. There is no evidence that doses against the archived b194a930 decremented a tombstoned inventory item. The real live-data issue is that each dose Aug 10-25 was logged against both the archived and the replacement Sacubitril/Valsartan prescription (a zombie-prescription issue covered elsewhere). The replacement flow also has no stock-transfer or duplicate-generic warning. Severity should be low (UX/design gap plus a user-data artifact), not a medium code bug.

title: No deterministic duplicate-prescription guard: two active Sacubitril/Valsartan prescriptions coexisted and were both dosed
description: The only check when adding a new prescription is an AI interaction call ('conflict' mode). It is skipped entirely when signed out (showAi false) and only blocks on AVOID/CAUTION severities. Nothing compares genericName (case-insensitively) against existing active prescriptions.
evidence: add-medication-wizard.tsx:235 `if (showAi && conflictCheckState === "idle" && formState.selectedPrescriptionId === "new") { const activeMeds = existingPrescriptions.filter((p) => p.isActive); ...checkInteractions(...)`. LIVE: 'Sacubitril/valsartan' (b194a930) and 'Sacubitril/Valsartan' (bddbea47) both have dose logs on 5 dates in August.
failure_scenario: The user adds 'Sacubitril/Valsartan' while 'Sacubitril/valsartan' already exists. Both show up in the schedule and 'take all' logs a double dose.
suggested_fix: Before saving, do a normalised (case, whitespace, compound order) genericName match against active, non-deleted prescriptions, and offer to add a phase to the existing one instead.
verifier_corrections: The duplicate is historical. At HEAD's live data, only bddbea47 "Sacubitril/Valsartan" is active and b194a930 is no longer active, so the two are not currently both scheduled. The failure scenario should be read as something that can happen again, not as an ongoing double dose. A minor point: even when signed in, the AI check does not guard against duplicates. It is an interaction check, and it is skipped when the AI call fails or returns nothing.

The finding leaves out that the search step (search-step.tsx:56-65) has a manual dropdown for picking an existing prescription, which avoids the duplicate if the user uses it. The real defect is that nothing automatically matches or warns on a same-name entry. The AI check is also skipped whenever the AI call errors (caught, then save proceeds), not only when signed out. I did not independently verify the live-data evidence (the two prescription IDs with overlapping dose logs).

title: Medication adherence data is too sparse to be meaningful: 46 of 172 days, no skipped/missed records, dose logging absent since 2026-08-25
description: All 414 dose logs are 'taken'. Nothing is ever 'skipped', and missed doses are never persisted, only derived at render time. Logs exist for 46 dates between 2026-04-06 and 2026-08-25, with an unbroken 79-day gap (05-23 to 08-09) and nothing in the last 31 days, even though water, BP and urination were logged daily over the same periods. Many logs are backfills (10 rows share one actionTimestamp, e.g. 1777960800000). adherenceRate also rebuilds history from the current schedules via getDailyDoseSchedule for every past date, so it counts zombie and replacement prescriptions against days they didn't apply to.
evidence: list_recent_doses(500) returned 414 rows. Status counter: {'taken': 414}. Last scheduledDate is '2026-08-25'. Dates missing: 2026-05-23..2026-08-09. analytics-service.ts:285 `const scheduleMap = await getDoseScheduleForDateRange(startDate, endDate);`
failure_scenario: The PDF export and AI insights report adherence of roughly 20-30%, and correlate BP with 'missed' meds that were probably taken. A clinician reading the export would be misled.
suggested_fix: Persist historical schedule versions (phase start/end) and compute adherence only over phases active on each date. Show 'unlogged' as distinct from 'missed'. Consider a daily 'confirm yesterday's doses' prompt so gaps are explicit.
verifier_corrections:
1. It is not true that replacement prescriptions are counted against days they didn't apply to. getDailyDoseSchedule skips any date before the prescription's createdAt (`if (createdDate && dateStr < createdDate) continue;`), so a newer prescription is not charged for days before it existed. Deactivated or "zombie" prescriptions are also excluded, because only isActive === true prescriptions are used. The real distortion runs the other way:
   - Past days are judged against the current phases and schedules, so taken logs recorded under a different phaseId/scheduleId stop matching.
   - Retired prescriptions and their taken logs disappear from the calculation.
2. The "roughly 20-30% adherence" figure was never computed. It is speculation.
3. Nothing checked here supports the claim that AI insights correlate BP with missed meds.
4. The sparse logging (the 79-day gap and nothing since 08-25) is user behaviour seen in the live data, not a code defect by itself. The code defect is that unlogged days are shown as "missed" and that history is rebuilt from the current regimen. Medium severity is appropriate.

- The headline blames the user's logging habits: 46 of 172 days, no skips, nothing since 08-25. That is user behaviour, not a code bug, and the app does support skipping.
- The defect that can be traced in code is narrower: `getDailyDoseSchedule` (dose-schedule-service.ts:104-133) uses today's active prescriptions and phases, with no phase start/end check, and `deriveStatus` (lines 74-76) marks every unlogged past slot "missed". So `adherenceRate` counts replaced or ended phases wrongly. Taken logs that point to an old phaseId, or to an archived prescription, drop out of the count.
- The "about 20-30% adherence" figure was estimated, not measured.
- I only re-verified the data claims I could see in a 30-row sample (latest date 2026-08-25, all "taken", shared backfill timestamps). The 414-row count and the 79-day gap were not re-checked.

title: The 'salt' intake type stores sodium mg, but the MCP labels it salt_mg / 'salt'; pre-2026-03-29 manual rows were entered under a 'Salt' label with no migration
description: Since commit 5467bd46 (2026-03-29), everything written under type 'salt' is sodium mg: table salt is multiplied by 0.39 and the voice prompt converts salt g x 400. The MCP still reports `salt_mg` and describes the totals as 'water/salt/sugar/potassium', so an AI consumer treats 1,400 mg sodium as 1.4 g salt (about 0.55 g sodium), a 2.5x under-read. The 109 manual 'salt' rows before the rename were entered under a 'Salt' label and were never converted or marked, so historical sodium mixes two units.
evidence:
queries.ts:137 `salt_mg: 0,` / :143 `else if (row.type === "salt") intakeTotals.salt_mg = ...`. LIVE: get_today_summary `"salt_mg": 1400`. Salt sources after 2026-03-29 are 833 'manual:sodium' and 20 'manual:salt' (already converted, e.g. 312=800*0.39); before that, 109 plain 'manual' plus 74 'voice'.
---
[mcp-server-auth#9] queries.ts: `intakeTotals = { water_ml: 0, salt_mg: 0, ... }`; tools.ts: "Totals for water/salt/sugar/potassium intake". food-salt-card.tsx:71: `Sodium`.
failure_scenario: The owner asks Claude via MCP 'how much salt today?' and is told 1.4 g, well under limits, when it was actually about 3.5 g of salt equivalent.
suggested_fix: Rename the MCP field to sodium_mg and update the tool descriptions. Consider renaming the IntakeType to 'sodium' via a migration, and tag the pre-rename rows with a unit marker.
verifier_corrections: The claim that pre-2026-03-29 'salt' rows are in a different unit (salt rather than sodium) is not supported. Before the rename the UI already enforced a "max 1500mg/day" limit, which is a sodium-scale number, and commit 5467bd46 only changed labels for existing data. There is no evidence the old rows need converting. The confirmed defect is limited to the MCP API naming: `salt_mg` in apps/web/src/lib/mcp/queries.ts:137/143 and the "water/salt/sugar/potassium" descriptions in apps/web/src/lib/mcp/tools.ts:131 and :145. These describe sodium mg as salt, so an AI consumer can under-read salt intake about 2.5x.

The claim that "historical sodium mixes two units" is overstated. Before 2026-03-29 the stored 'salt' value was already defined as sodium mg: the AI prompt said so and the 1500 mg limit is a sodium limit. The rename commit only relabeled the UI and added conversion presets. Only the unit the user had in mind when hand-typing pre-rename rows is unknown, and it can't be verified. The part that holds is the MCP surface (salt_mg field, the "salt" wording in tool descriptions and the type enum, and no mention of sodium anywhere). That is a confirmed mislabel that could lead an AI consumer to under-read sodium about 2.5x. The fix should target the MCP field name and tool descriptions. A data migration for old rows is not justified by the evidence.

title: Urination quick-log buttons double-fire and act as instant-commit, not a selector (27 near-duplicate pairs, 5 rows in 3.5 s)
description: The re-entry guard is React state (`disabled={submittingAmount !== null}`), which doesn't disable the button until the next render, so two taps in the same frame both call addMutation. Each Small/Medium/Large button also commits immediately, with no undo, so users who treat the three as a size picker create one row per tap.
evidence: urination-card.tsx:77 `setSubmittingAmount(amountValue); try { await addMutation.mutateAsync(...)`. LIVE: 2026-04-16 23:31:06.934 and .989 both 'small'. 2026-06-19 08:55:39.123 and .173 both 'large'. 2026-08-17 20:46:40.703 and .807. 2026-06-22 00:45:56-59 has 5 rows (small, medium, large, medium, small) within 3.5 s.
failure_scenario: Fluid-balance analytics (intake vs estimated output) over-counts urination output, which matters for a heart-failure/diuretic patient, and the day count shows 12 voids on 2026-07-31.
suggested_fix: Use a ref-based in-flight guard, debounce identical taps within about 2 s, and show an undo toast. Or make the size a selection followed by a single 'Log' action.
verifier_corrections:
1. The 2026-08-17 pair (1786992400703 and .807) is wrong evidence. Both rows have note 'voice', so they came from the voice/AI logging path and not the quick-log buttons, which never set a note. That is a separate duplicate path and should not be counted here.

2. The explanation is imprecise. React 18 flushes state updates from click events before the next event is handled, so a 'same frame' race is not guaranteed. The more likely causes are a touch ghost click, or two events dispatched before the disabled attribute was committed. Either way the duplicates exist and a ref-based guard is still the right fix.

3. I did not verify the '27 near-duplicate pairs' total or the '12 voids on 2026-07-31' claim.

The finding blames React state not disabling the button "until the next render". That is inaccurate. In React 18+, click is a discrete event and its state updates are applied synchronously, so the button is already disabled before the next native tap arrives. The real gap is that addMutation is a local Dexie insert that finishes in a few milliseconds. The `finally` then resets submittingAmount to null and re-enables the buttons before a second tap 50 ms later. So a ref-based guard alone would not fix this. What would fix it is a debounce or minimum lockout, an undo toast, or a select-then-confirm flow. I did not verify the "12 voids on 2026-07-31" or the "27 near-duplicate pairs" figures, but the June samples I did check support the claim.

title: Timestamps can be saved in the future: the datetime-local max is advisory only (a live urination row is dated 8 h ahead)
description: The details form and every edit dialog parse the datetime-local value and save it with no `timestamp <= Date.now()` check. The `max={getCurrentDateTimeLocal()}` attribute is not enforced when the user types or when the value is set programmatically, and it is computed once at render.
evidence:
use-edit-record.ts:93 `newTimestamp = dateTimeLocalToTimestamp(editTimestamp);` then goes straight to buildUpdates/mutate. LIVE: urination 11788f47-... timestamp 1790372940000 = 2026-09-25 23:49:00 local, while now = 1790350391041 (15:33).
---
[health-records-inputs#9] weight-card handleSubmit: `const timestamp = showTimeInput ? dateTimeLocalToTimestamp(customTime) : undefined;` (no bound check); EditEstimateEntryDialog datetime-local has no max prop.
failure_scenario: The user meant 'yesterday 23:49' but only edited the time. The record lands tonight, the card header shows it as the latest urination, and today's counts and fluid-balance include an event that hasn't happened.
suggested_fix: Validate on submit in handleEditSubmit and the add forms: reject or clamp timestamps above Date.now() + small skew, and offer 'did you mean yesterday?' when the time is later than now.
verifier_corrections: Two small corrections. First, the edit dialogs are worse than "the max is advisory": edit-estimate-entry-dialog, edit-weight-dialog and recent-entries-list have no max attribute at all. Second, in urination-card the details form is submitted by a Button onClick handler, not a form submit, so the browser never checks the max even as a constraint. The live-row evidence was not independently confirmed, but the code evidence is enough on its own.

Minor:
- The `max` attribute is not just "advisory": the edit dialogs and recent-entries-list don't have one at all. Where it does exist, the urination details form never checks it because submission is a button click handler, not a native form submit.
- The cited use-edit-record line is 95, not 93.
- The live-data evidence (row 11788f47) was not independently verified. The code-level defect stands without it.

title: Beverage tab (and legacy juice/coffee sources) log alcoholic and caffeinated drinks as plain water with no substance record
description: The Beverage tab only writes a water row (plus optional sugar), whatever name is typed. 'Beer', 'IPA' or 'Moscow mule' typed there creates no alcohol record, whereas the same drink entered through the Preset tab or voice creates an alcohol SubstanceRecord. Older 'juice:' and 'coffee:' sources behaved the same way, and nothing backfilled them.
evidence: beverage-tab.tsx:66 ``const source = beverageName.trim() ? `beverage:${beverageName.trim()}` : "beverage";`` then `waterIntake.addRecord(amount, source, ...)`. LIVE: 98 beer/wine/cocktail water rows (juice:Beer x32, juice:IPA..., juice:Moscow mule x4, juice:Wine x2), of which only 1 has an alcohol substance within 2 min. All 71 'coffee:moka'/'coffee:double-espresso' rows have 0 caffeine records.
failure_scenario: Alcohol and caffeine analytics for February to April miss dozens of drinks, and a beer logged today via the Beverage tab never counts toward alcohol totals.
suggested_fix: Route named beverages through the drink-service with a substance lookup, or warn when the name matches an alcohol/caffeine keyword. Write a one-off backfill converting legacy juice:/coffee: alcohol and caffeine rows into substance records.
verifier_corrections: The Beverage tab is not the equivalent path to the Preset/voice flows. The same card has dedicated Coffee and Alcohol tabs (liquids-card.tsx:320-338), and those create substance records. Typing "Beer" in the generic Beverage tab is choosing the wrong input, not an inconsistency between equivalent inputs. The legacy juice:/coffee: rows date from before the substance service existed (commit 028dff6f), so they were never "dropped". Backfilling them would be an optional enhancement. Severity should be low (a UX guard and optional backfill), not medium.

The current Beverage tab isn't a divergence between equivalent inputs. It is by design a tab for drinks without caffeine or alcohol, and substance drinks have their own Coffee and Alcohol tabs. The better-supported defect is historical: the v12 migration (apps/web/src/lib/db.ts:302-350) matched substance keywords only against `note` and never against `source`, so legacy `juice:<alcohol>` and `coffee:<x>` rows without a note never got substance records. The live row counts are unverified. Severity should be low (missing analytics data; the water volume itself is correct).

title: Caffeine for the same drink varies 2-4x depending on entry path (moka: 67 mg/100 ml via voice vs 130-157 via preset vs 38 legacy)
description: The preset path uses stored per-100 ml values (AI substance-lookup, 130-157 mg/100 ml for moka). The voice path asks the model for an absolute caffeineMg anchored on a 'drip coffee 250ml ~95mg' example, which gives about 67 mg/100 ml for the same moka. Nothing reconciles the two, so equivalent inputs produce different data.
evidence: LIVE substance history, description containing 'moka': (314 mg, 200 ml, preset:manual) x23 = 157/100 ml. (260, 200, preset:default-moka) = 130. (134-135, 200, voice_drink) x5 = 67-68. (95, 250, legacy water_intake) = 38. voice-parse.ts:17 `caffeineMg (e.g. drip coffee 250ml ~ 95mg, espresso 30ml ~ 63mg...)`.
failure_scenario: Two identical 200 ml moka coffees logged by voice and by preset record 134 mg vs 314 mg, so daily caffeine totals and any caffeine-vs-BP/HR analysis swing on input method.
suggested_fix: When a voice drink matches a known preset or substance name, use the preset's per-100 ml value. Add a moka/espresso concentration anchor to the voice prompt.
verifier_corrections: The live numbers are unverified because the MCP query failed. The legacy 38 mg/100 ml figure is irrelevant to the current code. The default-moka preset is 130 mg/100 ml with a 50 ml default volume, so a 200 ml moka logged through the preset means the user changed the volume. The 314 mg/200 ml rows come from a user-made manual preset, not from the default. Users can edit the voice caffeineMg value in the review row before saving, which lowers the impact. The underlying issue is that the prompt has no moka or concentration anchor and nothing reconciles voice entries with presets. That is real, but it is an estimation-quality inconsistency, not a medium-severity data bug.

These are minor corrections and do not change the verdict.
- **Row count:** it is 22 rows at 157 mg/100 ml via `preset:manual`, not 23. Two more rows at 157 come from a custom preset.
- **Voice values:** they are not always 67-68. They range from 50 to 92 mg/100 ml, so the voice path is also inconsistent with itself.
- **Preset values:** these vary too (130 vs 157), because the user edited them or the AI lookup produced different values. The preset path is not one fixed value.
- **Files:** the logic that bypasses reconciliation lives in `apps/web/src/components/voice/voice-panel.tsx:261-272`, not `drink-service.ts`. `drink-service.ts` just stores whatever `caffeineMg` it is given.
- **Legacy value:** the 38 mg/100 ml figure is a single legacy row. The system has no inherent legacy path value.

title: Historical substance rows lack volume/ABV (128 caffeine and 66 alcohol rows), and nothing backfilled them
description: Until about 2026-08-08, the preset path wrote SubstanceRecords without volumeMl (and some alcohol rows without abvPercent). The volume survives only on the grouped water row, so any consumer reading substance_records alone, including the MCP substance tool and the export, has no volume. Legacy alcohol rows also record 'Alcohol free beer' and 'AF beer' as 1.0 standard drink.
evidence: LIVE: caffeine volumeMl null by path = {preset: 128}. Alcohol volume null = 66 of 340, abv null = 28. Latest null-volume row is 2026-08-08. Legacy rows include ('Alcohol free beer', 1 std drink, water_intake) on 2026-02-14 and ('AF beer', 1) on 2026-04-03.
failure_scenario: Per-100 ml caffeine and alcohol-grams analyses skip or mis-weight a third of the history, and two non-alcoholic beers count as 2 standard drinks.
suggested_fix: Write a one-off migration that copies volume from the grouped water row into substance.volumeMl, and zero out standard drinks for rows whose description matches AF/alkoholfrei/non-alcoholic.
verifier_corrections: The alcohol total is 336 rows, not 340. The "a third of the history" figure varies by substance: about 44% of caffeine rows and about 20% of alcohol rows lack volume, roughly 31% combined. The newest null-volume alcohol row is 2026-08-01; 2026-08-08 is the newest caffeine one. The suggested fix is also harder than it sounds. The 5 legacy water_intake rows have a null groupId and link only through sourceRecordId, so a backfill has to join on that as well as on groupId. The AF zero-out rule needs care too: many Alkoholfrei rows (0.1–0.2 standard drinks at 0.5% ABV) are logged correctly and should not be set to 0. Only the two legacy 1.0-drink rows are clearly wrong.

title: Every water save pauses (writes nothing) while the browser reports offline: React Query mutation networkMode defaults to 'online'
description: useAddIntake wraps the purely local Dexie write in `useMutation({ mutationFn: ... addIntakeRecord ... })`. No `networkMode` is set anywhere (grep for networkMode/onlineManager across apps/web/src and packages returns nothing), and the shared QueryClient only sets query defaults. TanStack Query v5.102's default mutation networkMode is 'online'. After the window receives an `offline` event, onlineManager.isOnline() becomes false and every mutation is PAUSED before mutationFn runs. So the IndexedDB write does not happen at all. WaterTab awaits `waterIntake.addRecord`, which resolves only when the device comes back online, and meanwhile shows 'Recording...' with the button disabled. The paused mutation lives only in memory: if the user closes the PWA, reloads, or the OS kills the tab first, the water entry is lost. This affects all 58 useMutation hooks in the app (every health write), which contradicts the offline-first design. It fits the intermittent symptom exactly: it only happens when signal drops.
evidence:
use-intake-queries.ts:69-84: `export function useAddIntake() { return useMutation({ mutationFn: async ({type, amount, ...}) => unwrap(await addIntakeRecord(type, amount, source, timestamp, note)), }); }` ; query-client.ts: `new QueryClient({ defaultOptions: { queries: { staleTime: 1000 * 60, refetchOnWindowFocus: false } } })` (no mutations.networkMode).
Repro (scratch jsdom test with the real WaterTab + renderWithFixtures + fake-indexeddb): `window.dispatchEvent(new Event('offline'))` then click 'Confirm Entry' and wait 1.5 s. Output: `onlineManager.isOnline() false, navigator.onLine true` / `R1 rows after 1.5s offline: 0, button text: 'Recording...', disabled: true`. Dispatching `online` afterwards made the row appear, which confirms the write was paused, not failed.
failure_scenario: The user is on a train, plane or in a basement with no signal (Android Chrome fires `offline`) and taps 'Confirm Entry' for 250 ml. Nothing is written to IndexedDB, and the button spins on 'Recording...' with no toast. The user closes the app or swipes it away and the drink is never recorded. Or the user returns later and the entry appears with a timestamp from when connectivity came back (addIntakeRecord uses Date.now() at execution time), so it can land in the wrong day or hour.
suggested_fix: Set `mutations: { networkMode: 'always' }` (and `queries: { networkMode: 'always' }` for the Dexie reads) in makeQueryClient, since these mutations only touch IndexedDB; the sync engine already handles connectivity. Add a regression test that dispatches `offline` and asserts the Dexie row is written.
verifier_corrections:
I lowered severity from critical to high, for three reasons.
- The pause only starts after an `offline` event fires while the app is open. onlineManager starts at `#online = true` and does not read navigator.onLine at startup, so a cold start while already offline saves normally.
- Data is lost only if the page or process is killed while the mutation is paused. Otherwise it resumes and writes when the device reconnects.
- The user sees a stuck "Recording..." button, so the failure is not silent. The real harm is a delayed write with a wrong timestamp, plus loss if the app is closed first, not guaranteed silent corruption.

The claim of "58 useMutation hooks" was not recounted, but the default does apply to every mutation hook. The finding is otherwise accurate.

The mechanism and the evidence are accurate. The severity is overstated: the mutation is paused, not dropped. The user sees a stuck "Recording..." button rather than a silent failure. Loss needs the app to be killed or reloaded while paused, and a cold start while offline is not affected because v5 `onlineManager` defaults to online until an `offline` event fires. "58 useMutation hooks" could not be verified: `useMutation` appears in 15 files. The claim that every write through a `useMutation` hook is affected is correct. Resuming depends on the `QueryClientProvider` being mounted; the app mounts it in `providers.tsx:92`, so paused writes do resume when the device comes back online. The suggested fix, `networkMode: 'always'`, is appropriate.

Severity is overstated. Data loss needs the user to close or kill the app while the 'Recording...' state is visible; otherwise the write goes through later with a timestamp from when signal came back. That is high (core logging broken offline, wrong timestamps), not critical. Two scope notes: the mutations are spread across 15 files (the 58 useMutation hooks were not individually verified), and the Capacitor shell loads the live site, so this bites when the app is already open and then loses connectivity.

title: Clearing the custom date/time in the water dialog throws inside the submit handler: nothing saves, no error toast, and the dialog stays open
description: handleSubmit computes `showTimeInput ? dateTimeLocalToTimestamp(customTime) : undefined` outside any try/catch. dateTimeLocalToTimestamp throws `Invalid date value` for an empty string. Mobile datetime pickers offer a 'Clear' action that sets the value to ''. The Add Entry button's disabled check only looks at the amount, so the user can submit and the async handler rejects. The result is an unhandled promise rejection, onSubmit is never called, and there is no feedback. The same dialog is used by the Beverage tab and by salt.
evidence:
manual-input-dialog.tsx:91-92: `const timestamp = showTimeInput ? dateTimeLocalToTimestamp(customTime) : undefined; await onSubmit(parsed.data.amount, timestamp, trimmedNote);`; date-utils.ts:34-37 `if (isNaN(timestamp)) { throw new Error(`Invalid date value: "${value}"`); }`.
Repro (scratch jsdom test, real WaterTab): tap 'tap to edit', then 'Set different time', set #custom-time to '', submit. Output: `R2 rows: 0, dialog still open: true, errors: ["Error: Invalid date value: \"\""]`.
---
[liquids-save#1] manual-input-dialog.tsx:91 `const timestamp = showTimeInput ? dateTimeLocalToTimestamp(customTime) : undefined;` (no try). Scratch DOM test on <WaterTab/>: open dialog → 'Set different time' → set custom-time to '' → click 'Add Entry' ⇒ `rows 0 dialog still open true alerts 0 unhandled [ 'Error: Invalid date value: ""' ]`.
failure_scenario: The user backfills a drink, opens 'Set different time', taps Clear in the Android date picker (or partially deletes the value) and taps 'Add Entry'. Nothing happens: no toast, no record. The user assumes it saved, or retries and gives up.
suggested_fix: Validate customTime in the zod schema (required when showTimeInput is on) and show a field error. Disable Add Entry while the time is invalid. Wrap the timestamp conversion in the existing validation path.
verifier_corrections: The claim that the dialog is also used for salt is wrong. Its only callers are water-tab.tsx:196 and beverage-tab.tsx:253, and both pass type="water", so the salt path never uses this dialog. Severity is overstated: this is an edge case with an easy recovery, so medium fits better than high. The phrase "nothing happens" is slightly incomplete: the global unhandledrejection handler writes the error to the in-app error log, but the user still gets no feedback.

The claim that "the same dialog is used by salt" is wrong for production. Only the water and beverage tabs use ManualInputDialog, both with type="water". type="salt" appears only in manual-input-dialog.dom.test.tsx. The severity should be medium, not high: the failure is safe (nothing is written, and fixing the time field recovers), and it needs the user to clear or corrupt the time field.

"The same dialog is used ... by salt" is wrong. In production, ManualInputDialog is only rendered with type="water" (water-tab.tsx and beverage-tab.tsx). type="salt" only appears in manual-input-dialog.dom.test.tsx. "The user assumes it saved" is overstated: the dialog stays open, which visibly shows the save did not happen. The unhandled rejection is not entirely silent either; the global error-log-service captures it, but the user sees nothing. Severity should be medium, not high: it is an edge case with no data loss that the user can recover from.

title: 'Tap to edit' amount opens a dialog that saves directly; cancelling it discards the typed amount and Confirm then saves the old amount
description: The pending-amount button is labelled 'tap to edit', which suggests it edits the pending amount before 'Confirm Entry'. Instead it opens ManualInputDialog, whose 'Add Entry' calls handleManualSubmit and immediately writes a record. It never updates pendingAmount. Closing the dialog (Cancel, backdrop, back gesture) throws away the typed value, and the main Confirm still shows and saves the previous pending amount. After a successful 'Add Entry', pendingAmount is also not reset, so a user who then taps 'Confirm Entry' out of habit logs a second, unintended entry. The Beverage tab behaves the same way, but its manual path does not clear the beverage name while its Confirm path does (beverage-tab.tsx:99 vs :124-125).
evidence: water-tab.tsx:150-171 `
failure_scenario: The user wants to log 330 ml: taps the number, types 330, dismisses the sheet with the back gesture, and taps 'Confirm Entry'. 250 ml is saved, and the total is wrong by 80 ml with nothing to indicate it.
suggested_fix: Choose one model: either the dialog sets pendingAmount (label 'Set amount', no write) and Confirm is the only commit, or relabel it as 'Log custom amount' and reset pendingAmount after it writes. Make the Beverage manual path reset the name consistently.
verifier_corrections: The cancel scenario is not a hidden wrong total. The user cancelled the dialog, then separately and explicitly confirmed the "+250ml" amount shown on the card. The dialog is titled "Enter Water Amount", says it will "add to your intake", and its button is "Add Entry", so its direct-save behaviour is disclosed. The only misleading part is the "tap to edit" caption. The double-entry case needs two separate commit taps, and the success toast confirms the first one. Severity should drop from medium to low. The code-level claims are accurate: pendingAmount is never updated or reset on the manual path, and the Beverage manual path clears sugarG but not beverageName.

- **"Wrong by 80 ml with nothing to indicate it":** overstated. The card visibly shows "+250ml" before Confirm, and the dialog says it will "add to your intake" with "Add Entry". It never claims to edit the pending amount. The only misleading text is the "tap to edit" caption.
- **Severity:** should be low, not medium. This is a labelling and state-reset inconsistency, not silent data corruption.
- **Beverage claim:** correct but minor. The manual path resets sugarG but not beverageName or pendingAmount, while Confirm resets all three (beverage-tab.tsx:98-100 vs :124).

title: Confirm double-submit guard relies on React state, not a ref, so two clicks dispatched in the same task write two records
description: handleConfirm returns early on `isSubmitting` read from the render closure. Two click events dispatched before React re-renders both see false and both call addRecord. Real separate taps are normally separate tasks (React flushes in between), so reaching this needs synthetic/ghost clicks or a slow device where events queue. The guard pattern is fragile, and Confirm also checks `waterIntake.isLoading`, which can never be true because the useLiveQuery defaults are 0.
evidence: water-tab.tsx:51-54 `const handleConfirm = useCallback(async () => { if (pendingAmount <= 0 || isSubmitting) return; setIsSubmitting(true); ...`. Repro (scratch jsdom): `btn.click(); btn.click();` gives `R5 rows after double tap: 2`. use-intake-queries.ts:141 `isLoading: dailyTotal === undefined || rollingTotal === undefined` is never true, given the `0` defaults at lines 37/48.
failure_scenario: On a lagging device, a double tap or ghost click on 'Confirm Entry' logs 250 ml twice.
suggested_fix: Use a useRef in-flight flag set synchronously before awaiting, and drop the dead isLoading gate (or pass `undefined` as the useLiveQuery default if a loading state is wanted).
verifier_corrections: The failure scenario ("on a lagging device a double tap or ghost click logs 250 ml twice") is overstated. Real separate taps and ghost clicks arrive as separate tasks, React flushes the sync-lane re-render in between, and the button is disabled by then. Only synthetic clicks in the same task, like the jsdom repro, get past the guard. The finding should be framed as a latent, fragile guard plus a dead `waterIntake.isLoading` check, not as reachable duplicate records. The ref-based guard is still a reasonable hardening.

title: Old preset-tab AI lookup cannot return or set sugar (the owner-reported bug's root cause)
description: The Coffee and Alcohol tabs' sparkle search calls /api/ai/substance-lookup. Its request enum is only caffeine|alcohol. The prompt and tool only ask for substancePer100ml, defaultVolumeMl, beverageName and waterContentPercent. The zod response has no sugar field. handleAiLookup sets caffeine/alcohol, volume, name and water%, and never touches sugarG. Sugary drinks looked up this way are logged with no sugar unless the user types it by hand, and nothing on screen tells them the lookup skipped it. The newer voice-parse path and the Food card's /api/ai/parse both return sugar for the same drink.
evidence:
schema.ts: `SubstanceLookupResponseSchema = z.object({ substancePer100ml, defaultVolumeMl, beverageName, reasoning, waterContentPercent })` (no sugar). preset-tab.tsx:213-226 sets only Caffeine/Alcohol/Volume/BeverageName/WaterContentPercent/AiLookupUsed. Scratch DOM test (mocked apiFetch, real Dexie): `REQUEST { query: 'Coca-Cola', type: 'caffeine' }`, `SUGAR FIELD after lookup: ""`, `SUGAR ROWS R1: 0` after Log Entry.
---
[substance-sugar#1] route.ts: `type: z.enum(["caffeine", "alcohol"])`; schema.ts: `substancePer100ml, defaultVolumeMl, beverageName, reasoning, waterContentPercent` (no sugar); preset-tab.tsx handleAiLookup sets only setCaffeinePer100ml/setAlcoholPer100ml/setVolumeMl/setBeverageName/setWaterContentPercent. setSugarG is never called, and setSaltPer100ml is not reset either.
failure_scenario: Coffee tab → search "Coca-Cola" → sparkle → the lookup fills 330 ml and caffeine → Log Entry. That writes one water row and one caffeine row, but no sugar row. Today's sugar total and the 30 g target bar ignore the ~35 g of sugar. The same drink entered by voice or on the Food card does record ~35 g.
suggested_fix: Add sugarPer100ml (g) to SUBSTANCE_LOOKUP_TOOL, the prompt and SubstanceLookupResponseSchema. In handleAiLookup, always set sugarG from the result (volume × per-100ml, rounded), or clear it when the result has none. Better still, retire substance-lookup and send this search through the same parse/voice-parse contract so there is one drink-nutrient schema.
verifier_corrections:
- **Severity:** I rate this medium, not high. Sugar is under-counted, but nothing corrupt is stored, dosing isn't affected, and the manual Sugar field is visible on screen.
- **"Nothing on screen tells them":** this is slightly overstated. There's no message that the lookup skipped sugar, but the empty "Sugar (g) — optional" field is shown right next to the lookup.
- **Beverage-tab branch:** the "beverage" branch in `handleAiLookup` is dead code, because `PresetTab` is only ever rendered with `tab="coffee"` or `tab="alcohol"`.
- **Stale values:** the stale-salt point is real. Salt from a previously selected preset isn't cleared by a lookup: `setSelectedPresetId(null)` clears the selection highlight but leaves `saltPer100ml` in place, and the same applies to any sugar the user typed earlier.
- **Root-cause claim:** that this is the root cause of the owner's reported bug is an assertion I can't verify from code, though it is consistent with it.
- **Not re-run:** I did not re-run the scratch DOM test. The static trace alone confirms the finding.

"Nothing on screen tells them" is overstated: an empty "Sugar (g) — optional" input is visible on the same form. Calling this "the owner-reported bug's root cause" is not supported; the task only says the owner suspects inconsistencies. There is an extra detail the finding does not state: the lookup does not clear sugarG or saltPer100ml, so leftover values from before the lookup carry into the looked-up drink. Severity should be medium, not high.

"Nothing on screen tells them the lookup skipped it" overstates the problem. The form shows a visible "Sugar (g) — optional" input (preset-tab.tsx:521-536) that stays empty after the lookup, so the gap can be seen, even though no message explains it. The finding also misses that a sugar value typed earlier is not reset by a new lookup and can be logged against the new drink. Severity should be medium, not high: the lookup's main job (caffeine and alcohol) works, and sugar can still be entered by hand on the same form.

title: Preset-tab sugar field is never reset by a new lookup or preset tap; stale sugar is booked on the next drink
description: sugarG is cleared only in resetFields(), which runs after a successful log. selectPreset, the preset deselect branch of handlePresetTap and handleAiLookup all overwrite volume, caffeine, ABV, salt and name, but leave sugarG as it was. Every other field changes to match the new drink while sugar keeps the old value, and buildDrink sends that value to logDrink.
evidence: selectPreset sets Volume/Caffeine/Alcohol/Salt/WaterContent/BeverageName and never calls setSugarG. The deselect branch at lines 146-153 also leaves sugarG alone. Scratch test: typed 35 g, then looked up "black coffee" and tapped Espresso: `SUGAR FIELD after 2nd lookup: 35`, `SUGAR FIELD after preset tap: 35`, then Log Entry → `SUGAR ROWS R2 (espresso): [ 35 ]`.
failure_scenario: The user starts entering a cola (types 35 g sugar), changes their mind, taps the Espresso preset (or runs a new AI lookup) and logs. The espresso is saved with 35 g of sugar. From the user's side, the sugar field "doesn't update" when they look up a different drink.
suggested_fix: Reset sugarG (or set it from the preset/lookup) inside selectPreset, the deselect branch and handleAiLookup. Better, keep the whole form in one reducer so each preset/lookup sets every field at once.
verifier_corrections: The cited lines and behaviour are accurate. Severity is overstated: the stale value is shown in the visible "Sugar (g) — optional" input at lines 521-539, so it is not a silent corruption. Medium fits better than high. Not mentioned in the finding: presets never store sugar (addPreset in handleSaveAndLog, 297-307, leaves it out), so a preset tap has no correct sugar value to apply and the fix would have to clear the field. Also, a stale sugar value makes an otherwise substance-less drink pass the hasSubstance gate.

Presets and AI lookups have no sugar value (LiquidPreset has no sugar field, and the lookup response isn't read for sugar). So sugar is not a drink property that "fails to update". It is a visible, user-entered, absolute-grams add-on that deliberately stays until the next log. Clearing it on every preset tap would break the natural flow of typing sugar and then picking a preset. The field is always visible, so the value is never booked silently. The defensible part is narrower: the explicit deselect branch (lines 146-153) resets every other field but not sugar, and arguably a fresh AI lookup should clear it too. Severity should be low (UX inconsistency), not high.

Accurate: the deselect branch and preset/lookup switches leave sugarG in place, and it gets logged. Overstated: presets and AI lookups have no sugar data, so there is no value they could set, and the stale value is visible in the form input before the user taps Log. It never carries over between separate logs because resetFields clears it after each one. The clearest bug is the deselect path, which clears every other field but not sugar. Severity should be medium, not high: it affects an optional field shown on screen, and it takes the user overlooking a number they typed themselves.

title: Food-card AI re-parse keeps the previous item's sugar/water/sodium when the new parse returns 0 or null
description: handleParse only writes a field when the new AI value is above 0. The same applies to sodium, water and potassium. A parse returning 0 or null for a nutrient is a real answer, but it leaves the previous parse's value in place. The form only resets after a successful save.
evidence:
food-section.tsx: `if (result.valueMg && result.valueMg > 0) {...} if (result.water && result.water > 0) {...} if (sugarEnabled && result.sugarG && result.sugarG > 0) {...}` with no else-branch clearing. Scratch test: parse "can of cola" (sugar 35, water 330), then re-parse "bag of plain crisps" (sugar 0, water 0, sodium 400) → `after re-parse: sugar= 35 water= 330` → Record → `ROWS for crisps: [ 'sugar=35', 'salt=400', 'water=330' ]`.
---
[food-salt-voice#4] `if (result.valueMg && result.valueMg > 0) { setSodiumMg(...) }` `if (result.water && result.water > 0) { setWaterMl(...) }` and nothing resets fields when the result is 0 or null.
---
[ai-routes-models#10] `if (result.valueMg && result.valueMg > 0) { setSodiumMg(...) } if (result.water && result.water > 0) {...} if (sugarEnabled && result.sugarG && result.sugarG > 0) {...}`
failure_scenario: The user parses one item, rephrases or switches to another food, parses again and saves. The saved meal carries the earlier item's 35 g sugar and 330 ml water, which inflates sugar and hydration totals.
suggested_fix: On each successful parse, set every field from the result, using '' for null or 0. Or reset the nutrient fields at the start of handleParse.
verifier_corrections: The mechanism is correct, but I rated it medium rather than high. The old values stay visible in the editable inputs on the form, so a careful user can spot and fix them before saving. Nothing is corrupted out of sight. It still silently inflates sugar and hydration totals for anyone who trusts the AI re-parse. The finding also merges three duplicate reports. Line 276 (potassium) has the same behaviour and should be fixed at the same time.

The mechanism and the failure are right. It is not silent, though: the stale values stay visible in the always-shown input fields, so users can catch them before saving. That makes this a medium-severity input inconsistency, not a high one. Also, the sodium source only resets to "sodium" when the parse returns sodium.

The code fact and the failure mechanism are accurate. The finding overstates severity: the bug needs a re-parse without saving, and the stale values are visible in the editable fields before Record is tapped, so medium fits better than high. The crisps example is slightly idealised, since the AI may return small non-zero water or sugar for crisps, which would overwrite the old values. Better triggers are zero-sugar or null answers, such as "black coffee" after "coffee with sugar", or a solid food where the AI returns null water after a drink.

title: Preset-tab summary never shows sugar, and hides salt whenever caffeine/ABV is present
description: calculatedDisplay lists caffeine and ABV, shows salt only when neither is present, and never shows sugar. The user can't see before logging that a stale or missing sugar value is about to be recorded.
evidence: `if (parts.length === 0 && saltPer100ml > 0) { parts.push(...mg salt) }`; memo deps `[volumeMl, caffeinePer100ml, alcoholPer100ml, saltPer100ml]` do not include sugarG.
failure_scenario: A stale 35 g of sugar is carried into an espresso entry. The summary shows only "63 mg caffeine", so the user logs without noticing the 35 g.
suggested_fix: Add every non-zero solute (sugar g, sodium mg) to the summary on its own, and include sugarG in the memo deps.
verifier_corrections: The summary line never shows sugar, but sugar is not hidden. It is typed into a visible input directly above the summary, so the user can see a stale 35 g before logging. A related detail the finding missed: selecting or deselecting a preset does not clear `sugarG`, so the value carries across preset switches, but it stays on screen. The missing `sugarG` in the memo deps is not a bug, because the memo does not read it. The real part of the finding is salt: this tab has no salt input, so salt coming from a caffeine or ABV preset is never shown before logging, yet `saltMg` is still recorded.

title: Single-compound dose label says 'N tablets of <total dose>', e.g. 'Take 2 tablets of 200mg' for a 200 mg dose on 100 mg tablets
description: formatDoseAmount uses the same template, '<pill count> of <X>', with two meanings. In the combo branch X is the per-pill strength ('2 tablets of 49/51mg'). In the single-compound branch X is the total scheduled dose (dosageMg), not the tablet strength. Any dose that isn't exactly one tablet therefore reads as that many tablets of the full dose. The label drives the dose row, the bulk-edit dialog, the prescription card's brand strip, and the dose-detail instruction 'Take {doseAmountLabel}'. The only existing test uses pillsPerDose=1, where the two meanings happen to match.
evidence: medication-ui-utils.ts:102-104: `return pillsPerDose != null ? `${formatPillCount(pillsPerDose)} of ${dosageMg}${unit}` : `${dosageMg}${unit}`;` vs combo branch :94-96 `const per = formatCompoundShort(inventory!.compounds, unit); ... `${formatPillCount(pillsPerDose)} of ${per}``. Scratch test (getDailyDoseSchedule, schedule dosage 200, inventory strength 100) → formatDoseAmount = "2 tablets of 200mg". Dose dialog renders `Take {doseAmountLabel}` → "Take 2 tablets of 200mg".
