failure_scenario: The Rx is 200 mg daily and the stocked tablets are 100 mg. The dose row and the detail dialog say 'Take 2 tablets of 200mg', which reads naturally as 2 × 200 mg = 400 mg. Likewise 0.5 × 50 mg tablets for a 25 mg dose shows '½ tablet of 25mg', i.e. half of a 25 mg tablet (12.5 mg).
suggested_fix: Always show the per-tablet strength after 'of', i.e. `${formatPillCount(p)} of ${inventory.strength}${inventory.unit}`, optionally followed by ' (= 200mg)'. Add tests for pillsPerDose ≠ 1.
verifier_corrections: I lowered severity from critical to high. The underlying numbers are all correct: the pill count, the stored dosageMg and the stock decrement. The problem is ambiguous wording, not corrupted data or a miscalculated dose. "2 tablets of 200mg" can also be read as "200mg made up of 2 tablets". The prescription card's brand strip shows the real tablet strength right beside the label (prescription-card.tsx:238-240, `${activeInventory.strength}${activeInventory.unit}`), which lessens the problem on that surface. On the dose row, the bulk-edit dialog and the pending dose-detail dialog there is no such context, so the finding is still valid.

I'm lowering the severity from critical to high. The computed values are all correct: the tablet count, the total mg and inventory deduction. Only the wording is misleading. A user who counts the tablets as stated still takes the right dose (2 physical 100 mg tablets = 200 mg). The risk is misreading the label, for example thinking the dose is 400 mg or buying the wrong strength. No data is corrupted. It's still a real medical-labelling defect on every screen where a dose isn't exactly one tablet, and nothing on those screens corrects it before the dose is taken.

Critical overstates it: no data is corrupted and the inventory/pill math is correct. The bug is ambiguous, misleading dose wording on the medication screens, and the prescription card shows the correct tablet strength right next to it. Severity should be high.

title: formatPillCount concatenates the whole number with a decimal fraction: 1⅓ → '10.33 tablets', 66⅔ → '660.67 tablets', 2.996 → '21 tablets'
description: When the fractional part isn't ¼, ½ or ¾, fracStr becomes `frac.toString()` (e.g. '0.33'). That string is then glued straight onto the whole part, giving '1' + '0.33' = '10.33'. A fraction that rounds to 1.00 yields '2' + '1' = '21'. The function formats both the per-dose pill count and fractional stock, so the dose row, the dialog, the Medicines list, the compound card and the brand picker all show inflated numbers. Other surfaces show the same quantity in other formats: the take toast prints the raw value ('66.6667 pill(s) deducted') and the inventory drawer prints '33.3333 pills'. All three disagree.
evidence: medication-ui-utils.ts:69 `const frac = Math.round((pills - whole) * 100) / 100;` … :79 `frac.toString();` … :81 `const combined = whole > 0 ? `${whole}${fracStr}` : fracStr;`. Scratch test output: formatPillCount(1.3333) → "10.33 tablets"; formatPillCount(66.6667) → "660.67 tablets"; formatPillCount(2.996) → "21 tablets". Schedule with dosage 200 / strength 3 → row "660.67 tablets of 200mg"; after takeDose stock 33.3333 → card shows "330.33 tablets".
failure_scenario: A 20 mg dose on 15 mg tablets (pillsPerDose 1.3333) shows 'Take 10.33 tablets of 20mg'. After a few one-third-pill doses, a stock of 12.3333 shows as '120.33 tablets' on the Medicines card and in the brand picker, while the drawer says '12.3333 pills'.
suggested_fix: Build the string as `${whole} ${fracStr}` using a unicode or 'n/d' fraction, and fall back to a single toFixed(2) number (e.g. '1.33') for non-quarter fractions. Carry the rounding-to-1 case into the whole part. Use one formatter for toast, drawer and cards.
verifier_corrections: Two cited locations are not formatPillCount call sites. schedule-view.tsx:127 is the take toast, which prints the raw `${slot.pillsPerDose ?? 1} pill(s) deducted`. The finding describes it correctly as a separate, inconsistent format, but the file list presents it as affected by the formatter. I did not check inventory-item-view-drawer.tsx:178 for formatPillCount usage, and it appears to use its own raw number format. The core claim is unaffected.

I didn't separately check the side claim that the toast shows "66.6667 pill(s) deducted" and the drawer shows "33.3333 pills". The core finding is proven by running the function. The finding lists schedule-view.tsx:127 and inventory-item-view-drawer.tsx:178 as call sites, but grep shows formatPillCount itself is called only in formatDoseAmount, compound-card, compound-card-expanded and brand-switch-picker. schedule-view probably gets the value through formatDoseAmount. It also leaves out one point: the scheduler treats thirds as clean fractions, so these doses show no warning.

Severity is overstated: medium, not high. The bug is display-only and needs a dose/strength ratio that is not a quarter; stored data is unaffected. The finding misses a related gap: when the fraction rounds to 0 (e.g. stock 12.0001 after three 0.3333 doses taken from 13), the `frac === 0` branch prints the raw value, "12.0001 tablets". The "2.996 → 21 tablets" case needs a stock ending in .995 or more, which is less likely than the thirds case. Of the files listed, schedule-view.tsx:127 and inventory-item-view-drawer.tsx:178 do not call formatPillCount. They print raw values, which is the inconsistency, not the concatenation bug.

title: Negative fractional stock is shown as a positive fraction: -2.5 and -0.5 both render as '½ tablets'
description: Negative stock is allowed by design, and the owner's live Entresto inventory reads -7. For a negative non-integer, Math.floor gives a negative whole part, and the `whole > 0` check then discards it together with its sign, so only the fraction is printed. The brand-switch picker has no 'Negative' badge, so there the value looks like a small positive balance.
evidence: `const whole = Math.floor(pills);` (-2.5 → -3), `frac = Math.round((pills - whole)*100)/100` (0.5), `const combined = whole > 0 ? ... : fracStr;` → "½ tablets". Scratch test: formatPillCount(-2.5) → "½ tablets"; formatPillCount(-0.5) → "½ tablets".
failure_scenario: A half-tablet regimen over-consumes to -6.5. The Switch Brand dialog lists that brand as 'Entresto 24/26mg · ½ tablets', so the user thinks half a pill is left when they are 6.5 pills short.
suggested_fix: Format Math.abs(pills) and prefix '-' when pills < 0. Add unit tests for negative and non-quarter values.
verifier_corrections: The finding misses a third affected caller: apps/web/src/components/medications/compound-card.tsx:24 (MedicationCard) formats stock the same way. In compound-card-expanded.tsx, stock below zero turns the text red, but the minus sign and whole part are still missing, so it shows a red "½ tablets". The owner's "-7" example is a whole number and displays correctly as "-7 pills". The bug only appears for negative non-integer stock.

Minor: the files list leaves out a third affected caller, apps/web/src/components/medications/compound-card.tsx:24, which also shows the wrong fraction text even though it tracks isNegativeStock. In compound-card-expanded the red colouring partly signals the negative state, so the misleading-positive problem is worst in brand-switch-picker. The scratch-test output quoted in the finding was not printed as literal output here (the console line was filtered out), but tracing the code gives the same result.

title: The same combo dose is labelled from three different compound sources; the Rx reference is frozen at the first brand and never reconciled with the active brand
description: Pill math always uses inventory.strength. Labels use one of three sources depending on the surface. (a) The dose row, bulk dialog and brand strip use the ACTIVE BRAND's per-pill compounds. (b) The dose-detail header splits the dose by the BRAND's ratio. (c) The prescription card chip, the expanded card (schedule and today), the maintenance and titration rows, web notifications, native local notifications and push payloads split the dose by PRESCRIPTION.compounds. prescription.compounds is copied from the first brand's per-pill compounds at creation, and no UI edits it. Nothing compares a later brand's ratio against it. scaleCompounds(brand.compounds, pillsPerDose), the helper that would give the true per-compound content, is used only in tests.
evidence: Scratch test: prescription compounds 49/51, active brand Entresto compounds 24/26 (strength 50), schedule dosage 100. Row formatDoseAmount → "2 tablets of 24/26mg"; Rx chip and notification text splitDose(100, rx.compounds) → "49/51mg"; dialog header splitDose(100, inventory.compounds) → "48/52mg". dose-detail-dialog.tsx:133 `formatCompoundShort(splitDose(schedule.dosage, inventory!.compounds), phase.unit)`; local-notifications.ts:78 `splitDose(schedule.dosage, prescription.compounds)`; grep: scaleCompounds has no non-test caller.
failure_scenario: The Rx was created with Vymada 100 (49/51), and the owner then switches the active brand to Entresto 24/26. The reminder says 'Take 49/51mg of Sacubitril / Valsartan' with no tablet count, the card chip says 49/51mg, the row says '2 tablets of 24/26mg', and the dialog title says 'Entresto 48/52mg'. A user holding 24/26 tablets and following the reminder may take one tablet, which is half the dose. If a brand is added with its compounds swapped (51/49), every Rx-level label still shows the old ratio.
suggested_fix: Make one labeller the single source of truth: when a combo brand is active, show scaleCompounds(brand.compounds, pillsPerDose) together with the tablet count everywhere, including notifications, push and native. Fall back to the reference split only when no brand is stocked. Warn when a brand's compound names or ratio differ from the prescription's.
verifier_corrections:
- The finding says "wrong dose". It is really a small per-compound ratio drift (for example 49/51 vs 48/52). Rx-level labels still show the correct total dose.

All the structural claims are accurate: three label sources, Rx compounds frozen at creation, and `scaleCompounds` used only in tests. What's overstated is the impact. With real brands of the same drug (Vymada 49/51 vs Entresto 24/26), the Rx-ratio label "49/51mg" is the correct total per-compound amount for a 100 mg dose, and it differs from the brand-based "48/52mg" only by rounding. Pill math and stock deduction use `strength` and are unaffected. The "takes one tablet = half dose" scenario is speculative. A genuinely wrong ratio needs a brand entered with a different ratio or compound order, which is an edge case. Severity should be medium, not high. The missing tablet count in notifications is true, but it's a UX gap rather than wrong dosing data.

1. The labels in the example do not contradict each other on dose. "49/51mg" (the Rx split of the 100mg dose) and "48/52mg" (the dialog, equal to 2 x 24/26) both represent the correct 100mg dose; they differ only by about 1mg of rounding per compound.
2. The "take one tablet = half dose" outcome is speculative. The reminder states the correct milligram amount.
3. The swapped-compound scenario is largely unreachable. The add-brand flow (add-medication-wizard.tsx:103-105) pre-fills compound names and order from the prescription.
4. Severity should be low (a cosmetic label inconsistency, plus a missing ratio-drift warning), not high.

title: splitDose's proportional rounding shows per-compound mg that no tablet contains (200 → 98/102 or 96/104; 50 → 24.5/25.5)
description: Marketed sacubitril/valsartan strengths don't share one exact ratio: 24/26 is 0.48, 49/51 is 0.49 and 97/103 is 0.485. splitDose scales the reference ratio linearly and rounds to 0.01 mg, so any Rx-level label for a titrated dose shows invented amounts. The existing test enshrines '98/102mg' for a 200 dose, even though an Entresto 200 tablet is 97/103.
evidence: compound-utils.ts:40 `strength: Math.round((dosageMg * (c.strength / total)) * 100) / 100`. Scratch output: splitDose(200, 49/51) → "98/102mg"; splitDose(200, 24/26) → "96/104mg"; splitDose(50, 49/51) → "24.5/25.5mg"; test file :165 `expect(formatDoseAmount(s)).toBe("98/102mg")`.

verifier_corrections: The finding under-counts the affected paths. title: A combo prescription whose active brand has no compounds shows only a compound split, with no tablet count
description: formatDoseAmount checks the brand first. If the brand isn't a combo (compounds missing, or a single entry because the combo toggle was off or only one compound was valid), the function falls through to the prescription split and returns without using pillsPerDose. The instruction then drops the number of tablets entirely, even though the stock math deducts pillsPerDose.

Scratch test: Rx compounds 49/51, brand strength 50 with no compounds, dosage 100 → row "49/51mg" while slot.pillsPerDose = 2 (and takeDose deducts 2).

verifier_corrections: The finding is accurate, with one detail to add. Nothing material. title: The odd_fraction warning is computed but never shown, and one-third fractions count as 'clean'

No component reads 'odd_fraction'; only the audit log records it. isCleanFraction also accepts anything within 0.01 of 1/3 or 2/3, so 66.6667 tablets counts as clean. Nothing warns the user when a dose can't be taken with whole, half or quarter tablets.

1. The failure scenario's numbers are wrong: 200 mg on 3 mg tablets is 66.67 tablets, not 660.67. 2. Counting thirds as 'clean' is intentional and documented in isCleanFraction's doc comment. It is not a logic bug. 3. The pill count per dose is still shown in the prescription card and in the deduction toasts, so the user is not entirely 'quiet'-ly misled. The only thing missing is the explicit odd_fraction warning. 4. The overwrite by negative_stock is real, but it only matters in the rare case where both conditions apply, and because odd_fraction is never rendered anyway, the overwrite has no visible effect. Severity should be low (a UX/validation gap), not medium.

title: strength = 0 silently makes every take deduct 0 pills ('0 tablets of 100mg', a -0 consumed transaction, ∞ days of supply)
description: calculatePillsConsumed hides a zero strength by returning 0 instead of flagging an error. Every consumer then treats 0 as valid: isCleanFraction(0) is true, and negative_stock never fires while stock ≥ 0. The row, the toast and stock all agree on 0. The refill estimate and alert fall back to Infinity, so the brand never triggers a days-based refill alert. This is the downstream effect of any path that stores strength 0, not the wizard regex itself.
evidence: dose-log-service.ts:89 `if (pillStrengthMg === 0) return 0;`. Scratch test: inventory strength 0, dosage 100 → row "0 tablets of 100mg", warning undefined; after takeDose stock stays 10 and a consumed transaction with amount -0 is written.
failure_scenario: A brand saved with strength 0 is dosed daily for a month. Stock never moves, the drawer shows 'Est. Supply ∞ days', no refill alert ever fires, and the user runs out without warning.
suggested_fix: Treat strength ≤ 0 as invalid: return undefined, raise an 'invalid_strength' warning, skip the transaction, and block saving such a brand.
verifier_corrections: If the user goes through the wizard only, `scheduleDosage = finalDosage * strength` is also 0, so the dose row shows "0 tablets of 0mg", not "of 100mg". Getting "0 tablets of 100mg" needs a later schedule edit in `edit-medication-drawer.tsx`. The main problem is that the wizard has no guard at all against a 0 strength on the single-compound path (`parseStrength` in `add-medication-wizard.tsx:263-272`). The finding plays this down as "not the wizard regex itself", but it is the actual entry point.

The example with a 100mg dose ("0 tablets of 100mg") needs strength 0 together with a non-zero schedule dosage. The wizard cannot produce that: it computes `scheduleDosage = (finalDosage || 1) * strength`, which is 0 when strength is 0, so a wizard-created medication shows "0 tablets of 0mg". A non-zero dosage needs another path, such as a titration or phase edit, or synced data. The main effect is the same either way: stock never goes down, supply shows as infinite, and no refill alert ever fires.

title: Missing or null strength writes NaN / -Infinity into currentStock and the transaction ledger, permanently
description: The only guard is `=== 0`. With strength undefined the result is 100/undefined = NaN; with null it is 100/null = Infinity. Both are written to currentStock and to the consumed transaction's amount. The backup inventoryItemSchema validates only prescriptionId and brandName (passthrough), so a backup row without strength imports cleanly, and pulled rows with null (the known pull-null issue) take the same path. Once a NaN transaction exists, getCurrentStock and recalculateAllStock sum it on every launch, so stock stays NaN forever. JSON turns NaN into null, which the NOT NULL amount column then rejects on sync. The compound jsonb is also unvalidated: a string strength makes compoundSum concatenate strings.
evidence: Scratch test: strength undefined → row "NaN tablets of 100mg"; after take, stock NaN, tx [NaN]. strength null → row "InfinityNaN tablets of 100mg"; stock -Infinity, tx [-Infinity]. backup-schemas.ts:108-113 `inventoryItemSchema = baseRecord.extend({ prescriptionId: z.string(), brandName: z.string() }).passthrough()`.
failure_scenario: The user restores an older or hand-edited backup whose inventory row lacks strength, then takes a dose. The card shows 'NaN tablets', the ledger gains a NaN row that no launch-time recalculation can repair, and that transaction never syncs.
suggested_fix: Guard with `!Number.isFinite(strength) || strength <= 0` in calculatePillsConsumed. Require a positive finite strength, and validate compounds[].strength as a number, in backup-schemas and in the sync pull normaliser.
verifier_corrections: Wrong claim: rows pulled from sync can arrive with a null strength. The Postgres inventory_items.strength column is NOT NULL, so that path is unreachable. The "older backup" scenario is also overstated. The app has never been able to create an inventory item without a strength (the type requires it and the UI enforces strength > 0), so only a hand-edited or corrupted backup triggers the bug. The claim that the NaN "can never be repaired" is too strong: deleting the bad transaction makes the stock sum correct again. The compounds string-concatenation point is speculative and has the same prerequisite: it also needs malformed imported data. The part that holds up: calculatePillsConsumed and the backup schema do not guard against a missing or non-finite strength. Severity should drop from medium to low.

The claim that pulled rows with a null strength take this path is wrong: the server column inventory_items.strength is NOT NULL (packages/db/src/schema.ts:455), so a pull cannot supply null or undefined. "Older backup" is also unsupported: every genuine export has included strength, because the field has been required since the inventory table was added. The only way to trigger this is to import a hand-edited or corrupted backup, which the passthrough inventoryItemSchema accepts. Downgrade to low: the missing guard plus missing backup validation is a real but latent robustness gap.

title: Combo dose inputs switch meaning between screens: the wizard asks 'pills per dose', while schedule edit and titration ask for a bare summed 'mg' with no compound hint or tablet preview

The schedule editor (Dose input with placeholder 'Dose' next to the free-text unit) and the titration editor (placeholder 'mg', hard-coded 'mg' label) ask for the summed total with no hint that 'mg' means sacubitril plus valsartan, and no preview of the resulting tablet count or split. The schedule stores 97, the row shows '0.97 tablets of 49/51mg' (or '1.94 tablets' with a 24/26 brand, rendered '10.94 tablets' by the formatter bug), reminders say '47.53/49.47mg', and every take deducts 0.97 pills.

I did not verify the exact downstream numbers in the failure scenario: the "10.94 tablets" formatter bug, the "47.53/49.47mg" reminder split, and the "deducts 0.97 pills" amount. One point is clearer than stated: the schedule editor's unit is an editable free-text field that defaults to "mg", not a fixed label. The user could even change it, which makes the summed-mg meaning of the value even less clear for combos.

The core claim is correct. I did not verify the "10.94 tablets" formatter bug in the failure scenario; it belongs to a separate finding and should not count as evidence here. The 0.97-pill deduction per dose depends on how inventory math divides the summed mg by the brand's strength sum, which I also did not verify in this pass. When editing an existing schedule, the pre-filled summed-mg value gives some hint of the field's meaning, so the ambiguity is worst for newly added rows and titration entries.

title: Days-of-supply turns negative once stock is negative ('-7 pills left (~-4 days)')
description: Both refill estimates use Math.floor(stock / dailyPills) with no clamp, so negative stock (allowed by design, and live for the owner) produces negative days in the drawer and in the notification body.
evidence: inventory-item-view-drawer.tsx:169 `daysLeft = Math.floor((item.currentStock ?? 0) / dailyPills);`; notification body `${currentStock} pills left (~${daysLeft} days)`.
failure_scenario: Entresto at -7 stock, 2 pills/day: the drawer shows 'Est. Supply -4 days' and the refill notification says '-7 pills left (~-4 days)'.
suggested_fix: Clamp to 0 and show an explicit 'out of stock / over-consumed' state.
verifier_corrections: The line citations are right: the drawer calculation is at line 169, the notification calculation at line 172, and the notification body template at line 58. The finding implies the negative notification appears whenever stock is negative. In fact it is sent once per prescription and usually earlier, while stock is still positive, so the negative text appears only in the case where stock was already negative at the first alert check. The drawer shows negative days every time stock is negative.

The drawer's Add button is disabled for amounts ≤ 0, and adjustStock's 'adjusted' type has no UI. After a pill count, the user can only lower stock by editing a past refill row, which rewrites history.

add-medication-wizard.tsx:308 `currentStock: parseInt(formState.currentStock) || 0,`; inventory-item-view-drawer.tsx:214 `disabled={refillMutation.isPending || refillAmount <= 0}`; grep: no caller passes type "adjusted".

[gap-inventory-refill-ui-flows#9] currentStock: parseInt(formState.currentStock) || 0,
const refillPills = parseInt(formState.refillAlertPills) || undefined;

title: The maintenance row's '/day' total sums every schedule regardless of weekdays, and labels that total with the reference split
description: totalDaily adds each schedule's dosage once, ignoring daysOfWeek, whereas the refill estimates weight by daysOfWeek.length/7. It then runs the total through splitDose (with the reference-ratio issue above) and suffixes '/day'.
evidence: maintenance-row.tsx:18 `const totalDaily = schedules.reduce((acc, s) => acc + s.dosage, 0);` … :30 `{fmtDose(totalDaily, maintenancePhase.unit)}/day`.
failure_scenario: A schedule of 100 mg daily plus 100 mg on Mon/Wed/Fri only shows '200mg/day'. The true average is about 143 mg/day, and on 4 of 7 days it is 100 mg.
suggested_fix: Show per-day totals or a weekday-weighted average, consistent with the refill estimate.
verifier_corrections: No factual errors. The finding refers to "the reference-ratio issue above" in splitDose without explaining it; that is a separate finding and has no bearing on the weekday-summing bug.

title: Dose Take / Mark All / Untake / Skip mutations pause while offline, then run later with the reconnect time
description: All dose mutation hooks use plain useMutation. The shared QueryClient sets no mutations.networkMode, so TanStack v5's default 'online' applies. When the browser fires 'offline', every dose action pauses before takeDose runs. Nothing is written to IndexedDB, even though this is a local-only operation. The awaiting handler never finishes, so no undo toast or confirmation appears and the Take button stays visible. When the device reconnects, the queued mutation runs. buildDoseLog/upsertDoseLog stamp actionTimestamp with Date.now() at run time, so an on-time Take is recorded at the reconnect time. Paused mutations are held only in memory, so closing the PWA before reconnecting loses the dose entirely. The known water-save item has the same root cause, but it is not fixed for medications, and here it also corrupts the dose time.
evidence: query-client.ts: `defaultOptions: { queries: { staleTime: ..., refetchOnWindowFocus: false } }` (no mutations.networkMode). use-medication-queries.ts:235 `useTakeDose() { return useMutation({ mutationFn: async (input) => unwrap(await takeDose(input)) }) }`. dose-log-service.ts:148 `actionTimestamp: Date.now()`. Scratch hook test: onlineManager.setOnline(false); mutateAsync(take) -> after 300ms `settled false logs 0 isPaused true`; setOnline(true) -> `settled true logs 1`.
failure_scenario: The user is on a plane or has no signal at 08:00 and taps Take on Metoprolol. Nothing happens: the row stays pending and no toast appears. They close the app. The dose is never recorded, the stock is not reduced, and adherence shows it as missed. If they keep the app open and reconnect at 13:00, the dose is logged as 'Taken at 13:00'.
suggested_fix: Set `mutations: { networkMode: 'always' }` in makeQueryClient, or on every Dexie-backed useMutation. Local IndexedDB writes do not depend on the network, and the sync queue already handles upload.
verifier_corrections: The trigger is narrower than described. TanStack v5's onlineManager starts as online=true and only changes on window 'online'/'offline' events; it does not check navigator.onLine at startup. So the pause only happens when connectivity is lost while the app is open or backgrounded and the browser or WebView fires 'offline'. A cold start already in airplane mode would not pause, and neither would weak signal where navigator stays online. The "on a plane" scenario therefore applies to losing connectivity mid-session, not to opening the app offline. The retroactive-take path, which passes takenAtTime, keeps the correct timestamp. The wrong-time problem applies only to plain Take, Skip and Untake, where Skip and Untake also get resume-time stamps. The scratch-test output quoted in the finding could not be re-run because that directory is not present in its original form. The conclusion rests on the code trace and documented v5 defaults.

The finding is accurate. Two small clarifications:
- The pause only starts after the browser fires an 'offline' event. onlineManager assumes the device is online at startup, so a PWA cold-started while already offline may still write normally until an 'offline' event arrives.
- The wrong timestamp does not apply everywhere. A caller that passes `takenAtTime` (for example, a past-time take) gets a timestamp built from that value rather than `Date.now()`.

The pause only starts when the browser fires an 'offline' event while the app is running. In TanStack v5, onlineManager starts as online and only listens for online/offline events. A cold launch with no connectivity (e.g. opening the app already on a plane) would not pause mutations: they run immediately and write to IndexedDB. The failure needs connectivity to drop during an open session. Also, tapping Take again while paused just queues another paused mutation. On reconnect the second one finds wasTaken and does not deduct stock twice, so the only harm is the wrong timestamp or the lost dose, not double inventory.

title: Take→untake/skip→take with no active inventory keeps the stale inventoryItemId; the next untake/skip adds pills that were never taken out
description: takeDose seeds `inventoryItemId` from the previous log. If no active inventory is found on this take, it skips the stock deduction but still writes the old inventoryItemId back onto the log. upsertDoseLog only merges fields and never clears inventoryItemId when a dose is untaken or skipped. untakeDose and skipDose then restore pills to `prev.inventoryItemId` whenever the status is 'taken'. That restores pills this take never deducted. Every take→untake (or take→skip) cycle adds pills.
evidence: dose-log-service.ts:278 `let inventoryItemId: string | undefined = prev?.inventoryItemId;` ... :288 `if (inventory) { inventoryItemId = inventory.id; ... }` (no else) ... :321 `if (inventoryItemId !== undefined) extra.inventoryItemId = inventoryItemId;` ... :477 `if (wasTaken && prev?.inventoryItemId) { ... newStock = currentStock + pillsConsumed`. Scratch test: take (30→29), untake (→30), archive item (isActive=false), take -> `retake log inventoryItemId <A> stock 30`, untake -> `stock after second untake 31`, take+skip -> `32`.
failure_scenario: The user takes then untakes a dose, which stamps item A onto the log. They archive the bottle, which sets isActive=false, and they have no other active brand. They re-take the dose: nothing is deducted, but the log still says item A. They then Untake or Skip it from the bulk drawer or the detail drawer, and item A gains a phantom pill each cycle. The refill alerts and 'Low stock' banner read the inflated count.
suggested_fix: In takeDose, set inventoryItemId only from the inventory actually debited in this call, and explicitly clear it when nothing was deducted. Better still, have untake and skip reverse the exact consumed inventoryTransaction linked to the log instead of recomputing pills.
verifier_corrections: The mechanism and the cited lines are accurate. What's overstated is the user-visible impact. Refill alerts, the 'Low stock' banner and getDoseLogsWithDetailsForDate only read active, non-archived items. The phantom pills land on the archived or inactive item A, so those surfaces don't show the inflated count unless A is reactivated or un-archived. The inflated stock only matters once the user reactivates A or views its archived history. It also needs a narrow sequence of actions. So the severity should be medium, not high. Separately, the take after archiving also writes a misleading inventoryItemId into the audit log and the dose log, with pillsConsumed=0.

The mechanism and repro are correct. Severity should be medium, not high. The inflated count sits on an archived or inactive item, so refill alerts and the "Low stock" banner, which read active inventory, only pick it up if the user reactivates or unarchives that item.

The claim that "refill alerts and 'Low stock' banner read the inflated count" is wrong for as long as the item stays archived or inactive. Refill checks filter to `isActive && !isArchived` (medication-notification-service.ts:164-166), so the phantom pills only matter if the bottle is later reactivated or un-archived. Reaching the bug needs a specific sequence (take → untake → deactivate the only active item → take → untake/skip), not an ordinary take/untake cycle. Severity should be low, not high. The code defect itself (the stale inventoryItemId is never cleared when nothing was deducted) is accurate.

title: Dose detail drawer lets you Take or Skip a FUTURE dose, bypassing the schedule's isFuture guard, and takes the stock down now
description: DoseRow hides Take/Skip on future dates (`isActionable = !isFuture && ...`). But any non-actionable row is clickable and opens DoseDetailDialog. The drawer only knows `isToday`, so for a future date it treats the slot as a 'past date': TAKE opens the retroactive picker (default slot.localTime), and SKIP runs immediately. takeDose has no date guard. It writes a 'taken' log for the future date, deducts stock right away, and records an actionTimestamp in the future.
evidence: dose-row.tsx:43 `const isActionable = !isFuture && (status === "pending" || status === "missed");` and :79 `onClick={!isActionable ? () => onDoseClick(slot) : undefined}`. dose-detail-dialog.tsx:47 `if (isToday) {...} else { // Past date -- open time picker setRetroactivePickerOpen(true); }`; :205 `{status !== "skipped" && (<button onClick={handleSkip}` (no future check). Scratch test: takeDose for today+5 -> `future date take success true stock 29`.
failure_scenario: The user looks ahead to Friday, taps the Friday 08:00 Metoprolol row out of curiosity, and taps TAKE, then Log Dose. On Friday the schedule already shows 'Taken', so they may skip the real dose. Stock drops by one pill today.
suggested_fix: Pass isFuture (or compare slot.scheduledDate with today) into DoseDetailDialog and hide Take/Skip/Untake for future dates. Also reject scheduledDate > today in takeDose and skipDose.
verifier_corrections: Every factual claim checks out. I lowered severity from high to medium for three reasons. It is not silent corruption. It takes deliberate steps: open a future day, tap the row, tap TAKE, then confirm a time (SKIP needs one tap, with no confirmation). The result shows up in the UI as "Taken"/"Skipped" on that future day. And UNTAKE can undo it and put the stock back. It is a real inconsistency where the same dose gets different rules depending on where you act on it, with a risk of the user skipping the real dose. But it falls under the medium definition ("incorrect in edge cases / inconsistent"), not a core feature being broken. One small precision point: the drawer never uses slot.localTime as the default time in the future-date TAKE flow. The retroactive picker supplies the time, and that time is then applied to the future date.

One claim is not quite right: "records an actionTimestamp in the future". The drawer's retroactive path does not pass `takenAtTime`, so `actionTimestampOverride` is never set and the log gets the default (current) action time, not a future one. The inventory transaction timestamp is also Date.now(). A related issue the finding did not mention: handleRetroactiveTakeConfirm passes the time the user picked as `time`, which is the slot key, instead of as `takenAtTime`. If the user changes the default time, the log is saved under a slot time that doesn't match the schedule. The slot then still shows as pending while stock has already been deducted.

Severity is overstated. The failure needs deliberate multi-step input (drawer, then TAKE, then confirm in the time picker) on a screen that shows the future date, and UNTAKE reverses it, so medium fits better than high. It's more accurate to say the drawer has no future-date guard at all than that it 'treats it as past': SKIP needs only one tap, and TAKE goes through the retroactive picker. The rest is accurate: dose-row.tsx:43/79, dose-detail-dialog.tsx:47/205, the missing guard in takeDose, the immediate stock decrement and the future actionTimestamp. Week navigation into the future is unbounded (week-day-selector.tsx shiftWeek), so this can be reached on any future week.

title: Retroactive time picker accepts future times and an empty value; empty silently logs 'now' even for a past date
description: The picker is a bare `<input type="time">` with no min or max, and the Log Dose button is never disabled. takeDose applies takenAtTime to the slot's date without checking it against now, so a late dose today can be logged hours in the future. If the field is cleared (Android/desktop time inputs have a Clear control), `takenAtTime` is "". That is falsy, so takeDose and executeMarkAll drop the override and use Date.now(). A past-date dose is then stamped with today's date and time. editDoseTime rejects "" instead: unwrap throws, the handler rejects without any catch, and nothing is shown.
evidence: retroactive-time-picker.tsx:32 `<input type="time" value={selectedTime} onChange=...` (no min/max); :49 `onClick={() => { onConfirm(selectedTime); onOpenChange(false); }}`. dose-log-service.ts:264 `if (takenAtTime) { ... }`. schedule-view.tsx:221 `...(takenAtTime ? { takenAtTime } : {})`. Scratch test: takenAtTime '23:59' today -> `ts in future? true`; takenAtTime '' for 2026-01-05 -> actionTimestamp `2026-09-25T19:09:51Z`.
failure_scenario: At 10:00 the user late-logs the 08:00 dose, mistypes 20:00 and taps Log Dose. The row says 'Taken at 20:00', ten hours from now. Or the user clears the field while back-filling January 5 and taps Log Dose: the January dose's actionTimestamp becomes today, Sep 25.
suggested_fix: Disable Log Dose when the value is empty or invalid. Pass a max (now, for today's slots) and reject a combined timestamp later than Date.now() in takeDose and editDoseTime.
verifier_corrections: The line citations are slightly off. In retroactive-time-picker.tsx the input is at line 50, not 32 (line 32 is a comment), and the onClick/onConfirm is at lines 66-70, not 49. The spread cited as schedule-view.tsx:221 is actually at line 233, and the service-level executeMarkAll equivalent is at dose-log-service.ts:699. The substance of the finding is correct.

These are additions rather than errors in the finding:
- The same picker is used in dose-row.tsx (take and edit), bulk-dose-edit-dialog.tsx, prescription-card.tsx (PRN doses) and dose-detail-dialog.tsx, so the missing validation affects more places than the four files listed.
- In the edit path, the rejection is caught by neither the mutation hook nor the handler, so it becomes an unhandled promise rejection rather than a caught error.

title: Past-date Mark All and row Take default the picker to the current clock time, not the scheduled time (the detail drawer uses the scheduled time)
description: On a past date, both Mark All and the row's Take always open RetroactiveTimePicker with `defaultTime={getCurrentTimeHHMM()}`. The dose-detail drawer opens the same picker with `defaultTime={slot.localTime}`. Three entry points for the same action back-fill different default times. Accepting the pre-filled value on the Schedule screen records the dose at today's clock time on the old date, which can be hours away from when it was scheduled.
evidence: schedule-view.tsx:343 `defaultTime={getCurrentTimeHHMM()}` (Mark All picker, used for past dates at :259). dose-row.tsx:164 `defaultTime={getCurrentTimeHHMM()}` (used for past dates at :55). dose-detail-dialog.tsx:276 `defaultTime={slot.localTime}`.
failure_scenario: At 22:30 the user opens yesterday, taps Mark All on the 08:00 group and hits Log Dose without editing. All of yesterday's morning doses are recorded as 'Taken at 22:30', 14.5 hours after the actual time, which misleads any timing or interaction review.
suggested_fix: For past dates, default to the slot or group scheduled time, as the detail drawer does. Use 'now' only for late doses today.
verifier_corrections: Nothing material is wrong. One addition: prescription-card.tsx:278 also defaults its RetroactiveTimePicker to getCurrentTimeHHMM(), which makes a fourth entry point. The row Take picker opens for late doses today as well as for past dates, and defaulting to "now" is reasonable in the late-today case.

One detail is slightly off, and it points to a related, separate bug. The detail drawer does not treat the chosen time the same way as the other two entry points. `handleRetroactiveTakeConfirm` (dose-detail-dialog.tsx:64-74) passes the selected time as `time`, which is the scheduled-slot key, instead of as `takenAtTime`. The Schedule screen passes it as `takenAtTime`. If the user edits the time in the drawer, the log is keyed to a different scheduled time rather than having its taken-at timestamp set. So the drawer's "scheduled-time default" happens to be correct mainly because it rewrites the slot key. The three entry points differ in which field the value goes into, not only in the default. The finding's core claim is still accurate.

title: Untake or Undo on a past date turns a 'missed' slot into a permanent 'pending' one (a pending log row is written and synced)
description: untakeDose never removes the log. It upserts it with status 'pending'. deriveStatus returns 'pending' for any pending log regardless of date, and only slots with no log become 'missed'. So Un-take All in the bulk drawer, detail-drawer UNTAKE, or the undo toast on a back-filled dose permanently change a past slot from 'missed' to 'pending'. The row loses its amber missed styling. It also writes a synced 'pending' dose log that other consumers (server, MCP) will see as a real record.
evidence: dose-log-service.ts:508 `const doseLog = await upsertDoseLog(prescriptionId, phaseId, scheduleId, date, time, "pending");`. dose-schedule-service.ts:70 `if (log.status === "pending") return "pending";` (checked before the `dateStr < todayStr` → 'missed' branch). Scratch test: 3 days ago, status before `missed`, take+untake -> `after untake pending`.
failure_scenario: The user back-fills last Monday's evening dose by mistake and taps Undo on the toast, or opens the Edit All drawer and taps UN-TAKE. Monday's slot now shows as a neutral 'pending' instead of 'missed', and a 'pending' row for last Monday syncs to the server.
suggested_fix: On untake, soft-delete the log (or restore the exact status it had before), so that deriveStatus can apply the date-based pending/missed rule again. Alternatively, have deriveStatus map a 'pending' log on a past date to 'missed'.
verifier_corrections: Minor clarification: the undo toast that triggers this is the Mark All undo in schedule-view.tsx (executeMarkAll). It is not specifically a back-fill flow, but the effect is the same on any past date. The slot stays actionable, so the user can still take it later. The harm is the wrong status and styling plus the extra synced row, not lost dose information.

Nothing material is wrong. The finding cites a scratch-test result as evidence, but that test was not in the tree to re-run; I confirmed the behaviour from the code alone. The damage is mostly how the slot is shown: it can still be re-taken, and I found no adherence calculation that uses "missed". Related case: rescheduleDose (dose-log-service.ts:657) also writes "pending" logs, which could hide a past slot's missed status in the same way.

title: Progress banner counts skipped (and rescheduled) doses as done, 'All done for today!' with 0 taken, while analytics adherence counts them as 0
description: computeProgress computes pct and allDone from taken+skipped. deriveStatus also maps 'rescheduled' logs to 'skipped'. The banner text says '{taken}/{total} taken' next to a percentage that includes skips, and it shows the celebratory 'All done for today!' when every dose was skipped. adherenceRate counts only status==='taken' over total. The same day therefore shows 100%/All done on the Schedule screen and 0% in analytics. PRN doses are left out of both, so they agree there.
evidence: medication-ui-utils.ts:156 `const handled = taken + skipped; const pct = ... Math.round((handled / total) * 100); const allDone = total > 0 && pending === 0;`. analytics-service.ts:297 `const dayTaken = filteredSlots.filter((s) => s.status === "taken").length;`. Scratch test (one slot skipped today): progress `{"taken":0,"skipped":1,"pct":100,"allDone":true}` vs adherence `0`.
failure_scenario: The user skips all 4 doses today because of side effects. The banner shows a green 'All done for today! 0/4 doses taken'. With 1 taken and 1 skipped out of 4, it reads '1/4 taken' next to a '50%' bar. Analytics reports 0% or 25% for the same day.
suggested_fix: Show separate taken and skipped counts, and base the percentage (and the 'All done' wording) on taken only, or on 'handled' with that label. Share one definition with adherenceRate.
verifier_corrections: The finding is right that "All done for today!" shows with 0 taken when every dose is skipped, and that "N/total taken" sits next to a percentage that includes skips. It is wrong that analytics shows the same day as 0%. `adherenceRate` is only shown as a per-prescription, per-titration-phase-range badge in titration-tab.tsx, and there is no per-day analytics view to set against the banner. Counting skips as handled is deliberate, as the unit tests at medication-ui-utils.test.ts:200-207 show, so this is a labelling issue rather than a logic bug. Severity should drop from medium to low.

- **Presented as broken logic:** the handled-based pct and allDone are intentional. The comment at dose-schedule-service.ts:69 and the unit and property tests in medication-ui-utils.test.ts and medication-ui-utils.property.test.ts assert exactly this behaviour.
- **Presented as a data inconsistency:** the Schedule banner ("handled today") and analytics adherence ("taken / scheduled") are different metrics, so it isn't a data or analytics inconsistency. The real defect is copy and labelling. "{taken}/{total} taken" is paired with a percentage that includes skipped and rescheduled doses, and the celebratory "All done" state appears with 0 taken.
- **Severity:** lower it from medium to low. No stored or analytic data is wrong, and the taken count shown to the user is accurate.

title: Undo toast is tied to a slot key, not to a log id or state: it reverses later actions, and a second action's toast drops the first action's Undo
description: onUndo closes over (prescription, phase, schedule, date, localTime) and calls untakeDose, which forces whatever log is there now back to 'pending'. If the user changes the dose in the 5-second window (for example, Skip with a reason from the detail drawer), Undo discards that change silently. TOAST_LIMIT is 1, so any later toast (another Take, 'time updated', a Skip All confirmation) replaces the Undo toast of the earlier action. The Mark All undo fires N untakes without awaiting them or checking the result.
evidence: schedule-view.tsx:133 `onUndo: () => { untakeDoseMut.mutateAsync({ prescriptionId: slot.prescriptionId, ... time: slot.localTime, ... }); }` (not awaited, no log id). :227 `for (const s of pendingSlots) { untakeDoseMut.mutateAsync({...}); }`. use-toast.ts:6 `const TOAST_LIMIT = 1;`.
failure_scenario: The user takes Metoprolol, which shows an Undo toast. They realise it was the wrong row, open it and SKIP it. The toast is still showing and they tap Undo: the skip is gone and the slot is 'pending'. Or they take A and then B within 5 seconds: A's Undo toast is replaced, so A can no longer be undone from the toast.
suggested_fix: Bind undo to the returned DoseLog id(s) and to the state before the action, and only revert if the log still matches. Allow more than one toast, or merge undo actions.
verifier_corrections: The cited lines and the behaviour are accurate. The severity is overstated: the impact is limited to a 5-second window and nothing is lost for good. Any lost Undo can be done by hand from the dose detail dialog. The discarded skip leaves the dose 'pending', and inventory stays consistent because untakeDose only restores stock when the log was 'taken'. Low fits better than medium. Minor detail: in the Take handlers the onUndo call starts at lines 133-134, and the Mark All loop is at line 226, not 227.

The scenario's "Skip with a reason from the detail drawer" is slightly wrong. The drawer's SKIP (dose-detail-dialog.tsx handleSkip) sends no reason. Skip-with-reason is the row's Skip button, which only appears for pending or missed rows (dose-row.tsx:43 isActionable), so it can't be used right after Take. The bug is the same with the drawer's reasonless skip. In the evidence, the Mark All undo loop starts at about schedule-view.tsx:226-227, and showUndoToast is called at :224.

title: Bulk actions are not atomic and a failure is invisible: completed slots stay taken or untaken, with no error and no undo
description: takeAllDoses, skipAllDoses and editAllDoseTimes give each slot its own transaction and collect errors. unwrap then throws after the earlier slots have been committed. In executeMarkAll the showUndoToast call comes after the await, so on any error the completed slots stay taken with no Undo. handleMarkAll and handleMarkAllTimeConfirm call executeMarkAll without await or catch, so the rejection only reaches the silent unhandled-rejection logger. handleUntakeAll awaits each slot in turn and stops at the first failure: later slots stay taken, the drawer stays open and no toast is shown. Missing inventory or insufficient stock never fails a take, because negative stock is allowed. Realistic triggers are Dexie errors such as a closed or severed database or quota errors.
evidence: dose-log-service.ts:681 `Each dose gets its own transaction — one failure does not block others.` ... :706 `return err(`Failed to take ${errors.length} dose(s)...`)`. schedule-view.tsx:264 `executeMarkAll(time, pendingSlots);` and :272 `executeMarkAll(markAllTarget.time, markAllTarget.slots, takenAtTime);` (no await or catch). bulk-dose-edit-dialog.tsx:76 `for (const s of takenSlots) { await untakeMut.mutateAsync({...}); }`.
failure_scenario: The database connection drops partway through Mark All on a 5-dose group. Slots 1–2 are recorded as taken with stock deducted, slots 3–5 are not, and the user sees no toast of any kind. They assume everything was logged or nothing was, and they have no Undo for the two that were written.
suggested_fix: Run all slots in a single Dexie transaction so the batch is all-or-nothing, or catch the error and show a toast saying which slots failed, plus an undo for the ones that succeeded.
verifier_corrections:
All cited lines and code quotes are accurate, and each described code path exists. Two small points:
1. `handleSkipAll` and `handleEditRecordConfirm` in bulk-dose-edit-dialog.tsx fail the same way (no try/catch; the drawer stays open with no toast), yet the finding only calls out `handleUntakeAll`.
2. The trigger is narrower than the medium rating implies. `takeDose`, `skipDose` and `untakeDose` have no validation paths that return `err`; only exceptions caught from Dexie do. The failure therefore needs a rare IndexedDB fault, not any realistic user input, so severity is closer to low.

The facts are right. The only change is severity: the triggers are limited to IndexedDB/Dexie infrastructure errors, because takeDose has no business-rule error returns, so this is a latent low-severity issue rather than medium. Minor additions: handleSkipAll and handleEditRecordConfirm in bulk-dose-edit-dialog.tsx also await without try/catch, so they fail silently in the same way (the drawer stays open and no toast is shown). There is no global mutation error handler in query-client.ts to catch any of these.

title: 'Skip All' in the Edit All drawer converts already-taken doses to skipped and restores their stock, with no confirmation, reason or undo
description: The bulk drawer is only reachable through 'Edit All', which appears only when the group has no pending slots and at least one taken. Its SKIP ALL targets every non-skipped slot, which means the taken ones. skipDose reverses their stock. No reason is recorded and no undo toast is shown. The single-row Skip requires a reason picker. The detail drawer's SKIP records no reason either, and because upsert only merges fields, an old skipReason left over from an earlier skip reappears.
evidence: time-slot-group.tsx:87 `{!isFuture && !hasPending && hasTaken && (<Button ... onClick={() => onEditAll(time, slots)}>Edit All`. bulk-dose-edit-dialog.tsx:59 `const target = slots.filter((s) => s.status !== "skipped");` then `skipAllMut.mutateAsync({ entries: ..., date, time })` (no reason). dose-detail-dialog.tsx:93 `skipMut.mutateAsync({... dosageMg })` (no reason). schedule-view.tsx:185 row skip goes through SkipReasonPicker.
failure_scenario: The user opens 'Edit All' on the 08:00 group to fix the recorded time and taps the leftmost button, SKIP ALL. Every dose they took is now 'Skipped' with no reason and the pills are back in stock. Adherence drops, and there is no undo.
suggested_fix: Limit bulk skip to pending or missed slots, or ask for confirmation and a reason through SkipReasonPicker. Show an undo toast, and clear skipReason when the status changes.
verifier_corrections: Putting stock back on SKIP ALL is not itself a defect: a dose converted from taken to skipped should return its pills to inventory. The defects are the missing confirmation and undo, the missing reason (the row Skip uses SkipReasonPicker, this path does not), and the stale skipReason that reappears because upsertDoseLog only merges fields. The 'misclick' failure scenario is plausible but depends on user error. A detail the finding missed: SKIP ALL uses the group-level `date`/`time`, while UN-TAKE uses each slot's own `scheduledDate`/`localTime`.

The finding overstates one point. Returning pills to stock when a taken dose is skipped is deliberate, documented behaviour ("If previously taken, reverses stock adjustment"), and the inventory stays correct. That part is not data corruption.

The real problems are these:
- A destructive action is always enabled, labelled SKIP ALL, and placed first in the drawer, with no confirmation, reason or undo. Single-row skip, by contrast, requires a reason.
- A leftover skipReason can reappear, because upsert never clears it. This part is a genuine data inconsistency, and it also affects the detail drawer.

The failure scenario, where a user wanting "Edit Record" taps SKIP ALL instead, depends on a mis-tap. The button is clearly labelled, so this is a UX/consistency issue rather than a logic bug. Medium severity is at the upper bound.

title: Retroactive picker resets the user's typed time whenever the parent re-renders after the minute changes
description: The reset effect depends on `[open, defaultTime]`, and callers pass `getCurrentTimeHHMM()`, which is evaluated on every render. While the dialog is open, any re-render of ScheduleView or DoseRow after the clock minute changes produces a new defaultTime. That happens on every Dexie change seen by useLiveQuery, including a sync pull or a write from another card. The effect then overwrites the selectedTime the user entered with the current time.
evidence: retroactive-time-picker.tsx:24 `useEffect(() => { if (open) { setSelectedTime(defaultTime); } }, [open, defaultTime]);`. dose-row.tsx:164 `defaultTime={getCurrentTimeHHMM()}`.
failure_scenario: At 10:14 the user opens the late-dose picker and types 07:30. Before they tap Log Dose the minute rolls to 10:15 and a background sync pull re-renders the schedule. The field jumps back to 10:15, and if they don't notice, the dose is logged at 10:15.
suggested_fix: Reset only when the dialog goes from closed to open (track the previous open value with a ref), or capture defaultTime once when it opens.
verifier_corrections: The effect is at retroactive-time-picker.tsx lines 34-38, not line 24; line 24 is the `defaultTime` prop in the destructuring. Everything else in the finding is accurate. The second picker in DoseRow, the edit-time one, uses `takenAtDisplay` and is only affected if that value changes, so the bug is limited to the late-dose picker and the Mark All picker.

title: Recalculation after a trip spanning the DST change permanently moves the dose to the wrong wall-clock time and overwrites the `time` field
description: recalculateScheduleTimezones decodes the stored scheduleTimeUTC with the anchor's CURRENT offset (getTimezoneOffsetMinutes uses `new Date()`), not the offset in force when the schedule was encoded. It then writes the decoded wall-clock into `time` and moves the anchor. After the DST change, the one-hour drift that was previously only a display error is written into the record as the user's intended time. The original 08:00 is lost from both `time` and the anchor, so a future DST fix that re-derives the time from `time` plus the anchor cannot recover it. This is distinct from the known generic drift, which leaves `time` intact.
failure_scenario: A Berlin user with an 08:00 Entresto dose goes to London on 20 Oct and taps 'Adjust Schedules', which is correct. They return on 1 Nov and tap 'Adjust Schedules' again. From then on the dose is scheduled, displayed and reminded at 07:00. The edit drawer and schedule list (which read `time`) also say 07:00, so nothing in the app still records 08:00.
suggested_fix: Treat `time` plus anchorTimezone as the source of truth. Recalculation should only change the anchor and recompute scheduleTimeUTC from `time` (never decode UTC back into `time`). Longer term, store wall-clock plus IANA zone and resolve to an instant per date, using the offset for that date.
verifier_corrections: One nuance that makes the finding stronger. Just before the second 'Adjust Schedules' tap on 1 Nov, the display was actually correct: anchor London with UTC 420, shown on a Berlin (CET +60) device, gives 08:00. So the recalculation does not just lock in an existing drift. It breaks a state that was showing the right time. Otherwise the cited lines, code quotes and arithmetic are accurate.

The trigger is broader than the finding says. It does not need a round trip that spans the DST change. A single recalculation after the anchor zone's offset has changed since the schedule was encoded is enough. For example, a schedule created in Berlin summer time, followed by one 'Adjust Schedules' tap to London after 25 Oct, stores 07:00 straight away. Minor note: the scratch test's console logs were not shown in the filtered output, but the `expect(b.time).toBe('07:00')` assertion passed.

The trigger is broader than "a trip spanning the DST change." Accepting any timezone adjustment while the anchor zone is in a different DST season from when the schedule was encoded corrupts `time`. For example, a schedule created in summer in Berlin and adjusted for a winter trip to London: 360 + 60 decodes to 07:00 immediately. A round trip is not needed. The finding also slightly understates the existing baseline: getDailyDoseSchedule already shows 07:00 after DST even for users who never travel. What this bug adds is that the drift gets written into `time` and can no longer be recovered, not that the displayed time is wrong.

title: Two devices in different timezones ping-pong the schedule anchor through sync; the other device silently shifts doses by an hour and falsely claims the user travelled
description: Detection is per device. It compares every schedule's anchorTimezone with that device's Intl zone by IANA name and knows nothing about other devices. Accepting rewrites scheduleTimeUTC and the anchor, bumps updatedAt and pushes. The other device then pulls the rows (plain bulkPut) and renders them with its own zone via formatLocalTime(scheduleTimeUTC, deviceTz). The pull path does not re-run detection. The prompt only reappears on the next visibilitychange or reload, and then says 'traveled from Johannesburg to Berlin'. Accepting it flips the anchor back, and the cycle repeats forever. Detection also fires between zones with identical offsets (Berlin and Johannesburg in summer), so every session prompts even when times are equal.
evidence:
const hasMismatch = anchorTimezones.some((tz) => tz !== deviceTz);

Scratch test at 2026-11-02: schedule 08:00 Europe/Berlin; laptop recalculateScheduleTimezones('Africa/Johannesburg') -> anchor JHB, UTC 360, time '08:00', queue [phaseSchedules:upsert, auditLogs:upsert]; phone getDailyDoseSchedule('2026-11-02','Europe/Berlin') -> localTime ['07:00'] while `time` field is '08:00'.
failure_scenario: After 25 Oct: the phone is in Berlin and the laptop's OS zone is Africa/Johannesburg. The laptop prompts 'traveled from Berlin to Johannesburg', and the user taps Adjust. The phone syncs: its dose list now shows 07:00 (while the med card and edit drawer still show 08:00), and native or in-app reminders follow whichever field they read. On the next resume the phone prompts 'traveled from Johannesburg to Berlin'. Each accept on either device rewrites and re-pushes every schedule. A dose taken on the laptop is also logged with scheduledTime '09:00' and the phone's with '08:00', which hits the known time-string lookups.
suggested_fix: Make the travel decision a user-level, synced setting ('home timezone' plus the time it was last confirmed) rather than inferring it per device from the schedule anchors. Only prompt when this device's zone differs from the synced home zone. Never auto-apply from a secondary device, and re-run detection after a pull only against the synced setting.
verifier_corrections: This needs two devices whose OS timezones differ at the same time; a single device travelling works correctly. Same-offset zones prompt only once per real anchor change on a single device; the "every session" behaviour exists only in the multi-device ping-pong. The prompt is not strictly false, because that device's zone really does differ from the anchor. Severity is overstated: there is no data loss, only a display shift and card/list time disagreement on the other device, so medium rather than high. The quoted scratch-test output could not be re-run (the directory was deleted per the rules), but the code path it describes checks out.

- **Severity is overstated.** The UTC instant is preserved and each device shows it correctly on its own clock, so there is no silent data corruption. The real damage is the repeating false "travelled" prompt, the `time` vs `localTime` mismatch (08:00 in the card vs 07:00 in the dose list), and scheduledTime strings that differ by device.
- **Line reference is off by one.** The `formatLocalTime` call is at `dose-schedule-service.ts:187`, not 188.
- **The trigger is broader than travel.** Any schedule create or edit re-stamps `anchorTimezone` with the editing device's zone (`medication-schedule-service.ts:133`, `phase-service.ts`, `titration-service.ts`), which starts the same cross-device prompt loop.

"Cycle repeats forever" requires two devices that sit in different OS timezones at the same time and a user who taps Adjust on both. For a single user that is uncommon. The typical case is a single mis-directed prompt after travel, and every rewrite requires an explicit tap (Dismiss suppresses it for the session). The "07:00 on phone" display is the absolute-time rendering of an anchor the user explicitly accepted on the other device. It is not silent corruption. Severity should be medium, not high.

title: Editing any prescription on a device in another timezone re-anchors that prescription's schedules without a prompt, splitting doses that were taken together
description: The edit drawer always sends every schedule row with its `time` string (the home wall-clock). updatePhase then re-encodes each one with the CURRENT device zone and sets anchorTimezone to that zone, even if the user changed only the food instruction or unit. After tapping 'Not Now' abroad, or on a second device that sits in another zone, this silently applies the travel adjustment to only the one edited prescription. The others stay on home time, which the dose list shows converted into local time.
failure_scenario: A Berlin user in New York taps 'Not Now', so the dose list shows both morning meds at 02:00. They edit Med A's food note and save. Med A now shows 08:00 while Med B still shows 02:00. Back home, the next prompt converts each schedule separately, and Med A lands at 14:00 Berlin. On a laptop that sits in Johannesburg, simply editing a note re-anchors the prescription to Johannesburg and pushes it to the phone.
suggested_fix: Only recompute scheduleTimeUTC and the anchor when the time actually changed, and encode it in the schedule's existing anchorTimezone, not the device zone. Travel re-anchoring should happen only through the explicit recalculation flow.
verifier_corrections:
The 'back home' consequence is wrong. recalculateScheduleTimezones (timezone-recalculation-service.ts) converts scheduleTimeUTC into the old anchor zone to get the wall-clock time, then re-encodes that same wall-clock time in the new zone. Med A's New York 08:00 therefore becomes Berlin 08:00, not 14:00. Med B is already anchored to Berlin, so the recalculation filter skips it. Both meds line up again at home once the user taps Adjust.

The Johannesburg-laptop case is also not fully silent. When the phone opens, use-timezone-detection sees the Johannesburg anchor and shows a confusing 'traveled from Johannesburg' prompt. If the user taps Adjust, the dose goes back to 08:00 local. Only 'Not Now' leaves it shifted by the zone offset.

The fix is still valid: only re-encode when the time changed, and use the schedule's existing anchorTimezone.

The "Med A lands at 14:00 Berlin" outcome is wrong. The recalculation keeps each schedule's wall clock as read in its own anchorTimezone, so after returning home and accepting the prompt, Med A goes back to 08:00 Berlin. The inconsistency lasts only while the device is in the other zone, or until the user accepts the prompt. The bug is also mainly in updatePhase (phase-service.ts:281-292). updateSchedule re-anchors only when `time` is in the update payload. Severity should be medium, not high.

The code fact and the within-trip split are correct. The claim that Med A "lands at 14:00 Berlin" back home is wrong: recalculateScheduleTimezones keeps the wall-clock time (it converts from the schedule's own anchor), so confirming the home prompt puts Med A back at 08:00. The re-anchor only persists if the user dismisses the prompt, which comes back every session. In the Johannesburg laptop example the shift is 0h in summer and 1h in winter, and the phone prompts afterwards. Severity should be medium, not high. The suggested fix is still sound: recompute scheduleTimeUTC only when the time changes, and encode it in the schedule's existing anchorTimezone.

title: Push-reminder server timezone is overwritten by whichever device last synced, and is not re-sent after an in-session 'Adjust Schedules'
description: sync-schedule sends the device's raw Intl zone and stores it per user (`WHERE user_id = ...`). The de-duplication hash includes only the entries (local HH:MM plus meds), not the timezone. After an in-session adjustment, localTime stays '08:00', the hash is unchanged, and the server keeps the old zone until a reload. With two devices, each one's sync overwrites the single per-user timezone with its own zone.
failure_scenario: The user lands in New York with the PWA resumed from background and taps Adjust. The server still holds Europe/Berlin with a timeSlot of '08:00', so the /api/push/check reminder fires at 02:00 New York time. With two devices, the Johannesburg laptop's sync makes the '08:00' reminders fire at 08:00 SAST, which is 07:00 in Berlin in winter. The impact is limited while the known 'push never fires in background' issue stands.
suggested_fix: Include the timezone in the hash. Store the reminder timezone as the synced home zone, not per-device Intl, or key it per subscription.
verifier_corrections: Push is only evaluated when an open client pings /api/push/check every 60 seconds. So a stale zone mostly causes missed or skipped reminders while the app is open, not a notification firing at 02:00 New York time, which would need the app open at 02:00. Also, push_subscriptions has one row per user, so the endpoint is also last-writer-wins across devices. The timezone overwrite is one part of a wider single-subscription-per-user design, not a separate defect.

The two-device overwrite scenario is wrong. Each device sends its entries and timezone together, and the entries are already converted from scheduleTimeUTC into that device's zone, so the pair on the server is always consistent. A Johannesburg laptop syncs '09:00' plus Africa/Johannesburg, not '08:00'. Only the in-session Adjust path causes a problem: the hash leaves out the timezone, and the Dexie live query does not re-run when the app resumes. That path also depends on no Dexie write happening in between, and it clears on reload. Reminders only fire from the in-app 60s ping (no cron is wired to /api/push/send), so severity should drop to low.

title: 'Not Now' is remembered only for the JS session: re-prompts on every launch, and there is no way to keep home-time dosing
description: Dismissal is a module-level boolean that resets on reload or cold start. Nothing persists the decision, so a user who deliberately keeps home-time dosing on a short trip (or has a second device in another zone) is prompted at every app start. One tap on the primary 'Adjust Schedules' button rewrites every schedule and pushes the change to all devices. Meanwhile the dismissed device's dose list shows home-time doses converted into local time (08:00 becomes 02:00), while the schedule cards read `time` and show 08:00.
failure_scenario: On a 4-day trip to New York the user taps 'Not Now' to stay on Berlin time. The Android app, which cold-starts often, re-prompts every launch. A mis-tap moves all doses by 6 hours on every device. During the trip the dose list says 02:00 while the medication card says 08:00.
suggested_fix: Persist the decision (for example a synced 'dismissedFor: {deviceTz, anchorTz}' entry) and offer an explicit 'Keep home times' choice. Show the same time in the list and the cards.
verifier_corrections:
These are minor points; none of them changes the verdict.
- The session-only reset is a deliberate design choice (the D-07 comment), not an accident. The real defect is that no choice to keep home time is ever stored.
- The mis-tap scenario is speculative, but the rewrite does sync to every device as described.
- The list-versus-card mismatch is the strongest user-visible part of the finding. It happens whenever the prompt is dismissed, not only on Android.

Minor points only:
- The "mis-tap" part of the failure scenario is speculative. The rewrite needs an explicit tap on "Adjust Schedules", and the result matches what the dialog says it will do (same clock times in the new timezone).
- Session-only dismissal is documented as intentional (D-07). It is a design flaw, not an accidental bug.
- The part about the dose list and cards disagreeing (02:00 vs 08:00) holds whether or not the user dismisses the dialog. It only depends on the device timezone differing from the schedule's anchor timezone.

title: After a dismissal the device-timezone cache is never refreshed for the rest of the session
description: checkTimezoneChange returns before clearTimezoneCache() once the session flag is set, and the hook is the only caller of clearTimezoneCache. A long-lived PWA or WebView session that crosses a second timezone keeps the first cached zone. That stale zone is used for dose-list rendering, new schedule anchors, and the timezone stamped on new records. The push sync and some other code read Intl directly, so the device disagrees with itself.
failure_scenario: The user dismisses the prompt during a Dubai layover, keeps the app backgrounded, and lands in Singapore. The dose list still renders in Dubai time, and a schedule added now is anchored to Asia/Dubai, 4 hours off from what the user typed.
suggested_fix: Always call clearTimezoneCache() on visibility or resume, independent of the dismissal flag.
verifier_corrections: The finding is accurate, with two small caveats. First, the stale cache only occurs after the mismatch prompt has been shown and dismissed, which requires enabled schedules. Second, the "4 hours off" figure is specific to the Dubai-to-Singapore example (UTC+4 to UTC+8); the size of the error depends on the difference between the two zones. Separately, a stale cache also depends on no visibilitychange firing before the prompt is shown. That is related but outside this finding.

title: Recalculation and detection include soft-deleted schedules and schedules of completed or deleted phases; tombstones are rewritten, counted and re-pushed
description: Both filters are `s.enabled === true` only, and soft-deletes never clear `enabled`. Tombstoned schedules and schedules of completed titration phases are therefore rewritten (anchor, UTC, `time`, updatedAt), included in the audit 'schedulesUpdated' count, and re-enqueued as 'upsert'. A pending 'delete' queue op is flipped to 'upsert' with attempts reset. The server does not bring them back because the pushed row still carries deletedAt, so there is no resurrection. But a tombstone pulled from another device, anchored in another zone, is enough to raise the 'you've traveled' prompt even when no live schedule differs.
evidence:
const activeSchedules = allSchedules.filter((s) => s.enabled === true && s.anchorTimezone !== newTimezone);

Scratch test: schedule with deletedAt=1000 plus a queued delete (attempts 3) -> recalc returned 1, deletedAt 1000, anchor America/New_York, updatedAt bumped, queue ['upsert/0'].
failure_scenario: The user deleted an old titration on the Johannesburg-zoned laptop after it had re-anchored. The phone pulls the tombstone, and on next resume shows 'traveled from Johannesburg to Berlin' although every live schedule is already Berlin. Accepting re-pushes every historical schedule and reports a misleading count.
suggested_fix: Filter `deletedAt === null`. Restrict detection and recalculation to schedules of non-deleted phases whose status is 'active' or 'pending' on active prescriptions.
verifier_corrections: Minor clarification only: the stray prompt appears when any enabled schedule, whether deleted or belonging to a completed phase, is anchored in a zone other than the device's. It does not need to come from another device; old local schedules from completed phases do the same. The description is otherwise accurate.

title: With mixed anchors the dialog names only one origin zone and says 'traveled' for zones the user was never in
description: The math is done per schedule from its own anchor, so mixed anchors convert correctly. But the dialog shows only the first mismatched anchor (Set insertion order), and it promises that '08:00 stays 08:00' for all doses. In reality each schedule keeps the wall-clock of its own anchor, so schedules created or edited in different zones keep their different effective times.
evidence:
const mismatchedTz = anchorTimezones.find((tz) => tz !== deviceTz);
setOldTimezone(mismatchedTz ?? "");
failure_scenario: Schedules are anchored in Berlin and New York (after an edit abroad). Back in Johannesburg, the dialog says 'traveled from Berlin to Johannesburg'. The New York-anchored schedule, which shows 14:00 locally before adjusting, becomes 08:00 while the user expects nothing about it to change.
suggested_fix: List every distinct anchor with the resulting before and after times per medication in the dialog, or normalise all anchors to a single home zone.
verifier_corrections: The part that holds is that the dialog names only one origin zone (the first mismatched anchor) when schedules have mixed anchors, and says "traveled from" a zone the user may not have come from. The failure scenario is exaggerated. The recalculation keeps each schedule's own anchor wall-clock time, and most medication views already show that time from `s.time`. So a New York-anchored schedule shows 08:00 both before and after the adjustment, consistent with the dialog's "08:00 stays 08:00" wording. Only the device-timezone daily schedule view (dose-schedule-service.ts:188) changes from 14:00 to 08:00. This is a cosmetic, misleading-message issue, not an input-inconsistency or data problem.

title: Reconcile merges genuinely different drinks when they share any single word, silently deleting a real drink's hydration
description: describesSameThing returns true when the two descriptions share even one identifying token. Combined with the loose ±25% volume tolerance, a caffeine or alcohol drink absorbs any food item (the kind the prompt uses for milk, juice, smoothies and coconut water) whose name shares one word such as milk, orange, coffee, water or tonic. The absorbed item is filtered out before the review list is built. The user cannot un-merge it; they only see a line of muted text saying it was merged. The code comment says it fixed 'a coffee and a glass of milk', but that fix only holds when the coffee's description does not mention milk.
failure_scenario: The user says 'I had a coffee with milk and a glass of milk'. The review list shows one Caffeine row (250 ml). 250 ml of hydration is lost, and the milk's sugar and potassium are silently re-attributed to the coffee. Same outcome for 'a vodka and orange, then a glass of OJ' or 'a coffee and a coffee milkshake'.
suggested_fix: Require a stronger identity check before merging: the drink's full token set equal to, or a subset of, the food's (not just one shared token), plus exclude a food item whose own description names a container ('glass of X') that differs from the drink's head noun. Better still, never drop a row: render the proposed merge as a pre-rejected companion row the user can re-approve.
verifier_corrections: The mechanism, lines, quotes and failure scenarios are all accurate. The only overstatement is severity: this is an edge case in the voice-input path, not a broken core feature. The merge is reported in the reasoning text (not fully "silent"), so the user can notice it and re-log the drink manually. Recommend medium rather than high.

I lowered severity from high to medium. Voice is one input path among several. It needs the model to name the caffeine or alcohol drink with a shared word (e.g. "coffee with milk") and also emit a separate food drink. The merge is shown to the user as a text note, so it isn't fully silent, even though no UI lets them undo it. The exact-token logic and the data loss (fluid dropped, sugar and potassium re-attributed) are accurate. I did not re-run the vodka/orange and whisky/coconut-water cases, but they follow from the same single-token rule: they share "orange" and "water", and 250 vs 240 and 200 vs 250 are both within the 25% tolerance.

1. The loss is not completely silent. The merge note, which names the absorbed food description, is shown in the reasoning text of the review panel, so the user can re-log the item manually. The finding is right that the row itself cannot be restored.
2. Severity is overstated. It only triggers when a single voice transcript contains a caffeine or alcohol drink plus a liquid food item that share a word and have a similar volume. Medium fits better than high.
3. The mechanism, the reachability and the example scenarios all check out.

title: Merged or parsed drink solutes (sugar, sodium, potassium) are saved but never shown in the review row
description: CaffeineItem and AlcoholItem carry sugarG, sodiumMg and potassiumMg, which the prompt fills and reconcile grafts on from absorbed food items. The caffeine editor shows only Description, Caffeine (mg) and Volume. The alcohol editor shows only Description, % ABV and Volume. None of the solute fields appear, yet saveItem passes all three to logDrink. Sodium is not even gated by a tracker toggle. The review list is billed as the step where the user approves exactly what gets written, but for drinks it approves values the user can't see.
evidence: parsed-item-row.tsx caffeine case renders only <Field label="Caffeine (mg)"> and <Field label="Volume (ml)">; voice-panel.tsx: ...(item.sodiumMg !== undefined && { saltMg: item.sodiumMg }). Scratch DOM test (passing): parse [caffeine latte 250ml, food latte waterMl 250 sodiumMg 900 sugarG 12]. The row has no 'Sodium' or 'Sugar' text; after Approve all + Save, one salt intake of 900 mg is written.
failure_scenario: The parser (or a merged companion) over-estimates a latte's sodium at 900 mg. The user reviews the row, sees nothing wrong because sodium isn't shown, approves it, and 900 mg of sodium lands on a sodium-restricted user's daily total with no chance to correct it before saving.
