suggested_fix: Render Sugar (g, when the tracker is on), Sodium (mg) and Potassium (mg, when the tracker is on) fields on caffeine and alcohol rows, the same as the food editor does, and mark values that came from a merge.
verifier_corrections: The claim holds as stated. The only change is severity: high to medium, because the records are saved normally and can still be fixed after saving.

Severity is overstated: this is an input-review gap, not broken core logic or data corruption, so medium fits better than high. The point that sodium is "not even gated by a tracker toggle" doesn't really count against the code, since salt is a core tracker with no toggle; the real problem is only that it isn't shown. The merge is not fully silent: a text note says an entry was merged, but it doesn't show the values that were carried over. The line ranges are approximately right.

Severity should be medium, not high. The failure scenario depends on an unrealistic 900 mg sodium estimate for a latte. Typical hidden values are small, sugar and potassium are only written when their trackers are on, and records can be corrected after saving. The core claim holds: the caffeine and alcohol review rows hide sugar, sodium and potassium, and sodium is saved with no tracker gate. The merge-reasoning text does mention that a food item was merged, but it doesn't show the grafted values.

title: Reconcile misses real #322 splits (different names, plurals, milk-portion volume), so fluid is still double-counted
description: The backstop only catches a split when the drink and its food companion share an exact token and have comparable volumes. Tokens are not stemmed ('lattes' ≠ 'latte'). A companion that names the ingredient rather than the drink ('flat white' plus 'milk') never matches. A companion carrying only the milk portion (250 ml in a 350 ml latte) falls outside the 25% tolerance. Descriptions made only of stopwords ('a double', 'double shot') tokenize to nothing and never match. Two duplicate caffeine or alcohol items are never compared at all. None of these cases produces a warning.
evidence: Scratch tests (all passing, 0 warnings): 'flat white' 200 + food 'milk' 180 -> 2 items, 380 ml; 'two lattes' 500 + food 'latte' 500 -> 2 items, 1000 ml; 'latte' 350 + food 'latte milk' 250 -> 2 items, 600 ml; 'a double' 60 + food 'double shot' 60 -> 2 items; two identical caffeine 'latte' 250 -> 2 items, warnings []. Only the drink-vs-food pair is examined: `if (!candidate || candidate.kind !== "food") continue;`
failure_scenario: The model emits the issue-#322 shape for 'a flat white': a caffeine item of 200 ml plus a food item 'milk' of 180 ml. Both rows are shown with no warning, the user taps Approve all, and 380 ml of water is booked for one 200 ml drink.
suggested_fix: Stem or lemmatise tokens, treat known drink-component words (milk, cream, syrup) in a food item next to a milk-based caffeine drink as a companion candidate, emit a warning (not a silent pass) for any food item with waterMl next to a drink, and flag duplicate same-description drink items.
verifier_corrections:
The code-level claims are accurate, but the framing overstates the problem.
- The #322 split is now forbidden by the prompt (voice-parse.ts:28). Reconcile is only a backstop, so the failure needs the model to break that rule.
- Not merging "flat white" plus "milk" is intentional: it matches the "coffee and a glass of milk" case the code comment says must not be merged. Only a missing warning can fairly be called a gap.
- The user sees and approves every row, so nothing is double-booked silently.
- Two identical caffeine items may really be two drinks, so not flagging them is arguable rather than a bug.
Severity should be low, not medium.

The code behaviour is described correctly, but four things are overstated:

- **Not a regression.** The finding treats the failure as the issue-#322 shape still getting through. The current prompt (voice-parse.ts:28) explicitly forbids food or water companions for drinks, and drinks carry their own solute fields. The reconcile step is a deliberately conservative backstop.
- **The suggested fix undoes a documented design choice.** Merging 'milk' into a coffee reintroduces the 'coffee + glass of milk' false merge that the name-match requirement exists to prevent.
- **Nothing is saved without review.** Every row passes per-row review before saving.
- **Some examples are weak.** The stopword example ('a double' / 'double shot') is contrived. Flagging duplicate same-description drinks would conflict with legitimate 'two lattes' dictation.

Severity should be low, not medium.

title: Offline at save time: drinks and food are written but water, sodium, weight, BP, urination and defecation rows pause forever and the panel sticks in 'saving'
description: saveItem mixes two write styles. logDrink and addComposableEntry are plain async callbacks. The water, salt, weight, BP, urination and defecation kinds go through useMutation().mutateAsync, which under React Query's default networkMode 'online' pauses without resolving while the browser is offline. The commit loop awaits it with no timeout, so it never finishes. Everything before the paused row is committed, the stage stays 'saving', Save and Approve are disabled, and no failure toast appears. If the user closes the sheet, the paused mutation resumes when the device reconnects and writes the record with a timestamp taken at that later moment, which can fall on a different day. Nothing prevents the user from re-dictating in the meantime, which creates duplicates because there is no idempotency key. This is a voice-specific consequence of the known water-tab networkMode issue, and it's worse here because it leaves a half-committed batch.
evidence: case "water": await addIntake.mutateAsync({...}) vs case "alcohol": await logDrinkEntry({...}); query-client.ts sets no mutations.networkMode. Scratch DOM test (passing): items [alcohol beer 500, water 300], Approve all, onlineManager.setOnline(false), Save, wait 1.5 s -> water rows [500] only; the Save button is still disabled (stage 'saving').
failure_scenario: On a train, the user dictates 'a beer and 300 ml water and my weight is 80.2'. Parsing succeeds, then the connection drops and they tap Save. The beer is logged, but the panel spins indefinitely. They close it and dictate again. Once they're back online, the first water and weight rows appear hours later next to the second set.
suggested_fix: Set mutations: { networkMode: 'always' } (all writes go to local IndexedDB), or call the service functions directly in saveItem, the way drinks do. Stamp one timestamp per commit and pass it to every writer.
verifier_corrections: Two minor points; the substance of the finding is accurate. First, the stage stuck in 'saving' and the disabled Save/Approve buttons come from the component's own stage logic. I did not re-read the button JSX line by line, but the commit loop clearly never reaches the code that resets the stage. Second, the finding says the paused water/weight/etc. rows 'pause forever'. More precisely, they stay paused until the browser fires an 'online' event, then they resume and write with a late timestamp. The finding does describe this later, so there's no contradiction.

Minor corrections:
- **Which rows get stuck.** Only the first paused row pauses. The rows after it are never attempted, because the loop is blocked, not paused themselves. Rows before it, and drink or food rows that come before it, are committed.
- **When it can happen.** The connection has to drop after the AI parse succeeds, because parsing needs the network. That narrows the window compared with "offline at save time" in general.
- **Duplicates.** They depend on the user re-dictating the same items, so they are a consequence of user behaviour and not automatic.
- **Stuck state.** The finding says the stuck state lasts "forever". It actually ends on reconnect if the panel is still mounted: the loop continues and the rows then save with the later timestamps.

title: Review editors accept negative values, and a cleared required field becomes 0, which is saved as a real record
description: numberOrZero turns '' and any garbage into 0 and passes negative numbers through. Required fields (water ml, sodium mg, weight kg, systolic, diastolic, caffeine mg, ABV) are set with it, and the writers (addIntakeRecord, addWeightRecord, addBloodPressureRecord) do no validation. A negative water row subtracts from the day's hydration total. Clearing a field writes a 0-valued record instead of blocking the save. Only alcohol volume is rejected (by logDrink), and that rejection surfaces as a generic save failure.
failure_scenario: The user fat-fingers '-' while correcting a 250 ml water row to '-250' and saves. Today's water total drops by 250 ml. Clearing the weight field while retyping and then approving saves a 0 kg weight, which corrupts the weight chart.
suggested_fix: Validate in the row, disabling Approve when a required field is empty or ≤ 0 or outside the manual form's range, and add min/positivity guards in the add* service functions.
verifier_corrections:
The "cleared field" scenario is milder than described. The input is controlled, so clearing it immediately shows "0". The user can see the 0 before approving; it is not silent. It still saves as a real 0-valued record without being blocked, which is correct as stated.

The negative case comes from editing an existing value, e.g. inserting '-' in front of 250. Typing a lone '-' parses to 0, not a negative.

The claim that caffeine mg and ABV are "set with it" does not affect the main path. The confirmed writers are water, salt, weight and BP.

These are minor points. The caffeine path only calls logDrink when volumeMl > 0. Otherwise it saves the dose without volume, so a negative caffeine volume is dropped quietly instead of rejected. The caffeineMg and ABV fields were not re-checked in this pass. However, the pattern is the same, since caffeineMg goes unguarded into addSubstance or addComposableEntry. The finding's claim that there is no validation anywhere on the direct water, salt, weight and BP paths is accurate.

title: A merge keeps the drink's explicit 0 over the companion's real nutrient value
description: The merge copies the food's sugar, sodium or potassium only when the drink's field is `undefined`. The model routinely returns an explicit 0 for 'no added sugar' on the drink item, and in that case the food companion's value (the milk sugar, the whole reason it was emitted) is discarded.
evidence:
if (merged.sugarG === undefined && food.sugarG !== undefined) { merged.sugarG = food.sugarG; }
Scratch test (passing): caffeine latte {sugarG:0, potassiumMg:0} + food latte {sugarG:12, potassiumMg:380} -> merged sugarG 0, potassiumMg 0.
failure_scenario: For 'a latte', the parser returns a caffeine item with sugarG 0 plus a food 'latte' item with 12 g sugar. After the merge, 0 g of sugar is recorded, and the row doesn't show sugar, so the user can't notice.
suggested_fix: Treat 0 like undefined when merging (take the max of the two), or show both values to the user.
verifier_corrections: "Routinely returns an explicit 0" is unsupported. The prompt now forbids the companion food item and tells the model to put a latte's sugar (~12 g) on the caffeine item, so the scenario only happens when the model breaks both instructions at once. Two further gaps: the caffeine review row has no sugar or potassium field at all, so sugar the model puts directly on a caffeine item can never be seen or edited either; and the failure scenario overstates how often it happens.

title: Reconcile warnings are unanchored reasoning text and only fire on exact-ml equality
description: Warnings are surfaced by concatenating them into the model's reasoning paragraph, which is rendered in small muted text below all the rows. They aren't attached to the rows they refer to, and 'Approve all' approves both flagged rows without a prompt. The duplicate-water check requires `water.ml !== volume` to be false, so a 473 ml water next to a 500 ml beer (the parser's own rounding) produces no warning.
evidence: setReasoning([data.reasoning, ...merges, ...warnings].filter(Boolean).join(" ") || null); if (water.ml !== volume || water.note !== undefined) continue; Scratch test: beer 500 + water 473 -> warnings [].
failure_scenario: The user dictates a pint and the parser adds a redundant 473 ml water item. No warning appears, the user taps Approve all, and the fluid is double-counted.
suggested_fix: Render warnings on the affected rows (and leave those rows pending when Approve all is used), and apply the same tolerance used for food companions.
verifier_corrections: The "500 ml beer + 473 ml water (the parser's own rounding)" example is invented. The voice-parse prompt sets a pint to 568 ml, and nothing produces 473. Near-miss duplicates depend on the model returning inconsistent volumes. The exact-equality water check is an intentional design choice, documented at voice-reconcile.ts:172-179, not an oversight. It is unlike the food-companion match, which also requires the descriptions to match. The valid parts are that warnings are merged into the reasoning paragraph instead of shown on the rows, and that Approve all approves flagged rows without a prompt.

title: A misclassified item cannot be corrected: no kind change and no unit choice in the review list
description: Each row's editor is fixed to its parsed kind, and every volume field is ml-only with no oz or L option. If the parser returns 'glass of milk' as a water item (no sugar or potassium) or a juice as caffeine, the only fix is to reject the row and re-enter it in another card. Unit conversion is entirely delegated to the model; a user correcting '12 oz' has to convert it themselves.
evidence: switch (item.kind) { ... case "water": <Field label="Water (ml)"> ... } — no kind selector exists in ParsedItemRow.
failure_scenario: The user says 'a can of coke', the parser returns {kind:'water', ml:330}, and the user can't turn it into a caffeine or sugar drink, so its caffeine and 35 g of sugar are lost unless they re-log it manually.
suggested_fix: Add a kind selector that maps the shared fields across kinds (volume to ml or waterMl or volumeMl), and optionally a unit toggle on volume fields.
verifier_corrections: The coke example is hypothetical: it only happens if the model misclassifies the drink. It is also slightly off. Even if the user could switch the row to the caffeine kind, the caffeine editor (lines 296-332) has no Sugar field, even though the drink type defines `sugarG` (voice-types.ts:69-70). Sugar is only editable on the food kind.

title: Voice is the only path that writes urination rows with no amount, and analytics silently imputes 'medium' (300 ml)
description: The voice urination row offers a '—' option, and an unspecified amount is saved without amountEstimate. The manual urination card always records one. Analytics then treats a missing estimate as medium, so 'no estimate' becomes a fabricated 300 ml data point in the output charts.
evidence: ...(item.amountEstimate !== undefined && { amountEstimate: item.amountEstimate }) ; value: URINATION_ESTIMATE_ML[r.amountEstimate ?? "medium"] ?? 300
failure_scenario: The user dictates 'went to the toilet twice'. Two urination rows with no amount are saved, and the fluid-output analytics show 600 ml of output that was never estimated.
suggested_fix: Exclude rows without an estimate from volume analytics (count them separately), or require an amount before approving a voice urination row, matching the manual card.
verifier_corrections:
These are small precision fixes; the substance of the finding stands.
- **"Only path" wording:** voice is the only add UI that writes rows with no amount. Rows can also lack an amount from older data or synced records, and the edit dialog keeps a record's empty amount if it was already empty.
- **Missing detail:** the imputed "medium" (300 ml) does not match the manual default of "small" (150 ml).

title: Recording again after a partial-save failure discards the unsaved rows without warning
description: After a partial failure the stage returns to 'ready', which re-enables the recorder. handleRecorded immediately calls setRows([]), so the failed, approved rows and the saved/unsaved distinction are thrown away with no confirmation.
evidence: } else { setStage("ready"); } ... busy={stage === "transcribing" || stage === "parsing" || stage === "saving"} ... setError(null); setRows([]);
failure_scenario: The BP row fails to save because of an IndexedDB error. The user taps record to add one more item, and the failed BP reading disappears from the review list without ever having been saved.
suggested_fix: Block recording, or ask for confirmation, while approved-but-unsaved rows exist, or append the new parse to the existing rows.
verifier_corrections: This isn't specific to a partial-save failure. In the "ready" stage, recording again always replaces the whole list. That includes rows the user hasn't reviewed yet, and rows approved but never saved when no save was attempted. It looks like general replace-on-record behaviour, not a special failure path. The partial-failure case is just where it hurts most, because a reading the user already approved gets dropped silently. The cited lines match HEAD: 76-82 handleRecorded/setRows([]), 435-437 setStage("ready"), and 462-465 the busy prop.

title: Weight card silently snaps a typed weight to the increment grid, so the stored weight differs from what was typed
description: The direct-entry field on the Weight card passes a roundOnBlur that snaps the typed number to the nearest multiple of settings.weightIncrement. The +/- step size therefore also quantizes typed values. The settings screen allows any increment from 0.05 to 1 in 0.01 steps (e.g. 0.07, 0.3, 1). If the increment does not divide the reading evenly, an exact scale reading is changed before it is saved. There is no indication, beyond the displayed number changing after blur.
evidence: weight-card.tsx:199 `roundOnBlur={(v) => { const increment = settings.weightIncrement; const rounded = Math.round(v / increment) * increment; return Math.round(rounded * 100) / 100; }}`. Scratch DOM test (real WeightCard + Dexie). Typed then 'Record Weight': inc=0.07 typed=72 stored=72.03; inc=0.25 typed=72.1 stored=72; inc=1 typed=72.4 stored=72; inc=0.05 (default) typed=72.33 stored=72.35.
failure_scenario: A user sets the weight increment to 1 kg so the +/- buttons move faster, then types the scale reading 72.4. 72.00 kg is recorded. With a 0.07 increment, typing an exact 72 records 72.03 kg. Weight trends used to judge fluid retention end up off by up to half an increment on every typed entry.
suggested_fix: Remove roundOnBlur from the typed path. Only round to 2 decimal places (Math.round(v*100)/100). Keep increment snapping, if wanted at all, for the +/- buttons only.
verifier_corrections: The finding says the settings screen offers "0.01 steps". In fact the settings +/- buttons step by 0.05 (weight-settings-section.tsx:81-82); values like 0.07 are only reachable by typing, and the store accepts them because it rounds to 2 decimals. "Silently" overstates it: the display updates to the snapped value on blur, before the user taps Record. With the default 0.05 increment, typical scale readings are stored unchanged. The 72.33 example needs a 0.01-resolution scale. Severity should drop from high to medium.

Severity is overstated: at the default 0.05 increment the error is at most 0.025 kg, and large errors need a user-chosen coarse increment. 'No indication' is too strong: the snapped value appears in the large display before the user taps Record, though the app gives no explicit warning. The finding cites weight-settings-section.tsx:189 for the '0.01 steps', but the increment input is around lines 72-85 and uses step={0.05}. Values like 0.07 are only reachable by typing, because the store sanitizes to 2 decimals.

The code facts are correct. Severity is overstated. Under the default 0.05 increment the error is at most 0.025 kg, and scale readings in 0.1 or 0.05 steps are stored exactly. Meaningful distortion (up to half an increment, e.g. 0.5 kg at increment 1) only happens after the user raises the increment. The snapped value is also shown before the explicit Record press, so it is not completely silent. The "off on every typed entry" claim only holds for non-default increments or 0.01-precision readings. Downgrade to medium.

title: BP card accepts swapped systolic/diastolic and shows 'Grade 3 hypertension' with a negative pulse pressure
description: BloodPressureFormSchema validates systolic (50-300) and diastolic (20-200) independently. There is no check that systolic > diastolic. A reading entered in the wrong boxes is saved and becomes the headline 'latest'. getBPCategory then labels it from the diastolic band, and the pulse pressure is negative (shown in red). The edit path (buildUpdates) has no cross-check either.
evidence: Schema: `systolic: z.number(...).int(...).min(50...).max(300...)`, `diastolic: z.number(...).int(...).min(20...).max(200...)`. There is no .refine. `const pulsePressure = latestReading ? latestReading.systolic - latestReading.diastolic : null;`. Scratch DOM test: entering 80 / 120 saved 1 record, the header showed 'Grade 3 hypertension' and the pulse pressure showed '-40'.
failure_scenario: The user types 80 into Systolic and 120 into Diastolic. The reading is saved as 80/120 and the dashboard shows 'Grade 3 hypertension' plus a pulse pressure of -40 mmHg. The wrong reading also feeds analytics, exports and AI insights.
suggested_fix: Add a schema refine (systolic > diastolic, and optionally pulse pressure >= 10) to the add form, the card edit form and the records-tab edit. Offer a 'swap values?' prompt instead of saving silently.
verifier_corrections: Only minor issues. I did not verify the finding's claim about the "records-tab edit". The standalone edit form lives in edit-blood-pressure-dialog.tsx and takes string props. From what I saw it adds no cross-check, but I did not fully trace where its values are validated. The statement that the swapped reading feeds analytics, exports and AI insights is inferred, not traced. It is plausible, because every reader uses the same stored record.

Mostly accurate, with one addition: the card's inline edit validation (buildUpdates) is weaker than the finding says. It checks only > 0 and not NaN, so it also skips the 50-300 and 20-200 range limits the add form uses. I did not verify the claims about the records-tab edit or about downstream use in AI insights and exports. They are plausible, since there is no validation at the service layer, but I did not trace them.

title: 'Over target but inside the buffer' shows three different colours on three surfaces for the same total
description: computeTwoStageProgress returns isOverTarget and isOverExtended, but each surface reads them differently. The Liquids header ignores the buffer and turns red at any total above the limit. The Food card turns orange above the target and red above the extended zone. The 'Today' metrics only change colour (red) once past limit+buffer, and stay in the neutral theme colour inside the buffer. The weekly grid on the same widget uses orange inside the buffer. So the buffer the user configured means 'already over (red)' in one place and 'fine (neutral)' in another.
evidence: liquids-card.tsx:242 `const isOverLimit = settings.waterLimit > 0 && waterIntake.dailyTotal > settings.waterLimit;` → red. text-metrics.tsx:235 `waterProgress.isOverExtended ? "text-red-600 ..." : CARD_THEMES.water.latestValueColor`. Scratch DOM test, water 1200 ml with limit 1000 and buffer 500: Liquids header class 'text-red-600', Today value class 'text-sky-700'. Sodium 1600 with limit 1500 and buffer 500: Food card 'text-orange-600', Today value 'text-amber-700' (neutral theme).
failure_scenario: With the default 1000 ml limit and 500 ml buffer, the user logs 1200 ml. The Liquids card header shows red (over the limit) while the Today summary a few centimetres away shows the normal blue value with the bar in its 'extended allowance' tone. The user cannot tell whether 1200 ml is acceptable. The same happens for sodium between 1500 and 2000 mg (orange on the Food card, neutral on Today).
suggested_fix: Derive a single tri-state (ok / extended / over) from computeTwoStageProgress in packages/core, map it to one colour set, and use it on every surface (Liquids header, water tab, Food card, Today row, weekly grid).
verifier_corrections: A small overstatement: inside the buffer, the Today row does show an "X / Y ml" buffer subline in muted text (text-metrics.tsx:246-262), so it isn't fully silent. Only its colour stays neutral. The Liquids-header vs Today mismatch is for water. The Food-card orange vs Today neutral mismatch is for sodium. Both claims are accurate.

No substantive corrections. I did not re-run the scratch DOM test; the finding holds from the code alone. One extra spot the finding missed: water-tab.tsx:39 sets `isOverLimit = progress.isOverTarget`, so the water tab also treats any total inside the buffer as over the limit, the same way the Liquids header does.

title: Food card, Liquids header and caffeine total print raw floating-point sums
description: formatAmount returns `${amount}${unit}` with no rounding for anything that is not ml >= 1000. Several write paths store fractional amounts: voice food items store the AI's sodiumMg/sugarG/potassiumMg unrounded, voice caffeine stores item.caffeineMg unrounded, and liquid-edit sugar uses parseFloat. The daily sum can therefore carry binary floating-point noise, which the Food card headline, the '24h' line and the Today caffeine line (`{caffeineTotal} mg`) print verbatim. The Today water/sodium/sugar values use toLocaleString, which hides the noise, so the same total reads differently on two surfaces.
evidence: utils.ts:13 `return `${amount}${unit}`;` and text-metrics.tsx:431 `{caffeineTotal} mg`. Scratch DOM test, seeding sugar rows of 0.1 g and 0.2 g plus caffeine rows of 0.1 mg and 0.2 mg: the Food card rendered '0.30000000000000004g / 30g' and Today rendered '0.30000000000000004 mg'. (12.3+5.1+2.2 = 19.599999999999998 in some summation orders.)
failure_scenario: The user dictates 'yoghurt 12.3 g sugar' and 'granola 5.1 g sugar' via voice. Depending on the order Dexie returns rows, the Food card can show '17.400000000000002g / 30g', or a 19.599999999999998-style value for three items.
suggested_fix: Round at write time (all paths, to match the integer server columns) and format for display (e.g. Math.round, or toLocaleString with maximumFractionDigits) in formatAmount and the caffeine line.
verifier_corrections: These are minor. I did not re-run the finding's scratch DOM test; the verdict rests on code tracing plus standard IEEE-754 behaviour (0.1+0.2 = 0.30000000000000004). The problem is limited to fractional values from the AI/voice paths (and any other unrounded writer). The edit paths for caffeine and sugar already apply Math.round.

title: Liquids header rounds to one decimal of a litre: 1040 ml shows as '1.0L / 1.0L' in red
description: formatAmount converts ml >= 1000 to litres with toFixed(1). Totals between 1000 and 1049 ml print exactly like the 1.0 L limit. The header colours them red, so the display says 'at limit' while the colour says 'over'. Meanwhile the Today row shows '1,040 / 1,000 ml'.
evidence: `if (unit === "ml" && amount >= 1000) { return `${(amount / 1000).toFixed(1)}L`; }`. Scratch DOM test: 1040 ml seeded, header text '1.0L / 1.0L' with class text-red-600.
failure_scenario: A fluid-restricted user at 1040 ml sees '1.0L / 1.0L' in red and cannot tell how far over the limit they are. The Today card says 1,040 / 1,000 ml.
suggested_fix: Show ml up to a larger threshold, or use two decimals for litres, so values above the limit never render equal to it.
verifier_corrections: I did not check the claim that the Today row shows "1,040 / 1,000 ml", and the finding does not need it. The problem is not limited to a 1.0 L limit: any limit that is a whole number of litres hits it for totals up to 49 ml over the limit. It also affects the 24h rolling total line.

title: Settings number fields silently revert out-of-range input, and can display a value that was never stored
description: validateAndSave falls back to the *current* value for any out-of-range input, with no toast or error text. Typing 15000 into the water limit (max 10000) does not clamp to 10000; it silently snaps back. For in-range fractions it calls setter(parsed) and then inputSetter(parsed.toString()), but the store setter's sanitizeNumericInput rounds to an integer. If the rounded value equals the old one, the store does not change and the useEffect resync never fires. The input then keeps showing the unsaved typed text.
evidence: `setter(defaultValue); inputSetter(defaultValue.toString());` in the else branch. sanitizeNumericInput `return Math.round(clamped);`. Scratch DOM test on WaterSettingsSection: after typing 15000 the store stayed at 1000 and the input showed 1000 (no message). After typing 1000.4 the store was 1000 while the input showed '1000.4'. SugarSettingsSection with 30.4: store 30, input '30.4'.
failure_scenario: The user types a 12000 ml limit, tabs away, and the field reverts to 1000 without explanation. Or the user types 30.4 g for sugar and the field keeps showing 30.4, while the dashboard uses 30.
suggested_fix: Clamp to [min,max] instead of reverting, show inline validation text, and always write the sanitized stored value back to the input (inputSetter(String(store value after set))).
verifier_corrections: One nuance is missing: the stale-display case only happens when the rounded value equals the value already stored. If the fraction rounds to a different number (e.g. 1500.4 when 1000 is stored), the store changes and the useEffect resyncs the input to "1500". Otherwise the finding is accurate.

title: Sodium 'Increment (mg)' setting has no consumer
description: The Sodium settings section exposes 'Increment (mg) — Amount added with each +/- tap (10-1000)', with validation, persistence and a migration default. No dashboard component reads saltIncrement: the Food card has no +/- sodium stepper, and useSaltSettings is itself unused. This setting is not in the already-known list of consumer-less settings.
evidence: `grep -rn saltIncrement` finds hits only in settings-store.ts, salt-settings-section.tsx and the unused useSaltSettings hook (use-settings.ts:20).
failure_scenario: The user changes the sodium increment to 100 mg expecting the +/- taps to change, and nothing anywhere in the app changes.
suggested_fix: Remove the field (and useSaltSettings/useWaterSettings/useSugarSettings if unused), or wire it into a sodium stepper.
verifier_corrections: One small correction: the cited range 30-46 in `salt-settings-section.tsx` is the JSX block. The state wiring for this setting is at lines 13-21. The finding also mentions a "migration default", but the only default I found is the store default at line 184; I didn't check whether a persist migration also sets one. Neither point changes the conclusion.

title: BP inputs truncate decimals with parseInt, so the schema's .int() check can never fire
description: Add and edit both parse with parseInt before validation. '120.9' becomes 120 and passes `.int("Must be a whole number")`, so the whole-number error is unreachable and decimal typos are saved silently truncated. (The known truncation finding covers water amounts, not BP.)
evidence: `const systolic = parseInt(systolicInput, 10);` then `BloodPressureFormSchema.safeParse({ systolic: ... })` with `.int("Must be a whole number")`. Scratch test: entering 120.9 / 80.9 stored 120/80 with no error.
failure_scenario: The user types '135.5' (for example a stray decimal key on the mobile keypad) and 135 is saved with no feedback. A typo like '1.35' becomes 1 → 'Too low', which is confusing because the user did not type 1.
suggested_fix: Parse with Number(), let zod .int() reject non-integers, and show the message.
verifier_corrections: The finding says the edit path parses "before validation", but the edit path never calls `BloodPressureFormSchema` at all. Its only check is `isNaN(x) || x <= 0`. On edit, "1.35" is saved as systolic 1 with no "Too low" error, because the edit path has no 50-300 / 20-200 range check. So on edit the issue is not only an unreachable `.int()` message: the edit path skips the range validation entirely, which is a small extra inconsistency between add and edit.

title: Two-stage bar fill drops from 100% to ~67% as soon as intake crosses the target
description: Below the target the bar denominator is `target`. Once current > target the bar rescales to target+buffer. So the bar goes from fully filled at 1000/1000 ml to 67.3% filled at 1010 ml with the default 500 ml buffer. The fill goes down as intake goes up. This is intentional per the code comments, but it means the bar's fill is not a monotonic signal.
evidence: `maxAmount = target + buffer; primaryPct = (target / maxAmount) * 100;`. Scratch test: computeTwoStageProgress(1000,1000,500).primaryPct = 100; at 1010, primaryPct+extendedPct = 67.33.
failure_scenario: The user at exactly 1000 ml sees a full bar, drinks 10 ml more, and the bar visibly shrinks to about two thirds. This is easy to misread as a deletion or a reset.
suggested_fix: Always render the bar on a 0..target+buffer scale (with the target marker visible from the start), or keep the target scale and overflow into a separate segment.
verifier_corrections: The finding cites lines 66-82. The two-stage branch is actually lines 68-76, and the single-stage branch is lines 77-84. It also leaves out that the rescale adds a target marker (`targetPct`, passed as `targetMarkerPct`) and a separately coloured extended segment, which signal the change of scale. This is an intentional, documented UX design choice with no data or logic error, so it fits the styling refresh better than a business-logic defect. Severity stays low.

title: Progress component never passes its value to Radix, so every intake bar is announced as 'indeterminate'
description: `value` is destructured out of the props and never forwarded to ProgressPrimitive.Root. Radix therefore renders data-state="indeterminate" with no aria-valuenow on every dashboard bar. The aria-label says 'as a percentage of the daily limit', but no percentage is exposed.
evidence: `({ className, value, indicatorClassName, ... , ...props }, ref) => ... <ProgressPrimitive.Root ref={ref} className=... {...props}>`. The rendered DOM in the scratch test showed `aria-valuemax="100" ... data-state="indeterminate" role="progressbar"` with no aria-valuenow.
failure_scenario: A screen-reader user on the dashboard hears 'Sodium intake today, as a percentage of the daily limit, progress bar, busy/indeterminate' and never hears the value.
suggested_fix: Pass value={primary + extended} (clamped) to ProgressPrimitive.Root, or set aria-valuenow and aria-valuetext explicitly.
verifier_corrections: This is slightly wider than just the dashboard intake bars: the migration upload-progress bar (apps/web/src/components/migration/upload-progress-step.tsx:58) is also announced as indeterminate. One more detail: the text-metrics bars use the aria-label "Water intake progress", not the "percentage of the daily limit" wording, which appears only in the food-salt card and the liquids tabs. When fixing, also consider the two-stage mode, where the value exposed to Radix should be primary + extended.

title: Liquids recent list shows the sugar badge even when the sugar tracker is disabled; the Food list hides it
description: The optional-tracker contract in settings-store says a disabled tracker is hidden from every surface. The Food card's recent list gates sugar on sugarEnabled; the Liquids card's recent list does not.
evidence: liquids-card.tsx:361 `{record.groupId && groupSugarMap.get(record.groupId) ? ({groupSugarMap.get(record.groupId)}g sugar) : null}` has no sugarEnabled check. food-section.tsx:599 `const sugar = sugarEnabled && record.groupId ? groupSugarMap.get(record.groupId) : undefined;`.
failure_scenario: The user disables sugar tracking. Recent drinks in the Liquids card still show '25g sugar' badges, while the Food card's meals no longer show sugar.
suggested_fix: Gate the badge on sugarEnabled, matching food-section.
verifier_corrections: None. The cited lines and quotes are correct.

title: BP card loading state is dead: the hook defaults to [], so !recentRecords is never true
description: useBloodPressureRecords passes [] as the useLiveQuery default, so recentRecords is never undefined and the skeleton branch never renders. The Weight card's hook has no default and does show its skeleton, so the two cards behave inconsistently while loading. (The known finding covers only the Water tab's equivalent guard.)
evidence: `return useLiveQuery(() => getBloodPressureRecords(limit), [limit], []);` and `const isLoading = !recentRecords;`.
failure_scenario: On a cold start with many records, the BP header is briefly empty (it looks like 'no readings') and then the latest reading pops in, instead of showing the loading skeleton.
suggested_fix: Drop the [] default (and handle undefined), or track loading separately.
verifier_corrections: The finding says the header looks like "no readings", which is a slight overstatement. While loading, the BP header area renders `null` (blank), not a "no readings" message. The recent-records list gets `[]` at line 434, so it may briefly show its empty state. Everything else in the finding is accurate.

title: During titration the AI medication summary reports an arbitrary phase: often the old maintenance dose and a days-on-phase of hundreds of days
description: buildMedicationSummary uses getActivePhaseForPrescription, which returns phases.find(p => p.status === 'active'). activateTitrationPlan activates the titration phases but leaves the maintenance phase 'active', so two active phases coexist for the whole titration. find() returns whichever comes first in Dexie index/primary-key order, and ids are random UUIDs, so the pick is random. The dose schedule service explicitly prefers the titration phase ('Titration overrides maintenance'). As a result, the AI and the Medications screen disagree on the current dose. The helper also does not filter deletedAt, so a soft-deleted phase that is still 'active' can be reported.
evidence: phase-service.ts:57 `return phases.find(p => p.status === "active");` vs dose-schedule-service.ts:129 `} else if (phase.type === "titration" && phase.titrationPlanId) { // Titration overrides maintenance`. Scratch test: one prescription with maintenance 2.5 mg (started 200 days ago) and titration 5 mg (started 3 days ago), 12 runs: ["maintenance:2.5 mg:200","titration:5 mg:3","titration:5 mg:3","maintenance:2.5 mg:200","maintenance:2.5 mg:200",...] (6 of 12 reported maintenance).
failure_scenario: The user is 3 days into up-titrating bisoprolol from 2.5 mg to 5 mg and runs Deep analysis with medications shared. The prompt says 'Bisoprolol: maintenance phase, 2.5 mg, once daily; current phase active 200 day(s)'. The deep prompt then relates BP and weight trends to the wrong dose and wrong phase, while the Medications screen shows 5 mg titration.
suggested_fix: Share one 'effective phase' selector between the dose schedule service and buildMedicationSummary: active, deletedAt === null, titration preferred over maintenance. Better, end or suspend the maintenance phase when a titration activates.
verifier_corrections:
These are nuances, not errors that change the verdict.
- The pick is not random on every run. For a given data set the order is fixed and deterministic, but it is arbitrary (decided by UUID order), so roughly half of titrations are affected, and consistently.
- The `deletedAt` part is a minor secondary point. It is latent unless a soft-delete leaves `status` as "active".
- The finding cites only `activateTitrationPlan`. `createTitrationPlan` with `startImmediately` also creates the dual-active state.
- The user-visible impact is limited to AI insight and nutrient-analysis prompts; the dose schedule and reminders show the right dose. That is why this stays high rather than critical.

Small refinement: the pick is not random for a given pair of phases. It is fixed by the lexical order of the two UUID ids, so a given user will usually see the same wrong phase every run rather than a coin flip each time. The finding's 6-of-12 result comes from making new random ids on each run. The `deletedAt` problem can also be triggered by editing an active titration plan (`titration-service.ts:245-247`), not only by `deletePhase`. A soft-deleted phase that gets picked would show "no active schedule".

The pick is not random per run. For a given pair of phases, IndexedDB ordering by UUID primary key is deterministic. The scratch test's 6/12 split came from generating new UUIDs each run. For a real user, a given titration is either reported correctly every time or wrong every time, with roughly 50% odds per titration. Severity is overstated: only the AI prompt context is affected (opt-in insights and nutrient analysis). The app's displayed dose and schedule are correct, so medium, not high. The soft-deleted phase case reports "no active schedule" rather than a stale dose, because deletePhase also soft-deletes the phase's schedules.

title: Water 'Daily Limit' (fluid restriction) is sent to the AI as a 'goal', and 'fluid balance on target' means drinking more
description: Settings label waterLimit as 'Daily Limit (ml)', and the Liquids tabs flag intake above it as over-limit, so for this user it is a fluid restriction. The insights card maps it to `waterGoalMl`, and the prompt renders 'water averaged X ml against a Y ml goal'. The fluid-balance metric counts a day as 'on target' only when intake >= estimated urination + 500 ml. It reaches the prompt as 'On target on N of M day(s)' with no definition. Both framings push the model toward 'drink more', which is the opposite of a restriction.
evidence: water-settings-section.tsx:48 `<Label htmlFor="water-limit">Daily Limit (ml)</Label>`; ai-insights-card.tsx:210 `const waterGoalMl = useSettingsStore((s) => s.waterLimit);`; prompt:368 `water averaged ${i.avgWaterMl.toFixed(0)} ml against a ${i.waterGoalMl} ml goal`; analytics-service.ts:230,259 `const target = urinationEstimatedMl + 500;` / `daily.filter((d) => d.intakeMl >= d.target)`.
failure_scenario: A heart-failure user sets a 1500 ml fluid limit and averages 1200 ml/day. The AI is told 'water averaged 1200 ml against a 1500 ml goal' and 'fluid balance on target on 3 of 25 days'. It reports under-hydration and missed targets for a patient who is correctly staying under their restriction.
suggested_fix: Send the value as a limit (`waterLimitMl`) and word it as 'against a X ml daily fluid limit'. Define the fluid-balance target in the prompt, or drop 'on target' for users with a limit. The Summary tab's 'below your goal' observation needs the same fix.
verifier_corrections: The evidence and line numbers are accurate. Severity is overstated at high: the numbers and stored data are correct, and only the AI and summary-text framing is wrong, so medium fits better. Also, the app's own progress model (computeTwoStageProgress with target plus extended buffer, "isOverTarget") treats waterLimit as a hybrid target/limit, so "goal" wording is not wholly unfounded. It still contradicts the "Daily Limit" label. The Summary tab issue is at apps/web/src/components/analytics/summary-tab.tsx:211-213.

Severity is arguably high only on medical-safety grounds. In terms of data and logic it is a semantic mislabel, not wrong computed data, so medium fits better. The fluid-balance "target" (`urinationEstimatedMl + 500`) is only half the problem: the "On target" phrasing itself also contradicts the restriction. A further point the finding missed: the default `waterLimit` of 1000 ml is sent to the AI as a "goal" even for users who never set it.

The severity is overstated. There is no data corruption and no wrong dosing: the failure is misleading AI and observation wording, so medium fits better than high. The fluid-balance "+500 ml above output" target is a deliberate metric that the app already uses elsewhere. The defect is that the prompt never defines it and treats it as good-when-higher, not that it was calculated wrongly. The limit-versus-goal ambiguity also exists outside the AI path: summary-tab.tsx:211-213 has the "below your goal" observation, and the Liquids tab's progress bar also treats the value as a target.

title: Alternate-day and extra-day schedules are sent as 'twice daily' with an ambiguous dose list
description: frequency counts schedule rows and takes the union of their weekdays. Any two schedules whose days together cover the whole week become 'twice daily', even when no single day has two doses. dose is a deduplicated, sorted list of the distinct amounts, which loses which amount goes with which day or time and gives no daily total.
evidence: `const count = schedules.length; ... frequency = dayUnion.size >= 7 ? `${per} daily` : ...`. Scratch test: Warfarin 5 mg Mon/Wed/Fri + 2.5 mg Tue/Thu/Sat/Sun → {"dose":"2.5 mg, 5 mg","frequency":"twice daily"}. Furosemide 40 mg daily + 40 mg Monday-only → {"dose":"40 mg","frequency":"twice daily"}.
failure_scenario: The user takes warfarin once a day, alternating 5 mg and 2.5 mg. The AI is told 'Warfarin: maintenance phase, 2.5 mg, 5 mg, twice daily', which it can read as up to 15 mg/day. A furosemide user with one extra Monday dose is described as taking 40 mg twice daily, doubling the apparent diuretic load in the deep analysis.
suggested_fix: Build the frequency per weekday: group schedules by day, report doses/day and daily total per day pattern (e.g. 'Mon/Wed/Fri 5 mg; other days 2.5 mg; once daily'), or send structured per-schedule entries.
verifier_corrections: The mechanics and both examples are correct. Severity is overstated: this only affects the opt-in medication context sent to the AI deep analysis (nutrient-analysis-card), not dosing data stored or shown in the app, so medium fits better than high. The finding also leaves out a narrower case: two schedules on the same days at the same time are also counted as "twice".

The logic is confirmed, but I lowered severity from high to medium. The misstated frequency only reaches the AI's context text. It does not reach stored records, dose logging, reminders, or any dosing shown in the medication UI, so no user data is corrupted and no core feature is broken. The claim that the AI 'can read it as up to 15 mg/day' is a guess about how the model interprets the text; the only proven harm is misleading context in the AI insights and nutrient analysis. A smaller point: 'twice' comes from counting schedule rows. Even two schedules on the same days at the same time would count as 'twice', so the problem is broader than complementary-day schedules.

The code claim and the example outputs are accurate. The impact is overstated: the AI can misread the regimen, for example as up to 15 mg/day or as a doubled diuretic load, but only in opt-in insight or nutrient-analysis text. The app never shows the user wrong doses, and the prompt forbids dosage recommendations. Severity should be medium, not high. One more case of the same issue: the dose list is also ambiguous for real twice-daily regimens with different amounts, because it never pairs an amount with its time and never gives a daily total.

title: Deep mode asks the model to link each medication to trends, but the snapshot has no adherence and omits PRN-only prescriptions
description: buildMedicationSummary skips any prescription without an active phase (`if (!phase) continue`). PRN/as-needed prescriptions are created with no phase ('no phase or schedules when schedule list is empty'), so they are never sent. The MedicationSchema phaseType enum can't express PRN, and PRN dose events are never counted. The snapshot also carries no adherence or dose-taken data (adherenceRate exists in analytics-service but is unused here). DEEP_SYSTEM_PROMPT nevertheless requires 'For EACH active medication... compare the observed metric trend against the expected clinical response'. The card and profile copy tell the user 'your active prescriptions' are shared.
evidence: analytics-snapshot.ts:56-57 `const phase = await getActivePhaseForPrescription(rx.id); if (!phase) continue;`; prescription-service.ts:77-79 `// PRN / as-needed meds: no phase or schedules ... const phase = hasSchedules ? buildPhase(...) : null;`. Scratch test: an active PRN-only prescription → buildMedicationSummary() returned [].
failure_scenario: The user takes as-needed furosemide several times in the month and stopped logging scheduled doses weeks ago. Deep analysis never learns about the diuretic, so it can't explain weight drops. It attributes BP and weight trends to scheduled medications as if they were taken 100% of the time.
suggested_fix: Include PRN prescriptions (phaseType 'prn', dose from PRN logs, count of PRN doses in range). Add a per-medication adherence figure (taken/due, excluding not-yet-due doses) to the snapshot, and tell the model when adherence is unknown or sparse.
verifier_corrections:
The core claim is correct; three details need tightening.

1. **Adherence is a gap, not a contradiction.** The prompt never tells the model to assume full adherence. The real problems are that no adherence data is sent and nothing says adherence is unknown. So the "attributes to scheduled meds as if taken 100%" part of the failure scenario is a plausible model behaviour, not something the code does.
2. **"PRN dose events are never counted" is broader than stated.** No dose events of any kind are counted, scheduled or PRN.
3. **The omission is mainly a consistency/disclosure problem.** The copy says "your active prescriptions" are shared, but PRN prescriptions are silently left out. It is not a data-corruption issue. Medium severity is appropriate.

No factual errors found. Two minor notes. First, I verified this by reading the code rather than rerunning the scratch test the finding cites. Second, the missing adherence data is a design gap rather than a code defect. The part that is definitely wrong is that PRN medications are dropped while the UI says active prescriptions are shared.

title: 'Include previous summary' sends condition and medication text even after sharing is turned off, and the new report is marked not personalised
description: When includePrevious is set, the latest report's narrative and observations are attached as priorAssessments without checking the report's `personalised` flag against the current consent. A report generated while conditions and medications were shared contains that clinical detail ('Given your HFrEF and bisoprolol...'). It is still sent after the user turns both sharing toggles off. The new report is saved with personalised=false even though it was built from personalised text, so the flag can't be used to filter later either. This is separate from the known 'unsanitised' and 'latest-not-previous' items: this one bypasses the consent toggle.
evidence: use-insights.ts:86-99 `if (includePrevious) { const previous = await getLatestInsightReport(); if (previous) { ... summary: previous.narrative, observations: previous.observations ...` (no personalised check). Scratch hook test: prior report narrative 'Given your HFrEF and bisoprolol 5 mg titration...' with personalised:true. mutate({includePrevious:true}) with no conditions/meds → POST body has profile undefined, priorAssessments[0].summary contains 'HFrEF', and the stored new report has personalised === false.
failure_scenario: The user shares conditions once, then revokes sharing (the toggle now says 'Your conditions stay on this device and are not sent to the AI'). They tick 'Include my previous summary', and the HFrEF and medication details go to Anthropic and the server anyway.
suggested_fix: Only attach a prior report whose personalised flag is compatible with current consent, or strip it when consent is off. Set the new report's personalised = current flags OR prior.personalised.
verifier_corrections: The claim that the details go "to Anthropic and the server anyway" overstates the server part: prior reports are already synced to Neon, so only the resend to Anthropic is new. The finding also leaves out that the confirm dialog explicitly warns that the previous summary text is sent, so this is a mismatch between two consent messages, not a hidden bypass. The personalised=false on the new report is accurate. Severity lowered from medium to low.

Calling this a "consent bypass" overstates it. The user must tick an opt-in checkbox, and the dialog then says the previous summary's text will be sent. What's missing is a warning that this text may contain condition or medication details the user has since stopped sharing, or filtering or stripping of such prior reports. The claim that the flag can't be used "to filter later" is latent only: no code reads `personalised` today. The data goes only to the processor that already received it while sharing was on. The code-level facts are accurate: there is no personalised check at use-insights.ts:86-100 or :405-416, and the new report's flag ignores the prior report at :158-160. I'd lower severity from medium to low.

title: Trackers the user doesn't log are sent as real zero intake (water 0 ml, sodium 0 mg), and one entry is enough for a paid call
description: The intake block is emitted if any of water/salt/sugar/potassium has a single record in the window. It always includes avgWaterMl and avgSodiumMg, which are 0 when those trackers have no data. The prompt presents them as measured averages against the goal/limit. snapshotIsEmpty only checks group presence, so a lone entry 29 days ago produces a non-empty snapshot and a paid AI call built on an 8 ml/day 'average'.
evidence: `if ((water.length > 0 || salt.length > 0 || sugar.length > 0 || potassium.length > 0) && ...) { metrics.intake = { avgWaterMl: sum(water) / days, avgSodiumMg: sum(salt) / days, ...` Scratch test: only one 40 g sugar entry → intake {"avgWaterMl":0,"avgSodiumMg":0,...,"avgSugarG":1.33}; prompt 'Daily intake: water averaged 0 ml against a 1500 ml goal; sodium averaged 0 mg against a 1500 mg limit; sugar averaged 1 g against a 30 g limit.' and snapshotIsEmpty === false.
failure_scenario: A user who logs only BP and sugar gets an AI report warning about essentially zero fluid intake and praising excellent sodium control, neither of which was tracked.
suggested_fix: Emit each intake field only when that domain has data in the window, and send logged-day counts. Require a minimum number of logged days before the intake group counts toward 'not empty'.
verifier_corrections: The "one entry is enough for a paid call" point is not specific to intake. A single BP or weight reading also makes the snapshot non-empty, so that part is a general gating issue rather than an extra effect of this bug. The real defect is that water and sodium are sent as measured 0 averages, spread across the whole window rather than logged days. The sugar-only example also depends on the sugar tracker being enabled, because disabled trackers are never fetched.

One part is overstated. In the example scenario the user also logs BP, and BP readings alone already make the snapshot non-empty, so the paid call would happen with or without this issue. The call being triggered is not the defect. The defect is the zero-valued and diluted intake averages presented as real measurements. Also, water and salt are core trackers that can't be switched off like the optional ones, so the accurate wording is "not logged", not "not tracked". One more thing the finding doesn't mention: when a tracker does have data, its average is still divided by every day in the window, including days with no entries.

title: Caffeine and alcohol amounts never reach the AI, and users who log only those (or meals) are blocked
description: The Summary tab shows caffeine mg and alcohol standard-drink totals and daily averages for the range. The snapshot has no caffeine or alcohol intake field. Caffeine and alcohol only appear as correlations with BP, which are dropped entirely when there are no BP readings on the same days. With BP present they reduce to 'insufficient overlapping data', so the amounts themselves are never sent. Eating, urination-count and defecation data never contribute either. A user who tracks only drinks or meals always gets 'Not enough data'.
evidence: Snapshot inputs are bpTrend, weightTrend, fluidBalance, getRecordsByDomain water/salt/sugar/potassium, plus correlations; there is no caffeine/alcohol aggregate. Scratch test: 4 standard drinks of alcohol only → snapshotIsEmpty true. Adding one BP reading → prompt contains only 'alcohol intake vs blood pressure: insufficient overlapping data (1 day(s))' and no drink count.
failure_scenario: A heart-failure user drinks 4 standard drinks/day for a month. The Summary tab shows the alcohol KPI, but the AI summary cannot mention alcohol intake at all, and it is refused if the user hasn't logged BP.
suggested_fix: Add caffeineMg and alcoholStdDrinks daily averages (with logged-day counts) to the intake metrics. List them in the confirm dialog's 'Tracked data'.
verifier_corrections: Users who log only drinks are not blocked in normal use. logDrink always creates a water IntakeRecord for the drink volume, so the snapshot has intake and fluidBalance metrics and is not empty. The block only applies to substances logged with no volume (e.g. a caffeine tablet) or to meal-only/defecation-only users. Urination data does count through fluidBalance (urination-only days add to daysTotal), which contradicts "urination-count never contribute". The heart-failure scenario ("refused if no BP") is wrong for beers logged in the UI; the AI summary just gets their volume as water intake and never sees the drink count. The part that holds is that caffeine mg and alcohol standard-drink totals are never sent to the AI.

Users who log only drinks are not blocked. Every drink goes through `logDrink`, which writes a water IntakeRecord, so `metrics.intake` is populated and the snapshot is not empty. Urination data does contribute, via `fluidBalance`. The "insufficient overlapping data" line applies only when there are fewer than 3 paired days; with more, the correlation coefficient is sent. The valid core is narrower: absolute caffeine mg and alcohol standard-drink amounts are never included in the snapshot, so the AI summary can't mention intake volumes that the Summary tab shows. This is a missing feature, not a data-integrity bug, so severity is low. The "only meals" blocking claim was not checked, but it is secondary.

title: The AI card uses a fixed 30-day window inside a range-scoped Summary tab, and it disappears when the selected range is empty
description: AiInsightsCard is rendered at the top of SummaryTab but ignores its `range` prop and always analyses insightsRange() (last 30 days). The KPIs directly below it are computed for the user-selected range (7d, 90d, custom), so the AI numbers and the KPI numbers on the same screen disagree. Also, when the selected range has no records, SummaryTab returns early with only NutrientAnalysisCard. The AI card, including every saved report, is then hidden even though the 30-day window has data.
evidence:
ai-insights-card.tsx:283 `range: insightsRange(),`; summary-tab.tsx:247-262 `if (!hasAnyData) { return (
...
); }` (no ).
failure_scenario: The user picks '7 days' and sees an average of 1800 ml water. They open the AI report and read 'water averaged 1100 ml' for a different 30-day period. They then pick a quiet custom week and all past AI reports vanish from the screen.
suggested_fix: Render the AI card independently of the range-empty early return. Either pass the selected range to the snapshot, or label the card clearly as its own 30-day window distinct from the KPIs.
verifier_corrections: AiInsightsCard has no `range` prop to ignore. It takes no props, and SummaryTab never passes it one. The fixed 30-day window is labelled throughout the card (ai-insights-card.tsx:359, 468-469, 488), so seeing numbers that differ from the range-scoped KPIs is not a hidden inconsistency. The valid part of the finding is that the `!hasAnyData` early return in summary-tab.tsx:247-262 drops AiInsightsCard. NutrientAnalysisCard is kept there because of its fixed window, and AiInsightsCard should be kept for the same reason. The severity should be low, not medium.

AiInsightsCard has no `range` prop to ignore; it is declared with no props. The 30-day window is intentional and labelled in the UI ("your last 30 days", ai-insights-card.tsx:359 and 468-469), so the AI-vs-KPI mismatch is disclosed, not a hidden data bug. The only real defect is that the AI card is left out of the empty-range early return (summary-tab.tsx:247-262), unlike NutrientAnalysisCard, which is kept for exactly this reason. Its saved reports are hidden until the user widens the range. Nothing is lost, so severity drops to low.

title: A completed deep report reaches the device only through a sync pull that ignores storage mode; if that pull fails the paid result is not shown
description: On completion the hook clears the stored job id, calls schedulePull(), and the card immediately reset()s the state. The narrative in the poll response is discarded, and the report must arrive through /api/sync/pull. schedulePull, unlike schedulePush, is not gated on engineStarted or storage mode. A local-only device therefore runs a full pull of every table from the cloud just to fetch the report. If that single pull fails (offline, 401, server error), a local-only device never pulls again. The user sees the 'Deep analysis ready — now in the summary' toast but no report. The job id is gone, so polling cannot recover it.
evidence: use-insights.ts:334-338 `writeStoredJob(null); ... schedulePull();`; card:324-329 `toast({ title: "Deep analysis ready", ...}); deep.reset();`; sync-engine.ts:118-119 `export function schedulePush(...) { if (!engineStarted || engineSuspended) return;` vs 414-415 `export function schedulePull(): void { if (engineSuspended) return;`.
failure_scenario: A user on local-only storage runs a costly deep analysis. On completion, all cloud rows (e.g. from a second device) are silently merged into the local DB. Or, if the network drops at that moment, the paid report never appears on the device even though the toast said it was ready.
suggested_fix: Save the poll response into Dexie locally (keyed by the server resultReportId so sync dedupes it) instead of relying on a pull. Pull only the insightReports table, and only when cloud sync is enabled.
verifier_corrections: This is a minor overstatement. The report is not destroyed: it stays in Postgres and appears if the user later switches to cloud-sync. On cloud-sync devices a failed pull is retried by the normal engine cycles. So the "never shown" outcome only applies to local-only devices. The unwanted merge of all cloud rows into a local-only DB happens whenever the pull succeeds, which is the more certain of the two harms.

The "all cloud rows silently merged" scenario is overstated. A signed-in local-only user normally has no cloud dataset. Leaving cloud-sync goes through the wipe flow, which clears the server copy. On a new device, use-sync-auto-detect switches storageMode to "cloud-sync" when cloud data exists. So the full-table pull mostly brings back just the new insight report, not a surprise merge. The failure path applies only to signed-in local-only users. Cloud-sync users recover on later pull cycles. The server keeps the report (resultReportId), and the job endpoint can still return the narrative; only the client has thrown away the job id. Severity should be low, not medium.

title: Saved insight reports cannot be deleted; deleteInsightReport has no caller
description: deleteInsightReport exists and is tested but is referenced nowhere in the UI. Reports (including personalised narratives containing conditions and medications) accumulate forever locally and on the server via sync. A clearly wrong report stays in the history, and as the latest report it is the default 'previous summary' for the next comparison. There is no delete, so there is no undo and no delete/resurrect sync path to test.
evidence: grep for deleteInsightReport: only insight-report-service.ts and its test. The card renders ReportPreview rows with only an onOpen handler.
failure_scenario: The user revokes consent and wants their HFrEF-framed reports gone, or a report was generated from bad data. There is no way to remove it, and it keeps feeding the comparison prompt.
suggested_fix: Add delete (with the existing soft-delete + sync) to the reading dialog. Consider offering to purge personalised reports when sharing is turned off.
verifier_corrections: 1) The report is not the default 'previous summary' for the next comparison. openConfirm sets `setIncludePrevious(false)` (ai-insights-card.tsx:276), and the previous summary is sent only when the user ticks the 'Compare with history' checkbox (`...(includePrevious && hasPrevious && { includePrevious: true })`). A bad report is therefore fed into a comparison only if the user opts in; it is not automatic. 2) 'No way to remove it' is too strong. Bulk removal paths do exist: the account/user-data deletion flow lists insightReports (lib/user-data-deletion.ts:61), and a backup replace-import clears the table (backup-service.ts:494). What is missing is deleting a single report, and purging reports when AI-sharing consent is revoked.

title: 'Personalised' label and stored flag reflect the toggles, not what was actually sent
description: With 'Share medications' on, the card shows 'Personalised with your medical profile' and the confirm dialog says 'Medications included — your active prescriptions...' even when buildMedicationSummary returns [] (no prescriptions, PRN-only, or no active phase). A fast report is saved with personalised=true because includeMedications===true. Deep reports compute personalised from the actual payload, so fast and deep disagree for identical inputs.
evidence: use-insights.ts:158-160 `personalised: (conditions !== undefined && conditions.length > 0) || includeMedications === true,` vs jobs route:393 `Boolean(submitted.profile?.medications && submitted.profile.medications.length > 0)`.
failure_scenario: A user with only a PRN medication turns on medication sharing. The UI claims the report is personalised with their prescriptions, but nothing was sent.
suggested_fix: Derive personalised from snapshot.profile after building it, in both paths. Show the actual medication count in the confirm dialog.
verifier_corrections:
1. The PRN example is probably wrong. `getActivePhaseForPrescription` returns any phase with status 'active', and `buildMedicationSummary` still sends a prescription whose phase has no enabled schedules, labelled dose/frequency "no active schedule". A PRN-only medication with an active phase is therefore sent. The label is only wrong when there are no active prescriptions, every phase is inactive, or every name is blank.
2. No .tsx file reads the stored `personalised` flag (grep shows none), so the fast/deep mismatch in the saved record has no visible effect today. It is a latent data inconsistency.
3. The same toggle-based label also appears in nutrient-analysis-card.tsx:211, which the finding does not mention.

title: The profile says conditions 'stay on this device', but they cloud-sync to the server
description: The copy says 'Conditions you add stay on this device unless you turn on sharing below' and 'Your conditions stay on this device and are not sent to the AI'. saveUserProfile writes through writeWithSync and schedulePush, so conditions and the consent flags go to Neon Postgres whenever cloud sync is on, regardless of the sharing toggle.
evidence: profile-service.ts:106-110 `await writeWithSync("userProfile", "upsert", ...); schedulePush();`; medical-context-section.tsx:67 `Conditions you add stay on this device unless you turn on sharing below.`
failure_scenario: A user adds a sensitive diagnosis believing it never leaves the phone. It is stored server-side the next time sync runs.
suggested_fix: Change the copy to 'are not sent to the AI' (and mention cloud backup), or exclude the profile's conditions from sync unless the user opts in.
verifier_corrections: No factual errors. One point needs clarifying: the "sharing below" toggle only controls sharing with the AI. The data goes to the user's own cloud-sync backend, not to anyone else, which is why this stays low severity.

title: Fluid-balance day buckets include the partial first and last day of the rolling window
description: insightsRange is now minus 30×24h, so the window starts mid-day 30 days ago and ends mid-day today. fluidBalance buckets by calendar day, so the first and last buckets hold only part of a day's water and urination. The fixed +500 ml target makes those partial days likely to be counted as 'below target', and they are averaged into avgBalanceMl alongside full days.
evidence: `return { start: now - INSIGHTS_WINDOW_DAYS * MS_PER_DAY, end: now };` then groupByDay(waterPoints) and `const target = urinationEstimatedMl + 500;`
failure_scenario: Generating at 09:00, today's bucket has 300 ml intake and 1 urination (300 ml est.). Today counts as a miss and pulls the average balance down, as does the afternoon-only first day.
suggested_fix: Snap the range to day boundaries (using the day-start hour) and exclude the in-progress day from per-day target counts.
verifier_corrections: Minor: it isn't only a snapshot problem. `fluidBalance` also includes an in-progress current day when other callers pass a range ending at now, but whether those ranges line up with day boundaries wasn't checked here. For the insights path specifically, the finding is accurate as written.

title: BP and weight trend slope is fitted per reading, not per unit of time
description: trend() regresses value against the reading's array index, not its timestamp. Irregular logging (bursts of several readings on one day, then gaps of weeks) distorts both the direction and the 'confidence' sent to the AI. The raw slope is also sent as `slope` with no unit (per reading).
evidence: `const pairs: [number, number][] = points.map((p, i) => [i, p.value]);`
failure_scenario: The user takes 5 BP readings during one bad afternoon near the end of the month and one reading a day otherwise. The cluster gets 5x the leverage of a day, and the AI is told systolic is 'rising (confidence 60%)'.
suggested_fix: Regress on days since range start (timestamp / MS_PER_DAY), or on daily means, and document the slope unit as per day.
verifier_corrections: Nothing material. The example ("confidence 60%") is illustrative, not reproduced. The slope's unit also depends on the fixed 0.01 per-reading "rising"/"falling" threshold, which the finding doesn't mention.

title: Potassium intake rows are shown as 'Sodium' with the salt icon and theme in the Records tab
description: RecordRow chooses the theme with a two-way test, and anything that is not water or sugar falls through to 'salt'. CARD_THEMES has a potassium theme (label 'Potassium') that is never used here. Every potassium IntakeRecord therefore shows the 'Sodium' label and the salt icon and colour. The unit happens to come out right (mg).
failure_scenario: A user logs a banana through the food card, which writes a 'manual:potassium' 400 mg row. In Records > All they see 'SODIUM 400 mg' next to the meal's real sodium row, so they read two sodium entries and overestimate their sodium. With the 'K' filter on, the filtered list is full of rows labelled 'Sodium'.
suggested_fix: Map each record.type to its own theme key (water/salt/sugar/potassium), and do the same for the unit. Add a RecordRow test that covers every intake type.
verifier_corrections: Minor points only. The failure only occurs when the optional potassium tracker is enabled, since potassium rows are only created then. The HistoryDrawer path may not be mounted (a prior audit notes that HistoryDrawer is unmounted), so the analytics Records tab is the main path where users see this. Stored data and totals are correct; only the label, icon and colour are wrong.

No real errors. One thing to make clear: this only affects the display. Stored records and the sodium/potassium totals elsewhere are correct. The only thing wrong is the label, icon and colour in the Records tab and the history drawer.

The severity is overstated. This is a display-only mislabel in the Records list and history drawer. It only affects users who enabled the optional potassium tracker. Stored data, units and the sodium totals/limits (summary-tab.tsx:145, text-metrics) stay correct, so the user's actual sodium tracking is not corrupted. The finding cites only the Records tab, but the same bug also shows in the history drawer (history-drawer.tsx:267).

title: Drink labels come from the device's local preset list, not the row's stored name, so history is renamed or shows 'Beverage' on other devices
description: For 'preset:<id>' water rows, getLiquidTypeLabel looks the id up in the current, localStorage-only liquidPresets and ignores record.note. The note holds the drink name as it was at logging time, and the other branches (drink/voice/substance/food) do use it. Presets are not synced, so on a second device, after a reinstall, or after the preset is deleted, the label falls back to 'Beverage'. Renaming a preset also renames every past row. 'preset:manual' rows return null, which drops the stored note even though the drink was named.
failure_scenario: The user logs Club-Mate from a custom preset on their phone, then opens Records on the web app or after reinstalling. The row reads '500 ml · Beverage' instead of 'Club-Mate'. If they later rename the preset to 'Mate (sugar-free)', every past Club-Mate entry is relabelled with the new name.
suggested_fix: Use record.note as the first choice for preset:* sources and fall back to the preset name only when there is no note. Do not return null for 'preset:manual' when a note exists.
verifier_corrections: The cited line numbers are a little off: the preset branch is at about utils.ts:94-103, not 93-102. The same mislabelling also shows on the dashboard at liquids-card.tsx:351, not only in history. Default presets probably have stable ids across devices, so the "Beverage" fallback mainly hits custom (UUID) presets. The rename and `preset:manual` problems affect every preset.

No material errors. One point for accuracy: the history shows the wrong label, but the data is not damaged, because record.note still holds the original name and a display-side fix restores it. I did not check the '8 rows / 36 rows' counts from live data, but the claims don't depend on them.

title: Records imported from backups made before deletedAt existed are reported as imported but are invisible everywhere
description: The backup schema makes deletedAt optional, and importHealthTable writes records exactly as they appear in the file. The v10 Dexie upgrade that backfills deletedAt=null has already run, so imported rows keep deletedAt === undefined. Every read path (getRecordsByDateRange, getRecordsBetween, getActiveRecords, getDailyTotal, getAllRecords) filters with the strict test `r.deletedAt === null`, so those rows are dropped from Records, the dashboard totals and analytics. This happens even though the import toast says they were imported. The legacy v1 'records' format is explicitly supported, and its files predate the sync fields.
failure_scenario: The user restores an early-2026 JSON backup, from before sync fields existed, onto a fresh device. The result says '1,200 intake imported', but Records shows 'No records in this time range' and the dashboard stays at 0. The rows exist in IndexedDB but nothing can display, edit or delete them.
suggested_fix: When importing, normalise the sync fields: deletedAt ?? null, and createdAt, updatedAt, deviceId and timezone defaults. Alternatively, make active-row reads use `deletedAt == null`.
verifier_corrections: This is a small point, but the backups likely affected are those exported before about 2026-03-02, when Dexie v10 added the sync fields. The exposure is not limited to the v1 'records' format: a full-format backup from that period also lacks deletedAt. The impact also covers every table imported via importHealthTable, including medication tables in replace mode. I did not re-run the scratch test; the code path confirms it statically.

No material errors. Two small notes. First, the gap applies to every health table imported through importHealthTable (weight, BP and others), not just intake. Any v2-format backup whose records omit deletedAt is affected too, not only the legacy v1 `records` shape. Second, updatedAt and createdAt are also missing on these rows, which may affect sync/LWW. I did not verify that.

title: Deleting a caffeine or alcohol row in Records silently deletes the drink's water, sugar and salt rows, with no undo
description: In the Records tab, a substance delete calls deleteSubstanceRecord. For a drink group, that function soft-deletes every intake row in the group (water, sugar, salt, potassium) and any sibling substance. The Records tab treats it as a single-row delete: 'caffeine'/'alcohol' are not in UNDO_TOAST_TYPES, no undo function exists for substances, and the toast says 'Record removed'. The reverse case (deleting the water row, which leaves the caffeine) is already known. This is the opposite direction, where one delete removes several rows and cannot be recovered.
failure_scenario: A user who thinks a latte's caffeine estimate is wrong deletes only the Caffeine row in Records. The 250 ml water row and the 10 g sugar row also disappear, and the day's hydration total drops by 250 ml. The toast offers no Undo, so the water has to be re-entered by hand.
suggested_fix: Either confirm the cascade before deleting ('This also removes the drink's 250 ml water and 10 g sugar') and add undoDeleteSubstanceRecord with an undo toast, or make a substance-row delete remove only the substance and handle whole-drink deletion from the water row.
verifier_corrections: The cascade in deleteSubstanceRecord is deliberate and documented (it avoids orphan substances with no fluid attached), so the defect is the Records tab's missing confirmation and undo, not the service logic. The rows are soft-deleted (deletedAt), not hard-deleted, but no user-facing restore path exists. The cascade only happens for drink groups, meaning groups with no live eating record. Substance rows that belong to a meal group delete only themselves plus any source-linked intakes.

The cascade is a deliberate design choice, not an accident. Code comments in `deleteSubstanceRecord` explain that a drink is treated as one unit and that sibling substances are removed on purpose. The real defect is in the Records tab: it gives no confirmation, no undo and a misleading single-row toast, while one tap removes several linked rows. Weight and BP deletes in Records also have no undo, so missing undo alone is not unique here; the multi-row loss is what makes this case worse. The rows are soft-deleted, not destroyed, but no UI path restores them.

title: The '24h' range in Records and Analytics actually means 'since local midnight'
