description: The scope button is labelled '24h', but useTimeScopeRange sets start = startOfDay(now), which is calendar midnight. It uses neither now-24h nor dayStartHour. The dashboard uses dayStartHour, and the intake service has a separate real rolling-24h getRecordsInLast24Hours. The same word '24h' therefore means three different windows. The known findings cover the stale memo and the dayStartHour mismatch, but not that the '24h' preset isn't 24 hours.
failure_scenario: At 00:30 the user opens Records with '24h' to check last evening's drinks. The list shows only the last 30 minutes, 'No records in this time range', while the dashboard (dayStartHour=2) still shows 1.8 L for the current day.
suggested_fix: Either compute start = now - 24h, or rename the scope to 'Today' and make it follow getDayStartTimestamp(dayStartHour).
verifier_corrections: This is a small point: "Records" is a tab inside the /analytics page, not a separate screen, and the one scope selector drives every analytics tab and the export. The calendar-day alignment is documented as intentional in the useTimeScopeRange docstring, so the root cause is the misleading "24h" label rather than a calculation mistake. The dashboard figure in the scenario (dayStartHour=2 still showing the previous evening's total) is plausible but I did not verify it here.

This is a mislabelled preset, not an accidental calculation. The docstring shows the calendar-midnight alignment was deliberate. The claim that "24h" means three different windows is a stretch: the rolling `getRecordsInLast24Hours` in the intake service is never exposed in the UI under a "24h" label. The dashboard figure (1.8 L with dayStartHour=2) in the failure scenario is illustrative. It is plausible, but I did not reproduce it.

title: softDeleteRecord and undoSoftDeleteRecord skip the existence check that updateRecord has, and queue sync ops for ids that don't exist
description: updateRecord returns 'Record not found' for a missing id. The soft-delete and undo helpers, and updateWeightRecord/updateBloodPressureRecord in health-service, call table.update without checking. Dexie's update resolves to 0 without throwing, so these return ok and queue an op whose target doesn't exist.
failure_scenario: A stale UI row (for example, after a pull removed the record) is deleted or undone. The user sees success, and the orphan queue entry stays in the sync queue until the attempt cap is reached. That adds to the known queue-blocking behaviour.
suggested_fix: Check the update() return count, or get() first, in every helper. Return err('Record not found') and do not enqueue when nothing changed.
verifier_corrections:
- **Unrealistic trigger:** "after a pull removed the record" can't happen, because pull only soft-deletes and never hard-deletes local rows. Reaching this needs a local hard-delete path plus a stale UI row.
- **Queue behaviour is wrong in the description:**
  - An orphan delete op is sent as a stub. It gets dropped, either immediately as "invalid" or after MAX_PUSH_ATTEMPTS.
  - An orphan upsert op (from undoSoftDeleteRecord, undoDeleteWeightRecord or updateWeightRecord) is skipped at collect time. It never counts toward attempts, so it stays in the queue forever and queueDepth never returns to 0.
- **Line numbers:** the health-service citation should be about lines 72-101 (undoDeleteWeightRecord and updateWeightRecord), not 87-101.

title: The substance range query includes its end time while every other range query excludes it
description: getRecordsBetween, the intake query and the health queries use Dexie's default between(), which is [start, end). getSubstanceRecordsByDateRange passes (true, true), which is [start, end]. useRecordsTabData and analytics combine these sources over the same range. In back-to-back windows (for example, per-day buckets built as [d, d+1)), a substance stamped exactly on a boundary is counted in both windows, while its paired water row is counted only once.
evidence:
.between([type, startTime], [type, endTime], true, true)   // substances
.where("timestamp").between(startTime, endTime)           // everything else
failure_scenario: Caffeine logged exactly at a day boundary (00:00:00.000, as a 'pick date' entry would produce) shows under two adjacent daily buckets, but its water row appears in only one.
suggested_fix: Drop the inclusive flags so all range reads use the same half-open [start, end) convention.
verifier_corrections: The inconsistency is real, but the failure scenario is wrong. No caller queries substances over back-to-back per-day windows. Daily and weekly bucketing happens in memory from a single range query, and bucketByDay drops out-of-range indexes, so no substance is counted in two daily buckets. The only reachable effect is at a single-range edge: a substance stamped exactly at range.end shows in useRecordsTabData, but its paired water row does not. This needs a custom range end that matches a record's timestamp to the millisecond. Treat it as a latent consistency cleanup (low), not a user-visible double count. The suggested fix (drop the inclusive flags) is still correct.

title: Eating rows ignore grams and show '—' when the meal has no note
description: EatingRecord has an optional grams field, but RecordRow shows only note. A meal with grams and no note renders as '—', which makes it hard to tell apart from an empty record.
evidence:
measurement = unified.record.note ? unified.record.note : "—";
Scratch render: makeEatingRecord({grams:300, note:undefined}) rendered as 'Eating—'.
failure_scenario: A user logs a 300 g meal with no description. In Records it appears as 'Eating —', and the weight is visible only by opening the edit dialog.
suggested_fix: Show `${grams} g` when present and join it with the note.
verifier_corrections: Minor point: food-section's inline recent list already shows grams, so this is an inconsistency between two views, not a total absence. Also, history-drawer.tsx uses RecordRow, but prior audit notes say the drawer is unmounted, so the Records tab is the surface users actually see.

title: Day-group entry counts show only the loaded page, so a day split across pages shows too few entries
description: Pagination slices the filtered list to page*50 before grouping, so the badge for the last loaded day counts only its visible rows. The list is sorted before the slice, so the newest records are the ones kept, but the day header understates that day's total until 'Load More' is pressed.
failure_scenario: On a heavy logging day (the owner's data has about 15-20 intake rows a day, plus meal parts) that straddles row 50, the header says '6 entries' for a day that has 22. It changes to 22 after 'Load More'.
suggested_fix: Compute day counts from the full filtered list (group first, then paginate by day), or mark the header as partial.
verifier_corrections: The line numbers are off by one: the header count is at lines 432-434, not 433-435. The "15-20 intake rows a day" figure is the auditor's guess and I did not check it. Everything else in the finding is accurate.

title: The filter tab says 'Salt' while every row it shows is labelled 'Sodium'
description: The 'Salt' filter correctly selects type==='salt' rows, which store sodium mg, but the tab label disagrees with the row label ('Sodium', from CARD_THEMES.salt). This carries the known salt/sodium naming confusion into the listing UI: a user filtering for 'Salt' sees sodium mg values, which are about 2.5x smaller than salt.
evidence:
{ value: "salt", label: "Salt" },
salt: { label: "Sodium", ...
failure_scenario: A user taps 'Salt' expecting grams of salt and sees 'Sodium 480 mg', then cannot tell whether a 1.2 g salt entry was stored correctly.
suggested_fix: Rename the filter tab to 'Sodium'.
verifier_corrections:
The failure scenario overstates the risk. The row clearly says "Sodium ... mg", so the stored value is not ambiguous. The only problem is that the tab and row labels disagree.

The trace also shows a related problem the finding missed. In record-row.tsx:29-30 the theme key is `record.type === "water" ? "water" : record.type === "sugar" ? "sugar" : "salt"`, so potassium intake rows also fall back to the salt theme. Under the "K" filter tab, potassium rows are labelled "Sodium" and use the salt icon (the "mg" unit happens to be right). That mislabelling of real data is arguably more serious than the tab name and should be its own finding.

title: adjustStock (the refill 'Add' button) reads currentStock outside its transaction: concurrent writes lose updates and currentStock drifts from the transaction sum
description: adjustStock reads the item and computes newStock = currentStock + delta BEFORE opening the Dexie rw transaction. It then writes that absolute value inside the transaction. Another stock write that commits between the read and the write (a second refill tap, a take/PRN dose, or the launch recount) is overwritten. The transaction rows are all kept, so the cached currentStock (the number every card, badge and alert shows) no longer matches the ledger until the next launch recount. The Add button's guard is the React isPending state, so two clicks handled in the same task both fire.
evidence:
const item = await db.inventoryItems.get(inventoryItemId);  // outside tx
const newStock = Math.round((currentStock + delta) * 10000) / 10000;
await db.transaction("rw", [...], async () => { await db.inventoryItems.update(inventoryItemId, { currentStock: newStock, ... })

Scratch fake-indexeddb test (deleted):
- stock 10, Promise.all([adjustStock(+30), adjustStock(+30)]) -> currentStock 40, sum of transactions 70
- stock 10, Promise.all([adjustStock(+30), logPrnDose(10mg of 10mg pill)]) -> currentStock 40, sum 39 (the dose disappears from the displayed stock)
failure_scenario: The user double-taps 'Add' for a 30-pill refill, or logs a refill while a dose/PRN mutation is in flight. The card shows 40 pills while the history lists 70 (or 39). Refill decisions follow the wrong number until the next cold start, and the wrong value is pushed to the server with a fresh updatedAt.
suggested_fix: Move the get() inside the rw transaction, or better, recompute currentStock from the non-deleted transaction sum inside the transaction, as update/delete already do. Add a ref-based double-submit guard on the Add button.
verifier_corrections: The mechanism is real, but the severity is overstated. The race window is a few milliseconds between one IndexedDB get and the transaction opening. The isPending-disabled button blocks realistic double-taps, because adjustStock finishes well before a human's second tap. A dose mutation overlapping a refill is not realistically reachable from the drawer. The transaction ledger stays intact and the launch recount (recalculateAllStock) corrects the cached currentStock. The scratch-test result (Promise.all) shows programmatic concurrency, not a user-reachable path. Adjusted from high to low.

1. The double-tap trigger is overstated. Each click is dispatched as its own event, and isPending disables the button before a realistic second tap arrives. The race needs sub-millisecond-scale concurrency, such as a dose mutation in flight at the same moment.
2. The drift is temporary. The launch-time recalculateAllStock (providers.tsx calling initStockRecalculation) corrects currentStock from the ledger.
3. Severity should be medium, not high.
4. The launch recount (recalculateAllStock) has the same read-outside-transaction pattern. It calls getCurrentStock before its transaction, so it can also clobber a write that happens at the same time.

The double-tap scenario is overstated: isPending disables the button between separate tap events, and a second tap after the first write commits gives a duplicate refill, not lost-update drift. The concurrency window is milliseconds, not the length of the whole mutation. The drift fixes itself on the next launch through recalculateAllStock, and the ledger is never corrupted. Severity should be low (latent race), not high. Side note: recalculateAllStock itself also reads the sum outside its per-item transaction, so it has the same pattern.

title: Editing only a transaction's note silently rewrites the displayed stock (mixed delta and recompute methods); the absolute total is pushed over other devices
description: adjustStock and every dose path apply a delta to the cached currentStock. updateInventoryTransaction and deleteInventoryTransaction discard the cache and recompute from the locally known non-deleted transactions, even for a note-only edit. Wherever the two have drifted (the race above, or transactions from another device not yet pulled), an unrelated edit makes the stock jump. The recomputed absolute value is written with updatedAt=now and enqueued, so under LWW it overwrites the server's currentStock, which may already include consumption from another device whose transactions this device has not pulled yet. The sync pull never recomputes currentStock when transactions arrive (no currentStock handling in the sync-*.ts files). This is the same mechanism as the known launch-recount push, but triggered by any history edit or delete in-session.
failure_scenario: Phone B logs 3 doses. Before phone A pulls B's transactions, the user edits a refill note on phone A. A writes the stale sum with a newer updatedAt, the server takes it, and B's next pull shows 3 extra pills until B's next cold start.
suggested_fix: Pick one method: make currentStock a derived value (recompute on every write and after every pull that touches inventoryTransactions), or never push currentStock at all and have the server derive it. Do not rewrite stock on a note-only edit.
verifier_corrections: Recomputing from transactions is the correct, canonical method: the launch recount does the same thing, so a note edit fixes an already drifted cache rather than corrupting it. The cross-device LWW overwrite happens equally through adjustStock and dose logging, so it is not caused by the edit or delete path. The root cause is syncing a cached currentStock counter under LWW, and that is already covered by the known launch-recount issue. All that remains here is that the push window gets wider on non-amount edits, which is low severity.

A note-only edit does not produce a new wrong value. It rewrites the cache to the transaction-derived value that the app already writes on every launch, so on a single device it corrects drift rather than creating it. The cross-device overwrite under LWW is not caused by mixing delta and recompute: adjustStock and the dose paths also push an absolute currentStock computed from the stale local cache, and they overwrite another device's consumption in exactly the same way. The real root cause is syncing the cached absolute currentStock under LWW with no recompute after pull. It heals at the next cold-start recount. In the UI, the edit always sends the amount along with the note (TransactionRow.handleSave). Severity should be low.

title: No way to correct stock to a counted value: 'adjusted' is unreachable, 'initial' and consumed rows are locked, refill input rejects negatives
description: The only stock-mutation UI is 'Log Refill': it hardcodes type 'refill' and is disabled for amount <= 0. adjustStock accepts type 'adjusted', but no caller passes it (grep finds only the type declarations). The history only lets the user edit or delete 'refill' and 'adjusted' rows. 'initial' rows (created by the v10 migration) and 'consumed' rows cannot be changed. A user who counts the box ('I have 28, the app says 35') cannot record the -7 correction. The workarounds are to rewrite an old refill's amount (which changes history at the refill's date) or to log a positive 'refill' that is really a correction. Setting an absolute count is not modelled at all.
failure_scenario: Live example: the Entresto item reads -7. To fix it the user must log a fake '+7 Refill'. If the app shows 35 pills and the box holds 28, there is no way to lower the stock except editing last month's refill from 30 to 23. The days-remaining estimate and low-stock alerts stay 7 pills optimistic in the meantime.
suggested_fix: Add a 'Set count' action that writes one 'adjusted' delta transaction (counted minus current derived stock) timestamped now. Allow negative 'adjusted' amounts. Do not allow refill rows to be rewritten into corrections.
verifier_corrections:
Small clarifications:
- A negative adjustment is possible through the edit path. The edit input (drawer:264-268) has no sign guard, so a user can rewrite a refill row to any value, including a negative one. This is the history-rewriting workaround the finding already mentions.
- I could not confirm the "Entresto reads -7" example from code. It is anecdotal.
- Deleting a refill row is another way to lower stock, with the same history-distortion caveat.

One small correction to the evidence. Editing an existing refill row has no lower limit: the edit input is `parseFloat(...) || 0` and `updateInventoryTransaction` does no validation. So a user can edit a refill to any amount, including a negative one, and that does lower the stock. This is still a history-rewriting workaround, not a proper correction, so the finding stands. "Refill input rejects negatives" applies only to the new-refill form.

title: updateInventoryTransaction does no validation: a 'refill' can be edited to a negative, zero or NaN amount
description: The service writes { ...updates } unchecked. It keeps type 'refill' whatever the sign, and it accepts NaN, which then poisons currentStock (the sum becomes NaN). The drawer's edit input maps an empty field to 0 (parseFloat('')||0), so clearing the box and pressing Save turns the refill into a 0-pill refill. There is no guard against zero or a sign flip and no confirmation. The note is only sent when non-empty, so a note can never be cleared.
failure_scenario: The user opens a 30-pill refill to fix the note, accidentally clears the amount field, and taps Save. The refill silently becomes 0, stock drops by 30, and the item shows the 'Negative' or 'Low' badge. A sign-flipped refill shows as a red 'Refill -30'.
suggested_fix: Validate in the service: require a finite amount, positive for refill, non-zero for adjusted. Reject NaN. Disable Save on an empty or invalid amount. Treat an empty note as a clear (send note: undefined, explicitly deleted).
verifier_corrections: The UI cannot reach the NaN case, because `parseFloat(...) || 0` turns NaN into 0. NaN only gets in if the service is called directly, which is a latent risk and not a user-facing path. Everything else checks out at HEAD: clearing the field saves 0, a negative refill is accepted and keeps type 'refill', and the note can't be cleared.

The NaN path cannot be reached through any UI or caller. The only caller is the drawer, and its `|| 0` coerces NaN to 0, so "accepts NaN, which then poisons currentStock" applies only to direct service calls. The refill does not "silently" become 0: the controlled input shows 0 after the field is cleared, and the user has to press Save. The note-cannot-be-cleared claim is correct. Severity should be low, not medium.

title: Days-remaining is computed twice with different phase selection: the drawer uses titration, the refill notification uses a random active phase
description: The drawer's 'Est. Supply' uses getEffectivePhase: the active titration phase first, then the maintenance phase. If no maintenance phase is active, getMaintenancePhase falls back to ANY maintenance phase (completed, cancelled or soft-deleted, since getPhasesForPrescription does not filter deletedAt). checkRefillAlerts uses `phases.find(p => p.status === 'active')` on an index query ordered by random UUID primary key. During a titration both phases are 'active' (activateTitrationPlan leaves maintenance active), so the notification uses the maintenance or the titration dose depending on the ids. The prescription card and compound list compute no days-remaining at all. Both formulas divide phase-unit dosage by item.strength with no unit check.
failure_scenario: Maintenance is 50 mg/day and the active titration is 200 mg/day, with 20 x 50 mg pills and refillAlertDays=7. The drawer shows 5 days. If the notification picks the maintenance phase it computes 20 days, so the 7-day refill alert never fires and the user runs out on day 5.
suggested_fix: Put one shared function in @intake/core that takes the phase actually driving today's schedule (the same selection as useDailyDoseSchedule), filters deleted phases and schedules, and converts units. Use it in the drawer, the notification service and the card.
verifier_corrections:
These are minor inaccuracies; the core claim is right.
- The phase list the drawer uses (`getPhasesForPrescription`) is sorted newest-first by `createdAt`, so the drawer's choice is deterministic.
- Only the notification's query is in index/primary-key order. Calling that order "random" is loose: it is fixed for a given set of phase ids, but nothing in the code controls it.
- The refill check only runs when `/medications` is mounted, notification permission is granted and at least 12 hours have passed since the last check. That limits how often the wrong alert decision can happen, but the check is still reachable.

Minor points only:
- The refill check only runs while the /medications page is mounted and notification permission is granted. It is not a background check.
- The pill-count threshold (`refillAlertPills`) can still trigger an alert, so "never fires" holds only for the days-based threshold.
- A plan with several phases makes the problem worse: activateTitrationPlan activates all of the plan's pending phases at once. So `getActiveTitrationPhase` may also pick an arbitrary titration step.
- The claim that the card and compound list show no days-remaining is context, not part of the defect.

title: Archiving the active brand leaves no active brand: later doses deduct from no stock, with no warning
description: The Archive button sets isActive:false on the active brand and does not promote another brand. takeDose and logPrnDose then find no active inventory: they log the dose, skip the stock decrement and write no consumed transaction. The prescription card's active-medicine mini-card and its Low/Negative badges disappear, so nothing tells the user that stock is no longer tracked.
failure_scenario: The user archives the finished Brand A box and forgets to tap 'Set as active brand' on Brand B. A week of doses is logged but Brand B still shows its full count, and the days estimate and alerts are wrong by 7+ pills.
suggested_fix: When archiving the active brand, require a replacement choice or auto-promote the only other non-archived brand. Show an 'untracked stock' warning on the card when a scheduled prescription has no active brand.
verifier_corrections: One small overstatement. When no brand is active, the stock stays at the old count: Brand B keeps showing its full stock. Its days-remaining estimate and alerts are only shown on the card again after Brand B is made active, and at that point they are off by the number of doses that were never deducted. The core claim is accurate.

None of substance. One small precision point: the card's refill-alert check (lines 127-131) needs activeInventory, so the Low and Negative badges disappear rather than turning wrong. The brand that is really in use keeps its full stock count, so its days estimate and alerts are wrong wherever that brand's stock is shown.

title: No UI can edit an inventory item's strength, unit or refill-alert thresholds after creation
description: The edit-medication drawer edits only prescription fields (name, indication, notes, active) and the maintenance schedule. The inventory drawer's Manage tab only activates, archives or deletes. refillAlertDays and refillAlertPills are written only by the wizard (grep finds no other writer), and strength, unit and brandName have no edit path. A strength mis-entered in the wizard (e.g. the known silent 1 mg default) can only be fixed by archiving, deleting and re-adding the brand, which loses the stock ledger. A user who skipped the thresholds can never turn on low-stock flags. Because strength is never edited, existing pill counts are at least never reinterpreted, but a wrong strength keeps being used on every deduction.
evidence: grep refillAlertDays|refillAlertPills in components -> only add-medication-wizard.tsx and inventory-step.tsx write them; ManageTab calls updateMutation only with { isActive } / { isArchived }
failure_scenario: The wizard saved a 5 mg bisoprolol box as strength 1. Every 5 mg dose deducts 5 pills, so a 30-pill box shows empty after 6 days. The user has no screen to correct the strength and must delete the medicine and its history.
suggested_fix: Add an 'Edit medicine' form for brand, strength/compounds, unit, pill look and refill thresholds. If strength changes while stock exists, ask whether the counted pills keep their count (pills) or keep their mg total, and record an 'adjusted' transaction when needed.
verifier_corrections: The failure scenario is overstated for the plain new-medicine path. The wizard sets scheduleDosage = dosageAmount * strength (add-medication-wizard.tsx line 285). If strength silently defaults to 1, the schedule dosage is saved as 1 mg as well, so each dose deducts 1 pill, not 5. The "5 mg dose deducts 5 pills" result only happens when the schedule dosage is 5 mg: either the brand was added to an existing prescription whose schedule is already 5 mg, or the schedule was later corrected to 5 mg in the edit drawer while strength stayed at 1. Both paths can be reached, so the core claim stands, but the example needs one of those preconditions.

1. The claim that you must delete the medicine and lose its history is wrong. The wizard can attach a new brand to an existing prescription: search-step has an existingPrescriptions picker, and the wizard has a separate inventory-add path around lines 309/330. The user can add a corrected brand, set it active and archive the wrong one. Archiving keeps the history ("Archiving hides this medicine ... but keeps its history"), and deleteInventoryItem is only a soft delete. The workaround is clunky, since stock has to be re-entered and the old box stays as an archived duplicate, but no data is lost.
2. The failure scenario is contrived. When strength falls back to 1, the wizard also computes the schedule as `scheduleDosage = (finalDosage || 1) * strength`, so the schedule is saved as 1 mg and each dose deducts 1 pill. Counts stay consistent; what's wrong is the mg shown. Deducting 5 pills per dose only happens if the user later changes the schedule dose to 5 mg in the edit drawer, which is possible but is not the default outcome.
3. Minor: brandName also has no edit path, as stated. Pill shape and colour are likewise not editable, which the finding doesn't mention.

title: Edit-medication 'Dosage unit' is free text that relabels doses without converting them against pill strength
description: The Schedule tab lets the user type any unit (it defaults to 'mg' when the phase has none) and saves it with the row dosages. Pill math (calculatePillsConsumed) and both days-left formulas divide the schedule dosage by item.strength as plain numbers, ignoring phase.unit and item.unit. Changing the unit to mcg and entering the dose in mcg multiplies the deduction by 1000.
evidence:
<Input value={unit} onChange={(e) => { setUnit(e.target.value); setDirty(true); }} placeholder="mg" />
export function calculatePillsConsumed(doseMg: number, pillStrengthMg: number) { const raw = doseMg / pillStrengthMg; ...}
---
[gap-combo-drugs-pill-math#10] edit-medication-drawer.tsx:218 `onChange={(e) => { setUnit(e.target.value); ... }}`; medication-ui-utils.ts:94 `formatCompoundShort(inventory!.compounds, unit)` where unit = slot.unit (phase.unit); dose-detail-dialog.tsx:190 `{inventory.brandName} {inventory.strength}{phase.unit}`.
failure_scenario: The item is Levothyroxine 0.1 mg. The user changes the schedule unit to 'mcg' and enters 100. Each 'take' deducts 1000 pills, and stock and days-left go hugely negative.
suggested_fix: Remove the free-text unit or restrict it to the item's unit. Validate phase.unit === inventory.unit, or convert, before any pill calculation.
verifier_corrections: No material corrections. One addition: the mismatch can also come from the add-medication wizard, where the inventory unit is parsed from strength text such as "mcg" while the phase unit is set separately, not only from the edit drawer. Stock deduction happens in five call sites in dose-log-service.ts (lines 290, 389, 480, 549 and 620), not just the lines cited.

No material errors. One small point: the extreme result requires the user to change the unit and also type the dose in the new unit. If they change only the label and leave the number alone, the pill math is unaffected and only the displayed labels are wrong. I only confirmed the calculatePillsConsumed side, not the days-left formulas at dose-schedule-service.ts:200 or inventory-item-view-drawer.tsx:166-167.

title: Days-remaining and low-stock count only the active brand's stock and ignore spare boxes
description: The Low badge and the refill alert look only at the single active, non-archived item. Non-archived inactive brands of the same prescription (a second pharmacy box) do not count toward supply. The drawer also shows a days-left figure for an inactive brand using the full daily dose, even though no dose deducts from it. With negative stock the drawer prints negative days (Math.floor(-7/1) = -7).
evidence:
const activeInventory = inventoryItems.find((item) => item.isActive && !item.isArchived);
const stock = activeInventory.currentStock ?? 0;
failure_scenario: The active box has 5 pills and a spare generic box has 60. The card shows 'Low' and the alert fires for a refill the user does not need, while the drawer shows 5 days of supply.
suggested_fix: Base supply on all non-archived, non-deleted items of the prescription (normalised by strength), and label the result for the active box separately.
verifier_corrections:
The main claim, that the Low badge and refill alert ignore spare inactive boxes, describes intentional per-brand tracking (only the active item is deducted). It is not clearly a bug, and it only matters in the uncommon case where a user keeps a spare box as a separate inactive item instead of logging a refill. The confirmed defects are in the drawer (inventory-item-view-drawer.tsx:164-170 and the display at ~182):
1. It shows an estimated supply in days for an inactive brand using the full daily dose, even though that stock is never deducted.
2. It shows negative days when stock is negative, because there is no clamp or special case, unlike prescription-card.tsx, which checks isNegativeStock.

title: Refill form pre-fills 30 pills; one tap books a 30-pill refill whatever the box size
description: refillAmount initialises to 30 and resets to 30 after each save, so Add is enabled immediately. Refills are always stamped 'now' with no date field, so a refill collected earlier cannot be backdated.
evidence:
const [refillAmount, setRefillAmount] = useState<number>(30);
{ onSuccess: () => { setRefillAmount(30); setRefillNote(""); } }
failure_scenario: The user picks up a 28-pill pack and taps Add without editing the number. Stock is overstated by 2 pills and there is no edit prompt.
suggested_fix: Start the field empty (or at the pack size stored on the item) and require an explicit value.
verifier_corrections: The suggested fix proposes using "the pack size stored on the item", but the schema has no such field: packSize, pillsPerPack and boxSize do not appear anywhere in packages/types or apps/web/src. The failure scenario says the overstated stock can't be corrected. That is wrong: refill transactions can be edited afterwards from the History list, so the amount can be fixed. Only the timestamp can't be edited, because the edit form updates just the amount and note. Nothing warns the user when they save the default, but the default is shown in plain view in the field.

title: Deleting an inventory transaction has no undo
description: Delete uses window.confirm and then soft-deletes. There is no undo toast and no restore function. currentStock is recomputed correctly at once (checked in the scratch test), but the only way back is to re-enter the refill by hand with a new timestamp. The known launch-recount bug then adds the deleted row back into the total anyway.
evidence: if (window.confirm("Delete this transaction? Stock will be recalculated.")) { deleteMutation.mutate(tx.id); }
failure_scenario: The user deletes the wrong refill row. Stock drops by 30, and restoring it means logging a new '+30 Refill' dated today, which scrambles the history.
suggested_fix: Add an undo toast that clears deletedAt (and enqueues sync), matching the other domains.
verifier_corrections: No factual errors. One nuance: the lack of undo is a UX gap and low severity. The larger problem is the recount bug it mentions, where getCurrentStock ignores deletedAt. That bug means deleted transactions come back into stock at the next launch, and it should be tracked separately at higher severity.
